This Act is applicable for all including migrants, irrespective of citizenship. However, the medium of primary education is Bengali.

question_text_en: Right to be free from discrimination on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The Bangladesh Open University Act, 1992 (Act no. 38 of 1992) provides for adult education. However, the Act is silent about non-citizens or immigrants.

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after convictions.
citation_text_en: National law in Bangladesh regulates this right in The Control of Entry Act, 1952; the Foreigners Act, 1946; the Naturalization Act, 1926, Section 16(3)(c) of the Citizenship Act, 1951 (Act No. II of 1951); and Section 8(2)(b) of the Naturalization Act, 1926 (Act No.VII of 1926).

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of torture or inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in Bangladesh protects this right. Though there is no specific provision in national law that bans refoulement on the basis of a risk of return to torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment, Bangladesh is a party to the UN Convention Against Torture, Cruel, Inhuman, or Degrading Treatment or Punishment, and the High-Court decision in Refugee and Migratory Movements Research Unit (RMMRU) v. Government of Bangladesh, 19 (2020) ALR (HCD) 17, Writ petition no. 10504 of 2016, Bangladesh: Supreme Court, 31 May 2017 affirmed that the prohibition against return to torture is a binding obligation. Therefore, under Article 111 of the Constitution, the principle of non-refoulement has now become 'law declared by the Suprmeme Court' which must be followed by the Executive and the Judiciary.'

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of persecution.
citation_text_en: National law in Bangladesh protects this right. Even though there is no national legal provision formally codifying this right, the High Court Division has confirmed that the customary international law protection of the right against refoulement on the basis of a risk of return to persecution on the basis of race, religion, nationality, membership of a particular social group, or political opinion applies to protect migrants. The four 2017 judgements of the High Court Division are as follows: 1) - Refugee and Migratory Movement Research Unit (RMMRU) vs. Government of Bangladesh, Writ Petition No. 10504 of 2016. Judgment Delivered on 31.05.2017. 2) RMMRU v. Government of Bangladesh, Writ Petition No. 6989 of 2016. Judgment Delivered on 31.05.2017. 3) RMMRU v. Government of Bangladesh, Writ Petition No. 12492 of 2016. Judgment Delivered on 31.05.2017. 4) RMMRU v. Government of Bangladesh, Writ Petition No. 12493 of 2016. Judgment Delivered on 31.05.2017. These four decisions were consolidated and reported as Refugee and Migratory Movements Research Unit (RMMRU) v. Government of Bangladesh, 19 (2020) ALR (HCD) 17. Therefore, under Article 111 of the Constitution, the principle of non-refoulement has now become 'law declared by the Suprmeme Court' which must be followed by the Executive and the Judiciary.'

question_text_en: Right to not return to a deprivations of fundamental human rights.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to be advised of availability of asylum before expulsion.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from chain refoulement.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to protection against expulsion except following a legal judgment.
citation_text_en: National law in Bangladesh protects this right for all migrants in 1) Section 3 of The Foreigners Act, 1946 (Act no. XXXI). 2) Section 16(3) of the Citizenship Act, 1951 (Act No. II of 1951). 3) Section 8(2) of the Naturalization Act, 1926 (Act No.VII of 1926). 4) Paragraph No. 10 of the Bangladesh Board of Investments (now renamed as Bangladesh Investment Development Authority [BIDA]) Guidelines 2011.

question_text_en: Right to submit reasons against expulsion and have case reviewed before deportation.
citation_text_en: National law in Bangladesh protects this right in Section 16(6) of the Citizenship Act, 1951 (Act No. II of 1951); and Section 8(4) of the Naturalization Act, 1926 (Act No.VII of 1926) and Article 102 of the Constitution of Bangladesh.

question_text_en: Right of settled migrants to family reunification.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to judicial remedy for denials of right to family reunification.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Reunification with family members of the migrants is facilitated under the administrative Visa Policy of Bangladesh. Visa Policy of Bangladesh does not have the force of law and any part of the policy may be changed by an executive. However, the policy is treated as soft law and usually strictly followed. Therefore, if it is ever invoked in judicial proceedings, it is likely to carry substantial weight and may compel executive action.

question_text_en: Right to recognition of same-sex marital relationships.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Bangladeshi Visa Policy does not have any provision for filing appeal against any of the decisions taken under the said policy. Visa Policy of Bangladesh does not have the force of law and any part of the policy may be changed by an executive. However, the policy is treated as soft law and usually strictly followed. Therefore, if it is ever invoked in judicial proceedings, it is likely to carry substantial weight and may compel executive action.

question_text_en: Right to family reunification without resource conditions
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Same-sex relationships are prohibited under Section 377 of the Penal Code.

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services.
citation_text_en: In Bangladesh, temporary migrant workers' switch to permanent status is unconditional on visa as regulated in Section 9 of the Citizenship Act, 1951; and Sections 3, 4, and 5 of the Naturalization Act, 1926 (Act No. VII of 1926).

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services regardless of status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The Naturalization Act, 1926 and the Citizenship Act, 1951 do not provide avenues for irregular migrants to regularize their status as a migrant.

question_text_en: Right of access to public housing programs.
citation_text_en: National law in Bangladesh protects this right in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, which protects breaches of contract. However, it should be noted that refugees and irregular migrants are not covered under this provision.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to free primary education for migrant children.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. There is no law guaranteeing public access to health care services, including emergecny services, in Bangladesh. However, as a practical matter migrants, including irregular migrants and refugees are able to access to emergency medical services in public hospitals. In addition, migrants can easily access private health care services if they can pay for them.

question_text_en: Right to equal pay for the same work.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Article 66 (1) of the Constitution of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh; Section 19(1) of the Local Government (Municipalities) Act 2009; Section 9(1) of Local Government (City Corporation) Act 2009; and Section 26(1) Local Government (Union Porishad) Act 2009 mandate that only citizens can be candidates in local and national elections.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of choice of employment.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right of spouse/partner of principal migrant to work.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after loss of employment.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for all migrants. Only the salaries of skilled migrants are negotiated by employers and a special minimum salary structure (not equal salary) is provided in the Table in Paragraph 13 of the Guidelines 2011 issued by Board of Investment (now renamed as Bangladesh Investment Development Authority- BIDA).

question_text_en: Right to equal employment conditions and protection.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. In order to change the employer, migrant worker requires to leave Bangladesh and re-apply for a new visa and new work permit. This issue is regulated in: (1) Paragraph 6(f) of the Guidelines 2011 issued by Board of Investment, Bangladesh for Granting permission for Establishing/Opening of Branch, Liaison & Representative Office of Foreign Companies in Bangladesh & Issuing Work Permit of Foreign National(s); (2) Section 35(2) of the Bangladesh Investment Development Authority Act, 2016 (Act No. XXXVI of 2016); and (3) Visa Policy of Bangladesh.

question_text_en: Right to form trade unions and other associations.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. No such right is provided in the Guidelines, 2011 issued by Board of Investment, Bangladesh for Granting permission for Establishing/Opening of Branch, Liaison & Representative Office of Foreign Companies in Bangladesh & Issuing Work Permit of Foreign National(s).

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to redress before deportation or withdrawal of residency permit.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to social security protections.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. There is no national law in Bangladesh that regulates overtime payment, paid leave, and other benefits of a migrant worker.

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to become lawfully settled.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Article 15(d) of the Constitution of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh states that the right to social security applies to citizens only.

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to settle regardless of initial status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Article 15(d) of the Constitution of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh states that the right to unemployment benefit applies to citizens only.

question_text_en: Right to redress following employer breach of employment contract.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Rather, national law in Bangladesh provides a pathway to citizenship for temporary migrant workers provided certain conditions are met in Section 3 and Section 5 of the Naturalization Act, 1926 (Act. No. VII of 1926).

question_text_en: Right not to have identity documents confiscated.
citation_text_en: National law in Bangladesh protects this right in Sections 96 to 99 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 and Articles 31 and 32 of the Constitution and this right is guaranteed for all staying in Bangladesh irrespective of citizenship.

question_text_en: Right to birth registration.
citation_text_en: National law in Bangladesh protects this right in Birth and Death Registration Act, 2004; Section 2 and Section 6 (Act No. 29 of 2004). Under the Birth and Death Registration Act, 2004 (Act No. 29 of 2004) birth and death registration of any person staying in Bangladesh is mandatory. Section 2 of this Act specifically mentions that the word "person" includes any Bangladeshi or any foreigner or refugee staying in Bangladesh.

question_text_en: Right to government document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Bangladesh Visa Policy specifies that visa stamps are to be granted to all regular migrants which provide for the identity of the individual, and the conditions of their permission to enter/stay, including work status. Visa Policy of Bangladesh does not have the force of law and any part of the policy may be changed by an executive. However, the policy is treated as soft law and usually strictly followed. Therefore, if it is ever invoked in judicial proceedings, it is likely to carry substantial weight and may compel executive action. Additionally, the Data Bank of the Board of Investment, Bangladesh preserves data for the above purpose under Paragraph 15(Data Bank) of the Guidelines, 2011 issued by the Board of Investment, which can issue documents granting permission for the establishment/opening of branch, liaison & representative office of foreign companies in Bangladesh, as well as for issuing work permits for foreign naationals. However, in both instances, there is no legal requirement for the Bangladeshi authorities issue an identity document.

question_text_en: Right against destruction of document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: National law in Bangladesh protects this right in: (a) Section 477 of the Penal Code (Act No. XLV of 1860) which makes the destruction of a document issued by the government a criminal offense; (b)Visa Policy; (c) the Guidelines 2011 issued by the Board of Investment, Bangladesh for Granting permission for Establishing/Opening of Branch, Liaison & Representative Office of Foreign Companies in Bangladesh & Issuing Work Permit of Foreign National(s). Additionally, right to protection of law and right to personal liberty is guaranteed under Article 31 and 32 of the Constitution of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh irrespective of citizenship and status.

question_text_en: Right to communicate with consular officials.
citation_text_en: There is no formal protection of this right in national law. However, there is a consistent practice of providing consular access in a manner that broadly correlates with Article 36 of the Vienna Convention.

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. However, Section 44 of the Children Act, 2013 (Act No. 24 of 2013) does prohibit arrest and detention of migrant children under 9 years old. Migrant children older than 9 years may not be detained in adult prisons but the Children Act provides detention of such children in conflict with the law in juvenile centers.

question_text_en: Right of migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The migrants can be detained, arrested or punished for commission of offenses under the Control of Entry Act, 1952 (Act LV of 1952), the Foreigners Act, 1946 (Act No. XXXI of 1946) or under any other penal provision of existing laws of Bangladesh. The Foreigners Act of 1946 allows the detention of persons entering Bangladesh without proper documentation.

question_text_en: Right to appeal legality, conditions, and length of detention
citation_text_en: National law in the People's Republic of Bangladesh protects this right in Articles 31, 32, and 33 of the Constitution. According to these articles, any person irrespective of citizenship has a right to appeal against any order detaining him/her in custody. Besides the provision of appeal, the legality and length of detention order can also be challenged under Article 102(2)(b)(i) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh (Habeas Corpus).

question_text_en: Right to an individualized detention decision.
citation_text_en: National law in Bangladesh allows individual determination of responsibility under Section 3(2)(g) and Section 14 of the Foreigners Act, 1946 (Act No. XXXI of 1946); and Section 4 of the 'the Control of Entry Act, 1952 (Act LV of 1952). Furthermore, Article 31, 32, 33 and 35 of the Constitution of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh also approves individual determination of responsibility.

question_text_en: Right to be free from torture and inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in Bangladesh protects this right in Article 35(5) of the Constitution. This article prohibits torture or cruel, inhuman, or degrading punishment or treatment to any person including migrants.

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: National law in Bangladesh protects this right in the Border Guard of Bangladesh Act, 2010 and article 35 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. Border Guard of Bangladesh Act, 2010 expressly does not permit the use of any force. Article 35 of the "Constitution of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh" prohibits any kind of torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading punishment or treatment to any person.

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of lethal force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: National law in Bangladesh protects this right in the Border Guard of Bangladesh Act, 2010 and article 35 (5) of the Constitution.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from trafficking or smuggling.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. National law in Bangladesh does not exempt any smuggled or trafficked migrant from prosecution, as the notion of ‘victim protection’ is not protected under the Bangladeshi criminal justice system.

question_text_en: Right to maintain citizenship status after convictions.
citation_text_en: National law in Bangladesh protects this right in Section 16 of the Citizenship Act, 1951 (Act No. II of 1951); and Section 8 of the Naturalization Act, 1926 (Act No.VII of 1926). Any conviction with imprisonment of more than 12 months during the first 5 years of naturalization may lead to revocation of citizenship.

question_text_en: Right of economic migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Bangladesh protects this right in Section 3 of the Naturalization Act, 1926 and Section 9 of the Citizenship Act, 1951 (Act No. II of 1951). Primary requirement for naturalization is residency in Bangladesh for a period of 5 years and this requirement applies to all categories of migrants. In addition to the conditions laid down in section 3 of the Naturalization Act (1926), section 9 of the Citizenship Act (1951) confers discretionary power on the executive to grant citizenship without satisfying the requirements of the Naturalization Act.

question_text_en: Right of humanitarian migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Bangladesh protects this right in Sections 3, 4 and 5 of the Naturalization Act, 1926; Section 9 of the Citizenship Act, 1951 (Act No. II of 1951).

question_text_en: Right of family migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Bangladesh protects this right in Sections 3 and 5 of the Naturalization Act, 1926; Section 9 and 10 of the Citizenship Act, 1951 (Act No. II of 1951). The requirements of The Naturalization Act 1926 and The Citizenship Act, 1951 have to be fulfilled, particularly 5-year residency requirement.

question_text_en: Right to dual nationality.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for all migrants. National law in Bangladesh regulates this right in Sections 14 and 20 of the Citizenship Act, 1951. Section 14 of the Citizenship Act, 1951 (Act No. II of 1951) prohibits dual citizenship. However, Section 20 of the Citizenship Act, 1951 (Act No. II of 1951) provides an exception where Commonwealth Citizens can obtain dual citizenship.

question_text_en: Right to freedom to hold opinion.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Article 39(1) of the Constitution does protect the right to freedom of thought and conscience for all persons. However, Article 41 of the Constitution regulates the right to freedom of religion and guarantees this right only to citizens.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of expression.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Article 39(2) of the Constitution allows freedom of speech and opinion to citizens only.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of association.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Article 39(2) of the Constitution of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh allows freedom of speech and expression to citizens only.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of assembly.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Article 38 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh recognizes this right only to the citizens.

category: Thought, conscience, and religion or belief
question_text_en: Right of freedom of thought, conscience and religion or belief.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The Bangladeshi Visa Policy indicates that the migrant applicant is required to provide recommendation of his/her employer and solvency certificates before they are able to request family reunification for immediate family members. Visa Policy of Bangladesh does not have the force of law and any part of the policy may be changed by an executive. However, the policy is treated as soft law and usually strictly followed. Therefore, if it is ever invoked in judicial proceedings, it is likely to carry substantial weight and may compel executive action.

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to access criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: National law in Bangladesh protects this right in Articles 31 and 32 of the Constitution. Article 31 of the Constitution guarantees equal (substantive and procedural) protection of law and mandates that every person is treated equally irrespective of citizenship, nationality, ethnicity, gender, religion etc.

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to immigration status or relief from expulsion.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Children Act, 2013 (Act No. 24 of 2013) provides special protections and rights for the children, but it is silent on migrant children.

question_text_en: Right of women migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Even if national laws in Bangladesh protect rights of women and girl in general in legislations such as the Suppression of Violence against Women and Children Act, 2000; Child Marriage Restraint Act 2017; Dowry Prohibition Act, 2018; these laws do not provide special protection for migrant women who are vulnerable in comparison to other migrants.

question_text_en: Rights of migrants with disabilities to special protection.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The "Rights and Protection of the Persons with Disabilities Act, 2013" (Act No. 39 of 2013) provides special protections and rights for the persons with disabilities, but it is silent about the migrants with disabilities. Furthermore, Article 15 of the "Constitution of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh" has secured the right and protection for only the citizens with disabilities, and not the the migrants.

question_text_en: What is your name?
citation_text_en: [1]: Birte Schorpion. [2]: Sylvie Sarolea.

question_text_en: What country are you coding?
citation_text_en: Belgium.

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to vote in local and/or regional elections.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in 1) the Belgian Constitution, Article 26 and 191. 2) European Convention on Human Rights, Art. 11 (Law of 13 May 1955 approving the Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms, signed in Rome on 4 November 1950 and the Additional Protocol to that Convention, signed in Paris on 20 March 1952).

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to stand for election.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. However, several categories of migrants are able to vote in municipal and communal elections in several circumstances. These include 1) the Municipal Electoral Act, Articles 1b, and 86. 2) The Local Provincial Electoral Decree of 8 July 2011. 3) Law of 19 March 2004 On Granting the Right to Vote in Communal Elections to Certain Foreigners. European Union (EU) citizens can vote in communal/municipal elections under the conditions that they have to reside in Belgium and ask to be listed on the voting list of their municipality (commune). EU citizens can vote in local elections and elections for the European parliament (on the condition they don't vote for the latter in their home EU member state), while those coming from a third country can only vote in local elections. Other non-EU migrants must have established their principal residence in Belgium in an interrupted manner during the 5 years preceding the application, they must be registered in the Belgian population registry or in the foreigners registry (not the waiting registry), they must ask to be enlisted on the voting list in their municipality (commune), and they must sign a declaration by which he or she undertakes to respect the Constitution, the laws of the Belgian people and the Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms.

question_text_en: Right to equal protection of the law before courts.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Belgian Constitution, Article 191 and the Anti-Discrimination Law. While neither law stipulates migratory status as a prohibited criteria, discrimination on the basis of nationality, race, color, origin or national or ethnic origin is prohibited.

question_text_en: Right to government-provided counsel in proceedings related to migrant status.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in 1) the Belgian Constitution, Article 23, §3, 2°, which stipulates that the right to legal aid is one of the elements of the right to lead a life in conformity with human dignity. Legal aid may be free of charge for people (migrants and non migrants) with insufficient means of livelihood. Note that an alien without a residence permit or an asylum-seeker enjoys a rebuttable presumption of insufficient financial means which enables them to receive legal aid with regard to procedures in connection with their application for residence or asylum (Royal Decree of 18 December 2003, Article 1, §2). A minor alien benefits from an irrebuttable presumption (Royal Decree of 18 December 2003, Art. 1, §4). 2) The Judiciary Code, Articles 664 - 668 . 3) The Aliens law, Article 90.

question_text_en: Right to government-provided interpretation in criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Code of Criminal Procedures, Articles 152bis, and 184bis and the Judiciary Code Article 691.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from prosecution for unauthorized entry.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. One exception is found in Article 53 of the Aliens Law, which states that, "An applicant for international protection who attempts to enter the Kingdom without fulfilling the requirements set forth in Articles 2 and 3, or who is illegally residing in the Kingdom, shall not be subject to criminal prosecution on this ground until a final decision has been made on his application for international protection."

question_text_en: Right to equal access to public adult education institutions.
citation_text_en: Belgium, being a federal state, has housing as a defederalised competence. So while there is no national law in place (logical, as this is a defederalised competence), regular migrants benefit from protection at the regional level (each defederated region has some level of legal provision for housing of regular migrants). For example, in Flanders, this is protected under Title VII of the Flemish Housing Code which protects both Belgians and regular migrants with equal access to public housing. Further, Asylum seekers are provided with accommodation in accordance with the national Law of 12 January 2007 on the reception of asylum-seekers and certain other categories of foreigners, Article 2, 6°. Finally, Irregular migrants have no specific right to housing

question_text_en: Right of access to public adult education institutions regardless of status.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Belgian Constitution, Article 24 and the Aliens Law, Articles 74/14 and 57/35. All children have the right to education, as is stipulated in the constitution. Expulsion can even be delayed in case children are enrolled in schools to ensure that they can finish the year.

question_text_en: Right to be free from discrimination on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: Belgium, being a federal state, has education as a defederalised competence. So while there is no national law in place (logical, as this is a defederalised competence), there are regional provisions that guarantee access to public adult educational institutions and services to migrants commensurate with citizens, such as the Flemish Decree on adult education (15 June 2007), Articles 31-37.

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after convictions.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Alien Laws, Articles 11, 15bis, 16bis, 19, 21 - 23, 43, 44bis, 49, 49/2, 55/3/1, 55/4, 55/5/1, 61/1/3 and 74/20. A recognized refugee can lose their residence status when, having been convicted of a particularly serious offense, it is considered that they constitute a danger to society or when there are reasonable grounds for considering that the foreign national is a danger to national security. An alien shall be excluded from subsidiary protection status where there are substantial grounds for considering that he or she has committed a crime against peace, a war crime or a crime against humanity, has been guilty of acts contrary to the purposes and principles of the United Nations or has committed a serious crime. They may also lose his or her residence status when they represent a danger to society or national security or when they have left their country of origin exclusively in order to escape punishment for an offense that would be punishable by imprisonment if committed in Belgium.

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of torture or inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in 1) the Aliens Law, Articles 20, 24, 49, 49/2, 49/3/1, 55/5/1, 57/6, 57/6/1, 57/6/2, 67/6/6, 61/8, 74/17. 2) European Convention on Human Rights, Art. 3 (Law of 13 May 1955 approving the Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms, signed in Rome on 4 November 1950 and the Additional Protocol to that Convention, signed in Paris on 20 March 1952) 3) The European Charter of Fundamental Rights, Art. 4.

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of persecution.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Aliens Law, Articles 48/3, 55/5/1, 57/6/6 and 74/17.

question_text_en: Right to not return to a deprivations of fundamental human rights.
citation_text_en: National law protects this right in 1) the Aliens Law, Articles 20, 24, 49, 49/2, 49/3/1, 55,5,1, 57/6/1, 57/6/2, 61/8, and 74/17. 2) European Convention on Human Rights, Art. 2 (Law of 13 May 1955 approving the Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms, signed in Rome on 4 November 1950 and the Additional Protocol to that Convention, signed in Paris on 20 March 1952). Belgium has incorporated the principle of non-refoulement into its domestic law by prohibiting any return to a country that is not considered as "safe". The Belgian legal framework, based on the European legal framework, has multiple concepts of safe country: safe third country, safe country of origin, first country of asylum, and European safe third country.

question_text_en: Right to be advised of availability of asylum before expulsion.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from chain refoulement.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Aliens Law, Articles 39/70 and 57/6/6.

question_text_en: Right to protection against expulsion except following a legal judgment.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Aliens Law, Articles 4, 7, 8, 13, 21-23, 24, 26, 27, 44ter - 44quinquies, 46bis, 62, §2, 74/13. Rejection at the border must be motivated. As regards to removal orders, a distinction must be made between those that are notified following a simple establishment of the migrants' illegal stay, and those that are incidental to a decision to refuse or withdraw a residence permit. Finally, as regards to ministerial return orders and royal expulsion orders, decisions must be based exclusively on the personal conduct of the person concerned.

question_text_en: Right to submit reasons against expulsion and have case reviewed before deportation.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Aliens Law, Articles 39/2, 39/82, 62. The right to be heard principle, stated in Article 62, allows for the migrant to submit their reasons against their expulsion (so long as the decision has not been made). Once the decision has been adopted, the migrant also has the opportunity to challenge this decision (when needed, in extreme urgency) before the judge (the Aliens Litigation Council). The judge in these proceedings can only rule on the legality of the decision, without being able to substitute their assessment for that of the Aliens Office. The discretion of the administration is, however, tempered by several factors: the obligation to provide adequate reasons to the migrant, the necessity to take into account the reasons that the migrant has given before the adoption of the decision, and the restriction of the migrants freedom with regard to internationally protected fundamental rights.

question_text_en: Right of settled migrants to family reunification.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Belgian Nationality Code, Articles 10, 19§2, 22, 23, 23/1 and 23/2. The law stipulates that a child born in Belgium and who has no other nationality is to be attributed the Belgian nationality according to Article 10. It also allows for persons who are stateless to apply for naturalization under certain conditions, Article 19§2.

question_text_en: Right to judicial remedy for denials of right to family reunification.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium conditionally protects this right in the Aliens Law, Articles 10, 10bis, and 40bis. Provided that the sponsor meets the socio-economic criteria, the nuclear family is entitled to family reunification under Articles 10 and 10bis. The dependency relationship applies only to family members who do not belong to the nuclear family. Article 40 is only applicable to people from the European Economic Zone, and unsettled migrants (e.g. asylum seekers) do not have this right.

question_text_en: Right to recognition of same-sex marital relationships.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in 1) the Aliens Law, Articles 39/1, 39/2, 39/82 and 63 2) The Judiciary Code, Article 584. A decision refusing to allow family formation can be challenged before a civil judge (e.g., in case of suspicion of a sham marriage), whereas a decision refusing to allow family reunification can be challenged before the Aliens Litigation Council.

question_text_en: Right to family reunification without resource conditions
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in 1) the Aliens Law, 10, §1, 4° and 5°. 2) The Belgian Code of Private International Law, Articles 46 (under title "Law applicable to marriage").

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services.
citation_text_en: NA

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services regardless of status.
citation_text_en: Irregular migrant workers can regularize if some conditions are met. If a migrant has at least a temporary right to stay, they may seek a "permit to work and stay", from the Belgian soil, under Art. 61/25-1 and following of the Aliens Law. An irregular migrant in Belgium cannot envisage such a request but they can try to regularize through a request based on Article 9ter of the Aliens Law on the condition that the person has a medical condition. They could also try to regularize through a request based on Article 9bis of the Aliens Law but the decision is entirely at the discretion of the immigration authorities.

question_text_en: Right of access to public housing programs.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in Law of 3 July 1978 on employment contracts, Article 20.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to free primary education for migrant children.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in 1) the Belgian Constitution, Article 23. 2) The Organic Law on Public Centres for Social Action of 8 July 1976, Article 57, §2. 3) The Law on Compulsory Health Care and Indemnity Insurance coordinated 14 July 1994. 4) The Law of 6 August 1990 on Mutual Insurance Companies and National Unions of Mutual Insurance Companies. With the exception of irregular migrants who receive only urgent medical assistance, migrants are subject to the same health care regime as citizens, i.e. membership of a mutual insurance company. Membership of the mutual society is through participation in a contributory scheme for workers and is automatic for the beneficiaries of the public centre for social action.

question_text_en: Right to equal pay for the same work.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. One exception to this are European Union Citizens, who can run for office in European Parliament elections in Belgium.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of choice of employment.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. National discrimination law does not include the ground of status as migrant, but only includes protection against discrimination based on age, citizen orientation, marital status, birth, property, religion or belief, political belief, language, current or future health condition, disability, physical or genetic trait or social origin. The question arose with regard to nationality of residence permit. As far as nationality is concerned, a distinction must be made between established foreigners, for whom case law clearly treats them differently from citizens (Belgian Constitutional Court, 12 December 2007, No. 153/2007; European Court of Human Rights, Gaygusuz v. Austria, 23 May 1996), and foreigners on the move, where the nature of discrimination based on nationality is blurred insofar as the question focuses instead on the right to migrate (European Court of Human Rights, Moustaquim v. Belgium, 18 February 1991; European Court of Human Rights, C. v. Belgium, 7 August 1996; Belgian Constitutional Court, 22 March 2006, No. 46/2006; Belgian Constitutional Court, 26 September 2013, No. 121/2013). As far as the quality of residence is concerned, discrimination is justified and only the hard core of rights relating to one’s dignity can be protected (Belgian Constitutional Court, 29 June 1994, No. 51/94). The European Court of Human Rights is, however, more generous, considering that “there must be particularly compelling reasons for justifying a difference in treatment between persons holding a residence permit and persons without one” (European Court of Human Rights, Anakomba Yula v. Belgium, 10 March 2009, §37).

question_text_en: Right of spouse/partner of principal migrant to work.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. There are no national legal frameworks that are applicable to this right, but there do exist regional frameworks that ban discrimination, such as the Anti-Discrimination Law of Flanders, Articles 33-42.

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after loss of employment.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Anti-Discrimination Law, Article 4 and the Labor Contract Act of 3 July 1978.

question_text_en: Right to equal employment conditions and protection.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in 1) the Aliens Law, Articles 61/26 and 61/29-5 and Chapters VIIbis and VIII. 2) Cooperation Agreement between the Federal State, the Walloon Region, the Flemish Region, the Brussels-Capital Region and the German-speaking Community on the coordination of policies on the granting of work permits and residence permits, as well as on standards relating to the employment and residence of foreign workers. 3) The Law of 22/07/2018 amending the law of 15/12/1980 on access to the territory, stay, settlement and removal of foreigners. 4) Law of February 19, 1965 on the exercise by foreigners of independent professional activities. If they do not otherwise have a right of residence, foreigners who wish to work (as employees) in Belgium can only do so on the basis of a contract concluded with an employer established in Belgium. The latter must apply for an occupation permit by showing that the employer and the worker both fulfill several conditions. The application for a work permit is equivalent to an application for a residence permit (single application). If the migrant wishes to work on an independent basis in Belgium, they must apply for a professional card (demonstrating they fulfill many conditions). Here again, a change of activity will require a new work and residence permit.

question_text_en: Right to form trade unions and other associations.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in Royal Decree amending the Royal Decree of 8 October 1981 on access to the territory, stay, establishment and removal of foreigners, Annex 6 and Annex 9. A migrant (third country) who came to Belgium via family reunification will receive, if their spouse is a foreigner of a third country, an "A-card". This card will allow them to have access to the employer market (unlimited). If the migrant wishes to have an independent activity, then they must ask for a professional card. The migrant (third country) who came thanks to family reunification will receive, if their spouse is a Belgian or EU citizen, an "F-card". This will give them automatic access to work (employee as well as independent).

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to redress before deportation or withdrawal of residency permit.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for low-skilled migrants. Highly skilled migrant workers have the right to remain unemployed for up to three months without the risk of losing their residence permits. This exception is part of European Law (Blue Card directive) to which Belgium is bound. For those other migrants who reside in Belgium on labor permits, this does not apply.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to social security protections.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in 1) the Labor contract Act of 3 of July 1978 that is a public order regulation. 2) The Blue Card Directive, Article 14. 3) The Seasonal Workers Directive, Article 23. 4) The Constitution, Article 10, 11, and 191, which prevents discrimination or unequal treatment, and the anti-discrimination law (10.05.2007) further clarifies that there cannot be any unequal treatment on the basis of origin or nationality.

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to become lawfully settled.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in 1) the Law of 30 March 1994 on Social Provisions. 2) Royal Decree No. 50 (24 October 1967) on the retirement and survivor's pension for employees, Article 27. For social insurance programs, such as unemployment, pensions, medical expenses, etc., the general rule is that everyone who works and resides in Belgium legally is entitled to social security benefits in Belgium (and must contribute on a mandatory basis), provided that they fulfill the general conditions (such as waiting periods and minimum contributions). This means that everyone, Belgians, permanent and temporary immigrants must participate in the system. However, the most striking difference is the rule that third-country nationals who have not concluded a bilateral social security agreement with Belgium cannot "export" their pension rights. Even if they have contributed to the social security system during their entire career, they must reside in Belgium / Europe to receive their pension.

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to settle regardless of initial status.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Royal Decree of 25 November 1991 regulating unemployment, Articles 30-34, and 43. For social insurance programs, such as unemployment, pensions, medical expenses, etc., the general rule is that everyone who works and resides in Belgium legally is entitled to social security benefits in Belgium (and must contribute on a mandatory basis), provided that they fulfill the general conditions (such as waiting periods and minimum contributions). This means that everyone, Belgians, permanent and temporary immigrants must participate in the system. However, the most striking difference is the rule that third-country nationals who have not concluded a bilateral social security agreement with Belgium cannot "export" their pension rights. Even if they have contributed to the social security system during their entire career, they must reside in Belgium / Europe to receive their pension.

question_text_en: Right to redress following employer breach of employment contract.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Article 15 of the Aliens Law specifically exlcudes temporary migrants.

question_text_en: Right not to have identity documents confiscated.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to birth registration.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Civil Code, Articles 42-44. The birth of a child must be registered regardless their status, but there are different registers to differentiate categories of people (for example, waiting register, foreign register, population register).

question_text_en: Right to government document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Aliens Law, Articles 5, 12, 17, 41bis, 42quinquies, §5.

question_text_en: Right against destruction of document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to communicate with consular officials.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in 1) the Royal Decree of 2 August 2002 "Establishing the Regime and Operating Rules Applicable to Places Located on Belgian territory , managed by the Aliens Office, where an alien is detained, placed at the disposal of the Government or maintained, pursuant to the provisions cited in Art. 74/8, § 1", Articles 32-33 2) The Aliens Law, Article 74/8. 3) The Vienna Convention on Consular Relations, Art. 36 (Law of 17 July 1970 approving the following international acts: 1. Vienna Convention on Consular Relations; 2. optional signature protocol on the compulsory settlement of disputes; 3. optional signature protocol on the acquisition of nationality, done at Vienna on 24 April 1963).

question_text_en: Right of migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The Aliens law, Articles 7, 8bis, 27 - 29, 44septies, 51/5, 57/32, 74/5, 74/6 and 74/7 authorizes the detention of migrants solely based on their immigration status in several cases: on arrival at the border, on the territory while illegally present, or during the asylum procedure. However, it is not automatic and requires that conditions be met in each case: compliance with certain time limits on arrival at the border, the effectiveness of the prospect of removal for migrants in an illegal situation, or the risk of flight for asylum seekers, for example.

question_text_en: Right to appeal legality, conditions, and length of detention
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Aliens Law, Articles 71-74, which stipulates that the judge will only be able to rule on the legality of the detention.

question_text_en: Right to an individualized detention decision.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Aliens Act, Articles 7, 27, 51/5, 51/5/1, 62§2, 74/5, 74/6, and 74/7. Detention always requires a reasoned and individual decision (Article 62, §2). With regard to foreigners at the borders, (Article 74/5) and foreigners in irregular situation (Articles 7, 27 and 74/7), detention is not mandatory but a possibility, and should thus requires an individual assessment of each particular case. The same applies to asylum seekers who submit their applications at the border (Article 74/5). With regard to asylum seekers suspected of having committed fraud during the application procedures (Article 74/6) or for whom it is suspected that another Euorpean Union State is responsible (Articles 51/5 and 51/5/1), the law explicitly provides that they are subject to "an individual examination."

question_text_en: Right to be free from torture and inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in 1) the Aliens Law, Articles 48/4§2, 48/9, §5, 57/6/1 and 57/6/6, §1. 2) European Convention on Human Rights, Art. 3 (Law of 13 May 1955 approving the Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms, signed in Rome on 4 November 1950 and the Additional Protocol to that Convention, signed in Paris on 20 March 1952). 3) The Charter of Fundamental Rights, Art. 4.

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The use of force to prevent migrants from entering Belgian territory is not direclty referenced in national law. However, police officers are prohibited overall from using force, unless force is required to enforce specific provisions of the law, according to the Law on Police Functions, Article 37. This general prohibition has not yet been interpreted to apply to border enforcement.

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of lethal force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The use of lethal force to prevent migrants from entering Belgian territory is not direclty referenced in national law. However, police officers are prohibited overall from using force, unless force is required to enforce specific provisions of the law, according to the Law on Police Functions, Article 37. This general prohibition has not yet been interpreted to apply to border enforcement.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from trafficking or smuggling.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in 1) The Criminal Code, Article 433quinquies, which exempts explicitly trafficked migrants (victims) from criminal prosecutions. 2) The "Royal Decree of 8 October 1981 on the access to the territory, stay, establishment and return of the foreigners," Articles 110bis, 110ter, which created the possibility of obtaining a residence permit for migrant victims of trafficking or smuggling, as long as they cooperate with the competent authorities responsible for the investigation or prosecution of these offences.

question_text_en: Right to maintain citizenship status after convictions.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Belgian Nationality Code, Articles 23-23/2. The forfeiture of nationality can either be direct or indirect. The indirect forfeiture of nationality can be pronounced a posteriori by the Court of Appeals in cases of fraud or serious breaches of civic duty, according to Article 23, but may not apply to Belgian nationals by virtue of iure sanguinis or iure soli. The direct forfeiture of nationality may be ordered directly by the judge hearing criminal proceedings or proceedings for annulment of marriage, as an additional measure. The forfeiture of nationality may accompany a sentence of imprisonment for more than five years without suspension, according to Articles 23/1 and 23/2, or the annulment of a marriage of convenience where nationality has been acquired by such a marriage according to Article 23/1. This does not apply to Belgian nationals by attribution iure sanguinis or iure soli of whom at least one of the parents was born in Belgium and has had their main residence in Belgium for five years during the ten years preceding the birth of the child.

question_text_en: Right of economic migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Belgian Nationality Code, Article 12, 12bis, and 19. Economic migrants can obtain citizenship as long as they have a residence permit and reside in Belgium for a period of 5 years, but they must also meet other criteria, as well. For example, it is also necessary to prove linguistic, social and economic integration according to Article 12bis. It is also possible to obtain citizenship through naturalization, which is rarer since one must either prove outstanding merits according to Article 19 §1, or be stateless according to Article 19§2.

question_text_en: Right of humanitarian migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Belgian Nationality Code, Article 12bis, and 19. Humanitarian migrants can obtain citizenship as long as they have a residence permit and reside in Belgium for a period of 5 years, but they must also meet other criteria, as well. For example, it is also necessary to prove linguistic, social and economic integration according to Article 12bis. Vulnerable persons (due to disability, invalidity or old age) have easier access to citizenship as they will only have to meet the residence requirements and will not have to fulfil any of the integration conditions. It is also possible to obtain citizenship through naturalization, which is rarer since one must either prove outstanding merits according to Article 19 §1, or be stateless according to Article 19§2.

question_text_en: Right of family migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Belgian Nationality Code, Article 12bis, and 19. Family migrants can obtain citizenship as long as they have a residence permit and reside in Belgium for a period of 5 years, but they must also meet other criteria, as well. For example, it is also necessary to prove linguistic, social and economic integration according to Article 12bis. Conditions are nonetheless easier for foreigners married to a Belgian or parents of a Belgian child who are exempted from proof of economic integration. It is also possible to obtain citizenship through naturalization, which is rarer since one must either prove outstanding merits according to Article 19 §1, or be stateless according to Article 19§2.

question_text_en: Right to dual nationality.
citation_text_en: National law protects this right in 1) Chapter III of the Belgian Nationality Code, 2) Programme Law of 27 December 2006, Article 386 (which modifies the Belgian Nationality Code, Article 22), which repealed the rule that said the acquisition of a new nationality would cause loss of Belgian nationality.

question_text_en: Right to freedom to hold opinion.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Belgian Constitution, Articles 19, 24, 191.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of expression.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Belgian Constitution, Articles 19, and 191.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of association.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Belgian Constitution, Articles 19, and 191.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of assembly.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in 1) Art. 27 and 191 of the Belgian Constitution. 2) European Convention on Human Rights, Art. 11 (Law of 13 May 1955 approving the Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms, signed in Rome on 4 November 1950 and the Additional Protocol to that Convention, signed in Paris on 20 March 1952). 3) Art. 1/2 of the Aliens Law, for which an acontrario interpretation clarifies that aliens/migrants should be treated equal with regards to freedom of association.

category: Thought, conscience, and religion or belief
question_text_en: Right of freedom of thought, conscience and religion or belief.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. In principle, the migrant must prove that they have adequate housing, stable, regular and sufficient resources, and health care coverage before family reunification can be granted. There are exceptions, however. Article 10, §1, 7°, of the Aliens Law provides exceptions for young children and unaccompanied minors, so long as their parents or guardians reside in Belgium. Article 10, §2 states that, if the minor is unaccompanied and the sponsoring guardian in Belgium has an unlimited stay visa, resource criteria will be nullified. Article 10, §2 states that the wife/husband and children of a migrant from a third country (who was recognized as a refugee or granted subsidiary protection) can join them in Belgium without proving the previous conditions only if 1) the relationship (of kinship or alliance) or registered partnership predates the foreigner's entry into the Kingdom, and 2) provided that the application for residence on the basis of this Article was filed within one year of the decision recognizing refugee status or granting subsidiary protection to the joined migrant. Finally, article 40ter, §2, 2° states that the father and mother of a minor with Belgian citizenship can reside in Beligian so long as they can prove their identity. For European Union (EU) citizens who lives in Belgium, the rule is inverted: the principle is that the migrant (EU citizen) does not have to meet resource criteria, with some exceptions to be found in Article 40 and 40bis of the Aliens Law.

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to access criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Belgian Constitution, Article 191, which states that "All foreigners on Belgian soil benefit from that protection provided to persons and property, save for those exceptions provided for by law."

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to immigration status or relief from expulsion.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in the Aliens Law, Articles 11, 42quater, 61/2, 61/5. This includes circumstance where the migrant is confirmed as a victim, must cooperate, must be under investigation or proceedings, must have severed all contact with the fledgling community, must attempt to provide proof of his or her identity and must not represent any danger to public order or national security. In addition, persons holding a residence permit through family reunification may be protected from expulsion despite not meeting or no longer meeting the relevant legal requirements for immigration status if they prove to have been victims of difficult situations (such as violences) or certain crimes during a marriage or partnership.

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in 1) the Aliens Law (Law of 15 December 1980 on the access to the territory, stay, establishment and return of the foreigners), Article 1, §1, 12°, Articles 61/14-61/17 (under the title "mineurs ?trangers non accompagn?s"), and Article 74/16 (-the relevant articles of the Aliens Law provide that it must be interpreted in line with the Convention on the Right of the Child) and in 2) The Dublin III Regulation (Regulation (EU) nr. 604/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 June 2013 establising the criteria ans mechanisms for determining the Member State responsible for examining an application for international protection lodged in one of the Member States by a third-country national or a stateless person), Articles 6 and 8.

question_text_en: Right of women migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in 1) the Aliens Law, Article 1,§1, 12°, which specifically include pregnant women in the category of vulnerable persons. 2) The "Royal Decree of 11 July 2003 laying down the procedure before the Office of the Commissioner General for Refugees and Stateless Persons and its functioning," Article 15, which provides that if there are indications of gender-related persecution, the officer will consider whether the claimant has no objection to being heard by a person of a gender other than the claimant's own.

question_text_en: Rights of migrants with disabilities to special protection.
citation_text_en: National law in Belgium protects this right in 1) the Aliens Law, Article 1,§1, 12°, 10, which takes disabilities into consideration during the asylum procedure: agents trained in the specific needs of vulnerable persons (which includes disabilities). 2) The Royal Decree of 11 July 2003 laying down the procedure before the Office of the Commissioner General for Refugees and Stateless Persons and its functioning. 3) The Belgian Nationality Code. in Article 12bis, §1, 4°. 4) Decision by the Belgian Constitutional Court, 18 July 2013, n°107/2013, which rules on the determination of a “safe country”, where the interpretation must be in accordance with the principle of non-discrimination.

question_text_en: What is your name?
citation_text_en: [1]: Laura Madrid Sartoretto. [2]: Charles Gomes.

question_text_en: What country are you coding?
citation_text_en: Brazil.

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to vote in local and/or regional elections.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Article 5 of the 1988 Federal Constitution the Republic of Brazil (Item XVI - everyone can meet peacefully, without weapons, in places open to the public, regardless of authorization, as long as they do not frustrate another meeting previously called for the same place, only requiring prior notice to the competent authority); and in Article 4 of Law n. 13.445/2017 ? Brazilian Migration Law (Migrants can stay in the national territory, on an equal basis as nationals, they enjoy full inviolability of the right to life, freedom, equality, security and property, as well as the following: Item VI - right to assemble for peaceful purposes).

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to stand for election.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. As explained in the Brazilian Constitution, Article 14, § 2, migrants may not be listed as voters.

question_text_en: Right to equal protection of the law before courts.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in: 1) 1988 Federal Constitution the Republic of Brazil Article 5 - Everyone is equal before the law, without distinction of any kind, guaranteeing Brazilians and foreigners residing in the country the inviolability of the right to life, liberty, equality, security and property, in the following terms: Item XXXIV - it should be granted to all, regardless of the payment of fees: Line a) the right to petition the Public Authorities in defense of rights or against illegality or abuse of power; Line b) obtaining certificates from public offices, for the defence of rights and clarification of situations of personal interest; 2) Law n. 13.445/2017 - Brazilian Migration Law Article 3 - The Brazilian migration policy is governed by the following principles and guidelines: Item XI - equal and free access of migrants to services, programs and social benefits, public goods, education, comprehensive public legal assistance, work, housing, banking services and social security; Article 4 - The migrant is guaranteed in the national territory, on an equal basis with nationals, the inviolability of the right to life, freedom, equality, security and property, as well as the following: Item IX - broad access to justice and free full legal assistance to those who prove insufficient resources.

question_text_en: Right to government-provided counsel in proceedings related to migrant status.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in: 1) Law n. 13.445/2017 - Brazilian Migration Law Repatriation: Article 49 - Repatriation consists of an administrative measure to return a person in a situation of impediment to the country of origin or nationality. Paragraph 2 - The Federal Public Defender's Office will be notified, preferably electronically, in the case of paragraph 4 of this article or when immediate repatriation is not possible. Article 51 - The proceedings leading to deportation must respect the due process and the guarantee of appeal with suspensive effect. Paragraph 1 - The Public Defender's Office of the Union must be notified, preferably by electronic means, in order to provide assistance to the deported person in all administrative procedures for deportation. Article 58 - In the expulsion process due process will be observed Paragraph 1 - The Federal Public Defender's Office will be notified of the initiation of an expulsion process if there is no appointed defender; 2) Law n. 13.445/17 (Brazilian Migration Law) - Art. 4, Item IX - broad access to justice and free legal assistance to those who prove low revenue; and Supplementary Law n. 80/94 (Federal Public Defence Law).

question_text_en: Right to government-provided interpretation in criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Law n. 10.792/03 (Brazilian Code of Criminal Procedure)- Article 193 which states that when the interrogated person does not speak the national language, the interrogation will be done through an interpreter.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from prosecution for unauthorized entry.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Law n. 13.445/2017 - Brazilian Migration Law Article 3 - The Brazilian migration policy is governed by the following principles and guidelines: Item III - non-criminalization of migration. Migrants' unauthorized entry constitutes an infraction but due to the principle of non-criminalization of migration there is no criminal or civil sanctions for migrants that enter in the Brazilian territory without authorization. Article 109 of the Brazilian Migration Law provides administrative sanctions in some cases.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to public adult education institutions.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Article 3, Item XI of Law n. 13.445/2017 (Brazilian Migration Law): The Brazilian migration policy is governed by the following principles and guidelines: Item XI - equal and free access of migrants to services, programs and social benefits, public goods, education, comprehensive public legal assistance, work, housing, banking services and social security.

question_text_en: Right of access to public adult education institutions regardless of status.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in: 1) Article 6 of the 1988 Federal Constitution the Republic of Brazil: Social rights are education, health, food, work, housing, transportation, leisure, security, social security, maternity and childhood protection, assistance to the destitute, in the form of this Constitution; 2) Law n. 13.445/2017 ? Brazilian Migration Law, Article 3 - The Brazilian migration policy is governed by the following principles and guidelines: Item XI - equal and free access of migrants to services, programs and social benefits, public goods, education, comprehensive public legal assistance, work, housing, banking services and social security. Article 4 - The migrant is guaranteed in the national territory, on an equal basis with nationals, the inviolability of the right to life, freedom, equality, security and property, as well as the following: Item X - right to public education, with discrimination based on nationality and immigration status prohibited.

question_text_en: Right to be free from discrimination on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Article 3 of Law n. 13.445/2017 (Brazilian Migration Law): The Brazilian migration policy is governed by the following principles and guidelines: Item XI - equal and free access of migrants to services, programs and social benefits, public goods, education, comprehensive public legal assistance, work, housing, banking services and social security. Article 4 - The migrant is guaranteed in the national territory, on an equal basis with nationals, the inviolability of the right to life, freedom, equality, security and property, as well as the following: Item X - right to public education, with discrimination based on nationality and immigration status prohibited. Free degree-level and training education is available in Brazil, but in general migrants need to have their certificates recognized under the Brazilian Law and pass the selection processes.

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after convictions.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Law n. 13.445/2017 - Brazilian Migration Law, Article 54, Regulation n. 770/19. Ministry of Justice and Public Security sets new rules on preventing the entry, on repatriation and deportation of a dangerous person or who has performed an act contrary to the principles and objectives set out in the Federal Constitution.

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of torture or inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in: 1) Law n. 13.445/2017 (Brazilian Migration Law) Articles 49 and 62; 2) Decree n. 9.199/2017 - Regulates the Brazilian Migration Law Article 274 - The surrender of the extradited person will not take place without the requesting State assuming the commitment to: Item VI - not subject the person being extradited to torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment; 3) Law n. 9.474/1997 ? Refugee Statute Article 37 - The expulsion of refugees from national territory will not result in their removal to a country where their life, freedom or physical integrity may be at risk, and will only be effective when their admission to a country where there is no risk of persecution is assured.

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of persecution.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Law n. 9.474/1997 ? Refugee Statute Article 37: "The expulsion of refugees from national territory will not result in their removal to a country where their life, freedom or physical integrity may be at risk, and will only be effective when their admission to a country where there is no risk of persecution is assured."

question_text_en: Right to not return to a deprivations of fundamental human rights.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Law n. 13.445/2017 (Brazilian Migration Law), Article 62, which states "no individual will be repatriated, deported or expelled when there are reasons to believe that the measure could endanger life or personal integrity" and Art. 49, which states: "Repatriation consists of an administrative measure to return a person in a situation of impediment to the country of origin or nationality. Paragraph 4 - The repatriation measure shall not be applied to a person in a situation of refuge or statelessness, in fact or in law, to a minor under 18 (eighteen) years of age unaccompanied or separated from his/her family, except in cases where it proves to be favorable to the guarantee of their rights or for the reintegration of their family of origin, or for those who need humanitarian reception, nor, in any case, a measure of return to a country or region that may pose a risk to the life, personal integrity or freedom of the person."

question_text_en: Right to be advised of availability of asylum before expulsion.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in article 4, item XVI of the Brazilian Migration Law (Law n. 13.445/2017). ? Brazilian Migration Law Article 4 - The migrant is guaranteed in the national territory, on an equal basis with nationals, the inviolability of the right to life, freedom, equality, security and property, as well as the following: Item XVI - migrants' right to be informed about the protections that are guaranteed for the purposes of migratory regularisation including the right to be informed about the availability of asylum. Law n. 9.474/1997 - Brazilian Refugee Law Article 7 - The foreigner who arrives in the national territory may express his will to apply for asylum to any immigration authority located at the border, which will provide him with the necessary information regarding the appropriate procedure.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from chain refoulement.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Law n. 13.445/17 (Brazilian Migration Law) art. 50 to art. 62 establish all the legal procedures and due process for denial of entry, deportation, and expulsion.

question_text_en: Right to protection against expulsion except following a legal judgment.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in: 1) Law n. 13.445/2017 (Brazilian Migration Law), Articles 48, 54, 61, 62.

question_text_en: Right to submit reasons against expulsion and have case reviewed before deportation.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in: 1) Law n. 13.445/2017 (Brazilian Migration Law), Article 203; 2) Decree n. 9.199/17 (Regulates the Brazilian Migration Law) - §5.

question_text_en: Right of settled migrants to family reunification.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Law n. 13.445/2017 ? Brazilian Migration Law Protection of Stateless Persons and Reduction of Statelessness Article 26 - Regulation (Decree No. 9.199/2017, articles 95 to 107) will provide for a special protective institute for stateless persons, consolidated in a simplified naturalization process.

question_text_en: Right to judicial remedy for denials of right to family reunification.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right, for migrants in regular status, in Law n. 13.445/2017 (Brazilian Migration Law), Chapter III, section V - Family Reunification and Decree No 9.199/2017, article 45.

question_text_en: Right to recognition of same-sex marital relationships.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in 1988 Federal Constitution of the Republic of Brazil, Article 5 - Everyone is equal before the law, without distinction of any kind, guaranteeing Brazilians and foreigners residing in the country the inviolability of the right to life, liberty, equality, security and property, in the following terms: Item XXV - The law shall not exclude from the judicial review any injury or threat to a right and Item LXIX - a writ (injunction) will be granted to protect a clear and certain right, not supported by "habeas-corpus" or "habeas-data", when the person responsible for the illegality or abuse of power is a public authority or agent of a legal entity in the exercise of attributions of the Public Power.

question_text_en: Right to family reunification without resource conditions
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in: 1) Decree n. 9.199/2017 - Regulates the Brazilian Migration Law Article 45 - The temporary visa for the purposes of family reunion will be granted to the immigrant: Item I - spouse or partner, without any discrimination, under the terms of the Brazilian legal system; Article 153 - The residence permit for the purposes of family reunion will be granted to the immigrant: Item I - spouse or partner, without any discrimination, under the terms of the Brazilian legal system; 2) Law n. 13.445/17 (Brazilian Migration Law), Chapter II, Section V on family reunification. Same sex marital relationships enjoy the same rights as heterosexual relationships under the Article 1790 of the Brazilian Civil Code .

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services.
citation_text_en: The visa type is not important when changing from temporary to permanent resident permit. According to Decree n. 9.199/2017 - Regulates the Brazilian Migration Law Article 50 - Temporary visas may be transformed into a residence permit or a diplomatic, official or courtesy visa, in national territory, provided that the immigrant meets the requirements established in this Decree.

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services regardless of status.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Article 176 of Decree n. 9.199/2017: The immigrant who is in an irregular migratory situation will be personally notified so that, within a period of sixty days, counted from the date of the notification, he can regularize his migratory situation or leave the country voluntarily. The Migration Law offers different avenues to have legal residence in Brazil: family reunification, a promise of a job contract, a new job contract, among others.

question_text_en: Right of access to public housing programs.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Article 461 of Decree Law n. 5.452/1943: Consolidation of Brazilian Labour Laws; and in article 4, item XI of Law n. 13.445/17 (Brazilian Migration Law).

question_text_en: Right to equal access to free primary education for migrant children.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Article 4, item VIII of Law n. 13.445/2017 (Brazilian Migration Law): The migrant is guaranteed in the national territory, on an equal basis with nationals, the inviolability of the right to life, freedom, equality, security and property, as well as the following: Item VIII - access to public health and social assistance services and social security, under the terms of the law, without discrimination on grounds of nationality and immigration status.

question_text_en: Right to equal pay for the same work.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. As explained in the Brazilian Constitution, Art. 14, § 3, Brazilian nationality is an eligibility condition to stand for election.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of choice of employment.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Article 5 of the 1988 Federal Constitution the Republic of Brazil; and in Article 3, Item II (repudiation and prevention of xenophobia, racism and any form of discrimination) and Item IV (non-discrimination due to the criteria or procedures by which the person was admitted to national territory) of the Law n. 13.445/2017 (Brazilian Migration Law).

question_text_en: Right of spouse/partner of principal migrant to work.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Article 5 of the 1988 Federal Constitution the Republic of Brazil emphasizing equality before the law, without distinction of any kind, guaranteeing Brazilians and foreigners residing in the country the inviolability of the right to life, freedom, equality, security and property; and in Articles 3 and 4 of Law n. 13.445/2017 (Brazilian Migration Law). Additionally, Law n.9459/97 relates to the crimes of discrimination on the bases of race, color, ethnicity, religion or national origin; and Law n. 7.716/1989 - Code of Criminal Procedure Article 1 - Crimes resulting from discrimination or prejudice based on race, color, ethnicity, religion or national origin shall be punished under this Law.

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after loss of employment.
