citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in: 1) Decree Law n. 5.452/1943 - Consolidation of Brazilian Labour Laws Article 461 - Being similar work made in the same location, it will correspond to equal salary, without distinction of sex, nationality or age; 2) Law n. 13.445/17 (Brazilian Migration Law) - Article 4, Item XI. Additionally, Brazil has ratified Convention n. 100 and Convention n. 111 of the International Labor Organization. Although irregular migrants do not have the right to work, the guarantee of compliance with legal and contractual labor obligations and application of worker protection rules applies without discrimination on grounds of nationality and migratory condition.

question_text_en: Right to equal employment conditions and protection.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in: 1)Decree n. 9.199/2017 - Regulates the Brazilian Migration Law Article 38 - The temporary work visa may be granted to immigrants who come to work with or without an employment contract in the country. Paragraph 7 - The possibility of modifying the place where they work, in the same company or in the same economic group, will be recognized to the immigrant who has been granted a temporary work visa, through communication to the Ministry of Labour. Article 147 - Paragraph 8 After the decision regarding the change of employer referred to in paragraph 7, the Ministry of Labour will inform the Federal Police for the purpose of updating the registration; 2) Ordinance n. 1/2017-Immigration Department, Ministry of Labour Article 4 - The hypotheses of transferring the immigrant to another company of the same economic group, or changing function and/or adding other activities to those originally performed, oblige the contracting person to communicate and justify the act to the Ministry of Labor within a maximum period of up to 30 (thirty) days after its occurrence, presenting an amendment to the employment contract, when applicable. In certain cases, the law permits change of employer without new work permit application, but in general it requires a new application.

question_text_en: Right to form trade unions and other associations.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Article 45 of Decree n. 9.199/2017 that regulates the Brazilian Migration Law. Article 45 - The temporary visa for the purposes of family reunion will be granted to the immigrant: Paragraph 3 - The holder of the visa mentioned in article 45 may carry out any work activity in the country, including remunerated, under equal conditions with the Brazilian national, under the terms of the law.

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to redress before deportation or withdrawal of residency permit.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil regulates this right in: 1) Law n? 13.445/17; and 2) Decree n. 9.199/2017, Article 135: The loss of the residence permit will be decreed in the following cases: Item I - cessation of the grounds on which the residence permit was based; Item II - obtaining a residence permit based on another hypothesis; Item III - absence from the country for a period of more than two years without presenting justification. Paragraph 1 - The immigrant must notify the Federal Police whenever he no longer has the conditions that supported the granting of his residence permit during its term. Paragraph 2 - The provisions of item I of the caput do not prevent the immigrant from applying for a residence permit based on another hypothesis. Interministerial Ordinance n. 6/2018 Article 3 - Once the loss of residence procedure has been initiated, notification will be made to the immigrant, preferably by electronic means, for the presentation of a defence, within a period of ten days. The defence mentioned in article 3 of the Interministerial Ordinance n. 6/2018 might be a new labour contract or any other type of residence permit provided by Decree n. 9.199/2017.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to social security protections.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Article 461 of the Decree Law n. 5.452/1943; and in Article 4, Item XI of the Law n. 13.445/17 (Brazilian Migration Law). As the right to work is a considered a fundamental social right in Brazil, and migrants should be treated in equality of conditions to nationals regarding their social rights, it is forbidden to have unequal pay for migrants doing the same work. Although irregular migrants do not have the right to work, Item XI guarantees compliance with legal and contractual labor obligations and the application of worker protection rules without discrimination based on nationality and migratory status.

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to become lawfully settled.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Article 3 and Article 4, Item VIII of the Law n. 13.445/2017 (Brazilian Migration Law).

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to settle regardless of initial status.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Article 3, Item XI and Article 4, Item VIII of the Law n. 13.445/2017 (Brazilian Migration Law). Article 3 states that the Brazilian migration policy is governed by the following principles and guidelines: Item XI - equal and free access of migrants to services, programs and social benefits, public goods, education, comprehensive public legal assistance, work, housing, banking services and social security.

question_text_en: Right to redress following employer breach of employment contract.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Article 50 and Article 176 of the Decree n. 9.199/2017 which regulates the Brazilian Migration Law. According to article 50: Temporary visas may be transformed into a residence permit or a diplomatic, official or courtesy visa, in national territory, provided that the immigrant meets the requirements established in this Decree.

question_text_en: Right not to have identity documents confiscated.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in 1) Law Decree n. 2.848/1940- Brazilian Criminal Code Article 149; 2) Law n. 5.553/68 (Provides for the presentation and use of personal identification documents). Brazilian law does not state explicitly that of migrant workers have the right not to have identity documents confiscated by anyone, however it punishes employers "who maintains overt surveillance in the workplace or takes possession of documents or personal objects of the worker, to retain him at the workplace."

question_text_en: Right to birth registration.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Law n. 8.069/1990 - Statute of the Child and Adolescent Article 3: Children and adolescents enjoy all the fundamental rights inherent to the human person, without prejudice to the full protection provided for in this Law, ensuring them, by law or by other means, all opportunities and facilities, in order to provide them with physical, mental, moral, spiritual and social development, in conditions of freedom and dignity. The rights set forth in this Law apply to all children and adolescents, without discrimination based on birth, family situation, age, sex, race, ethnicity or color, religion or belief, disability, personal development and learning condition, economic condition, environment social status, region and place of residence or any other condition that differentiates people, families or the community in which they live. Article 102 - The protection measures dealt with in this Chapter will be accompanied by regularisation of the civil registry. Paragraph 1 - Once the absence of a previous record has been verified, the birth record of the child or adolescent will be made in view of the available elements, upon request of the judicial authority. Paragraph 2 - The records and certificates necessary for the regularization referred to in this article are exempt from fines, costs and fees, enjoying absolute priority. This right is also protected in Law n. 13.484, of September 26, 2017 (Amends Law n. 6. 015, of December 31, 1973), which provides for public records.

question_text_en: Right to government document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in relation to documents that recognize migrants' residency status, work status, and identity in: 1) Decree n. 9.199/2017 - Regulates the Brazilian Migration Law Article 58 - It is incumbent upon the Federal Police to: Item I - organize, maintain and manage the immigrant's civil identification processes; Item II - produce the National Migration Registration Card; and Item III - manage the database related to the National Migratory Registry; 2) Art.30 of Law n. 13.445/17 (Brazilian Migration Law).

question_text_en: Right against destruction of document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Law n. 5.553/68 (Provides for the presentation and use of personal identification documents), article 305 Brazilian Penal Code.

question_text_en: Right to communicate with consular officials.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Decree No. 61,078, of July 26, 1967 (Vienna Convention on Consular Relations). Aditionally, Law No. 13.445/2017, article 49 and Decree No. 9.199/2017, article 188(a) and 195(para 4) provide that act of repatriation shall be immediately communicated to the transport company and to the consular authority of the country of origin or nationality of the migrant or visitor, or whoever represents this person.

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Law n. 13.445/2017 - Brazilian Migration Law Article 3 . The Brazilian migration policy is governed by the following principles and guidelines: Item III - non-criminalization of migration; Item XVII - comprehensive protection and attention to the best interests of migrant children and adolescents. Article 40 - The exceptional admission to the country of a person who meets one of the following conditions may be authorized, provided that he or she is in possession of a valid travel document: Item V - is a child or adolescent unaccompanied by a legal guardian and without express authorisation to travel unaccompanied, regardless of the travel document they carry, in which case there will be immediate referral to the Tutelary Council or, if necessary, to the institution indicated by the competent authority. This right is also protected in Law n. 8.069/90 (Children and Adolescent Statute).

question_text_en: Right of migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Law n. 13.445/2017 - Brazilian Migration Law Article 3. According to this law, the Brazilian migration policy is governed by the following principles and guidelines: Item III - non-criminalization of migration. As detention on account of migrant status is forbidden in Brazilian law, migrants will be arrested only if they commit a crime, in this case they are entitled to appeal according to the Brazilian Penal Code.

question_text_en: Right to appeal legality, conditions, and length of detention
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects migrants' right to appeal legality, conditions, and length of detention in Article 3, III, Law n. 13.445/2017 (Brazilian Migration Law) as well as in Article 5 of the 1988 Federal Constitution of the Republic of Brazil.

question_text_en: Right to an individualized detention decision.
citation_text_en: As detention on the basis of migrant status is forbidden in Brazilian law, migrants will be arrested only if they committed a crime, in this case they are entitled to appeal according to the Brazilian Penal Code. If any person is illegally arrested, she/he has the right to file an habeas corpus. National law in Brazil protects this right in: 1) 1988 Federal Constitution of the Republic of Brazil, Article 5 - Everyone is equal before the law, without distinction of any kind, guaranteeing Brazilians and foreigners residing in the country the inviolability of the right to life, liberty, equality, security and property, in the following terms: Item XLVI - the law shall regulate the individualization of the penalty... 2) Article 3, III, Law n. 13.445/2017 (Brazilian Migration Law).

question_text_en: Right to be free from torture and inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right for everyone, including migrants, in 1988 Federal Constitution of the Republic of Brazil, Article 5. This article states that "Everyone is equal before the law, without distinction of any kind, guaranteeing Brazilians and foreigners residing in the country the inviolability of the right to life, liberty, equality, security and property, in the following terms: Item III - no one shall be subjected to torture or to inhuman or degrading treatment. Additionally, according to the Law n. 13.445/2017 ? Brazilian Migration Law Extradition Article 274, the surrender of the extradited person will not take place without the requesting State assuming the commitment to: Item VI - not subject the person being extradited to torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of lethal force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from trafficking or smuggling.
citation_text_en: Regarding the irregular entry of all migrants, the Migration Law of Brazil Law No. 13,445/2017, takes a humanitarian approach and does not criminalize irregular entry itself, but it establishes administrative procedures to regularize the migratory status of foreigners who wish to reside in the country. In this sense, both trafficked and smuggled migrants are exempted from prosecution for irregular entry (not on account of being victims of crime). Victims of trafficking (though not smuggled migrants) receive additional protection and assistance including legal, social, work, employment, and health assistance among other things under Law n. 13.344/2016 ? Law for the repression of internal and international trafficking of persons Article 6.

question_text_en: Right to maintain citizenship status after convictions.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil regulates this right in Law n. 13.445/2017 (Brazilian Migration Law), Article 75 - The naturalised person will lose nationality due to a final and unappealable conviction for an activity harmful to the national interest, pursuant to item I of paragraph 4 of article 12 of the 1988 Federal Constitution of the Republic of Brazil. The risk of generating a situation of statelessness will be taken into account before the loss of nationality takes effect. Article 65 - Ordinary naturalization will be granted to those who meet the following conditions: Item IV - does not have a criminal conviction or is rehabilitated, under the terms of the law. Article 67 - Extraordinary naturalization will be granted to a person of any nationality established in Brazil for more than 15 (fifteen) uninterrupted years and without criminal conviction, provided that he or she applies for Brazilian nationality. Article 68 - Special naturalization may be granted to foreigners who are in one of the following situations: Item III - does not have a criminal conviction or is rehabilitated, under the terms of the law.

question_text_en: Right of economic migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right for economic migrants in Law n. 13.445/17 (Brazilian Migration Law), Art. 65. According to the law, ordinary naturalization shall be granted to those who fulfill the following conditions: I - civil capacity, according to Brazilian law; II - residence in national territory for a minimum period of four (4) years; III - communicate in Portuguese, considering the conditions of the naturalizing person; and IV - has no criminal conviction or is rehabilitated, under the terms of the law. Art. 66. The period of residence set in item II of the caput of art. 65 will be reduced to at least one (1) year if the naturalizer meets any of the following conditions: II - have a Brazilian child; III - have a Brazilian spouse or partner and are not legally or in fact separated from him at the time of granting naturalization; V - have provided or could provide relevant service to Brazil; or VI - to be recommended for their professional, scientific or artistic ability.

question_text_en: Right of humanitarian migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right for humanitarian migrants in: 1) Law n. 13.445/2017 (Brazilian Migration Law), Articles 14 and 65; 2) Decree n. 9.199/2017 - Regulates the Brazilian Migration Law Humanitarian visa: Article 36 - A temporary visa for humanitarian reception may be granted to a stateless person or national of any country in a situation of serious or imminent institutional instability, armed conflict, major calamity, environmental disaster or serious violation of human rights or human rights under international humanitarian law. Residence permit under humanitarian circumstances Article 145 - The residence permit for the purposes of humanitarian reception may be granted to the stateless person or to the national of any country in situation of: Item I - serious or imminent institutional instability; Item II - armed conflict; Item III - calamity of great proportion; Item IV - environmental disaster; or Item V - serious violation of human rights or international humanitarian law. Ordinary naturalization Article 233 - In the procedure for granting ordinary naturalization, the following must be proven: Item I - civil capacity, according to Brazilian law; Item II - residence in the national territory, for a minimum period of four years; Item III - ability to communicate in Portuguese, considering the conditions of naturalizing; and Item IV - absence of criminal conviction or proof of rehabilitation, under the terms of current legislation. Article 235 - The minimum period of residence established in item II of the caput of article 233 will be reduced to one year if the naturalized person meets one of the following requirements: Item I - have a Brazilian born or naturalized child, except for provisional naturalization; or Item II - have a Brazilian spouse or partner and not be legally or de facto separated from him or her at the time the naturalization is granted. Article 236 - The minimum residence period established in item II of the caput of article 233 will be reduced to two years if the naturalized person meets one of the following requirements: Item I - have rendered or be able to render a relevant service to the Country; or Item II - to be recommended for their professional, scientific or artistic capacity.

question_text_en: Right of family migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right for family migrants in: 1) Law n. 13.445/17 (Brazilian Migration Law) Art. 65; 2) Decree n. 9.199/2017 - Regulates the Brazilian Migration Law Article 33 - The temporary visa may be granted to immigrants who come to the country with the intention of establishing residency for a specific period of time and who fit into at least one of the following hypotheses: Line k) family reunion. Article 35 - paragraph 2 - Exceptionally, a temporary visa may be granted to more than one companion, even if the requirements for family reunion are not met, provided that medical necessity is proven. Article 45 - The temporary visa for the purposes of family reunion will be granted to the immigrant: Item I - spouse or partner, without any discrimination, under the terms of the Brazilian legal system; Item II - child of a Brazilian or immigrant beneficiary of a residence permit; Item III - who has a Brazilian child; Item IV - who has an immigrant child who is the beneficiary of a residence permit; Item V - ascending to the second degree of Brazilian or immigrant beneficiary of residence permit; Item VI - descendant up to the second degree of Brazilian or immigrant beneficiary of a residence permit; Item VII - brother of a Brazilian or an immigrant who is the beneficiary of a residence permit; or Item VIII - who has a Brazilian under his guardianship, curatorship or guard. Article 132 - The residence permit will not be granted to the person criminally convicted in the Country or abroad by a final and unappealable sentence, provided that the conduct is typified in the Brazilian criminal legislation, except for the hypotheses in which: Line c) family reunion; Ordinary naturalization Article 233 - In the procedure for granting ordinary naturalisation, the following must be proven: Item I - civil capacity, according to Brazilian law; Item II - residence in the national territory, for a minimum period of four years; Item III - ability to communicate in Portuguese, considering the conditions of naturalizing; and Item IV - absence of criminal conviction or proof of rehabilitation, under the terms of current legislation. Article 235 - The minimum period of residence established in item II of the caput of art. 233 will be reduced to one year if the naturalized person meets one of the following requirements: Item I - have a Brazilian born or naturalized child, except for provisional naturalization; or Item II - have a Brazilian spouse or partner and not be legally or de facto separated from him or her at the time the naturalization is granted. Article 236 The minimum residence period established in item II of the caput of article 233 will be reduced to two years if the naturalized person meets one of the following requirements: Item I - have rendered or be able to render a relevant service to the Country; or Item II - to be recommended for their professional, scientific or artistic capacity.

question_text_en: Right to dual nationality.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil regulates the naturalization process, for migrants, in Migration Law No. 13,445 of May 24, 2017. The law does not mention migrants losing their nationality of origin when they obtain Brazilian citizenship.

question_text_en: Right to freedom to hold opinion.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in: 1) 1988 Federal Constitution the Republic of Brazil, Article 5; 2) Law n. 13.445/2017 (Brazilian Migration Law), Article 3 & 4. According to Article 5 of the 1988 Federal Constitution the Republic of Brazil, "Everyone is equal before the law, without distinction of any kind, guaranteeing Brazilians and foreigners residing in the country the inviolability of the right to life, liberty, equality, security and property, in the following terms: Item IV - the expression of thought is free, being prohibited anonymity; Item VI - freedom of conscience and belief is inviolable, the free exercise of religious cults being ensured and the protection of places of worship and their liturgies guaranteed under the terms of the law; Item VIII - no one will be deprived of rights due to religious beliefs or philosophical or political convictions, unless they are invoked to exempt themselves from legal obligations imposed on all and refuse to comply with the alternative provision established by law; Item IX - the expression of intellectual, artistic, scientific and communication activity is free, regardless of censorship or license; Item VI - freedom of conscience and belief is inviolable, the free exercise of religious cults being ensured and the protection of places of worship and their liturgies guaranteed under the terms of the law." Furthermore, Law n. 13.445/2017 ? Brazilian Migration Law Article 3 explains that "The Brazilian migration policy is governed by the following principles and guidelines: Item XII - promotion and dissemination of migrant rights, freedoms, guarantees and obligations; Item VIII - no one will be deprived of rights due to religious beliefs or philosophical or political convictions, unless they are invoked to exempt themselves from legal obligations imposed on all and refuse to comply with the alternative provision established by law; Item IX - the expression of intellectual, artistic, scientific and communication activity is free, regardless of censorship or license."

question_text_en: Right to freedom of expression.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Article 5 of the 1988 Federal Constitution the Republic of Brazil; and in Article 4 of Law n. 13.445/2017 - Brazilian Migration Law.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of association.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Article 5 of the 1988 Federal Constitution the Republic of Brazil; and in Article 4 of the Law n. 13.445/17 (Brazilian Migration Law).

question_text_en: Right to freedom of assembly.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Article 5 of the 1988 Federal Constitution the Republic of Brazil; and in Art. 4, Item VI (right of assembly for peaceful purposes) and VII (right of association, including union, for lawful purposes) of Law n. 13.445/17 (Brazilian Migration Law).

category: Thought, conscience, and religion or belief
question_text_en: Right of freedom of thought, conscience and religion or belief.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in: 1) Decree n. 9.199/2017 - Regulates the Brazilian Migration Law Article 153; 2) Law n. 13.445/17 (Brazilian Migration Law), Chapter II, Section V on family reunification. Even if there is no requirement in the law of any proof of economic conditions, the only exception regarding resource conditions relates to siblings over 18 years as mentioned in item VII of article 153.

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to access criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Article 5, item Item XXXIV of the 1988 Federal Constitution the Republic of Brazil which states: "Everyone is equal before the law, without distinction of any kind, guaranteeing Brazilians and foreigners residing in the country the inviolability of the right to life, liberty, equality, security and property, in the following terms: Item XXXIV - Regardless of the payment of fees is granted to all persons: Line a) the right to petition the Public Authorities in defense of rights or against illegality or abuse of power."

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to immigration status or relief from expulsion.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Art. 30 (2) point G of the Law n. 13.445/17 (Brazilian Migration Law. The following legislation is also in relation to this right: 1) Law n. 13.445/2017 - Brazilian Migration Law, Article 30; 2) Law n. 13.344/2017 ? Law for the repression of internal and international trafficking of persons Article 6; 3) Article 7 - Law n. 6.815/1980 (replaced by Law n. 13.445/2017) shall come into force with the addition of the following articles: Article 18-A - Permanent residency will be granted to victims of human trafficking in the national territory, regardless of their immigration status and collaboration in administrative, police or judicial proceedings. Paragraph 1 - The visa or permanent residence may be granted, as a family reunion: Item I - to spouses, partners, ascendants and descendants; and Item II - to other members of the family group who prove economic dependence or habitual coexistence with the victim. Paragraph 2 - The beneficiaries of the permanent visa or residence are exempt from paying the fine provided for in item II of article 125. Paragraph 3 - The beneficiaries of the permanent visa or residence referred to in this article are exempt from paying the fees and emoluments provided for in articles 20, 33 and 131.” 4) Article 18-B - Act of the Minister of Justice and Citizenship will establish the procedures for granting permanent residence referred to in article 18-A.

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Law n. 13.445/2017 - Brazilian Migration Law Articles 3, 30, 40, 49. Additionally, this right is protected in 1) Decree n. 9.199/2017 that regulates the Brazilian Migration Law Article 157; 2) Article 5 of Law n. 10.406/2002 - Civil Code; 3) Federal Constitution article n. 227; 4) Law n. 8.069/90 (Children and Adolescent Statute).

question_text_en: Right of women migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Rights of migrants with disabilities to special protection.
citation_text_en: National law in Brazil protects this right in Decree n. 9.199/2017 that regulates the Brazilian Migration Law Article 74. According to this law, the National Migration Registration Card for migrants with disabilities is issued for an indefinite period while for others, it will be valid for nine years.
