citation_text_en: [1]: Bassah Khalaf [2]: Peter Starup

question_text_en: What country are you coding?
citation_text_en: Denmark

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to vote in local and/or regional elections.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in the Constitutional Act of Denmark [Grundloven], Section 79, which recognizes and protects the right of freedom of assembly commensurate with that afforded to citizens.

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to stand for election.
citation_text_en: Being lawfully present does not create a legal right for migrants to vote in Denmark. However, according to LBK nr 295 af 07.03.2022, Act on municipal and regional elections, Section 1 [Bekendtg?relse af lov om kommunale og regionale valg], a migrant who has had their residence in Denmark with no interruption for three years prior to the election (over the age of 18) has the right to vote in municipal and regional elections.

question_text_en: Right to equal protection of the law before courts.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in Article 6 of the European Convention on Human Rights, as incorporated in Danish law by means of act nr. 285 af 29.4.1992, which protects the right to a fair trial, and as a part of the Danish legal system it is applicable to both Danish citizens and migrants.

question_text_en: Right to government-provided counsel in proceedings related to migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for all migrants. Section 55 of thr Aliens Act stipulates that only an exeptionally few categories of migrants have a right to free counsel. Danish legislation provides a right to counsel at government expense only in proceedings related to asylum applications. In other cases, migrants have to pay for their lawyer's fees, unless the authorities appoint an attorney at their expense, which happens only in special cases when economic requirements are met.

question_text_en: Right to government-provided interpretation in criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in the Judicial Procedure Act (Retsplejeloven), section 149, which establishes that the language of legal proceedings is Danish, but in cases regarding foreigners who do not master the language, the proceedings are to be held with the assistance of a translator.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from prosecution for unauthorized entry.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Aside from Asylum Seekers, migrants will be met with civil sanctions for unauthorized entry in the form of an entry ban, although the law does protect migrants from criminal sanctions for unauthorized entry (the Aliens Consolidation Act, Chapter 1 and 4).

question_text_en: Right to equal access to public adult education institutions.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right for some, but not all migrants in 1) LBK nr 1877 af 27.09.2021, Act on public housing [Lovbekendtg?relse om almene boliger m.v.], which regulates access for vulnerable groups of people residing in Denmark, which can include migrants. 2) LBK nr. 438 of 16.05.2012, Act on ethnic legal treatment [Lovbekendtg?relse om etnisk ligebehandling], which protects against discrimination on account of race and ethnic origin and is enforced also as regards to social housing and protects both migrants and citizens. 3) LBK nr. 119 of 01.02.2019, Act on public housing [Lovbekendtg?relse om almene boliger m.v.].

question_text_en: Right of access to public adult education institutions regardless of status.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in 1) the Constitutional Act, Section 76, which establishes that all children are entitled to and obligated to be provided a free education at the Folkeskole. 2) LBK nr 1396 af 05.10.2022, The Act on Primary and Lower Secondary Education [Bekendtg?relse af lov om folkeskolen], Section 32, which states that, "Every child living in Denmark is subject to compulsory education." This includes children of migrants, and the provision does not distinguish between the residence status of children.

question_text_en: Right to be free from discrimination on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in LBK nr. 778 of 07.08.2019, The University Act [Lovbekendtg?relse om universiteter]. The University Act does not discriminate between migrants and citizens in regards to admission at higher education institutions. Admission requirements are set by ministerial orders and differ from institution to institution, but only focus on qualifications and language requirements. However, only migrants with a valid residence permit in Denmark can apply for admission at adult education institutions, thus irregular migrants are excluded from this protection.

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after convictions.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. National law in Denmark regulates the ability of migrants’ criminal and other convictions affecting residence status in the Aliens Act section 10, chapter 3a and chapter 4. Section 10: Prior criminal convictions may impede obtaining a residence status, and getting convicted for a criminal offence may lead to a residence status being lost. Chapter 3a establishes the possibility to revoke a migrant's permission to stay if there are reasons to believe that they engaged in criminal activities abroad that could endanger national security, or other states' national security and public order. Chapter 4 establishes the "staircase-model" for deportation, as to say, a system where a criminal conviction is considered against the length of the migrants' stay in Denmark, in order to evaluate whether a deportation order can be executed following a criminal offence. Also administrative offences, such as stay in the country without a valid permission to stay, can result in a deportation order, see UDL section 25 b.

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of torture or inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in the Aliens Act section 7, stk 2, section 26, stk. 2. and section 31. Section 7 stk. 2 establishes the possibility to grant asylum to a migrant that would risk torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment upon return to their homeland. Section 26, stk. 2 states that deportation of a migrant cannot be executed when that would go against Denmark's international obligations as regards to non-refoulement. Section 31 incorporates Article 3 of the European Convention on Human Rights and the prohibition of refoulment to countries where there is a risk of return to torture or cruel, inhumane or degrading treatment or punishment.

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of persecution.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in tje Aliens Act, Section 7, stk 1, which provides that a permission to stay on grounds of asylum will be issued to a migrant whose situation is covered by the 1951 UN Refugee Convention. An application as referred to in the first sentence hereof is also considered an application for a residence permit under subsection (1).. The provision also incorporates Article 1A of the UN Refugee Convention.

question_text_en: Right to not return to a deprivations of fundamental human rights.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in the Aliens Act section 7, stk 2, section 26, stk 2, section 48 a and section 3. These provisions can be understood as a ban of refoulement on the basis of a risk of serious deprivation of fundamental human rights. Section 7 stk. 2 establishes the possibility to grant asylum to a migrant that would risk torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment upon return to their homeland. Section 26, stk. 2 states that deportation of a migrant cannot be executed when that would go against Denmark's international obligations as regards non-refoulement. In case when an asylum application is rejected, Section 48a ensures that the migrant applicant is not to be sent to a country where they risk death penalty or to suffer torture or cruel, inhumane, and degrading treatment. Section 31 also incorporates Article 3 of the European Convention on Human Rights.

question_text_en: Right to be advised of availability of asylum before expulsion.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in LBK nr. 433 of 22.04.2014, the Danish Public Administration Act [Forvaltningsloven] Section 7. According to Section 7, a public authority shall provide guidance and assistance to persons addressing matters within the authority's area of responsibility. It is therefore a legal requirement to follow from the general duty of guidance, that public immigration authorities must provide foreigners with information regarding the possibility to apply for asylum, complain avenues, deadlines, procedures, and so forth. The executive power is therefore ex officio obliged to inform about the possible availability of asylum before an alien is being expelled or prevented entry.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from chain refoulement.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in the Aliens Consolidation Act, Section 31, which incorporates Article 3 of the European Convention on Human and Rights and and Article 1 A of the Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees (28 July 1951) - both conventions ban expulsion to any country where a migrant is likely to be subjected to refoulement through a subsequent expulsion.

question_text_en: Right to protection against expulsion except following a legal judgment.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in the Aliens Act, Chapter 4, which establishes the "staircase-model" for deportation, as to say, a system where a criminal conviction or administrative offence is considered against the length of the migrants' stay in Denmark, in order to evaluate whether a deportation order can be executed. Each case where a migrant might be expelled is decided according to the merit of the individual case, and in accordance with the law.The "staircase-model" does not apply to severe criminal acts. These cases are decided after an assessment of the proportionality of the expulsion which is based on the case-law on Article 8 of the European Convention on Human Rights.

question_text_en: Right to submit reasons against expulsion and have case reviewed before deportation.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in the Aliens Act, UDL Chapter 7b and Section 49. Chapter 7b sets rules for judicial review of administrative expulsion orders. Expulsion/deportation orders on the basis of criminal offences are decided by the courts according the Section 49 and can be appealed following the two-tier principle in the Danish judicial system. The Danish court system is based on the so-called two-tier principle, which means that the parties to a case generally have the option of appealing the ruling of one court to a higher instance. The higher court can then either reach the same conclusion (uphold the ruling) or change the ruling.

question_text_en: Right of settled migrants to family reunification.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in 1) 1961 Convention on the Reduction of Statelessness (in Denmark, persons aged 18-21 years), which was incorporated into Danish law in the Naturalisation Circular, Section 26, and states that persons born stateless in Denmark may apply for Danish citizenship between the ages of 18 ? 21 years. To acquire Danish citizenship, they must have habitual residence in Denmark and fulfil all requirements under the 1961 Convention. 2) The Convention on the Rights of the Child (children below the age of 18 years). The Convention on the Rights of the Child has been incorporated into Danish law by Naturalisation Circular, Section 17, and states that lawfully resident Danish born stateless children may apply for Danish citizenship from birth without needing to meet otherwise applicable requirements.

question_text_en: Right to judicial remedy for denials of right to family reunification.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in the Aliens Act section 9, section 9 c, section 9 m and section 9 n. Section 9 regulates access to a residence permit for family reunification purposes in Denmark. The most important change to the content of the rules took place in 2002, when the former right to family reunification with spouses, minor children or parents over sixty years of age was revoked. Family reunification with spouses and minor children is now conditional on a number of requirements, focused on economic selfsufficiency, giving rise to a restrictive practice of granting residence permits. Family reunification with parents was completely abolished in 2002, and it is now only possible in very exceptional cases where a permit follows from Denmark's international obligations. In those cases where there is a right to family reunification as a consequence of international obligations, a residence permit is given on the basis of Section 9 c. The rules in the Aliens Act on family reunification are enforced only as regards migrants who are not EU citizens, Nordic citizens, or refugees, which follow different rules. Turkish citizens also fall under the EU-rules according to recent case-law.

question_text_en: Right to recognition of same-sex marital relationships.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in the Aliens Act, Section 46a, which specifies which authority has the competence to receive a complaint in the case of refusal by the authorities to allow family reunification. The avenue for remedy is administrative: firstly, the department of the Ministry of Immigration and Integration, and, in case of repeated refusal, the Immigration Appeals Board. 2) Section 63 of the Danish Constitution, which grants general access to judicial review of administrative decisions.

question_text_en: Right to family reunification without resource conditions
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in 1) the Aliens Act section 9. 2) LBK nr 771 of 07.08.2019, Danish Marriage Act section 1 [Bekendtg?relse af lov om ?gteskabs indg?else og opl?sning. Family reunification with a spouse who is a migrant residing in Denmark is conditional on valid marriage under Danish law (whether if the marriage has occurred in the country or abroad), or a documented period of cohabitation.

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in Aliens Act Sections 9 and 11. All migrant workers who want to settle/achieve permanent residence permit in Denmark have to meet the same requirements on integration, self-sufficiency, language proficiency, continuous residence (typically 8 years) in the country. Visa type is not decisive but may play of role for the outcome.

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services regardless of status.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in Aliens Act Sections 9, 9a, and 9f. According to Section 9, irregular migrant workers may apply for a temporary permission to stay on grounds of employment, which can be extended to permanent stay so long as conditions of residency (among others) are met. The provision is administered in accordance with Article 8 of the Human Rights Convention.

question_text_en: Right of access to public housing programs.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in LBK nr 1003 af 24.08.2017, Act on employment tribunal and professional arbitration [Bekendtg?relse af lov om Arbejdsretten og faglige voldgiftsretter]. 2) Section 1 of The Board of equal Treatment. Both laws provide protections to migrant workers in Denmark commensurate with that of citizens. In case of violation of their employment contract, the migrant worker can seek redress at the Employment Tribunal. Additionally, if the migrant worker is a member of a trade union, the union can address the issue with the employer.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to free primary education for migrant children.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in 1) National law in Denmark protects this right in LBK nr. 903 of 26.08.2019 The Health Act, section 7 [Sundhedsloven], which grants equal and universal access to health care for all resident who are registered in the national registry on the basis of a valid residence permit. The relevant provisions guarantee access to health care services on an equal basis with citizens. Asylum seekers and migrants without legal residence in Denmark are not covered by the national health insurance system. Instead, their healthcare expenses are covered by the Danish Immigration Service. The Immigration Service pays healthcare expenses, provided the treatment is necessary and urgent (treatment cannot be postponed), and/or Pain-relieving Treatment is considered urgent if delaying it could lead to life-threatening injuries, degeneration or serious worsening of your condition, or your condition becoming chronic. Minor asylum seekers are entitled to the same healthcare as children who are residents of Denmark. 2) The Health Act (Sundhedsloven), LBK 17. June 2023, number 1011, Section 7, which establishes that anyone residing in Denmark is entitled to health care.

question_text_en: Right to equal pay for the same work.
citation_text_en: Being lawfully present does not create a legal right for migrants to stand for election in Denmark. However, national law in Denmark grants this right after three years of continuous residence in LBK nr 295 af 07.03.2022, Act on municipal and regional elections, section 3 [Bekendtg?relse af lov om kommunale og regionale valg]. Section 3 in the act on municipal and regional elections establishes that a migrant who has the right to vote in municipal and regional elections pursuant to section 1 also has a right to stand for the those elections.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of choice of employment.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. National law in Denmark does not prohibit discrimination against migrants on the basis of their status as a migrant, according to provisions in the Aliens Act and other relevant acts.

question_text_en: Right of spouse/partner of principal migrant to work.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in 1) Article 14 of the European Convention of Human Rights, which has been incorporated into Danish law via act nr. 285 af 29.4.1992., which states that the enjoyment of the rights and freedoms shall be secured without discrimination on any ground such as sex, race, colour, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, association with a national minority, property, birth or other status. 2) The Act on Assistance for Ukrainian Citizens [Lov om midlertidig opholdstilladelse til personer, der er fordrevet fra Ukraine], which provides special protections for refugees from Ukraine.

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after loss of employment.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in LBK nr. 1001 of 24.08.2017, the Act of Equal Treatment on the Labour Market [Bekendtg?relse af lov om forbud mod forskelsbehandling p? arbejdsmarkedet m.v.]. Danish and migrant workers who work at Danish companies are covered by the same rules, and thus migrant workers are covered by the same pay and employment conditions as local workers. The act also implements all relevant EU Directives.

question_text_en: Right to equal employment conditions and protection.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in the Aliens Act, Section 14, which states that the general rule is that migrant workers have completely free choice of employment. Only in cases where a residence permit has been granted on the basis of a specific occupation, the worker is expected to work in that occupation only (for example a researcher can not also have a another job that is not related to the research sector). However, in these cases, a migrant worker has the freedom to choose another employment and apply for a residence permit based on the new occupation. There are rare exceptions to Section 14 of the Aliens Act, and in some cases employment is tied to a work contract with a specific employer.

question_text_en: Right to form trade unions and other associations.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in the Aliens Act, Section 14, which establishes that the spouse or partner of the principal migrant, if in possession of a valid residence permit, is not required to apply for permission in order to work. The provision gives the spouse/partner of the principal migrant a right to work (without having to apply for permission).

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to redress before deportation or withdrawal of residency permit.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for migrants on labor-related visas. When a residence permit is given explicitly on the basis of employment, when a migrant changes employment (section 9a , subsection 10, Aliens Act) or loses employment without fault of their own (section 9a, subsection 11, Aliens Act), their residence status may be affected consequently. In the first case, the migrant has to apply to the authorities for a new residence permit on the basis of the new employment, and in the second case, the migrant has a six months period to find new employment, or their residence permit will lapse.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to social security protections.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in LBK nr 1001 of 24.08.2017, The Act on Equal Treatment on the Labour Market [Bekendtg?relse af lov om forbud mod forskelsbehandling p? arbejdsmarkedet m.v.]. When employing a migrant worker, a Danish employer has to offer equal employment conditions and protections as local workers. Danish law protects migrant workers in Denmark, and so employers must respect, for examples, the rules on holiday, safety and health at work, non-discrimination on basis of gender or on the basis of ethnicity. The act also implements the relevant EU Directives.

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to become lawfully settled.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protect this right for some migrants in 1) the Aliens Act, Section 9-9q. Access to social security protection varies between different categories of migrant workers and different categories of social security protections. Broadly speaking, refugees are entitled to all kinds of social benefits. Other migrants are entitled to free education, but not welfare benefits. 2) LBK nr 983 of 23.09.2019, Act on social pension, section 2 [Bekendtg?relse af lov om social pension], which establishes that social pension is conditional upon having Danish citizenship or, for migrant workers, 10 years of residence in Denmark since the age of 15.

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to settle regardless of initial status.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark provides equal access to all types of unemployment benefits after a duration of stay in the Social Benefit Act, Section 11, which states that migrant workers and local workers are covered in social benefits schemes, which in this case follows the conditions set up in either the public or private unemployment benefits system (including the condition of a certain period of employment before being able to receive unemployment benefits). The right to full unemployment benefits requires 9 years of residence within the last 10 years.

question_text_en: Right to redress following employer breach of employment contract.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in Aliens Act Sections 9, and 11. If a worker's temporary permission to stay has been renewed, and other conditions on integration, self-sufficiency, language proficiency, continuous residence in the country (typically 8 years) have been met, the permission to stay can become permanent.

question_text_en: Right not to have identity documents confiscated.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in 1) the Aliens Act, Section 34. The police holds the authority to check migrants' identity documents at entry in the country, or during their stay. Conversely no other individual can confiscate migrant workers' identity documents unless authorized by law. However, an employer has a right to request a copy of a worker's passport in order to verify that they are in possession of a valid work permit. Migrants' identity documents can only be confiscated a public official duly authorized by the law.

question_text_en: Right to birth registration.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protect this right in 1) LBK nr 646 of 02.06.2017, Central Persons Register Act [Lov om Det Centrale Personregister, CPR-loven], section 3, which states that "the Central Persons Register Act regulate the Danish civil registration system, whose objective is to set up a system that registers important information about everyone living in Denmark, by assigning a 10-digit number to every person that is born in, or moves to Denmark. All newly born are registrered in a civil register." This also includes children of migrants.

question_text_en: Right to government document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in 1) BEK nr 1206 af 23.08.2022, Ministerial Order on migrants entry in the country. Ministerial Order on migrants entry in the country chapter 1: establishes the rules for identity documents for migrants entering or living in Denmark. Section 9-9p, states that each group of migrant must be issued documents that recognize migrants' residency status, work status, or identity.

question_text_en: Right against destruction of document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to communicate with consular officials.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations, which has been incorporated intp Danish law by means of Ministerial Order BKI nr. 83 af 11/12/1972

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in 1) Aliens Act section 37, stk. 10. section 37, stk. 10, which establishes that unaccompanied minors, while awaiting deportation, cannot be detained in prison facilities. 2) The Aliens Act, which does not allow for the detention of children.

question_text_en: Right of migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The Aliens Act, Section 36 establishes the possibility to imprison and detain migrants who are awaiting deportation, in order to carry out the deportation order.

question_text_en: Right to appeal legality, conditions, and length of detention
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in 1) The Aliens Act section 37, which establishes that a migrant detained awaiting decision of their case or deportation has the right to a judicial review within three days after the start of the inprisonment. According to this provision, decisions of detainment are automatically brought before the courts and are supervised by the Ombudsman. The courts decide on the legality, conditions, and length of detention.

question_text_en: Right to an individualized detention decision.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in The Aliens Consolidation Act, Section 37. In all cases where a migrant is to be detained, the decision has to be individualized and submitted to a court.

question_text_en: Right to be free from torture and inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in 1) BKI nr. 83 af 11.12.1972, Executive Order on The Vienna Convention on consular relations and the related two optional protocols of the same date on the acquisition of citizenship and on the compulsory settlement of disputes [Bekendtg?relse af Wienerkonventionen af 24. april 1963 om konsul?re forbindelser samt de dertil knyttede to fakultative protokoller af samme dato om erhvervelse af statsborgerret og om tvungen bil?ggelse af tvistigheder.] The Vienna Convention on Consular Relations: The convention is incorporated in Danish law by means of Ministerial Order BKI nr. 83 af 11/12/1972. 2) The Aliens Consolidation Act, UDL section 7, stk. 2, section 9 b, section 9 c, section 31, section 48 a. UDL section 7 stk. 2 provides the legal basis for granting asylum for those asylum seekers who risk to suffer torture or cruel, inhumane, and degrading treatment if returned to their homeland. UDL section 31 provides that a migrant cannot be sent to a country where they risk death penalty or to suffer torture or cruel, inhumane, and degrading treatment, or to a country where the migrant is not protected against transfer to such a country. In case an asylum application is rejected, UDL section 48 a ensures that the migrant applicant is not to be sent to a country where they risk death penalty or to suffer torture or cruel, inhumane, and degrading treatment. Section 9 b and section 9 c provide subsidiary protection as these provisions incorporate Article 3 the European Convention on Human Rights which declares that no one shall be subjected to torture or to inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. UDL section 36 gives the police the authority to imprison/detain a migrant that enters the country in order to seek asylum, to establish their identity and register their fingerprints. Other aliens are, however, prevented from entering the country without adequate legal basis.

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of lethal force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in 1) Aliens Act section 36, which only gives the police the authority to imprison a migrant who illegally enters the country in order to seek asylum. 2) Act of Criminal Code (Bekendtg?relse af straffeloven), LBK nr 1360 af 28.09.1022 (referred herinafter as to as Criminal Code) section 13. Danish law entails the use of lethal force only when "necessary" in response to a threat according the section 13 of the penal code. Migrants attempting to enter the country, are not considered a threat in that regard.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from trafficking or smuggling.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in 1) the Danish Criminal Code, [Straffeloven], section 262 a. 2) The Aliens Act section 26 a and section 50. 3) LBK nr. 976 of 17.09.2019. Only traffickers and smugglers are charged criminally. Trafficked and smuggled migrants are exempt from criminal prosecutions under Danish law.

question_text_en: Right to maintain citizenship status after convictions.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in LBK nr 1029 of 23.12.2022, Danish Citizenship Consolidation Act [Lovbekendtg?relse om dansk indf?dsret], section 8 a and section 8 b. 2) LOV nr 1057 af 24.10.2019, Act changing the Danish Citizenship Consolidation Act and the Aliens Act (withdrawal of citizenship for foreign fighters ect.) [Lov om ?ndring af lov om dansk indf?dsret og udl?ndingeloven (Fratagelse af statsborgerskab fra fremmedkrigere m.v.)], Section 1. Citizenship can be revoked in cases of crimes against the state or national security, and if the applicant has forged information during the application. Since 2019, Act nr. 1057 of 24.10.2019 has introduced an amendment that can lead to loss of citizenship for those who fight for foreign states. Danish nationality can be lost by court order if a person is convicted in violation of one or more provisions of Chapters 12 and 13 of the Danish Criminal Code (crimes against national security), unless this would render the person stateless.

question_text_en: Right of economic migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in 1) LBK nr 1656 af 23.12.2022, Section 9 a of the Aliens Act, UDL, cf. section 11 of the same Act [Bekendtg?relse af lov om dansk indf?dsret]. 2)Circular on naturalisation nr. 9461 af 17.06.2021 [Cirkul?reskrivelse om naturalisation] and the Aliens Act, Section 9a.

question_text_en: Right of humanitarian migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in 1) LBK nr. 1656 of 23.12.2022, Danish Citizenship Consolidation Act, Circular on naturalisation nr. 9461 af 17.06.2021 [Cirkul?reskrivelse om naturalisation]. 2) Aliens Act section 9 b. Humanitarian migrants have a pathway to citizenship via shorter residence requirements than other categories (eight years instead of nine years of uninterrupted residence in the country).

question_text_en: Right of family migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in 1) LBK nr. 1656 of 23.12.2022, Danish Citizenship Consolidation Act. 2) Circular on naturalisation nr. 9461 af 17.06.2021 [Cirkul?reskrivelse om naturalisation]. 3) The Aliens Act section 9, section 9 c, section 9 n and section 9 m.

question_text_en: Right to dual nationality.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in 1) Lov nr. 1496 of 23.12.2014, Act on the acceptance of dual citizenship and payment of fees in cases regarding Danish nationality [Accept af dobbelt statsborgerskab og betaling af gebyr i sager om dansk indf?dsret]. 2) The Citizenship Act section 6. Danish legislation has been amended via Act nr. 1496 of 23.12.2014 to allow dual nationality in naturalization cases. The country in which the migrant holds citizenship must accept dual citizenship.

question_text_en: Right to freedom to hold opinion.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in the Constitutional Act of Denmark [Grundloven], Sections 67, 70, 77, and 78, which protect the right of freedom of thought, conscience and religion or belief of migrants on an equal basis with citizens.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of expression.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in the Constitutional Act of Denmark [Grundloven], Section 77, which provides migrants with full freedom to hold opinions commensurate with that afforded to citizens.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of association.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in the Constitutional Act of Denmark [Grundloven], Section 77, which provides migrants with full freedom of expression commensurate with that afforded to citizens.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of assembly.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in the Constitutional Act of Denmark [Grundloven], Section 78, which guarantees freedom of association commensurate with that afforded to citizens.

category: Thought, conscience, and religion or belief
question_text_en: Right of freedom of thought, conscience and religion or belief.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Section 9 of the Aliens Act establishes a long list of requirements for migrant applicants to family reunification in Denmark. Among these: a valid marriage or fast cohabitation; a marriage which is neither forced or pro-forma in order to achieve a residence permit; at least 24 years of age (for both partners); passing of two tests of Danish language and other integration requirements regarding employment and education (for the applicant not living in Denmark); be in possession of a dwelling of reasonable size; economic self-sufficiency, integration, absence of criminal charges for violence against a spouse and permanent residence in Denmark (for the applicant living in the country), and a collateral in the form of a financial guarantee of 110.293 DKK (~ 16,470 USD). These requirements can be waived in special cases, such as when the spouse is a refugee, the spouse has an illness or other disability, or in the case where the couple has a child.

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to access criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in 1) LBK No. 1655, 25-12-2022, which states that the Danish Procedure Code establishes that the public prosecution together with the police have a duty to investigate any crime that occurs on Danish territory, irrespective of whether the victim was a migrant. The rules do not distinguish between nationals and migrants. 2) The Administration of Justice Act, Chapter 10 (Bekendtg?relse af lov om rettens pleje).

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to immigration status or relief from expulsion.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in 1) Aliens Act section 19 and section 26a. Section 19 states that only in rare cases migrant victims of crime are provided an avenue to immigration status or relief from expulsion as a result of being a victim of a crime. The exception that provides victims of crime relief from expulsion is violence and threats against a spouse or partner. Additionally, Section 26a establishes that in deportation decisions, special consideration must be taken if the circumstances that can lead to deportation are a consequence of trafficking of the migrant.

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in 1) BK nr. 1205 of 25.08.2022. 2) Aliens Consolidation Act [Udl?ndingeloven] referred herinafter as to as UDL, UDL section 9, stk. 1, nr. 2; section 9 stk. 20 section 9 stk. 21; section 9 c; section 9 c stk. 3; section 37, stk. 10; section 42 a; section 42 b; and section 56 a. UDL section 9, stk. 1, nr. 2, which establishes the possibility of granting a permission to stay for minors on the basis of adoption, foster care, or residence with family members. Section 9 stk. 221 establishes the possibility to deny a permission to stay to a child in case that decision would entail going against the child’s best interest, for fear of neglect or abuse at the hand of the family living in Denmark. Section 9 c establishes the possibility of granting a permission to stay “on special grounds” to a child under 18 years of age, in accordance with the best interest of the child and consideration of family unity in respect of article 8 ECHR. The ECHR is incorporated into Danish law by Act nr. 285 af 29.4.1992. As regards unaccompanied minors, section 9 c stk. 3 establishes the possibility to grant a residence permit to a child under 18 years of age if deportation would entail an unbearable situation for the child, such as if they had no family network or possibility to stay in a dedicated center. Special procedural rules apply during their asylum application, while minors under 12 years of age and some between 12 and 15 would receive a permission to stay without having to go through an asylum procedure. section 37, stk. 10 establishes that unaccompanied minors, while awaiting deportation, cannot be detained in prison facilities. section 42 a establishes special considerations to be taken for unaccompanied minors as regards lodging in asylum centers. section 42 b sets basic cash benefits specifically for unaccompanied minors. section 56 a grants the possibility to appoint a representative for unaccompanied minors for safeguarding their interests; the possibility to have help in locating their family; and the possibility to have counseling by a court-appointed lawyer during their asylum proceedings. 3) The authorities have to respect Art. 8 on the right to family life in the European Convention on Human Rights (referred to as ECHR) and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (referred to as UNCRC) when exercising discretionary powers. Respect of the ECHR does however not automatically ensure that family life can be conducted in Denmark. The rule only includes children under 15 years of age, who live with their parents, and are not married. Various conditions to the status of the parent residing in Denmark apply. Restrictions to family reunification with children for asylum seekers with temporary protection also apply, and have not been found in breach of ECHR by the courts. Section 9 stk. 20 establishes that the child has to apply within 3 months after being eligible for family reunification.

question_text_en: Right of women migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right specifically for women in the context of migration. National law in Denmark protects this generally for both men and women in right in the Aliens Consolidation Act, UDL section 19, stk. 7. This establishes that in a case where a permission to stay for a spouse can be revoked because of cessation of cohabitation, an exception can be made in the case the cohabitation ended on grounds of domestic violence and/or threats to the alien or his/her child. Additionally, the Alien Consolidation Act, section 7, stk. 1. deals with cases involving Afghan women and girls, and has interpreted Section 7 to provide a relaxed assessment of evidence, given the arbitrariness and uncertainty with which the Taliban's de facto exercise of authority takes place, as well as the continued serious deterioration of the situation of women and girls.

question_text_en: Rights of migrants with disabilities to special protection.
citation_text_en: National law in Denmark protects this right in 1) Aliens Consolidation Act, UDL section 9, section 9 c, section 9 q, stk. 9, section 11, section 42 a. UDL. Section 9 establishes the conditions to be fulfilled by the migrant residing in Denmark in case of application for family reunification. If one of more of these conditions cannot be met because of handicap, an exception can be made in line with the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD), and family reunification can be granted. Section 11 establishes an exception to one or more of the conditions for permanent residence for applicants with a handicap, in line with the CRPD. These can be for example in relation to the employment or language requirements for permanent residence. UDL. Section 42 a establishes that the Danish authorities will undertake the costs associated with the support of a minor asylum seekers with a handicap, who lives with their parents, in accordance with the CRPD. 2) Non-discrimination act on the basis of handicap nr. 688 of 08.06.2018, which provides protections for all people in Denmark with disabilities, and thereby provides special protections for migrants with disabilities vis-a-vis other migrants.

citation_text_en: Ecuador

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to vote in local and/or regional elections.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in 1) the Constitution of Ecuador, Articles, 9, 11, 66. Article 9 states that, "Foreigners who are in Ecuadorian territory have the same rights rights and duties as Ecuadorian citizens, in accordance with the Constitution." Article 11 states that, "2. All people are equal and will enjoy the same rights, duties and opportunities: No one may be discriminated against for reasons of ethnicity, place of birth, age, sex, identity of gender, cultural identity, marital status, language, religion, ideology, political affiliation, judicial past, socioeconomic status, migratory status, sexual orientation, health status, carrying HIV, disability, physical difference; nor for any other distinction, personal or collective, temporal or permanent, whose purpose or result is to impair or annul the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of rights. The law shall punish all forms of discrimination." Article 66 states that, "The right to associate, meet and demonstrate freely and voluntarily..." 2) The Organic Law of Human Mobility, Articles 46 and 49. Article 46 states that, "Right to participation and social organization.- Foreigners will have the right to form social organizations to exercise their rights and carry out activities that allow their integration and participation in society in accordance with the regulations in force, as long as they do not disturb the peace or public order." Article 49 states that, "Right to political participation.- Foreigners who reside in the Ecuador will have the right to vote and be elected to public office, as long as they have legally resided in the country for at least five years, in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution and the law."

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to stand for election.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. However, Article 63 of the Constitution, and Article 63 of the Electoral law allows for migrants to vote assuming they have attained the age of 16, and also have legally resided in the country for at least five years.

question_text_en: Right to equal protection of the law before courts.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in 1) the Organic Law of Human Mbility, Articles 2 and 47. Article 47 states that, "foreigners, regardless of their situation immigration, will have the right to access justice and the guarantees of due process for the effective protection of their rights, in accordance with the Constitution, the current international instruments, and the Law." 2) The Constitution of Ecuador, Article 9.

question_text_en: Right to government-provided counsel in proceedings related to migrant status.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in the Organic Law of Human Mobility, Articles 12, 52.B, 99, 113, 136.A, 138, 143.A, 144. Article 52.B, specifically, states that "Without prejudice to the specific rights and guarantees provided for in this Law, every foreign person in Ecuador is assured, in each of the procedures, the right to due process, which will include, at least, the following basic guarantees: c) Be assisted by a lawyer of your choice or by a defender public, as well as by a translator or interpreter when appropriate; Article 99:Guarantees of due process in the procedure for determining the refugee status.- Without prejudice to the guarantees contemplated in the Constitution, in the procedure for the determination of refugee status, the following guarantees must be observed:11. In the case of children and adolescents alone, unaccompanied or separated from their legal representatives, the competent authority will coordinate the appointment of a guardian or legal representative. The human mobility authority will immediately notify the Public Defender's Office to assume sponsorship in defense of the rights of the child, girl or adolescent."

question_text_en: Right to government-provided interpretation in criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in Organic Criminal Code, Articles 11, 563. Article 11 states that, "in all criminal proceedings, the victim of the infractions will enjoy the following rights:7. To be assisted free of charge by a translator or interpreter, if you do not understand or speak the language in which the procedure is carried out as well as to receive specialized assistance." Articles 563 states that, "hearings will be governed by the following rules: 6. The official language is Spanish, if the person cannot understand or express it easily, processed, the victim or other participants, will be assisted by a translator designated by the or the judge."

question_text_en: Right to be protected from prosecution for unauthorized entry.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in Organic Law of Human Mobility, Articles 2, and 113. Article 2 states that, "No person will be subject to criminal sanctions for their condition of human mobility. Any immigration offense will have an administrative nature." Article 113 states that, "the procedure for the recognition of stateless person, will be carried out respecting the following guarantees, in addition to the contemplated in the Constitution: (...) To the applicant, while he is in said situation or when he has been recognized as a stateless person, no sanction will be imposed for reasons of entry or irregular stay in the country. Constitution of Ecuador, Article 41 (...)Criminal sanctions will not be applied to persons seeking asylum or refuge due to the fact of their entry or their permanence in an irregular situation. Paragraph 49: Therefore, in no case does the Irregular entry can be considered a criminal offense and, consequently, Nor can criminal control mechanisms be used for these purposes."

question_text_en: Right to equal access to public adult education institutions.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Article's 27 and 30 of the Constitution of Ecuador only guarantee this right for Ecuadoran citizens who return to the national territory.

question_text_en: Right of access to public adult education institutions regardless of status.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in 1) the Constitution of Ecuador, Articles 9, 11, 26, and 28. Article 28 states that, "Public education shall be universal and secular at all levels and shall be free of charge up to and including the third level of higher education [post-secondary undergraduate schooling]." 2) The Constitutional Court in case 1497-19-JP/21 of December 21, 2021 recently reviewed regulations addressing the accessibility of public education to migrant children regardless of status, and other people in vulnerable situations, and stated, "The indicated measures are intended to guarantee that students, in general, and those in vulnerable situations, in particular, can easily access appropriate to the corresponding level of studies, without the circumstances preventing the full enjoyment of their right to education."

question_text_en: Right to be free from discrimination on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right for documented migrants in the Organic Law of Higher Education, Article 71 which recognizes that, "The institutions that make up the Higher Education System will strive, to the best of their abilities, to ensure that the principle of equal opportunities is fulfilled in favor of migrants."

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after convictions.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in the Organic Law on Human Mobility Articles 68 and 143. Article 143 states that, "a foreign person who incurs any of the following grounds will be deported from Ecuadorian territory: 8. The person has received executory conviction for the commission of a crime punishable by custodial sentence of more than five years in accordance with criminal legislation current; 9. The person been sanctioned for the commission of any of the contraventions contained in the criminal legislation in force for disturbing and putting at risk the tranquility and peace of the citizenry, or disturbing the order."

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of torture or inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in 1) the Constitution of Ecuador, Articles 41 and 66. Article 41 states that, "the rights of asylum and refuge are recognized, in accordance with the law and instruments international human rights. People who are in asylum status or refuge will enjoy special protection that guarantees the full exercise of their rights. The state will respect and guarantee the principle of non-refoulement, in addition to humanitarian and legal assistance of emergency." Article 66 states that "foreign persons may not be returned or expelled to a country where their life, freedom, security or integrity or that of their family members is endangered because of their ethnicity, religion, nationality, ideology, membership in a certain social group, or their political opinions." 2) Organic Law of Human Mobility, Article 2, which states that, "The person may not be returned or expelled to another country, whether or not it is the country of origin, in which their rights to life, liberty, integrity and personal security of their relatives, run the risk of being violated because of their ethnicity, religion, nationality, ideology, gender, sexual orientation, membership in a certain group social, political opinions or when there are well-founded reasons that he would be in danger of be subjected to serious violations of human rights, in accordance with this Law and international human rights instruments."

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of persecution.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in 1) the Constitution of Ecuador, Articles 41 and 66. Article 41 states that, "the rights of asylum and refuge are recognized, in accordance with the law and instruments international human rights. People who are in asylum status or refuge will enjoy special protection that guarantees the full exercise of their rights. The state will respect and guarantee the principle of non-refoulement, in addition to humanitarian and legal assistance of emergency." Article 66 states that "foreign persons may not be returned or expelled to a country where their life, freedom, security or integrity or that of their family members is endangered because of their ethnicity, religion, nationality, ideology, membership in a certain social group, or their political opinions." 2) Organic Law of Human Mobility, Article 2, which states that, "The person may not be returned or expelled to another country, whether or not it is the country of origin, in which their rights to life, liberty, integrity and personal security of their relatives, run the risk of being violated because of their ethnicity, religion, nationality, ideology, gender, sexual orientation, membership in a certain group social, political opinions or when there are well-founded reasons that he would be in danger of be subjected to serious violations of human rights, in accordance with this Law and international human rights instruments."

question_text_en: Right to not return to a deprivations of fundamental human rights.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in 1) the Constitution of Ecuador, Articles 41 and 66. Article 41 states that, "the rights of asylum and refuge are recognized, in accordance with the law and instruments international human rights. People who are in asylum status or refuge will enjoy special protection that guarantees the full exercise of their rights. The state will respect and guarantee the principle of non-refoulement, in addition to humanitarian and legal assistance of emergency." Article 66 states that "foreign persons may not be returned or expelled to a country where their life, freedom, security or integrity or that of their family members is endangered because of their ethnicity, religion, nationality, ideology, membership in a certain social group, or their political opinions." 2) Organic Law of Human Mobility, Article 2, which states that, "The person may not be returned or expelled to another country, whether or not it is the country of origin, in which their rights to life, liberty, integrity and personal security of their relatives, run the risk of being violated because of their ethnicity, religion, nationality, ideology, gender, sexual orientation, membership in a certain group social, political opinions or when there are well-founded reasons that he would be in danger of be subjected to serious violations of human rights, in accordance with this Law and international human rights instruments."

question_text_en: Right to be advised of availability of asylum before expulsion.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in the Organic Law of Human Mobility, Articles 100 and 143. Article 100 states that, "any public employee who has knowledge of the entry into the national territory of a person who could be inserted in the assumptions that underlie the grant of international protection, has the duty to immediately refer it to the human mobility authority to present the respective request. Article 143.A states that, "in the deportation procedures the Government has the duty to respect and guarantee, at least the following guarantees and rights of migrants: i) The right not to be deported in the following cases: 1. When a person presents needs for international protection or protection by humanitarian reasons in accordance with indicated in this Law, even when you have not accessed the formal procedure to determine such condition."

question_text_en: Right to be protected from chain refoulement.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to protection against expulsion except following a legal judgment.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in 1) the Organic Law of Human Mobility, Article 141 and 143A. Article 141 states that, "deportation will proceed only for the causes established by this Law and will maintain unrestricted respect for the guarantees of due process enshrined in the Constitution." 2) The Deceision 159-11-JH/19 of the Constitutional Court of Ecuador established in paragraph 100, which states, "deportation must be of last resort and guarantee the principle of non-refoulement for all foreigners. a) Deportation must be ultima ratio and guarantee the principle of non-refoulement for all foreigners." 3) In decision 639-19-JP/20 the Constitutional Court of Ecuador, established as guarantees of the deportation process, which states, that, "due process for people in human mobility includes, at least, the individual right to: a) Expressly and formally inform of the charges against and the reasons for the expulsion or deportation. b) Listen to the person on the move so that they can explain their reasons and oppose the charges against him. c) Request and receive consular assistance, legal advice and, if applicable, translation or interpretation. d) Submit your case to review before the competent authority and appear before it, in case of an unfavorable decision."

question_text_en: Right to submit reasons against expulsion and have case reviewed before deportation.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in 1) Articles 143.A and 219 The Regulation of the Organic Law of Human Mobility. 2) Decision 639-19-JP/20 the Constitutional Court, which states that "Due process for people in human mobility includes, at least, the individual right to: a) Expressly and formally inform of the charges against and the reasons for the expulsion or deportation. b) Listen to the person on the move so that they can explain their reasons and oppose the charges against him. c) Request and receive consular assistance, legal advice and, if applicable, translation or interpretation. d) Submit your case to review before the competent authority and appear before it, in case of an unfavorable decision."

question_text_en: Right of settled migrants to family reunification.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. However, Ecuador provides for citizenship by birth in the Constitution, Article 7.

question_text_en: Right to judicial remedy for denials of right to family reunification.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador conditionally protects this right in Articles 60, 64, 65A, and 155 of the Regulation to the Organic Law of Human Mobility.

question_text_en: Right to recognition of same-sex marital relationships.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in Article 224 of the Organic Administrative code which allows a specific right of appeal on decisions related to family reunification in front of an administrative, not judicial body. In addition, all administrative decisions related to family reunification can be challenged judicially through ordinary means before the Contentious Administrative Court or through a judicial action for constitutional protection.

question_text_en: Right to family reunification without resource conditions
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in 1) Constitutional Court decisions, 11-18-CN/19 and 12-18-CN/19 of June 12, 2019. These decisions recognized same-sex marriage in Ecuador. 2) Article 155 of the Regulation to the Organic Law of Human Mobility, recognizes Constitutional Court Decision 11-18-CN/19 of the Constitutional Court of Ecuador.

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in Articles 63 and 64 of the Organic Law of Human Mobility. The requirement to access the permanent visa is to complete at least 21 months of continuous residence in Ecuador, no matter the previous visa category.

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services regardless of status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right of access to public housing programs.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in 1) the Organic Law of Human Mobility, Article 47, which states that "Foreigners, regardless of their situation immigration, will have the right to access justice and the guarantees of due process for the effective protection of their rights, in accordance with the Constitution, the current international instruments, and the Law." 2) The Labor Code, Articles 73, 342-344, and 568. Article 73 states that, "Causes for the worker to terminate the contract.- The worker may terminate the employment contract, and with prior approval, in the following cases: 1. For serious injuries inflicted by the employer, his family members or representatives to the worker, his spouse or cohabitant in a de facto union, ascendants or descendants; 2. Due to a decrease or lack of payment or punctuality in the payment of the agreed remuneration; and, 3. By requiring the employer that the worker perform a task other than that agreed upon, except in cases of urgency provided for in article 52 of this Code, but always within what was agreed upon in the contract or agreement."

question_text_en: Right to equal access to free primary education for migrant children.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right for regular migrants in 1) the Organic Law of Human Mobility, Article , which states that, "Foreigners residing in Ecuador have the right to access the health systems in accordance with law and ratified international instruments by the Ecuadorian State. Public or private institutions that provide health services may not, in any way, case, refuse to provide emergency care due to nationality or status migration of a person. The Ecuadorian State will promote policies that protect foreigners in the country. Ecuador in case of illness, accidents or death, being necessary for the person resident have public or private insurance that consolidates this benefit." 2) The Constitutional Court in case 983-18-JP/21 of August 25, 2021 which established in paragraph 365 that, "Every person has the right to have the State guarantee access to assistance health independently of the geographical area in which it is located; in In this sense, the residence, domicile or place of habitation occupied by a person in the territorial space of a country, does not constitute a coherent excuse to justify the deprivation of their right to health."

question_text_en: Right to equal pay for the same work.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of choice of employment.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in 1) the Constitution of Ecuador, Articles 9, 11, 40, 156, and 416. reinforced immigration status as a protected ground of discrimination. 2) Additionally, the Constitutional Court confrimed that migrant status is explicitly protected in decisions159-11-JH/19 of November 26, 2019; decision 983-18-JP/21 of August 25, 2021; 2185-19-JP/ dated December 1, 2021.

question_text_en: Right of spouse/partner of principal migrant to work.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in 1) the Constitution of Ecuador, Article 11.2, which states that, "2: All people are equal and will enjoy the same rights, duties and opportunities. No one may be discriminated against for reasons of ethnicity, place of birth, age, sex, identity of gender, cultural identity, marital status, language, religion, ideology, political affiliation, judicial past, socioeconomic status, migratory status, sexual orientation, health status, carrying HIV, disability, physical difference; nor by any other distinction, personal or collective, temporal or permanent, whose purpose or result is to impair or annul the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of rights. The law shall punish all forms of discrimination." 2) Organic Law of Human Mobility, Article 2, which states, "Equality before the Law and non-discrimination: All people in human mobility, who are located in Ecuadorian territory, enjoy the rights recognized in the Constitution, international instruments ratified by Ecuador and the Law. none person will be discriminated against due to their immigration status, national origin, sex, gender, sexual orientation or other social, economic, ethnic or cultural condition."

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after loss of employment.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in 1) the Constitution of Ecuador, Articles 11.2 and 326. Article 11.2 states that, "2: All people are equal and will enjoy the same rights, duties and opportunities. No one may be discriminated against for reasons of ethnicity, place of birth, age, sex, identity of gender, cultural identity, marital status, language, religion, ideology, political affiliation, judicial past, socioeconomic status, migratory status, sexual orientation, health status, carrying HIV, disability, physical difference; nor by any other distinction, personal or collective, temporal or permanent, whose purpose or result is to impair or annul the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of rights. The law shall punish all forms of discrimination." Article 326 states that, "The right to work is based on the following principles: 4. Equal remuneration will correspond to work of equal value." 2) Organic Law of Human Mobility, Article 51, which states, "Right to work and social security.- Foreigners residing in Ecuador included Subjects of international protection have the right to work and access to social security, for which your contributions will be calculated based on real income declared to obtain their residence. When the resident person works under a dependency relationship, their contributions are will be calculated based on your remuneration. Lack of affiliation to the Ecuadorian Social Security Institute will be sanctioned in accordance with current regulations for this purpose."

question_text_en: Right to equal employment conditions and protection.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in 1) Articles 51, 60.1, and 61 of the Organic Law of Human Mobility. 2) Article 66 of the Constitution of Ecuador.

question_text_en: Right to form trade unions and other associations.
citation_text_en: National Law in Ecuador protects this right under Article 79 of the Regulation to the Organic Law of Human Mobility, which recognizes that 'the holder of a temporary residence visa may apply for this category of [amparo visa] for their children, spouse, or partner,' allowing them to work without an additional permit.

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to redress before deportation or withdrawal of residency permit.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in Article 62 of the Regulation to the Organic Law of Human Mobility.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to social security protections.

The right to freedom of contract. 17. The right to freedom of work. question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to settle regardless of initial status.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in 1) the Constitution of Ecuador, Article 34, which states, "The right to social security is an inalienable right of all people, and will be primary duty and responsibility of the State. Social security will be governed by the principles of solidarity, obligatory nature, universality, equity, efficiency, subsidiarity, sufficiency, transparency and participation, to address individual and collective needs. The Government will guarantee and make effective the full exercise of the right to social security, which includes to people who do unpaid work in homes, self-sustaining activities in the countryside, all forms of self employment and those who are unemployed." 2) Organic Law of Human Mobility: Article 51, which states, "Right to work and social security.- Foreigners residing in Ecuador included Subjects of international protection have the right to work and access to social security, for which their contributions will be calculated based on real income declared to obtain their residence. When the resident person works under a dependency relationship, their contributions are will be calculated based on your remuneration. Lack of affiliation to the Ecuadorian Social Security Institute will be sanctioned in accordance with current regulations for this purpose." 3) Articles 275.1 and 283 of the Organic Law of Social Security. Article 283 states that, "Unemployment benefit.- Unemployment benefit consists of the delivery of money to the member, by the IESS in cases in which the latter requires it due to being in a situation of unemployment. The amount of the benefit will be given by the fund accumulated in the individual account of the affiliate and may be received as many times as he/she is unemployed, provided that in each opportunity meets the requirements and conditions established by law."

question_text_en: Right to redress following employer breach of employment contract.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in 1) Organic Law of Human Mobility, Articles 63 and 64. Article 63 states that, "it is the immigration condition that authorizes the stay in the national territory of indefinite manner to which people who meet at least one of the following conditions: 1. Complete at least twenty-one continuous months of stay in Ecuador, in quality resident and submit the corresponding application, prior to the expiration of the residence held, in accordance with the provisions of the Regulations of this Law..." 2) Article 83 of the Regulation to the Organic Law of Human Mobility. The requirement to access the permanent visa is to complete at least 21 months of continuous residence in Ecuador, no matter the previous visa category.

question_text_en: Right not to have identity documents confiscated.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in the Organic Law of Human Mobility in article 159, which states that, "Prohibition of retention, alteration or tearing of documents.- It is prohibited the retention of travel documents of any person entering, leaving or remain in Ecuadorian territory, except when its falsehood has been identified or nullity. Likewise, the immigration control authority or the human mobility authority, in the review of documents, the authority will not be able to adulterate or break them to the detriment of the user. Exceptionally, the human mobility or immigration control authority may retain travel documents when, there is a legal obligation to return the diplomatic, official passport or special travel document, the person has not returned."

question_text_en: Right to birth registration.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in 1) Article 35 of the Code of Childhood and Adolescence. 2) Decision No. 2185-19-JP/21 of the Constitutional Court of Ecuador, which protects the right to birth registration regardless of the immigration status of the parents, and the duty of the state to proceed with those registrations, including the ones of migrants teenagers underage.

question_text_en: Right to government document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in in Articles 44 of the Organic Law of Human Mobility.

question_text_en: Right against destruction of document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in Article 159 of Organic Law of Human Mobility, which states that, "it is prohibited the retention of travel documents of any person entering, leaving or remain in Ecuadorian territory, except when its falsehood has been identified or nullity.
