question_text_en: Right to communicate with consular officials.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in Organic Law of Human Mobility, articles 52B, and 136A. Article 136.A states that, "people subject to the procedure administrative inadmissibility will have the following minimum guarantees: f) They will be able to communicate with the consulate of their country and will have access to consular assistance where appropriate."

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in Article 2 of the Organic Law of Human Mobility, which states that "within the framework of the best interest of girls, children and adolescents, in all processes and procedures linked to mobility human,-the norms provided for in the Law of the matter will be taken into account, such as the principle of specialty of childhood and adolescence and the rights to have a family, family coexistence and be consulted on all matters that affect them. In no case may their detention be ordered for administrative immigration offenses. When the best interests of the girl, boy or adolescent require the maintenance of the family unit, the imperative of non-deprivation of liberty will extend to its parents, without prejudice to the alternative measures that may be dictated in the control migratory."

question_text_en: Right of migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in decisions No. 159-11-JH/19, 335-13-JP/20 and 2533-16-EP/21 of the Constitutional Court of Ecuador. Judicial decision 159-11-JH/19 issued by Constitutional Court of Ecuador, on November 26, 2019 established in paragraph 69 that: Migrants in an irregular situation may not be criminally sanctioned for their single immigration status. This prohibition implies that these people cannot be treated either as if they had committed a criminal offense. Consequently, the authorities will not be able to deprive freedom due to immigration status or initiate a deportation process that comes from an arbitrary deprivation of liberty.

question_text_en: Right to appeal legality, conditions, and length of detention
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in 1) Article 43 of Organic Law of Jurisdictional Guarantees and Constitutional Control. 2) In addition the Constitution of Ecuador establishes rapid judicial mechanisms for violations of rights. Among these mechanisms is habeas corpus in cases of illegal detentions (Articles 89 and 90 of the Constitution). In this regard, decision 159-11-JH/19 of the Constitutional Court established in paragraph 44 that habeas corpus is the appropriate mechanism. to protect freedom from arbitrary situations of people in human mobility. 3) Article 145 of the Organic Law of Human Mobility, which states, "the immigration control authority will guarantee the presence of the foreign person subject to the deportation procedure in conditions that protect their human rights, being able to do so, impose the precautionary measures that the law establishes as the periodic presentation, and the determination and limitation of residence, transit and payment, in guarantee, of a unified basic remuneration to guarantee the execution of the deportation procedure. In case of non-compliance with precautionary measures, the Immigration Control Authority will order the immediate deportation of the foreign person. For this purpose you may request the support of the National Police. The immigration control authority will inform the person linked to the immigration process deportation the consequences of non-compliance with the precautionary measures that have been willing. Prior to this, the person subject to the deportation process may present administrative appeals to prevent the deportation."

question_text_en: Right to an individualized detention decision.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in 1) the Constitution of Ecuador in Article 66.14, which establishes that: "the expulsion of groups of foreigners is prohibited. Immigration processes must be singularized." 2) Decision 639-19-JP/20 of October 21, 2020, the Constitutional Court of Ecuador established that: "the right to due process of people in mobility situations indicates that any decision of a state authority regarding the entry, permanence or departure of a person from the national territory, must be adopted through an individual procedure that allows the evaluation of the circumstances in each case and at the same time allows requesting and receive consular help. For this reason, a deportation or collective expulsion, like that of present case, does not observe due process and does not consider the circumstance of each person." 3) Article 2 of the Organic Law of Human Mobility establishes that: "deportation procedures from the country or any that affect the status immigration are of an individual nature. The expulsion of groups of people is prohibited."

question_text_en: Right to be free from torture and inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law protects this right in the Constitution of Ecuador, Article 9, 66.c, and 66.3.

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of lethal force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador does not directly address the use of lethal force in relation to illegal entry of migrants. However, national law in Ecuador does not criminalize migration related offenses, and therefore the use of lethal force to stop migrants from crossing the border would effectively never be proportional, or lawful based on 1) the Constitution of Ecuador, Article 40. 2) Organic Law of Human Mobility. 3) Decision 159-11-JH/19, Constitutional Court, november 26, 2019, paragraphs 68, 69, which states that a violation of an administrative rule, such as the failure to comply with an immigration regulation, cannot under any circumstances be understood or treated as a violation of criminal nature.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from trafficking or smuggling.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador exempts trafficked smuggled migrants from criminal prosecutions in 1) Article 213 of Criminal Code, which "only criminalizes individuals who directly or indirectly obtain economic benefits or other material gains through any means and engage in the promotion, recruitment, sheltering, facilitation, inducement, financing, collaboration, participation, or assistance of trafficked and smuggled migrants." 2) Organic Law against human traffiiking and smuggling, Article 4, which states that, "in matters of human trafficking and smuggling of migrants, without prejudice to what is stated in the Constitution and lower regulations, the following principles will be respected: j) Non-criminalization and no detention of victims: Victims of human trafficking and smuggling of migrants will not be detained, detained, accused, prosecuted, or sanctioned for carrying out acts that are the direct result of the irsituation as victims of such infractions. Nor will administrative sanctions or impediments provided for in immigration legislation be applied to them."

question_text_en: Right to maintain citizenship status after convictions.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in Articles 79 and 81 of the Organic Law of Human Mobility. Article 79 states that, "it will not be possible grant the naturalization letter after a resolution motivated by the following reasons: 1. Failure to comply with the requirements provided for in this Law. 2. Have received executory conviction sentence for any of the crimes indicated in the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court; for any crime provided for by law Ecuadorian whose custodial sentence exceeds five years; as well as for the crime of illicit trafficking of scheduled substances subject to control." Article 81 states that, "Without prejudice to the corresponding criminal sanction, prior action of lesivity, the human mobility authority will declare null the naturalization of a person when this has been granted on the basis of concealment of relevant facts, false documents or the commission of fraud against the law in the concession procedure. The procedure aimed at declaring the naturalization letter null and void must be developed individually and in all cases the human rights, the guarantees of due process and the guarantees recognized in the present Law. The decision that declares the nullity of the naturalization letter must be notified to the competent authorities. In all cases in which the nullity of the naturalization letter has been declared, the human mobility authority must inform the interested party of the possible migratory alternatives that could be availed of as appropriate and in accordance with the regulations that regulate immigration procedures."

question_text_en: Right to freedom of association.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Article 49 of the Human Mobillity Law states that: "Temporary visitors to Ecuador will not be able to interfere in matters of internal politics of Ecuador." This is broad limitation that allows the government to limit the freedom of speech and expression of migrants on issues related to policy. However, the freedom of speech and expression for migrants in all other subjects is protected in the Constitution of Ecuador, Articles, 9, 11, and 66. Article 9 states that, "Foreigners who are in Ecuadorian territory have the same rights rights and duties as Ecuadorian citizens, in accordance with the Constitution." Article 11 states that, "2. All people are equal and will enjoy the same rights, duties and opportunities: No one may be discriminated against for reasons of [...] migratory status [...]; nor for any other distinction, personal or collective, temporal or permanent, whose purpose or result is to impair or annul the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of rights. The law shall punish all forms of discrimination." Article 66 recognizes "The right to give an opinion and express your thoughts freely and in all its forms and manifestations"

Article 326 states that, "The right to work is based on the following principles: 7. The right and freedom of organization of workers will be guaranteed, without prior authorization. This right includes the right to form unions, guilds, associations and other forms of organization, join those of your choice andfreely disaffiliate. Likewise, it will guarantee the organization of employers. 8. The Government will encourage the creation of workers' organizations, and employers, in accordance with the law; and will promote its democratic functioning, participatory and transparent with alternation in direction." 2) Labor law (Código del Tranajo), Article 440, which states that, "Freedom of association.- Workers and employers, without any distinction and without need prior authorization, have the right to establish professional associations or unions that they deem appropriate, to join them or to withdraw from them, with observance of the law and the statutes of the respective associations." 3) Organic Law of Human Mobility Article 46, which states that, "Right to participation and social organization.- Foreigners will have the right to form social organizations to exercise their rights and carry out activities that allow their integration and participation in society in accordance with the regulations in force, as long as they do not disturb the peace or public order."

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to access criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in Article 11 of the Organic Criminal Code, which states that, "if the victim is of a nationality other than Ecuadorian, his or her temporary or permanent stay within the national territory will be permitted, for humanitarian and personal reasons, in accordance with the conditions of the national system of protection and assistance of victims, witnesses and others participants in the criminal process."

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to immigration status or relief from expulsion.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in Article 11.12 of the Organic Criminal Code.

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: Nationa law in Ecuador protects this right in 1) Articles 2, 3.16, 3.17, 3.18, 3.19, 21, 39, 52A, 94, 99, 113, 129, 129A, 137, of the Organic Law of Human Mobility. Article 2 states, "Within the framework of the best interests of child, in all processes and procedures related to human mobility the rules provided for this Law will be obeyed, such asthe principle of specialty of childhood and the rights to have a family, family reunification and the opportunity to be heard in all procedures that affect them. In no case may be ordered detention against a child for administrative immigration offenses. When the best interests of the child demands, the imperative of non-deprivation of liberty will extend to their parents, however, other measures may be adopted to the alternative measures that may be dictated in the control migratory." 2) Regulations of the Organic Law of Human Mobility (march 28, 2023), Articles: 155,159, 160, 170, 202, 203, 214, 215, 229. 3) The ecision No. 2120-19-JP/21 from the Constitutional Court of Ecuador, which established standards for a special procedure to identify the protection needs of children who migrate alone or are separated from their parents.

question_text_en: Right of women migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in 1) Articles 20.A, 21, 52A of the Organic Law of Human Mobility. Article 20.A states that, "rights ofpeople and groups of priority attention.-Older adults, girls, boys and adolescents, pregnant women, people with disabilities, those who suffer from catastrophic or highly complex diseases, inhuman mobility, will receive priority and specialized care. Likewise, those people who are at risk, whether victims of domestic and sexual violence, child abuse, human trafficking and trafficking ofmigrants, paying special attention to people in double status vulnerability, they will have prior attention." 2) Law to prevent and Eradicate Violence against women, articles 4 and 4.11. 3) Constitutional Court issued ruling 2185-19-JP/21, in which it developed standards for the protection of adolescent mothers and their children.

question_text_en: Rights of migrants with disabilities to special protection.
citation_text_en: National law in Ecuador protects this right in 1) Articles 20.A, 21, 52A, 136 of the Organic Law of Human Mobility. Article 20.A states that, "rights ofpeople and groups of priority attention.-Older adults, girls, boys and adolescents, pregnant women, people with disabilities, those who suffer from catastrophic or highly complex diseases, inhuman mobility, will receive priority and specialized care. Likewise, those people who are at risk, whether victims of domestic and sexual violence, child abuse, human trafficking and trafficking ofmigrants, paying special attention to people in double status vulnerability, they will have prior attention." 2) The decision No. 2496-21-EP/23 from the Constitutional Court of Ecuador, which establishes protection parameters for unaccompanied migrant children with mental disabilities.

citation_text_en: [1]: Jetu Edosa; [2]: Tadesse Kassa Woldetsadik (for backcoded questions: Abiy Ashenafi)

question_text_en: What country are you coding?
citation_text_en: Ethiopia

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to vote in local and/or regional elections.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. While the Constitution of Ethiopia, Article 30, states that "every person has the right to freedom of association for any cause or purpose," However, the National Refugee Proclamation No 1110/2019, and Ethiopian Political Parties Proclamation, article 2(13) & 3(2) that implement constitutional protections for migrants specifically limit their ability to participate in political activities.

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to stand for election.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. According to Article 38 of the Constitution of Ethiopia, "every Ethiopian national, without any discrimination based on colour, race, nation, nationality, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion or other status, has the following rights: (a) To take part in the conduct of public affairs, directly and through freely chosen representatives; (b) On the attainment of 18 years of age, to vote in accordance with law."

question_text_en: Right to equal protection of the law before courts.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in 1) the Constitution of Ethiopia, Article 25, and 37. Article 25 states that, "all persons are equal before the law and are entitled without any discrimination to the equal protection of the law." Article 37 of the Constitution states that everyone has the right to bring a judicial matter to the court, and to obtain a decision or judgment by a court of law or any other competent body with judicial power. 2) The Refugee Proclamation No. 1110/2019, Article 30(1)(2) states that every recognized refugee and asylum seeker shall have the same right as nationals in regard to bringing any judicial matter to a court, and to obtain a decision or judgment by the court or any other competent body with judicial power.

question_text_en: Right to government-provided counsel in proceedings related to migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for migrants as the right does not exist for citizens. However, according to the Refugee Proclamation No. 1110/2019 article 30 sub article 1, every recognized refugee or asylum-seeker may have access to legal counseling or assistance.

question_text_en: Right to government-provided interpretation in criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in 1) the Constitution of Ethiopia, Article 20(7), provides accused persons with the right to request the assistance of an interpreter at the states expense when court proceedings are conducted in a language they do not understand. 2) The Criminal Procedure Code of 1961, Articl 27(4), which stipulates that any arrested person interrogated by a police officer shall have the right to be supplied by a competent interpreter when he cannot understand the language in which his answers in interrogations are recoded. 3) The Refugee Proclamation No. 1110/2019, Article 30(2), which establishes the right of every recognized refugee or asylum seeker to have access to legal counseling and assistance -- the latter comprising their right to attain a government appointed interpreter for criminal proceedings.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from prosecution for unauthorized entry.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Article 243 of the Penal Code 2004 on "unlawful departure, entry or residence" provides that whoever intentionally "departs from, enters into or resides in the territory of the State in violation of the national law" is punishable with simple imprisonment or fine or with both. This does not include refugees or asylum seekers, though, according to Article 15 of the Refugee Proclamation No. 1110/2019 , "no criminal charge shall be commenced or continued or penalties be imposed against a person who has applied for refugee status or is about to apply pursuant to this Proclamation on account of his illegal entry and presence in the country (exemption because of possible status as refugee)." Article 20 of the Immigration Proclamation No.354/2003 stipulates that unless higher penalties are provided for in the Penal Code, any person who enters Ethiopia in violation of the law's provisions or who lives in Ethiopia without having a valid residence permit or who is an accomplice is punishable with imprisonment not exceeding three years or a fine not exceeding ten thousand Birror both-- which penalties may be raised up to four times.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to public adult education institutions.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Under both the Agency for Government Houses Establishment Proclamation No.555/2007 and the Federal Housing Corporation Establishment Council of Ministers Regulation No.398/2017, migrants, including refugees, have no access to public houses; such opportunities are confined to government officials and civil servants.

question_text_en: Right of access to public adult education institutions regardless of status.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right for refugees and asylum seekers in the Refugee Proclamation No. 1110/2019, Article 24(1). According to article 24, "access to education" is provided in sub-article 1, which states that, "every recognized refugee or asylum-seeker shall receive the same treatment as accorded to Ethiopian nationals with respect to access to pre-primary and primary education."

question_text_en: Right to be free from discrimination on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in Article 24(2) of the Refugee Proclamation No 1110/2019, which states that, "every recognized refugee and asylum-seeker may have access to secondary education; higher education; technical and vocation education and training; and adult and non-formal education within available resources and subject to the education policy of Ethiopia."

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after convictions.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia stipulates that criminal convictions can lead to loss of residence status in the Immigration Council of Ministers Regulation No. 114/2004, Article 30(2). Article 30 states that residence permits can only revoked, "where it is found to have been obtained by presenting false evidence. A permanent residence permit may be revoked if a migrant is convicted for a criminal offences. Criminal Code: Article 149.- "Withdrawal of Official Papers.Where special reasons, relating to supervision or safety require, the Court may in addition order the temporary retention or withdrawal of the official papers or passport of the convicted person. The reasons for such a measure and its duration shall be stated in the judgment." Article 150: "Prohibition from Residing in the Territory; Expulsion, (1) If the convicted person is an alien and proves to be undesirableor dangerous the Court may order expulsion from the territory of the State either temporarily or permanently.This measure may always be ordered in respect to a convicted person who has been sentenced to a term of simple imprisonment of three years or more, or to an irresponsible or partially responsible criminal recognized by expert opinion as a danger to public order." Under Article 8(1) of Refugee Proclamation No.1110/2019, a refugee status may be cancelled/revoked if it becomes known after status decision that he had committed serious crimes (against peace, humanity, serious nonpolitical crimes, or acts contrary to purposes of the UN and African Union).

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of torture or inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in Article 18 of the Ethiopian Constitution, which states that, "1. Everyone has the right to protection against cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. 2. No one shall be held in slavery or servitude." Additionally, the Refugee Proclamation No. 1110/2019, Article 11, only bans refoulement if the migrant's life, physical integrity or liberty would be threatened on account of external aggression, occupation, foreign domination or events seriously disturbing public order in part or whole of the country.

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of persecution.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right 1) in the Refugee Proclamation No. 1110/2019, Article 11(1)(a). According to Article 11, "(1) No person shall be refused entry in to Ethiopia or expelled or returned from Ethiopia to any other country or be subject to any similar measure if as a result of such refusal, expulsion or return or any other measure, such person is compelled to return to or remain in a country where: a) he may be subject to persecution on account of his race, religion, nationality, membership of a particular social group or political opinion: or (b) his life, physical integrity or liberty would be threatened on account of external aggression, occupation, foreign domination or events seriously disturbing public order in part or whole of the country."

question_text_en: Right to not return to a deprivations of fundamental human rights.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in 1) the Refugee Proclamation No. 1110/2019, Article 11. According to Article 11, "(1) No person shall be refused entry in to Ethiopia or expelled or returned from Ethiopia to any other country or be subject to any similar measure if as a result of such refusal, expulsion or return or any other measure, such person is compelled to return to or remain in a country where: a) he may be subject to persecution on account of his race, religion, nationality, membership of a particular social group or political opinion: or (b) his life, physical integrity or liberty would be threatened on account of external aggression, occupation, foreign domination or events seriously disturbing public order in part or whole of the country."

question_text_en: Right to be advised of availability of asylum before expulsion.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from chain refoulement.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Article 11 of Refugee Proclamation 1110/2019 on 'non-forceful repatriation’ only governs situations when a person may be refused entry or expelled or returned from Ethiopia to any other country. It makes no reference to risk scenarios emanating from subsequent or secondary expulsion. The same holds true when deportation measures are carried out as per Article 8 of the Immigration Proclamation No.354/2003.

question_text_en: Right to protection against expulsion except following a legal judgment.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in 1) the Immigration Proclamation No. 354/2003, Article 8-9. Article 8 and 9 of Immigration Proclamation No.354/2003 state that the government may take such measures only on basis of grounds clearly specified under the law, that the deportation decision must specify the reasons and date of departure, and includes that the foreigner/migrant aggrieved by such decision may also submit a petition to a higher body other than the implementing Agency. 2) The Refugee Proclamation No 1110/2019, Article 12 which stipulates that the government can expel a recognized refugee on the grounds of national security or public order only when such order is reached 'in accordance with due process of law', that is 'communicated to the refugee in writing' along with the specific reasons, and that the refugee is given the opportunity to challenge the order.

question_text_en: Right to submit reasons against expulsion and have case reviewed before deportation.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in 1) the Immigration Proclamation No. 354/2003, Article 9, which states that, “a foreigner who is aggrieved by a deportation order issued by the Authority may submit a petition against the order to the Grievance Hearing Committee, composed of representatives of the Ministry of justice and representatives of the Authority, within three working days from the date of receipt of the deportation order." 2) The Refugee Proclamation No 1110/2019, Article 16.4, which states that “any asylum-seeker who is aggrieved by the decision of the Agency may, within sixty days of being notified of such a decision, appeal in writing to the Appeal Hearing Council established in accordance with this Proclamation.”

question_text_en: Right of settled migrants to family reunification.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. National law of Ethiopia provides that a migrant child or adult can apply to acquire nationality under Article 5, subarticle 7 of the Ethiopian Nationality Proclamation No. 378/2003.

question_text_en: Right to judicial remedy for denials of right to family reunification.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right only for refugees and asylum seekers in 1) the Refugee Proclamation No 1110/2019, Article 14.5 According to Article 14.5, " the Agency shall facilitate reunification when requests are made by recognized refugees or asylum-seekers to reunify with their family members within Ethiopia." 2) Immigration Council of Ministers Regulation No. 114/2004, Article 17, Immigrant Visa: Immigrant visas shall be issued to the following: (1) Foreigners who have been adopted by Ethiopians or who have valid marriages with Ethiopians and are coming to reside in Ethiopia, and to members of their families.

question_text_en: Right to recognition of same-sex marital relationships.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right for refugees in the Refugee Proclamation No 1110/2019, Article 30. Articles 30 establishes that asylum-seekers, and refugees have the right to seek judicial remedy when they feel the right to family reunification has been violated.

question_text_en: Right to family reunification without resource conditions
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The Revised Family Code Proclamation No213/2000, Article 5 only recognizes foreign marriages as valid in Ethiopia so long as it does not contravene public morals. Same-sex relations are criminalized under Article 629 of the Penal Code of 2004 on ‘Homosexual and other Indecent Acts’ which states that "whoever performs with another person of the same sex a homosexual act, or any other indecent act, is punishable with simple imprisonment."

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in the Immigration Council of Ministers Regulation No. 114/2004 Article 16. Article 16 provides list of conditions for issuance of Business visa which includes the following: "A Business visa shall be issued to foreigners who are coming to Ethiopia: (a) for investment activities; (b) without prejudice to the provisions of the relevant law concerning work permits, for employment in any activity; (c) for various activities to be carried out in accordance with an agreement entered into with a foreign government, an international or regional organization or non-governmental organization; (d) for humanitarian service without remuneration; (e) for participation in symposia, exhibitions, workshops and similar activities to be held in Ethiopia or for giving a training; (f) for study and research; (g) for mass media activities."

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services regardless of status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right of access to public housing programs.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in 1) the Constitution of Ethiopia, Article 42(2). 2) The Labour Proclamation No. 1156/2019, Article 4, and 14(1)(f), Article 139. According to Article 4(5), "the contract of employment shall not laydown less favorable conditions for the employee than those provided for by law, collective agreement or work rules." In strict legal terms, migrant workers with work permits have the right to redress if the terms of their employment contract have been violated by their employer under Article 139 of the same proclamation. 3) The Refugee Proclamation No. 1110/2019. Article 26.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to free primary education for migrant children.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right for migrants with refugee status and asylum seekers in Article 25 of the Refugee Proclamation No. 1110/2019 which guarantees access to health services depending on whether the migrant is an asylum seeker/recognized refugees. It states that "every recognized refugee and asylum seeker shall have access to available health services in Ethiopia."

question_text_en: Right to equal pay for the same work.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. According to Article 38 of the Constitution of Ethiopia, "every Ethiopian national, without any discrimination based on colour, race, nation, nationality, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion or other status, has the following rights: (a) To take part in the conduct of public affairs, directly and through freely chosen representatives; (b) On the attainment of 18 years of age, to vote in accordance with law."

question_text_en: Right to freedom of choice of employment.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in 1) the Constitution of Ethiopia, Article 25, which states that "all persons are equal before the law and are entitled without any discrimination to the equal protection of the law," and furthermore establishes that "in this respect, the law shall guarantee to all persons equal and effective protection without discrimination on grounds of race, nation, nationality, or other social origin, color, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, property, birth or other status." 2) The Refugee Proclamation No 1110/2019, Article 4, states that refugees should be treated "without discrimination as to race, religion, nationality, membership of a particular social group, political opinion or other similar grounds."

question_text_en: Right of spouse/partner of principal migrant to work.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in 1) the Constitution of Ethiopia, Article 25, which states that "all persons are equal before the law and are entitled without any discrimination to the equal protection of the law," and furthermore establishes that "in this respect, the law shall guarantee to all persons equal and effective protection without discrimination on grounds of race, nation, nationality, or other social origin, color, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, property, birth or other status." 2) The Refugee Proclamation No 1110/2019, Article 4, states that refugees should be treated "without discrimination as to race, religion, nationality, membership of a particular social group, political opinion or other similar grounds."

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after loss of employment.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in 1) the Constitution, Article 42(2), which states that "workers have the right to reasonable limitation of working hours, to rest, to leisure, to periodic leaves with pay, to remuneration for public holidays as well as healthy and safe work environment." The Constitution also makes no distinction between nationality statuses of workers and hence permits no discrimination in wages. 2) The Labour Proclamation No. 1156/2019, Article 14(1)(f), which prohibits employers from discriminating between workers on the basis of ethnicity, sex, religion, political outlook, HIV/AIDS disablement, or any other grounds (any other grounds has been interpreted to include nationality status). 3) The Refugee Proclamation No. 1110/2019, Article 26, which states that "recognized refugees and asylum-seekers shall have the right to engage in wage earning employment in the same circumstance as the most favorable treatment accorded to foreign nationals pursuant to relevant laws."

question_text_en: Right to equal employment conditions and protection.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in 1) the Labour Proclamation No. 1156/2019, Article 176, states that specifically requires any foreigner/migrant to first obtain work permit before s/he engages in any type of work in Ethiopia. Article 176 provides that any foreigner may only be employed in any type of work in Ethiopia when he possesses a work permit, given for employment in a specific type of work for three years, renewed every year, and revoked when the Ministry ascertains that the foreigner is no longer required for the work (because the position can be covered by an Ethiopian replacement). 2) The Refugee Proclamation No 1110/2019, Article 26(1), states that "recognized refugees and asylum-seekers shall have the right to engage in wage-earning employment in the same circumstance as the most favorable treatment accorded to foreign nationals pursuant to relevant laws." In this case, this means investors, so only self-employment is guaranteed.

question_text_en: Right to form trade unions and other associations.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia provides limited protections for this right in 1) the Refugee Proclamation No 1110/2019 under Article 26(9), which states that "restrictive measures imposed, by applicable laws, on employment of foreign nationals for the protection of the national labor market shall not be applicable to recognized refugee or asylum seeker who is married to Ethiopian national or has one or more child in possession of Ethiopian nationality." 2) The Directive to Determine the Procedure for Refugees Right to Work Directive No. 02/2019, Article 16(3). Article 16(3) states that "a refugee or asylum seeker who is legally married to an Ethiopian national or has one or more child in possession of Ethiopian nationality may be employed without having to obtain a work permit." Sub article 4 establishes conditions stating that; (a) where his right to work ensues from marriage, the validity of the marriage and the registration of the marriage certificate shall be verified by the Agency; (b) where his right to work ensues from his minor child, proof of the child’s Ethiopian nationality shall be produced; or (c) When the refugee obtains a letter from the Agency confirming that he can work without a work permit on the basis of a procedure set by the Agency. However, it should be noted that according to Article 22, Investment Proclamation No. 1180/2020, "(1) any investor may employ duly qualified foreigners necessary for the operation of his investment in positions of higher management, supervision, trainers and other technical professions. However, foreigners may be employed only when it can be ascertained that Ethiopians possessing similar qualification or experience required by the sector are not available...(3) A work permit may be issued to a cohabiting spouse of any investor and a foreign worker employed pursuant to Sub-article (1) of this Article. (4) An investor who employs foreigners pursuant to Sub-article (1) of this Article shall be responsible for replacing, within a limited period of time, such foreign workers by Ethiopians by arranging and providing the necessary training."

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to redress before deportation or withdrawal of residency permit.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in Article 22(6) of the Investment Proclamation No. 1180/2020, which states that "where it is ascertained that a foreign worker is no longer required for the position he is employed, the Commission [Ethiopian Investment Commission] may decide not to renew or to cancel the work permit." When a work permit is cancelled or not renewed it means that employment status is lost, and that will result in the loss of immigration status unless a new job is found within a specific time.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to social security protections.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in 1) the Constitution of Ethiopia, Aticle 42(2), whcih provides that "workers have the right to reasonable limitation of working hours, to rest, to leisure, to periodic leaves with pay, to remuneration for public holidays as well as healthy and safe work environment." 2) The Labour Proclamation No. 1156/2019, Article 14(1)(f). 3) The Refugee Proclamation No. 1110/2019, Article 26, which states that "recognized refugees and asylum-seekers shall have the right to engage in wage earning employment in the same circumstance as the most favorable treatment accorded to foreign nationals pursuant to relevant laws."

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to become lawfully settled.
citation_text_en: National law of Ethiopia protects this right in 1) the Labour Proclamation No 1156/2019, Articles 85-112. Article 88.1 states that migrants with work permits have the right to social security protections commensurate with citizens. Article 88.1 also provides the right to maternity leave and states that "an employer shall grant leave to a pregnant worker with pay, for medical examination connected with her pregnancy, provided, however, that she may be required to present a medical certificate of her examination." Article 85 also entitles "a worker, who completed his probation period and who is rendered incapable of working due to sickness other than employment injury to a sick leave." Article 96 requires the employer to be "liable, irrespective of fault, for employment injuries sustained by his worker and such liability shall be determined in accordance with, the provisions of this Chapter." Article 95 defines "occupational injury" as "an employment accident or occupational disease." Additionally, Article 99 defines occupational disablement as "any employment injury as a consequence of which there is a decrease or loss of capacity to work." Finally, Articles 100-112 provides various packages and conditions of disability payments which also applies to migrant workers with work permits in the same way as nationals.

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to settle regardless of initial status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The Private Organization Employees Pension Proclamation No. 715/2011, Article 2 Sub-Article 7 defines 'benefit' as 'retirement pension, invalidity pension, incapacity pension or survivors pension and includes gratuity and the refundable pension contribution.' Similarly, the Public Servants' Pension Proclamation No. 714/2011, Article 2 Sub-Article 14 defines 'benefit' as 'retirement pension, invalidity pension, incapacity pension or survivors pension and includes gratuity and the refundable pension contribution.' Thus, there is no such a thing as an unemployment benefit in Ethiopia given in any form.

question_text_en: Right to redress following employer breach of employment contract.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in 1) the Immigration Council of Ministers' Regulation No 114/2004 Article 28, whcih regulates the ‘Permanent Residence Permit’. In sub article(1) it stipulates that ‘a permanent residence permit shall be issued to a foreigner who has entered Ethiopia by an immigrant visa as provided for in Sub-Article(1) or (2) of Article 17 of this Regulation. (2) Without prejudice to Sub-Article (1) of this Article, a permanent residence permit maybe issued to any foreigner who has: (a) established his domicile in Ethiopia and lived in Ethiopia for at least three years preceding the submission of his application; (b) sufficient and lawful source of income to maintain himself and his family; and (c) good character. Whether temporary or permanent, a migrant can engage in a work in Ethiopia only if she or he possesses work permit issued by the relevant agency of the government as per the Labor Proclamation No.1156/2019. His/her background notwithstanding, such a person issued with a work permit may then apply for registration as a foreigner (defined in the Immigration Proclamation No 354/2003 as "any person who is not an Ethiopian national") and receive a residence permit (Immigration Regulation No.114/2005 Article 26 and 27). In practice, this avenue applies mainly to migrants with high qualifications and is not meant to cater situations such as temporary migrant workers.

question_text_en: Right not to have identity documents confiscated.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in Article 12 of Proclamation no. 1178/202, which states that: "Whosoever having a license to provide overseas employment services receives money or materials from the worker in consideration of the employment services; withholds or refuses to return an identity card, passport, travel documents or any other document of the worker without his consent either before or after the worker engaged in work [...] shall be punishable considering the circumstances of the case with rigorous imprisonment from three years to seven years and fine from Thirty Thousand to Seventy Thousand Birr"

question_text_en: Right to birth registration.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in 1) the Registration of Vital Events and National Identity Card Proclamation No. 760/2012cum, Article 18(2). According to Article 18(2) of Registration of Vital Events and National Identity Card Proclamation No. 760/2012, any birth shall be registered within 90 days following the date of its occurrence unless there is sufficient cause for delay. 2) The Vital Events Registration and National Identity Card proclamation (amendment)Proclamation No 1049/2017, Article 2(2). According to Article 2(2) of Vital Events Registration and National Identity Card proclamation (amendment) Proclamation No 1049/2017, this legal requirement is applicable to any Ethiopian or foreigner found in Ethiopia. Pursuant to Article 2(2) of Registration of Vital Events and National Identity Card Proclamation No. 760/2012, a “vital event”means a birth, marriage, divorce or death, and includes adoption, and acknowledgement and judicial declaration of paternity. 3) The Refugee Proclamation No. 1110/2019cum, Article 36. Article 36 of the Refugee Proclamation No. 1110/2019 provides that Every refugee or asylum-seeker shall be treated in the same circumstances as nationals with respect to the registration and issuance of certificate of registration of vital events in accordance with applicable laws.

question_text_en: Right to government document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in 1) the Refugee Proclamation No. 1110/2019, Article 26, 32, 32(1). Article 32(1) of Refugee Proclamation No. 1110/2019 provides that every recognized refugee or asylum seeker shall be issued with identity papers attesting to their identity. 2) The Immigration Proclamation No. 354/2003, Articl 13(1). According to Article 13(1) of Immigration Proclamation No. 354/2003, all foreigners shall be registered; and those who get registered shall be required to obtain a temporary or permanent residence permit. 3) The Definition of Powers and Duties of the Executive Organs Proclamation No. 1263/2021, Article 25(1)(p). Article 25(1)(p) of Definition of Powers and Duties of the Executive Organs Proclamation No. 1263/2021 mandates the Ministry of Labor and Skills to issue work permits to foreign nationals.

question_text_en: Right against destruction of document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to communicate with consular officials.
citation_text_en: There is no such obligation under domestic, migrant-specific law. However, Ethiopia has aceded to the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations on 22 Mar 1979, and according to Art 9.4 of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopian Constitution (1995): "All international agreements ratified by Ethiopia are an integral part of the law of the land," Article 36 of the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations has not been domesticated. Therefore, there is no law that mandates the right to communication. This obligation is derived from the Vienna Convention, read in conjunction with article 9(4) of the Constitution. Moreover, Article 21(2) of the Ethiopian (FDRE) Constitution 1995 broadly guarantees that "all persons held in custody shall have the opportunity to communicate with, and be visited by, their spouses or partners, close relatives, friends, religious councilors, medical doctors and their legal counsel."

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: The Immigration Proclamation No. 354/2003. art 16.2.1.c states that, "immigration officers shall have the power to detain for investigation (i)any person who is attempting to enter or depart from Ethiopia; or (ii) any foreigner residing in Ethiopia in violation of the requirements hereof or of any Regulations issued hereunder." The aforementioned law does not distinguish between minor migrants and others when it comes to detention. As a principle, migrants are required to carry a 'migrant visa' under the conditions provided under the law. Although the Immigration Proclamation gives immigration officers to detain any person for investigation, this includes Ethiopian nationals, and it is not based on a migrant's migrant status per se.

question_text_en: Right of migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for all migrants. Immigration Proclamation No. 354/2003. art 16.2.1.c states that: "immigration officers shall have the power to detain for investigation (i) any person who is attempting to enter or depart from Ethiopia; or (ii) any foreigner residing in Ethiopia in violation of the requirements hereof or of any Regulations issued hereunder." It should be noted however that Article 15(8) of Refugee Proclamation No. 1110/2019 provides that no refugee may be criminally charged or subjected to penalties on account of illegal entry or presence in Ethiopia. Article 28(2) of Prevention and Suppression of Trafficking in Persons and Smuggling of Migrants Proclamation No. 909/2015 similarly provides that any foreign national who is victim of trafficking in persons and smuggling of migrants shall not be criminally liable on his illegal entry into Ethiopian territory. These rules have been interpreted to prohibit detention of refugees, victims of trafficking, and smuggled migrants on the basis of their status as a migrant.

question_text_en: Right to appeal legality, conditions, and length of detention
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in 1) the Immigration Proclamation No. 354/2003, Article 9. 2) The Refugee Proclamation No. 1110/2019, Articles 12-13. 3) The Federal Constitution of Ethiopia (FDRE), Article 19(3), which protects the right to challenge detention, its length or the conditions of detention.

question_text_en: Right to an individualized detention decision.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in Immigration Proclamation No. 354/2003, Article 8(3), 16(2), and 16(3). Particularly, Article 16(3) states that “Any person detained by an Immigration Officer pursuant to the provisions of Sub-Article (2) (c) of this Article shall be brought to the competent court without delay in accordance with the law.”

question_text_en: Right to be free from torture and inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in 1) the Federal Constitution of Ethiopia, Articles 17-18. According to Article 17, the Right to Liberty, "(1) No one shall be deprived of his or her liberty except on such grounds and in accordance with such procedure as are established by law. (2) No person may be subjected to arbitrary arrest, and no person may be detained without a charge or conviction against him." Additionally, Article 18: the Prohibition against Inhuman Treatment, states "(1) Everyone has the right to protection against cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. (2) No one shall be held in slavery or servitude. Trafficking in human beings for whatever purpose is prohibited." 2) The Refugee Proclamation No. 1110/2019, Article 22 guarantees the aforementioned rights to migrants.

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in the 1) Refugees Proclamation No. 1110/2019, Article 11. Article 11 protects migrants from 'Forceful Repatriation'. In sub-article 1, it provides that 'no person shall be refused entry in to Ethiopia or expelled or returned from Ethiopia to any other country or be subject to any similar measure...' However, because the Criminal Code criminalizes unlawful entry into the country (Art icle 243(1)(a)), law enforcement organs may, in practice, use force to enforce this provision should a person who entered into the country refuse to comply with their orders.

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of lethal force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protect this right in the Refugees Proclamation No. 1110/2019, Article 11. Article protects migrants from 'Forceful Repatriation'. In sub-article 1, it provides that 'no person shall be refused entry in to Ethiopia or expelled or returned from Ethiopia to any other country or be subject to any similar measure...' However, because the Criminal Code criminalizes unlawful entry into the country (Art 243(1)(a)),law enforcement organs may, in practice, use force to enforce this provision should a person who entered into the country refuse to comply with their orders. That being said, officers and agents are not authorized to use lethal force merely to prevent migrants from entering Ethiopian territory.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from trafficking or smuggling.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in 1) Prevention and Suppression of Trafficking in Persons and Smuggling of Persons Proclamation No. 1178/2020, Articles 3 and 8.

question_text_en: Right to maintain citizenship status after convictions.
citation_text_en: National law of Ethiopia protects this right in the Ethiopian Nationality Proclamation No. 378/2003. Accoridng to the proclamation, a criminal conviction or any other conviction is not grounds for loss of nationality/citizenship, but can result in denial of citizenship or nationality.

question_text_en: Right of economic migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in 1) the Ethiopian Nationality Proclamation No. 378/2003, Articles 4-12. According to Article 5.2: a foreigner who applies to acquire Ethiopian nationality by law shall have established his domicile in Ethiopia and have lived in Ethiopia for a total of at least four years preceding the submission of his application. In, theory, this applies to any and all migrants. There are also very exceptional cases such as marriage to an Ethiopian national, adoption and outstanding contribution that are listed as grounds for the grant of Ethiopian nationality in Article 6,7,8 of Proclamation on Ethiopian Nationality No.378/2003)

question_text_en: Right of humanitarian migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right, in Ethiopian Nationality Proclamation No. 378/2003, Article 4. According to Article 4, "any foreigner may acquire Ethiopian nationality by law in accordance with the provisions of Articles 5-12 of this Proclamation." Article 5.2 states that, "A foreigner who applies to acquire Ethiopian nationality By law shall:have established his domicile in Ethiopia and have lived in Ethiopia for a total of at least four years preceding the submission of his application."

question_text_en: Right of family migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in 1) the Ethiopian Nationality Proclamation No. 378/2003, Article 4-13. Article 6 states that "a foreigner who is married to an Ethiopian national may acquire Ethiopian nationality by law if: the marriage is concluded in accordance with the Ethiopian laws or in accordance with the laws of any other country where the marriage is contracted; there is a lapse of at least two years since the conclusion of the marriage; he has lived in Ethiopia for at least one year preceding the submission of his application; and he fulfilled the conditions stated under Sub-Articles (1), (7)and (8) of Article 5 of this Proclamation. Article 7 deals with caes of adoption, and states, a child adopted by Ethiopian National may acquire Ethiopian nationality by law if: (1) he has not attained the age of majority; (2)he lives in Ethiopia together with his adopting parent; (3)Where one of his adopting parents is a foreigner, such parent has expressed his consent in writing; and (4) the condition stated under Article 5(7) of this Proclamation has been fulfilled." Article 9 deals primarily with naturalized perions, and states, "(1) A person who has acquired Ethiopian Nationality by law may apply for the his minor child living with him in Ethiopia; provided, however, that where the applicant is the only naturalized parent, the consent of both parents shall be required for naturalization of the child. (2) A child whose application for naturalization has been submitted in accordance with Sub-Article (l) of this Article shall be conferred with Ethiopian nationality where the applicant is able to show that the child is released from his previous nationality or the possibility of obtaining such release." 2) The National Refugee Proclamation No 1110/2019, Article 42, which states that "every recognized refugee or asylum-seeker who fulfills the necessary requirements provided in the relevant provisions of the Ethiopian Nationality Law relating to naturalization may apply to acquire Ethiopian Nationality bylaw."

question_text_en: Right to dual nationality.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. According to Ethiopian Nationality Proclamation No. 378/2003, Article 5.7, "a foreigner who applies to acquire Ethiopian nationality by law shall be able to show that he has been released from his previous nationality or the possibility of obtaining such a release upon the acquisition of Ethiopian nationality or that he is a stateless person."

question_text_en: Right to freedom to hold opinion.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in 1) the Constitution of Ethiopia, Article 27(1). According to Article 27(1), "everyone (migrants included on equal basis as citizens) has the right to freedom of thought, conscience and religion. This right shall include the freedom to hold or to adopt a religion or belief of his choice, and the freedom, either individually or in community with others, and in public or private, to manifest his religion or belief in worship, observance, practice and teaching." 2) The Refugee Proclamation No 1110/2019, Article 22 also recognizes ‘every recognized refugee and asylum-seeker: (1) is entitled to the rights and be subjected to the obligations contained in the Refugee Convention, the OAU Refugee Convention and applicable international laws. One of such rights so recognized is the right to religion under Article 4 of the Refugee Convention which obliges the Contracting States to accord to refugees within their territories treatment at least as favourable as that accorded to their nationals with respect to freedom to practice their religion and freedom as regards the religious education of their children.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of expression.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in the Constitution of Ethiopia, Article 29. Article 29 recognizes that "(1.) everyone has the right to hold opinions without interference which shall include freedom to seek, receive and impart information and ideas of all kinds, regardless of frontiers, either orally, in writing or in print, in the form of art, or through any media of his choice."

question_text_en: Right to freedom of association.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in the Constitution of Ethiopia, Article 29. Article 29 recognizes that "(1.) everyone has the right to hold opinions without interference which shall include freedom to seek, receive and impart information and ideas of all kinds, regardless of frontiers, either orally, in writing or in print, in the form of art, or through any media of his choice."

question_text_en: Right to freedom of assembly.
citation_text_en: National law protects this right in the Constitution of Ethiopia, Article 31, which states that "every person has the right to freedom of association for any cause or purpose." The National Refugee Proclamation No 1110/2019, Article 27, states that "recognized refugees and asylum-seekers have the right to association, as regards to non-political and non-profit making associations and trade unions in the same circumstances as the most favorable treatment accorded to foreign nationals pursuant to relevant laws."

category: Thought, conscience, and religion or belief
question_text_en: Right of freedom of thought, conscience and religion or belief.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. According to the Immigration Council of Ministers Regulation No. 114/2004, Article 17: "Immigrant visas shall be issued to the following: (3) Foreigners coming to reside in Ethiopia without either being engaged in any gainful activities or becoming public burden, and to members of their families." However, Article 14 of the Refugee Proclamation 1110/2019, establishes the right of an asylum-seekers and recognized refugees to have his/her families united with him/her, but does not mention any preconditions for the exercise of such a right.

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to access criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in 1) the Constitution of Ethiopia, Article 37, which provides that everyone has the right to bring a judicial matter to, and to obtain a decision or judgment from a court of law or any other competent body with judicial power. This constitutional protection is universally applicable. 2) The Refugee Proclamation No. 1110/2019, Article 30(1)(2), which provides that every recognized refugee and asylum seeker shall have the same rights as nationals in regard to bringing any justiciable matter to, and to obtain a decision or judgment from the court or any other competent body with judicial power. This right of access to justice is applicable to both civil and criminal proceedings.

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to immigration status or relief from expulsion.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in Prevention and Suppression of Trafficking in Persons and Smuggling of Persons Proclamation No.1178/2020 Article 24(6). This article states that a victim who is a foreign national found in Ethiopia not having permanent residence permit shall receive appropriate support, including a temporary residence permit.

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in the 2) The Refugee Proclamation1110/2019, Article 38(2). Article 38 of the Refugee Proclamation states that 'recognized refugee and asylum-seeker children shall enjoy the rights and protections enshrined under relevant laws in particular; specific measures are taken to protect them from abuse, neglect, exploitation and trafficking.' 1) Article 36 of the Federal Constitution of Ethiopia; Article 36 provides legal protection to migrant children's right to life, to a name and nationality, to know their parents or legal guardians and to be cared for, not to be subjected to exploitative practices and corporal punishment. It also safeguards the principle of the 'best interests of the child' in decisions relating to children

question_text_en: Right of women migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in the Refugee Proclamation No. 1110/2019, Article 38(1). This provision states that 'recognized refugee and asylum seeker women shall enjoy the rights and protections enshrined under relevant laws. In particular, specific measures have to be taken to protect women from gender-based violence.'

question_text_en: Rights of migrants with disabilities to special protection.
citation_text_en: National law in Ethiopia protects this right in 1) Article 41 of the Federal Constitution of Ethiopia (FDRE), which states that the state, within its available means, must allocate resources to provide rehabilitation and assistance to physically and mentally disabled people, including migrants. 2) The Refugee Proclamation No. 1110/2019, Article 38(3) provides for 'special protection and assistance to refugees and asylum-seekers with specific needs.' Although disability is not explicitly mentioned in this provision, this provision has been interepreted to provide special protection to refugees and asylum seekers with disabilities.
