question_text_en: What country are you coding?
citation_text_en: Finland

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to vote in local and/or regional elections.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in Constitution 1999, Section 13, which states that "Everyone has the right to arrange meetings and demonstrations without a permit, as well as the right to participate in them."

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to stand for election.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland provides that being lawfully present creates a legal right for migrants to vote in local or regional elections in the Local Government Act 410/2015 chapter 5, Section 20, which states "Right to vote in local elections (1)Citizens of Finland or of other European Union Member States or Iceland or Norway who are at least 18 years old on the day of the election and whose municipality of residence as referred to in the Municipality of Residence Act is the municipality in question, according to information held in the Population Information System at the end of the 51st day before the election day, have the right tovote in local elections held in the municipality. Other foreigners meeting the requirements laid down above shall also have the right to vote in local elections if, at the time referred to, they have had a municipality of residence in Finland for two years."

question_text_en: Right to equal protection of the law before courts.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Constitution 1999, Section 21.

question_text_en: Right to government-provided counsel in proceedings related to migrant status.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Legal Aid Act, Section 21, which states that a person has a right to counsel at government expense if they reside permanently in Finland or their matter is processes in a Finnish court and they do not have the financial means to cover it themselves. Asylum seekers have a right to counsel throughout the process if they do not have the financial means to cover it themselves.

question_text_en: Right to government-provided interpretation in criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: Natioanl law in Finland protecs this right in the Criminal Procedure Act, Chapter 6a, Section 2(3), which states that, "A defendant or, in a case prosecuted by the prosecutor, an injured party who does not speak Finnish, Swedish or Sami has the right to cost-free interpretation in criminal proceedings. The court shall ex officio ensure that the defendant or the injured party receives the interpretation that he or she needs. (769/2013) (4) The court shall arrange for interpretation also when a party uses sign language or when interpretation is necessary due to a sensory or speaking impediment of a party."

question_text_en: Right to be protected from prosecution for unauthorized entry.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for all migrants. Though both trafficked migrants, and Asylum seekers are exempted from criminal sanctions, all other migrants can face imprisonment or fines for unauthorized entry. According to Penal Code 17:7, "A person who 1) crosses or attempts to cross the border of Finland without a valid travel document, visa, residence permit or other document equated with a travel document, or does so elsewhere than through a valid point of entry or departure, or in violation of a statutory prohibition other than an entry ban, 2) otherwise violates the provisions on border crossing, or 3) stays, moves or undertakes measures in the border zone in violation of section 51 of the Border Guard Act or without a permit required under section 52 of that Act shall be sentenced for a state border offence to a fine or imprisonment for at most one year."

question_text_en: Right to equal access to public adult education institutions.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for all migrants. However, permanent residents can access publicly supported housing based on the provisions found in the Act on the General Housing Allowance 2014, Section 2, and the Act on Residence Based Social Security in Crossborder Situations 2019, Sections 5, 7, 9 and 10.

question_text_en: Right of access to public adult education institutions regardless of status.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in 1) the Basic Education Act 1998, Sections 4, 31, and 32. 2) Constitution 1999, Section 16.

question_text_en: Right to be free from discrimination on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: National law conditionally protects this right based on visa type in 1) the Vocational Education and Training Act 2017, Section 38. 2) The Universities of Applied Sciences Act 2014, Section 25. 3) The Universities Act 2009, Sections 36 and 36a.

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after convictions.
citation_text_en: National law stipulates that only major convictions (e.g., criminal offenses) can lead to loss of residence status in the Aliens Act 2004, Sections 148 and 149. Section 148 states that, "(1) An alien may be denied admittance or stay if: 8) on the basis of an earlier sentence of imprisonment, or on other reasonable grounds, there is reason to suspect that he or she may commit an offence which is punishable by imprisonment in Finland, or there is reason to suspect that he or she may commit repeated offences; 9) he or she was sentenced for an offence during his or her stay in Finland." Section 149 states that, "An alien who has resided in Finland under a residence permit or who has lost Finnish citizenship may be deported if: 2) he or she is found guilty of an offence carrying a maximum sentence of imprisonment for a year or more, or if he or she is found guilty of repeated offences."

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of torture or inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in 1) the Constituion 1999, Section 9. 2) Aliens Act 2004, section 147, which states that, "No one may be denied admittance or stay and sent back, deported or, as a result of refusal of entry , returned to an area where he or she could be subject to the death penalty, torture, persecution or other treatment violating human dignity or from where he or she could be sent to such an area."

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of persecution.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in 1) the Aliens Act 2004, Section 147. 2) The Finnish Constitution, Section 9.4, which states that, "A foreigner shall not be deported, extradited or returned to anothe rcountry, if in consequence, he or she is in danger of a death sentence, torture or other treatment violating human dignity."

question_text_en: Right to not return to a deprivations of fundamental human rights.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to be advised of availability of asylum before expulsion.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. There is no obligation under the Aliens Act 2004 to inform an Asylum seeker that they have a right to request asylum.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from chain refoulement.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Aliens Act 2004, Section 147, which states that, "No one may be denied admittance or stay and sent back, deported or, as a result of refusal of entry, returned to an area where he or she could be subject to the death penalty, torture, persecution or other treatment violating human dignity or from where he or she could be sent to such an area."

question_text_en: Right to protection against expulsion except following a legal judgment.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Aliens Act 2004, Chapter 9, and sections 145 and 98 4). Section 145 states that, "an alien and his or her spouse or similar partner residing in Finland shall be provided with an opportunity to be heard in a matter related to refusal of entry, denial of admittance or stay, deportation or an entry ban concerning him or her." Section 98 4) states that, "(4) If the application is rejected, a decision on denial of admittance or stay or deportation is issued at the same time, unless special reasons have arisen for not making a decision on removing the applicant from the country."

question_text_en: Right to submit reasons against expulsion and have case reviewed before deportation.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Aliens Act 2004, Chapter 13, Section 190. According to Section 190, "(1)A decision of the Finnish Immigration Service, the police, a border control authority, an employment office, a Finnish mission or the Ministry of Education and Culture as referred to in this Act may be appealed against to an administrative court as provided in the Administrative Judicial Procedure Act. (850/2019) (2) A decision of the border control authority, the police or the Finnish Immigration Service to refuse entry under the Schengen Borders Code may be appealed against to an administrative court, as provided in the Administrative Judicial Procedure Act. (850/2019)."

question_text_en: Right of settled migrants to family reunification.
citation_text_en: No guarantee of citizenship for stateless migrants and children of stateless migrants. However, the law provides migrants with an application process citizenship, which can be granted on a case-by-case basis, in the Nationality Act Section 20:1 states "Exceptions pertaining to refugees and involuntarily stateless persons (1) An alien may be granted Finnish citizenship not withstanding section 13(1)(2) if: 1) he or she has refugee status in Finland, or a residence permit based on the need for protection or he or she is involuntarily stateless."

question_text_en: Right to judicial remedy for denials of right to family reunification.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland conditionally protects this right in the Aliens Act 2004, sections 37, 39, 114, and 115, which provides family reunification only for immediate family members (spouse, underaged children or parents of a minor) on condition that the family has sufficient financial resources.

question_text_en: Right to recognition of same-sex marital relationships.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Aliens Act 2004, Section 190.

question_text_en: Right to family reunification without resource conditions
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Aliens Act 2004, Section 37.

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services regardless of status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for all irregular migrants. However, according to Aliens Act Chapter 4, Section 52d, states that, "(1) A third-country national who is in Finland and has worked illegally is issued a temporary residence permit if he or she was residing in the country illegally during the period of work, and: 1) was a minor while working, or his or her work was performed under working conditions that indicate specific exploitation; 2) his or her residence in Finland is justified on account of a criminal investigation or court proceedings; 3) he or she is ready to cooperate with the authorities in apprehending suspected employers; and 4) he or she no longer has ties with any suspects in the crime. (2) Issuing the residence permit is not conditional on the alien having sufficient financial resources. (3) Family members of a person referred to in subsection 1 who are residing abroad are not issued a residence permit on the basis of family ties.(4) The provisions of section 52b apply to the reflection period granted to a person referred to ins ubsection 1, and the provisions of section 52c apply to deciding on the reflection period."

question_text_en: Right of access to public housing programs.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in 1) the Employment Contracts Act 2001, Chapter 12. 2) Penal Code Chapter 47.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to free primary education for migrant children.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right for permanent or continuous visa holders in 1) the Act on Organising Social and Health Care 2021, Section 2, 56 and 56a. The Act on Organising Social and Health Care protects this right for migrants who are permanently living in Finland, and additionally for most regular migrants (those who hold a EU blue card or is their family member; or who hold a permit based on intra-corporate transfer; or who are working or have worked in Finland for at least 6 months, who hold a residence permit of a temporary worker, researcher, student, trainee or voluntary worker). The Act also protects the right to essential heatlh care 2) Health Care Act 2010, Section 50, which provides for the right for emergency health care for all, including irregular migrants. Health care of irregular migrants happens fully at their own cost (aka differently from other residents, who only pay part of the costs of their care). 3) Municipality of Residence Act 201/1994, Section 4.

question_text_en: Right to equal pay for the same work.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland provides that being lawfully present creates a legal right for migrants to stand for for local or regional elections in the 1) Wellbeing Services Countries Act, 2021, Chapter 10. 2) The Local Government Act Chapter 10, Section 71, which states that "Persons eligible for election to a position of trust in a municipality are those: 1) whose municipality of residence is the municipality in question; 2) who, in the year when local councillors are being elected or when an election is being held for some other position of trust, have the right to vote in local elections in one of the municipalities; and 3) who have not been declared legally incompetent." Migrants must have a continuous residence of two years in the locality to be able to run for local or regional elections.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of choice of employment.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The Non-discrimination act (1325/2014) Chapter 3 section 8 does not explictly protect against discrimination based on migrant status.

question_text_en: Right of spouse/partner of principal migrant to work.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Non-Discrimination Act Chapter 3 section 8, which states that, "(1) No one may be discriminated against on the basis of age, origin, nationality, language, religion, belief, opinion, political activity, trade union activity, family relationships, state of health, disability, sexual orientation or other personal characteristics. Discrimination is prohibited, regardless of whether it is based on a fact or assumption concerning the person him/herself or another . (2) In addition to direct and indirect discrimination, harassment, denial of reasonable accommodation as well as an instruction or order to discriminate constitute discrimination as referred to in this Act."

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after loss of employment.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in 1) the Constitution 1999, Section 6. 2) Non-Discrimination Act Chapter 3 section 8 and Chapter 2 section 7.

question_text_en: Right to equal employment conditions and protection.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Aliens Act 2004, Sections 72, 73 and 74.

question_text_en: Right to form trade unions and other associations.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Aliens Act 2004, Section 81a. A family member has unlimited right to work if they are in Finland on a family-based residence permit.

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to redress before deportation or withdrawal of residency permit.
citation_text_en: The Aliens Act of Finland 2004, Section 54 decrees that a residence permit is renewed if the requirements under which the applicant was issued with the previous permit are still met. Section 58 decrees that a fixed-term residence permit may be withdrawn if the grounds on which the permit was issued no longer exist. Therefore, if the migrant who has been granted residence based on employment looses their work, their residence permit may be cancelled or not renewed.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to social security protections.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Constitution 1999, Sections 6, 7, and 8.

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to become lawfully settled.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland provides equal access to all types of social security protections after some period of time in 1) Act on Residence-based Social Security in Cross-border Situations, 2019. 2) The Municipality of Residence Act 1994, Section 4. As soon as a person becomes a permanent resident and is covered by the Finnish social security system, the eligibility rules for accessing social benefits are the same for citizens and non-citizens.

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to settle regardless of initial status.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right only for migrant workers with a permanent or continuous permit in the Unemployment Security Act, Chapter 2, Section 1. Temporary permit holders are specifically excluded in Chapter 2, Section 2.

question_text_en: Right to redress following employer breach of employment contract.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Aliens Act 2004, Sections 54.3, and 56. Section 54.3 states that, "An alien who has been issued with a temporary residence permit for employment or engaging in business activities under section 45(1) is issued with a continuous residence permit after two years of continuous residence in the country, if the requirements for issuing the permit are still met." In Finland, there are three types of residence permits: temporary, continuous, and permanent. Migrants residing in Finland with a temporary permit are not able to get the permanent permit, but - if the right conditions are met - they are able to switch to a continous residence permit, which allows - after certain time of residency - getting the permanent residence permit.

question_text_en: Right not to have identity documents confiscated.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Aliens Act 2004, Sections 61, which lists the situations in which only the authorities may confiscate documents. .

question_text_en: Right to birth registration.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Act on Forenames and Surnames.

question_text_en: Right to government document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Alien Act 2004, Sections 33a, 88a, 136, and 161.

question_text_en: Right against destruction of document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to communicate with consular officials.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for all migrants. National law in Finland, however, does protect this right for permanent residence holders in the Consular Services Act 1999/498, Section 5.

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The Aliens Act of 2004, section 122 provides the circumstances where a child migrant can be detained.

question_text_en: Right of migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The Aliens Act of 2004, section 121 specifies conditions for when a migrant can be detained based on their status as a migrant. Section 121 provides conditions for detentions of migrants, "(1) If the precautionary measures referred to in sections 118?120 areinsufficient, the alien may be detained on the basis of an individual assessment, if: 1) taking account of the alien’s personal or other circumstances, there are reasonable grounds to believe that the alien will hide, abscond or in some other way considerably hinder the issue of a decision concerning him or her or the enforcement of a decision to remove him or her from the country; 2) detention is necessary for establishing the alien’s identity; 3) the alien has committed or is suspected of having committed an offence and the detention is necessary to secure the preparations for or the enforcement of a decision on removal from the country; 4) the alien has, while in detention, lodged a new application concerning international protection predominantly fordelaying or disrupting the enforcement of a decision on removal from the country; 5) the detention is based on Article 28 of the Council Regulation on determining the State responsible for examining an asylum application; or 6) taking account of the alien’s personal and other circumstances, there are reasonable grounds to believe that he or she will pose a threat to national security."

question_text_en: Right to appeal legality, conditions, and length of detention
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. According to Aliens Act 129§ "(1) No judicial review may be requested by way of appeal in respect of a decision on detention made by the authorities or a district court. (2) The person detained may make a complaint about the decision of a district court. There is no deadline for the complaint. The complaint shall be handled with urgency."

question_text_en: Right to an individualized detention decision.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Alien Act, 2004, Section 121. Section 121 states that, "(1) If the precautionary measures referred to in sections 118?120 are insufficient, the alien may be detained on the basis of an individual assessment, if: 1) taking account of the alien’s personal or other circumstances, there are reasonable grounds to believe that the alien will hide, abscond or in some other way considerably hinder the issue of a decision concerning him or her or the enforcement of a decision to remove him or her from the country; 2) detention is necessary for establishing the alien’s identity; 3) the alien has committed or is suspected of having committed an offence and the detention is necessary to secure the preparations for or the enforcement of a decision on removalfrom the country; 4) the alien has, while in detention, lodged a new application concerning international protection predominantly for delaying or disrupting the enforcement of a decision on removalfrom the country; 5) the detention is based on Article 28 of the Council Regulation on determining the State responsible for examining an asylum application; or 6) taking account of the alien’s personal and other circumstances, there are reasonable grounds to believe that he or she will pose a threat to national security. (2) Provisions on the conditions for detaining a child are laid down in section 122."

question_text_en: Right to be free from torture and inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Constitution (1999), Section 8, which provides that all people in Finland have the right to be free from being "tortured or otherwise treated in a manner violating human dignity". The constitutional provision applies to migrants.

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The Border Guard Act 2005, Section 7 and 35. Section 7 states that "No individual’s rights may be infringed upon and no one may be caused more harm or inconvenience than is necessary for the duty to be carried out." Section 35 stipulates a border guard's right to use force "to overcome resistance, remove persons from places, apprehend persons, prevent the escape of those who have been deprived of their liberty, remove obstacles or prevent an imminent threat of an offence or another dangerous act or event."?

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of lethal force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: National law protects this rigth in the Border Guard Act, Section 35C. Firearms may be used only when it is necessary to stop the actions of those posing an imminent and serious danger to the life or health of another person and when no more moderate means to do this are available. When performing urgent and important duties, firearms may also be used to remove objects, animals or other similar obstacles. Firearms may not be used to disperse a crowd, unless gas cartridges or other similar projectiles are used in them in accordance with separately issued provisions.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from trafficking or smuggling.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for smuggled migrants. Criminal code 1889, Chapter 17, Section 7 exempts a trafficked migrant from criminal prosecution for a state border offence. However, smuggled migrants are not given this protection. According to the Criminal Code, "A person who 1) crosses or attempts to cross the border of Finland without a valid travel document, visa, residence permit or other document equated with a travel document, or does so elsewhere than through a valid point of entry or departure, or in violation of a statutory prohibition other than an entry ban, 2) otherwise violates the provisions on border crossing, or 3) stays, moves or undertakes measures in the border zone in violation of section 51 of the Border Guard Act or without a permit required under section 52 of that Act shall be sentenced for a state border offence to a fine or imprisonment for at most one year.An alien who is refused entry or deported due to an act referred to in subsection 1 or an alien who seeks asylum or applies for a residence permit on the basis of refugee status in Finland shall not be sentenced for a state border offence. An alien who has committed an act referred to in subsection 1 due to the fact that he or she has been subjected to trafficking in human beings referred to in chapter 25, section 3 or 3a shall neither be sentenced for a state border offence. (650/2004)"

question_text_en: Right to maintain citizenship status after convictions.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland states that only major convictions (e.g., criminal offenses) can lead to loss of citizenship status for naturalized migrants in the Nationality Act, 359/2003, Section 33a, which states that a person's citizenship status can only be lost if said person is guilty of treasonable offences, high treason or terrorism.

question_text_en: Right of economic migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: Nationa law in Finland protects this right in the Nationality Act 2003, Section 12, which stipulates that economic migrants can apply for citizenship after a period of residence, meet integrity, subsistence, and language requirements, and also meet pecuniary obligations.

question_text_en: Right of humanitarian migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: Nationa law in Finland protects this right in the Nationality Act 2003, Section 12, which stipulates that humanitarian migrants can apply for citizenship after a period of residence, meet integrity, subsistence, and language requirements, and also meet pecuniary obligations. According to Sections 3 to 20, though, there are exceptions pertaining to refugees and involuntarily stateless persons, which stipulate that "(1) An alien may be granted Finnish citizenship not withstanding section 13(1)(2) if: 1) he or she has refugee status in Finland, or a residence permit based on the need for protection or he or she is involuntarily stateless; and 2) he or she is and has been permanently resident and domiciled in Finland: a) for the last four years without interruption; or b) for a total of six years since reaching the age of 15 years with the last two years without interruption. (2) A citizenship application made by a person referred to in subsection 1 above is processed expeditiously."

question_text_en: Right of family migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Nationality Act, Sections 12, and 22. According to Section 12, family migrants can apply for citizenshipcan apply for citizenship after a period of residence, meet integrity, subsistence, and language requirements, and also meet pecuniary obligations. Additionally, there is a separate pathway for children of migrants stipulated in Section 24 of the Nationality Act. Children of nationals, or former nationals, or those adopted by Finnish nationals, also have special exemptions laid out in Sections 26 and 27.

question_text_en: Right to dual nationality.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Nationality Act in Chapter 3 section 13, does not require a migrant to abandon his/her nationality when applying for Finnish citizenship.

question_text_en: Right to freedom to hold opinion.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Constitution 1999, Sections 11 and 12. Section 11 states that, "Freedom of religion and conscience Everyone has the freedom of religion andconscience. Freedom of religion and conscience entails the right to profess an practice a religious, the right to express one's convictions and theright to be a member of or decline to be a member of a religious community. No one is under theobligation, against his or her conscience, to participate in the practice of a religion." Section 12 states that, "Freedom of expression and right of access to information Everyone has the freedom ofexpression. Freedom of expression entails the right to express, disseminate and receiveinformation, opinions and other communications without prior prevention by anyone."

question_text_en: Right to freedom of expression.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Constitution 1999, Section 12, which states that, "Freedom of expression and right of access to information Everyone has the freedom ofexpression. Freedom of expression entails the right to express, disseminate and receiveinformation, opinions and other communications without prior prevention by anyone."

question_text_en: Right to freedom of association.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Constitution 1999, Section 12, which states that, "Freedom of expression and right of access to information Everyone has the freedom ofexpression. Freedom of expression entails the right to express, disseminate and receiveinformation, opinions and other communications without prior prevention by anyone."

question_text_en: Right to freedom of assembly.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. While the Finnish Constitution 1999, Section 13 states that "Everyone has the right to arrange meetings and demonstrations without a permit, as well as the right to participate in them. Everyone has the freedom of association. Freedom of association entails the right to forman association without a permit, to be a member or not to be a member of an association and to participate in the activities of an association. The freedom to form trade unions and to organise in order to look after other interests is likewise guaranteed," Section 10 of the Associations Act 503/1989 states that, "an association may have private individuals, corporations and foundations as members. If the primary purpose of the association is to exercise influence over State affairs, it may have as members only Finnish citizens, foreigners residing in Finland and associations whose members or whose direct or indirect member association members are Finnish citizens or foreigners residing in Finland." Therefore, there are restrictions on joining political organizations for migrants.

category: Thought, conscience, and religion or belief
question_text_en: Right of freedom of thought, conscience and religion or belief.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Section 39 of the Aliens Act 2004 stipulates "(1) Issuing a residence permit requires that the alien has sufficient financial resources unless otherwise provided in this Act. In individual cases, a derogation may be made from the requirement if there are exceptionally serious grounds for such a derogation or if the derogation is in the best interest of the child. The requirement for sufficient financial resources does not apply if a residence permit is issued under chapter 6, unless otherwise provided in section 114(4)." However, the requirement for sufficient financial resources does not apply if: 1) theapplication for a residence permit on the basis of family ties has been submitted within three months of the date on which a) the sponsor was served the decision that he or she has been granted asylum; or b) the sponsor was served the decision that he or she has been admitted to Finland under the refugee quota; 2) the sponsor's family was established a) before the sponsor arrived in Finland in cases where he or she has been granted asylum; or b) before the sponsor was admitted to Finland under the refugee quota; and 3) family reunification is not possible in a third country to which the sponsor or family member has special ties.

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to access criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the 1) Constitution 1999, Sections 2, and 21. 2) The Criminal Procedure Act. In Finland, the criminal procedure is the same for everyone, regardless of background, wealth, gender, sexual orientation, health or other personal factors. All victims of crime have the right to, for example, report a crime and, if necessary, access support services, protection and legal aid, such as an attorney, which is stipulated in the Criminal Procedure Act.

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to immigration status or relief from expulsion.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Aliens Act 2004, Sections 52a (victims of human trafficking) and 52d (victims of work-based exploitation). According section 52a, "(1) A victim of trafficking in human beings staying in Finland is issued with a temporary residence permit if: 1) the residence of the victim of trafficking in human beings in Finland is justified onaccount of a criminal investigation or court proceedings concerning trafficking in human beings; 2) the victim of trafficking in human beings is prepared to cooperate with the authorities in apprehending those suspected of trafficking in human beings; and 3) the victim of trafficking inhuman beings no longer has any ties with those suspected of trafficking in human beings. (2) If the victim of trafficking in human beings is in a particularly vulnerable position, the residence permit may be issued on a continuous basis regardless of whether the requirements laid down in subsection 1(1?2) are met. (3) Issuing the residence permit is not conditional on the alien having sufficient financial resources. (4) If a victim of trafficking in human beings is issued with a temporary residence permit, his or her family members residing abroad are not issued with a residence permit on the basis of family ties. If he or she is issued with a continuous residence permit, family members are issued with a residence permit under section 47(3)."

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in 1) the Aliens Act 301/2004, 6§, 39§, 105 a §, 146 §, 97 a §, 104 §. Particularly, Section 6 stipulates that: a) special attention shall be paid to the best interest of the child and to circumstances related to the child’s development and health; b) that the child has a right to be heard unless such testimony is manifestly unnecessary, and their views shall be taken into account in accordance with the child’s age and maturity, and c) that matter shall be processed with urgency. 2) Administrative Procedure Act 434/2003 14§.

question_text_en: Right of women migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Rights of migrants with disabilities to special protection.
citation_text_en: National law in Finland protects this right in the Act on the Reception of Persons Applying for International Protections, and on the Identification of Assistance to Victims of Trafficing in Human Beings, section 6.
