question_text_en: What country are you coding?
citation_text_en: France

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to vote in local and/or regional elections.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in article 11 of the European Convention on Human Rights. 1/ Law of June 30, 1881 on the freedom of assembly that provides that "Public meetings are free. They can take place without prior authorization" 2/ Charter of fundamental rights of the European Union (article 12). 3/ Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms of 1950 (article 11). Article 11 of the European Convention on Human Rights : “1. Toute personne a droit ? la libert? de r?union pacifique et ? la libert? d’association, y compris le droit de fonder avec d’autres des syndicats et de s’affilier ? des syndicats pour la d?fense de ses int?r?ts. 2. L’exercice de ces droits ne peut faire l’objet d’autres restrictions que celles qui, pr?vues par la loi, constituent des mesures n?cessaires, dans une soci?t? d?mocratique, ? la s?curit? nationale ? la s?ret? publique ? la d?fense de l’ordre et ? la pr?vention du crime, ? la protection de la sant? ou de la morale, ou ? la protection des droits et libert?s d’autrui. Le pr?sent article n’interdit pas que des restrictions l?gitimes soient impos?es ? l’exercice de ces droits par les membres des forces arm?es, de la police ou de l’administration de l’Etat.”

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to stand for election.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for all migrants. Article 3 of the Constitution states that only nationals can vote. For national elections (presidential elections, parliamentary elections) and main local elections (regional, departmental elections) only French citizens can vote (article 3 of the French Constitution) 2/ For Municipal and European elections, Europeans citizens who live in France can vote in France (article 88-3 of the French Constitution, article LO227-1 electoral Code and article 2-1 law n° 77-729 of July 7, 1977. 3/ Non-European migrants can never vote in France. As mentioned in article 88-3 of the constitution: “Sous r?serve de r?ciprocit? et selon les modalit?s pr?vues par le Trait? sur l'Union europ?enne sign? le 7 f?vrier 1992, le droit de vote et d'?ligibilit? aux ?lections municipales peut ?tre accord? aux seuls citoyens de l'Union r?sidant en France. Ces citoyens ne peuvent exercer les fonctions de maire ou d'adjoint ni participer ? la d?signation des ?lecteurs s?natoriaux et ? l'?lection des s?nateurs. Une loi organique vot?e dans les m?mes termes par les deux assembl?es d?termine les conditions d'application du pr?sent article.”

question_text_en: Right to equal protection of the law before courts.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in : 1/ Guaranteeing equality before the law without distinction of nationality (article 1 of the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen of 26 August 1789 ; article 1 of the French Constitution of 1958). 2/ Ensuring equal access to justice without distinction of nationality (Administrative, Civil and Criminal Courts : article 47 of the European Convention on Human Rights ; article L. 111-2 of the Code of Judicial Organisation).

question_text_en: Right to government-provided counsel in proceedings related to migrant status.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in : - The law n° 91-647 of July 10, 1991 and the decree n° 2020-1717 of December 28, 2020. While refugees have unconditional right to legal aid, for other categories of migrants, it is subject to resource conditions.

question_text_en: Right to government-provided interpretation in criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in the Code of Criminal Procedure. The preliminary article of the Code provides that : "If the suspected or accused person does not understand French, he or she has the right, in a language he or she understands and until the end of the proceedings, to the assistance of an interpreter, including for meetings with his or her lawyer directly related to any questioning or hearing, and, unless he or she expressly and knowingly waives this right, to the translation of documents essential to the exercise of his or her defense and to guaranteeing the fairness of the trial, which are required to be given to him or her or to be notified to him or her in application of the present code."

question_text_en: Right to be protected from prosecution for unauthorized entry.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Non-Europeans who entered France irregularly shall be punished by a term of one year's imprisonment and a 15,000 Euro fine (article L. 821-1 CESEDA as of January 1, 2023 and former article L. 621-2 CESEDA as of January 1, 2020).

question_text_en: Right to equal access to public adult education institutions.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right for regular migrants in article L441 of the Code of Construction and Housing (Code de la construction et de l'habitation). Article L. 441 Construction and Housing Code deals with allowing regular migrants to apply for social housing. L. 552-8 CESEDA provides asylum seekers with an accommodation in a reception center for asylum seekers (CADA which is a facility specializing in the accommodation and assistance of asylum seekers throughout the procedure. These structures have four main missions : receiving and accommodating asylum seekers, providing them with administrative, social and medical assistance, schooling children and running the center and managing the departure of asylum seekers from the center) or in another similar structure, depending on their situation and the places available.

question_text_en: Right of access to public adult education institutions regardless of status.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in article 13 of the preamble to the Constitution. This right is also protected in : - The Education Code that provides that access to free primary education is a right for all children residing on the national territory regardless of their nationality, migratory status or previous experience (articles L. 111-1, L. 122-1 et L. 131-1 Education code). Schooling is mandatory for children from 6 to 16 years old. - French educational system has the obligation to set up specific actions for the reception and schooling of migrants children who do no speak French (articles L. 321-4 et L. 332-4 Education Code).

question_text_en: Right to be free from discrimination on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in article 13 of the preamble to the Constitution. The preamble of the 1946 constitution provides that "The Nation guarantees equal access of children and adults to education, professional training and culture. The organization of free and secular public education at all levels is a duty of the State." Non-European migrants are subjected to a special procedure to access public courses at the University. They need to prove that they have obtained sufficient diplomas in their own country, to pass an French exam and to apply by a special procedure (article D. 612-12 Education Code). The conditions to be fulfilled for non-European migrants refer to the academic competences of the migrants, not to their legal status.

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after convictions.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Residence permit can be withdrawn if the migrant is found guilty of several listed criminal offenses such as drug trafficking, slavery, human trafficking, pimping, theft in public transportation, soliciting, aggressive begging. (L. 432-6 and L. 432-7 CESEDA). Additionally, any residence permit can be refused or withdrawn for any conviction, if the migrant is considered as a threat to public order (L.432-1 and L. 432-4 CESEDA).

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of torture or inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in France bans refoulement on the basis of a risk of return to torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment in Article 3 of the European Convention on Human Rights. A European Court of Human Rights case, Soering v. Royaume-Uni (7 july 1989) Dans cette affair, ruled that a planned extradition towards the United States was in violation of article 6, as the plaintiff would be placed on death row. Migrants who face such treatment in their native country can also apply for subsidiary protection (L. 512-1 CESEDA).

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of persecution.
citation_text_en: National law in France bans refoulement on the basis of a risk of return to persecution based on race, religion, nationality, membership of a particular social group, or political opinion in the Geneva Convention of 1951, which states that asylum will be granted to any person who fears persecution on the basis of race, religion, nationality, membership to a particular social group, political opinion. Indeed, article L511-1 of the Code de l'entr?e et du s?jour des ?trangers et du droit d'asile states that: “La qualit? de r?fugi? est reconnue : 1° A toute personne pers?cut?e en raison de son action en faveur de la libert? ; 2° A toute personne sur laquelle le Haut- Commissariat des Nations unies pour les r?fugi?s exerce son mandat aux termes des articles 6 et 7 de son statut tel qu'adopt? par l'Assembl?e g?n?rale des Nations unies le 14 d?cembre 1950 ; 3° A toute personne qui r?pond aux d?finitions de l'article 1er de la convention de Gen?ve du 28 juillet 1951 relative au statut des r?fugi?s.”

question_text_en: Right to not return to a deprivations of fundamental human rights.
citation_text_en: National law in France bans refoulement on the basis on the basis of a risk of serious deprivations of fundamental human rights in Articles 2 (right to life), 3 (prohibition of torture, cruel, inhuman or humiliating punishment or treatment), and 8 (protection of private life) of the European Convention on Human Rights. A European Court of Human Rights case, Soering v. Royaume-Uni (7 july 1989) Dans cette affair, ruled that a planned extradition towards the United States was in violation of article 6, as the plaintiff would be placed on death row. Article L. 512-1 CESEDA guarantees a subsidiary protection to migrants who fear death penalty or an execution.

question_text_en: Right to be advised of availability of asylum before expulsion.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from chain refoulement.
citation_text_en: National law in France bans expulsion to any country where a migrant is likely to be subjected to refoulement through a subsequent expulsion in Article 3 of the European Convention on Human Rights. A European Court of Human Rights case, Soering v. Royaume-Uni (7 july 1989) Dans cette affair, ruled that a planned extradition towards the United States was in violation of article 6, as the plaintiff would be placed on death row.

question_text_en: Right to protection against expulsion except following a legal judgment.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in: - Article L611-1 of the Code de l'entr?e et du s?jour des ?trangers et du droit d'asile; - Article L251-1 and L.211-5 Public Relations Code : An obligation to leave French territory (OQTF) has to be motivated by legal and personnal facts and meet legal criteria; - Article L. 252-1 CESEDA: Expulsion decisions must motivated and "take into account all the circumstances relating to the situation of the migrant, in particular the length of their stay in France, their age, their state of health, their family and economic situation, their social and cultural integration into French society, as well as the intensity of their links with their country of origin."

question_text_en: Right to submit reasons against expulsion and have case reviewed before deportation.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in: - Article L614-1 of the Code de l'entr?e et du s?jour des ?trangers et du droit d'asile: “L'?tranger qui fait l'objet d'une d?cision portant obligation de quitter le territoire fran?ais peut, dans les conditions et d?lais pr?vus au pr?sent chapitre, demander au tribunal administratif l'annulation de cette d?cision, ainsi que l'annulation de la d?cision relative au s?jour, de la d?cision relative au d?lai de d?part volontaire et de la d?cision d'interdiction de retour sur le territoire fran?ais qui l'accompagnent le cas ?ch?ant. Les dispositions du pr?sent chapitre sont applicables au jugement de la d?cision fixant le pays de renvoi contest?e en application de l'article L. 721-5 et de la d?cision d'assignation ? r?sidence contest?e en application de l'article L.732-8."; - L.632-1 CESEDA: During the decision-making process of decisions of expulsion, the migrant is heard by a special administrative commission. ; - Article L. 614-1 CESEDA: When the expulsion or the OQTF decision has been taken, migrants can appeal to the Ministre of the Interior (article L. 410-1 Public relations code) or directly to the Administrative Tribunal.

question_text_en: Right of settled migrants to family reunification.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Stateless migrants can only have a residence permit in France (article L. 424-18 CESEDA). French Citizenship is given to a stateless child who is born in France if his/her two parents were stateless or if his/her parents are unknown (article 19-1 Civil Code).

question_text_en: Right to judicial remedy for denials of right to family reunification.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in article L434-2 of the Code de l'entr?e et du s?jour des ?trangers et du droit d'asile. 1/ The close family (spouse/unmaried partner/ children) of economic migrants have the right to have a residence permit, depending on the kind of residence permit the migrant already in France has (passeport talent : L. 421-22 and L. 422-12 CESEDA). 2/ The close family members of a refugee (spouse/unmaried partner/ children) have the right to a 10-year residence permit (L. 424- 11 CESEDA / "familial reunification" : article L. 561-2 CESEDA) 3/ For all other migrants who have been legally in France for at least 18 months, under cover of one of a French or internationally recognized residency permit with a validity period of at least one year, they may request family reunification for spouse and the minor children of the couple. This right is subject to several and strict conditions (size of housing, incomes) (article L. 423-14 CESEDA).

question_text_en: Right to recognition of same-sex marital relationships.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in article L434-2 of the Code for the Entry and Stay of Foreigners and the Right to Asylum (Code de l'entr?e et du s?jour des ?trangers et du droit d'asile). National law also protects this right in article R421-1 Code de justice administrative. Any administrative decision may be the subject of an informal or hierarchical appeal which interrupts the course of this time limit (article L. 431-1 Public relations code/ Administrative justice code).

question_text_en: Right to family reunification without resource conditions
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in article 143 of the Civil Code.

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services.
citation_text_en: Temporary migrant workers' switch to permanent status is conditional on visa type. Many kind of residency permits prevent migrants from entering the process of becoming permanent residents (article L. 426-18 CESEDA)

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services regardless of status.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in article L435-1 of the Code of entry and residence of foreigners and the right to asylum (Code d'entr?e et du s?jour des ?trangers et du droit d'asile). Article L. 435.1 CESEDA allows irregular migrant workers to apply for a 1-year residence permit. Criteria is defined in: Circulaire du 28 novembre 2012.

question_text_en: Right of access to public housing programs.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in article L. 1111-1 of the Labour Code: the Labour laws apply to every employees regardless their nationality. Special provisions protect illegal migrants who are illegaly employed (L. 8252-2 Labour Code).

question_text_en: Right to equal access to free primary education for migrant children.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in article 11 of the preamble to the Constitution 27 October 1946. This right is protected in : - Universal health protection (Puma) for every migrants who is legal and in France for at least 3 months (article L. 160-1 Social Security Code) - State medical aid (AME) is a means of providing access to care for migrants in an irregular situation. It is allocated under conditions of residence and resources (article L. 251-1 Social Security Code).

question_text_en: Right to equal pay for the same work.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Only French citizens can stand for local and national election (article 3 of the French Constitution and L. 2 of the Electoral Code). The only exception is for European citizens who live in France : they can stand for municipal and european Elections (article 88-3 of the French Constitution, article LO227-1 electoral Code and article 2-1 law n° 77-729 of July 7, 1977).

question_text_en: Right to freedom of choice of employment.
citation_text_en: National law in France prohibits discrimination against migrants on the basis of their status as a migrant in : 1/ The Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen of 26 August 1789 that provides that "Men are born and remain free and equal before the law" (article 1). 2/ The Criminal Code (article 225-1) that prohibits discrimination based on "the origin" or on ""the ability to express in a language other than French, membership or nonmembership, real or supposed, of an ethnic group, a Nation". 3/ In its 13 August 1993 decision, the Constitutional Council has noted that different treatment between citizens and non-citizens can be justified under certain circumstances and therefore does not constitute discrimination.

question_text_en: Right of spouse/partner of principal migrant to work.
citation_text_en: National law in France prohibits discrimination against migrants on the ground of race or ethnicity in article 4 of the European Convention on Human Rights. 1/ The Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen of 26 August 1789 that provides that "Men are born and remain free and equal before the law" (article 1). 2/ The Criminal Code (article 225-1) that prohibits discrimination based on "the origin" or on ""the ability to express in a language other than French, membership or nonmembership, real or supposed, of an ethnic group, a Nation".

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after loss of employment.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in article L1132-1 of the Labor Code (Code du travail): - The Labour Code (article L. 1132-1) that prohibits discrimination at work based on "the origin" or on ""the ability to express in a language other than French, membership or non-membership, real or supposed, of an ethnic group, a Nation". - The Labour Code (R. 5221-20) provides that work permits are given only if the remuneration offered to the migrant respects the minimum growth wage or the minimum remuneration provided for by the collective agreement applicable to the employer or the host company.

question_text_en: Right to equal employment conditions and protection.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in article L421-1 of the Code for the entry and stay of foreigners and the right to asylum (Code de l'entr?e et du s?jour des ?trangers et du droit d'asile). 1/ Migrant workers have the right to free choose of employment and to change it. The exception is if the work permit may be limited to certain professional activities or geographical areas. (article L. 5221-7 Labour Code). 2/ If a work permit is required, a new work permit is mandatory for every new contract (R. 5221-1 Labour Code).

question_text_en: Right to form trade unions and other associations.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects migrant spouse/partner’s right to work in R.5221-2 of the Labor Code: Authorizing spouse/partner to work without a work permit if they have a residence permit mentioned on a list, delivered as a member of the family of the principal migrant (list in article R. 5221-2 Labour Code).

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to redress before deportation or withdrawal of residency permit.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in article L.433-1 of the Code de l'entr?e et du s?jour des ?trangers et du droit d'asile: “A l'exception de la carte de s?jour pluriannuelle portant la mention " salari? d?tach? ICT ", pr?vue ? l'article L. 421-26, et de la carte de s?jour pluriannuelle portant la mention " recherche d'emploi ou cr?ation d'entreprise ", pr?vue ? l'article L. 422-10, qui ne sont pas renouvelables, le renouvellement de la carte de s?jour temporaire ou pluriannuelle est subordonn? ? la preuve par le ressortissant ?tranger qu'il continue de remplir les conditions requises pour la d?livrance de cette carte. L'autorit? administrative peut proc?der aux v?rifications utiles pour s'assurer du maintien du droit au s?jour de l'int?ress? et, ? cette fin, convoquer celui-ci ? un ou plusieurs entretiens. Par d?rogation au pr?sent article la carte de s?jour temporaire portant la mention " salari? " pr?vue ? l'article L. 421-1, ainsi que la carte de s?jour pluriannuelle portant la mention " passeport talent " pr?vue aux articles L. 421-9, L. 421-10, L. 421-11 ou L. 421-14, sont renouvel?es dans les conditions pr?vues ? ces m?mes articles.” There won't be any consequence for a migrant with a family residence permit. However, a migrant whose visa status is linked to employment (a migrant with a "working" residence permit) will need to find a new job to keep his/her status.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to social security protections.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in the Labor Code, Chapter 2. The Labour Code applies "to employers under private law and to their employees." regardless of their nationality (article L. 1111-1 Labour Code). Additionally, the Criminal and the Labor Codes prohibit any discrimination based on the origin or the nationality. Furthermore, European workers have extended rights under EU rules. In France, labour laws and migration laws are separated. Employing an irregular migrant is a crime and employers can be prosecuted if they employ irregular migrants. However, at the same time, an irregular migrant who has been illegaly employed has the same rights than other employees (article L. 8252-2 Labor Code). If the employer has not respected the employment conditions and protection, the irregular migrant can sue his/her employer and claim for money/wage arrears etc. This legislation aims to protect irregular migrants from slavery.

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to become lawfully settled.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects migrant workers’ rights to social security protections in article R5221-48 of the Labor Code. L.160-1 of the French Social Security Code obliges the affiliation to the social security system of any person working in France, even migrants (L. 160-1 French Social Security Code).

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to settle regardless of initial status.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in article R5221-48 of the Labor Code (Code du travail). Only migrants with a work permit and a specific/listed type of residence permit have access to unemployment benefits (20 types of residence permit listed to article R. 5221-48 Labour Code).

question_text_en: Right to redress following employer breach of employment contract.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in article 426-17 of the Code of entry and residence of foreigners and the right to asylum (Code d'entr?e et du s?jour des ?trangers et du droit d'asile). Temporary worker who are legally in France for at least 5 years can apply for a permanent resident status if : - They have stable, regular and sufficient resources (at least the minimum wage) - They have a health insurance - The can prove their "republican integration into French society" (article L. 426-17 CESEDA). Article 426-17 of the Code d'entr?e et du s?jour des ?trangers et du droit d'asile: " L'?tranger qui justifie d'une r?sidence r?guli?re ininterrompue d'au moins cinq ans en France au titre d'une carte de s?jour temporaire ou pluriannuelle ou d'une carte de r?sident, de ressources stables, r?guli?res et suffisantes pour subvenir ? ses besoins et d'une assurance maladie se voit d?livrer, sous r?serve des exceptions pr?vues ? l'article L. 426-18, une carte de r?sident portant la mention " r?sident de longue dur?e-UE " d'une dur?e de dix ans. Les ann?es de r?sidence sous couvert d'une carte de s?jour temporaire portant la mention " vie priv?e et familiale " retir?e par l'autorit? administrative sur le fondement d'un mariage ayant eu pour seules fins d'obtenir un titre de s?jour ou d'acqu?rir la nationalit? fran?aise ne peuvent ?tre prises en compte pour obtenir la carte de r?sident pr?vue au premier alin?a. Les ressources mentionn?es au premier alin?a doivent atteindre un montant au moins ?gal au salaire minimum de croissance. Sont prises en compte toutes les ressources propres du demandeur, ind?pendamment des prestations familiales et des allocations pr?vues ? l'article L. 262-1 du code de l'action sociale et des familles ainsi qu'aux articles L. 5423-1, L. 5423-2 et L. 5423-3 du code du travail. La condition de ressources pr?vue au premier alin?a n'est pas applicable lorsque la personne qui demande la carte de r?sident est titulaire de l'allocation aux adultes handicap?s mentionn?e ? l'article L. 821-1 du code de la s?curit? sociale ou de l'allocation suppl?mentaire mentionn?e ? l'article L. 815-24 du m?me code. Les modalit?s d'application du pr?sent article sont d?finies par d?cret en Conseil d'Etat."

question_text_en: Right not to have identity documents confiscated.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in: - Article L814-1 of the Code de l'entr?e et du s?jour des ?trangers et du droit d'asile : only public authorities and police officers are allowed to confiscate passports or travel documents. An employer who confiscates the passport of a working migrant could be convicted of forced labour (article 225-13 and 225-14-1 Criminal code).

question_text_en: Right to birth registration.
citation_text_en: National law in France requires birth registration of migrant children, regardless of their status, in article 55 of the Civil Code. Birth registration is mandatory for every child born on the French territory, regardless the migrant status of the parents even if they are irregular.

question_text_en: Right to government document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: As of January 1, 2023, national law in France mandates the issuing of documents that recognize migrants’ residency status, work status, and identity in article L411-1 of the Code de l'entr?e et du s?jour des ?trangers et du droit d'asile. This same right is protected in article L311-1 of the Code de l'entr?e et du s?jour des ?trangers et du droit d'asile, as of January 1, 2020 (the article number has changed since january 2020, the content remains unchanged). Every migrant over 18 and staying in France for more than 3 months must hold a residence permit that can take different forms: long-term visa, provisional residence permit (maximum 1 year), temporary residence card (between 1 and 4 years) or a 10-year residence card (article L. 411-1 CESEDA). Most of these residence permit gives the right to work in France (article L. 414-10 CESEDA). For paid employment, a written work authorization is often required in addition (articles L. 5221-2 and R. 5221-1 Labour Code).

question_text_en: Right against destruction of document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: National law in France makes it illegal for anyone to destroy documents that recognize migrants’ residency status, work status, and identity in article 322-1 of the Criminal Code.

question_text_en: Right to communicate with consular officials.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in: - Allowing every migrant who is held in an Administrative Holding Center or under house arrest to communicate with the consulate (article L. 744-4 CESEDA / R. 732-5 CESEDA) - Allowing every migrant who has been refused the entry on the French territory to inform the consulate (Article L. 332-2 and L. 352-3 CESEDA).

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: National law in France prohibits the detention of children in article L741-5 al.1 Code de l'entr?e et du s?jour des ?trangers et du droit d'asile : “L'?tranger mineur de dix-huit ans ne peut faire l'objet d'une d?cision de placement en r?tention. ? However, this is not an absolute protection. A minor can only be held in administrative detention with an adult under certain strict conditions, guided by the best interests of the child. These conditions are outlined in article L741-5 al.2 Code de l'entr?e et du s?jour des ?trangers et du droit d'asile: " L'?tranger accompagn? d'un mineur ne peut ?tre plac? en r?tention que dans les cas suivants : 1° L'?tranger n'a pas respect? l'une des prescriptions d'une pr?c?dente mesure d'assignation ? r?sidence ; 2° A l'occasion de la mise en ?uvre de la d?cision d'?loignement, l'?tranger a pris la fuite ou oppos? un refus ;3° En consid?ration de l'int?r?t du mineur, le placement en r?tention de l'?tranger dans les quarante-huit heures pr?c?dant le d?part programm? pr?serve l'int?ress? et le mineur qui l'accompagne des contraintes li?es aux n?cessit?s de transfert. La dur?e de r?tention d'un ?tranger accompagn? d'un mineur est la plus br?ve possible, eu ?gard au temps strictement n?cessaire ? l'organisation du d?part. Dans tous les cas, le placement en r?tention d'un ?tranger accompagn? d'un mineur n'est possible que dans un lieu de r?tention administrative b?n?ficiant de chambres isol?es et adapt?es, sp?cifiquement destin?es ? l'accueil des familles L'int?r?t sup?rieur de l'enfant est une consid?ration primordiale pour l'application de la pr?sente section."

question_text_en: Right of migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Migrants can be held in administrative detention if they do not show sufficient guarantees that they are not going to escape (article L. 741-1 ? L. 741-10 CESEDA). Criminal offenses may also concern illegal migrants in France, especially in case of illegal entrance in France (articles L. 821- 1 and following CESEDA).

question_text_en: Right to appeal legality, conditions, and length of detention
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in: - Article L552-9 Code de l'entr?e et du s?jour des ?trangers et du droit d'asile; - Article 6 of the European Convention on Human Rights; and - Article 13 of the same convention. 1/ The liberties and detention judge (JLD) is automatically seized in case of Administrative detention. To extend administrative detention beyond 48 hours, migrants attend a hearing before a judge (“JLD”) (article L. 741-10 CESEDA ; L. 742-1 CESEDA). The judge can authorize the prolongation for a period of 28 more days (L. 742-3 CESEDA). And, in special and strict conditions, for an extra period of 30 more days, for a maximum of 90 days (articles L. 742-4 et L. 742-5 CESEDA). 2/ The migrant can also request the end of the retention at any moment (article L. 741-10 CESEDA).

question_text_en: Right to an individualized detention decision.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in: - Article 5 of the European Convention on Human Rights: ; - Article 9-1 of the Pacte international relatif aux droits civils et politiques; - Article 12 1. of the same pacte; - Criminal code (code p?nal) article 132-1. Every detention decision must be written and motivated (article L. 741-6 CESEDA). The decision has to respect legal detention requirements and take into account the personal situation of the migrant (family, vulnerability, assurance that they will appear) (article L. 211-5 CRPA and article L. 741-4 CESEDA).

question_text_en: Right to be free from torture and inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in: - The European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR): “no one shall be subjected to torture or to inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.” (article 3 of the ECHR) - Administrative Holding Centers must be kept and ruled in conditions consistent with the dignity and safety of its occupants (article R. 744-12 CESEDA) - Criminal sanctions are more severe against smugglers if migrants are subject to conditions of life, transport, work or accommodation that are incompatible with human dignity (article L. 823-3 du CESEDA).

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in: 1) States shall not expel or return a refugee to a territory where his life or freedom is threatened (article 33 Convention relating to the Status of Refugees). 2) Each refusal of entry to the French territory must be notified by a signed and motivated decision (article L. 332-2 CESEDA). The migrant may refuse to be repatriated before the expiration of a one clear day period (article L. 333-2 CESEDA). The force can be used only after this decision has been notified and the migrant has had the possibility to challenge it.

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of lethal force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in: - The use of lethal force by the police/military/customs officers is strictly limited in France to 5 situations : 1/ if their life or physical integrity or that of others is threatened ; 2/ if, after two summonses, they have no other means of protecting the premises or the persons they are guarding ; 3 and 4/ if they have no other means of arresting someone who may be endangering the lives of others ; 5/ to prevent the repetition of a murder that has just been committed (article L. 435-1 code de la s?curit? int?rieure ; article 56 code des douanes) . In addition, the ECHR’s case law has strictly limited the use of lethal force in cases of absolute necessity and the force used must be strictly proportionate to the aims mentioned in that provision (article 2 of the European Convention on Human Rights -ECHR, 27 Sept. 1995, McCann et a. C / United Kingdom, no.18984 / 91).

question_text_en: Right to be protected from trafficking or smuggling.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to maintain citizenship status after convictions.
citation_text_en: National law in France provides that convictions for criminal or other offenses leads to a loss of the citizenship status of naturalized migrants in articles 25 and 25-1 of the Civil Code.

question_text_en: Right of economic migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in France provides pathway to citizenship for economic migrants, if several conditions are met, such as residency requirements, "republicain integration into French society" and certain resource conditions (article 21-17 Code civil and following). The duration of residence is in principle 5 years, but it can be less in certain specific cases (e.g. studies in France).

question_text_en: Right of humanitarian migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in France provides pathway to citizenship for humanitarian migrants, if several conditions are met, such as residency requirements, "republicain integration into French society" and certain ressource conditions (article 21-17 Code civil and following). The duration of residence is in principle 5 years, but it can be less in certain specific cases (e.g. migrant with the refugee status).

question_text_en: Right of family migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in France provides pathway to citizenship for family migrants, if several conditions are met, such as residency requirements, "republicain integration into French society" and certain ressource conditions (article 21-17 Code civil and following). The duration of residence is in principle 5 years, but it can be less in certain specific cases (e.g. mariage with a French citizen).

question_text_en: Right to dual nationality.
citation_text_en: The Civil code has no provisions against dual nationals. Obtaining dual nationality is not prohibited.

question_text_en: Right to freedom to hold opinion.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen which provides that no one should worry for their beliefs, including religious beliefs (articles 10 and 11). This right is also protected in the Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms of 1950 (articles 9 and 10).

question_text_en: Right to freedom of expression.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in article 10 of the European Convention on Human Rights : "§1: Toute personne a droit ? la libert? d'expression. Ce droit comprend la libert? d'opinion et la libert? de recevoir ou de communiquer des informations ou des id?es sans qu'il puisse y avoir ing?rence d'autorit?s publiques et sans consid?ration de fronti?re. Le pr?sent article n'emp?che pas les ?tats de soumettre les entreprises de radiodiffusion, de cin?ma ou de t?l?vision ? un r?gime d'autorisations. §2: L'exercice de ces libert?s comportant des devoirs et des responsabilit?s, peut ?tre soumis ? certaines formalit?s, conditions, restrictions ou sanctions pr?vues par la loi, qui constituent des mesures n?cessaires, dans une soci?t? d?mocratique, ? la s?curit? nationale, ? l'int?grit? territoriale ou ? la s?ret? publique, ? la d?fense de l'ordre et ? la pr?vention du crime, ? la protection de la sant? ou de la morale, ? la protection de la r?putation ou des droits d'autrui, pour emp?cher la divulgation d'informations confidentielles ou pour garantir l'autorit? et l'impartialit? du pouvoir judiciaire."

question_text_en: Right to freedom of association.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in article 10 of the European Convention on Human Rights. 1/ Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen garuantees free communication of thoughts and opinions as "one of the most precious rights of man: every citizen can therefore speak, write and print freely, except for the abuse of this freedom in the cases determined by the law" (article 11). 2/ Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms of 1950 (article 10). Article 10 of the European Convention on Human Rights: "§1: Toute personne a droit ? la libert? d'expression. Ce droit comprend la libert? d'opinion et la libert? de recevoir ou de communiquer des informations ou des id?es sans qu'il puisse y avoir ing?rence d'autorit?s publiques et sans consid?ration de fronti?re. Le pr?sent article n'emp?che pas les ?tats de soumettre les entreprises de radiodiffusion, de cin?ma ou de t?l?vision ? un r?gime d'autorisations. §2: L'exercice de ces libert?s comportant des devoirs et des responsabilit?s, peut ?tre soumis ? certaines formalit?s, conditions, restrictions ou sanctions pr?vues par la loi, qui constituent des mesures n?cessaires, dans une soci?t? d?mocratique, ? la s?curit? nationale, ? l'int?grit? territoriale ou ? la s?ret? publique, ? la d?fense de l'ordre et ? la pr?vention du crime, ? la protection de la sant? ou de la morale, ? la protection de la r?putation ou des droits d'autrui, pour emp?cher la divulgation d'informations confidentielles ou pour garantir l'autorit? et l'impartialit? du pouvoir judiciaire."

question_text_en: Right to freedom of assembly.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in article 11 of the European Convention on Human Rights. 1/ Decision of the Constitutional council of 16 July 1971 that confers a constitutional value to the freedom of association. 2/The law of July 1, 1901. 3/ Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms of 1950 (article 11). The right to join trade unions has also a contitutionnal value (paragraph 7 of the preamble of the 1946 constitution & decision of the Constitutional council of July 25, 1989 n°89-257). Article 11 of the European Convention on Human Rights : “1. Toute personne a droit ? la libert? de r?union pacifique et ? la libert? d’association, y compris le droit de fonder avec d’autres des syndicats et de s’affilier ? des syndicats pour la d?fense de ses int?r?ts. 2. L’exercice de ces droits ne peut faire l’objet d’autres restrictions que celles qui, pr?vues par la loi, constituent des mesures n?cessaires, dans une soci?t? d?mocratique, ? la s?curit? nationale ? la s?ret? publique ? la d?fense de l’ordre et ? la pr?vention du crime, ? la protection de la sant? ou de la morale, ou ? la protection des droits et libert?s d’autrui. Le pr?sent article n’interdit pas que des restrictions l?gitimes soient impos?es ? l’exercice de ces droits par les membres des forces arm?es, de la police ou de l’administration de l’Etat.”

category: Thought, conscience, and religion or belief
question_text_en: Right of freedom of thought, conscience and religion or belief.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for all migrants. National law in France protects this right for certain categories of migrants in article L434-7 of the Code de l'entr?e et du s?jour des ?trangers et du droit d'asile. 1/ The close family (spouse/unmaried partner/ children) of economic migrants have the right to have a residence permit regardless of resource conditions but depending on the kind of residence permit the migrant already in France has (passeport talent : L. 421-22 and L. 422-12 CESEDA). 2/ The close family members of a refugee or beneficiary of the subsidiary protection (spouse/unmaried partner/ children) have the right to a 10-year residence permit regardless of resource conditions (subsidiary protection : L. 424-11 CESEDA / "familial reunification" : article L. 561-2 CESEDA).

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to access criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in Article 113-2 of the French Criminal Code.

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to immigration status or relief from expulsion.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in Article L. 425-1 CESEDA; article L. 425-2 CESEDA; and Article L. 425-3 CESEDA.

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in: 1) Some articles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child (adopted 20 November 1989 - ratified by France September 6th, 1990). 2) For minor asylum seekers: The EU regulation (Section 8 - Regulation (EU) No 674/2010) which allows minors to remain in the country in which they first filed an asylum claim, or to reach a country in which a parent is an asylum seeker. Finally, child asylum seekers are not required to have identity papers and can be schooled. For unaccompanied minors (minors without parents or other legal representatives), an official representative is appointed by the general attorney (section L. 521-9 CESEDA ; section L. 223-2 CASF). Unaccompanied minors can be provided with an emergency accommodation by the public local authority (d?partement) (article R.221-11 CASF). 3) For minor migrants who are not asylum seekers: - Minors need a visa to enter France. But minors do not have to obtain a residence permit to stay in France: their legal status is determined by the status of their legal representatives (article L. 411-1 CESEDA) - Minors could obtain a document for the movement of foreign minors to travel abroad and come back to France without a visa (document de circulation pour ?trangers mineurs - DCEM) (article L. 414-4 CESEDA) - Minors cannot be held alone in administrative detention. A minor can only be held in administrative detention with an adult under certain strict conditions, guided by the best interests of the child (article L. 741-5 CESEDA).

question_text_en: Right of women migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in: 1) Protecting women who were victims of human trafficking or prostitution. A 1-year residence permit during the criminal investigations. This statement applies also to woman who testifies during the trial (article L. 425-1 CESEDA). During the criminal investigations, women in such case can benefit from the financial aid reserved for asylum seekers (article L. 425-2 CESEDA) A 10-years residence is delivered if the accused person is found guilty (article L. 425-3 CESEDA). 2) Protecting women, including minors, in case of danger of sexual mutilation or forced and marriages. (article L. 561-8 CESEDA + case law of the Cour nationale du droit d’asile).

question_text_en: Rights of migrants with disabilities to special protection.
citation_text_en: National law in France protects this right in: - Protecting migrants with an illness or a disability. A 1-year residence permit is delivered if his/her health state implies medical care that would have dramatic consequences if not provided and if he couldn't benefit from an appropriated treatment in his own country (article L. 425-9 CESEDA). Treatment has to be not accessible to the general population in the migrant’s home country or not affordable (CE, 07/04/2010, n°301640). Parents of children an illness or a disability can also have a 6-months residence permit (article L. 425-10 CESEDA) - For asylum seekers only, disabilities are considered to appreciate the vulnerability of the migrants (article L. 522-3 CESEDA). During its personal interview, the asylum seeker with disabilities can be accompanied by the health professional who usually follows him or her or by the representative of an association that helps people with disabilities (article L. 531-18 CESEDA). - Before placing a migrant with disabilities in administrative holding centres, the French authorities must take “the motor, cognitive or psychological disability and the support needs of the migrant” into account (article L. 741-4 CESEDA).
