The right of the European Union citizen for family reunification is also recognized for his/her spouse regardless of his/her nationality with whom the European Union citizen has a duly proven stable relationship." This right is also protected for family members of a Greek citizen, as outlined in Article 1 of Migration Code, but this right is not protected for other categories of migrants within the country.

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The opportunity for temporary migrant workers to switch to permanent status after certain conditions are met is conditional on visa as stated in Law 3251/2014, Article 18.

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services regardless of status.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in: 1) Law 4251/2014 (Migration Code), Article 19, which states: "“1. The Coordinator of the Decentralized Administration may exceptionally grant a three (3) year residence permit to third-country nationals residing in Greece. The residence permit is granted once and can be renewed for one of the other reasons of this Code. A third-country national has the right to submit an application for such residence permit, if he /she proves with documents his/her actual residence in the country for at least seven (7) consecutive years, before submission of the application.” 2) Law 4540/2018 (Government Gazette A 91/22.5.2018), Article 19 which does not speak of exceptional reasons but of ''exceptional granting of residence permits to foreigners residing illegally in the country for at least the last seven years and also to parents of minor nationals...''

question_text_en: Right of access to public housing programs.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in: 1) Law 4251/2014 (Migration Code), Article 21A, which states: "1. Employees holders of a uniform residence permit, enjoy equal treatment with nationals as regards: […] c) the terms of employment, including the minimum age limit permitted for work, working conditions, including remuneration and dismissal conditions, working hours, leave and holidays […].” 2) Presidential Decree 80/4.12.2022. Article 17 (which codified article 3 of L. 4443/2016 on the principle of equal treatment): “1. Without prejudice to par. 3 and 4, as well as article 18, the principle of equal treatment regardless of race, color, national or ethnic origin, descent, religious or other beliefs, disability or chronic illness, age, family or social status, sexual orientation, identity or gender characteristics in the working and employment sector, applies to all persons, in the public and private sector, regarding: c) the terms and conditions of work and employment, in particular as regards remuneration, dismissal, health and safety at work and, in the event of unemployment, reintegration and re-employment […].” 3) Law 4939/2022, Article 26, in relation to beneficiaries of international protection.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to free primary education for migrant children.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right only for migrants in regular status, or children regardless of status, in: 1) L. 4251/2014 (Migration Code), Article 26: “1. Public services, legal public entities, local authorities […] social security organizations are obliged not to provide their services to third-country nationals who do not have a passport or other travel document recognized by international conventions and an entry visa or residence permit and generally do not prove that they have entered and reside legally in Greece... 2. The following are excluded from the provisions of the previous paragraph: a) hospitals and clinics in the case of third-country nationals who are urgently admitted to hospital and in the case of children [...].” 2) L. 4939/2022, Article 30 (Medical care): “1. Beneficiaries of international protection have access to medical care under the conditions that apply to Greek citizens. 2. Beneficiaries of international protection who have special needs and in particular pregnant women, persons with disabilities, victims of torture, rape or other serious forms of psychological, physical or sexual violence or minors who have been victims of any form of ill treatment, neglect, exploitation, torture, cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment […], shall be provided with adequate medical care, including treatment for mental and psychical disability, where necessary, under the conditions applicable to Greek citizens.” 3) Regarding asylum seekers right to access to health care services is regulated in: Ministerial Decision 605869/18.10.2022.

question_text_en: Right to equal pay for the same work.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for all migrants. 1) According to Law 3528/2007 (Code of Public Servants), Article 4: “1. Only Greek citizens are appointed as employees [in the public sector]. 2. Citizens of EU member states are allowed to be appointed to positions that do not fall under the exception of par. 4 article 39 of the EU Constitution, according to the provisions of a special law. 3. The appointment of aliens who are not citizens of EU member countries is allowed only in the cases provided for by special laws.” The possibility of a third country national to run for public office happens only for those aliens of Greek descent. 2)

question_text_en: Right to freedom of choice of employment.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece prohibits discrimination against migrants on the basis of their status as a migrant in: 1) The Charter of fundamental rights of the European Union Article 21, which states: “1. Any discrimination based on any ground such as sex, race, color, ethnic or social origin, genetic features, language, religion or belief, political or any other opinion, membership of a national minority, property, birth, disability, age or sexual orientation shall be prohibited. 2. Within the scope of application of the Treaty establishing the European Community and of the Treaty on European Union, and without prejudice to the special provisions of those Treaties, any discrimination on grounds of nationality shall be prohibited.” Moreover, Greece has ratified most of the international Conventions regarding the principle of non-discrimination, including: a) the 1965 UN Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (ratified by legislative decree 494/1970), b) the 1966 UN International Covenant on economic, social and cultural rights (ratified by L. 1532/1985), c) the 1966 UN International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ratified by L. 2462/1997), d) the 1950 Council of Europe European Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms (ratified by legislative decree 53 of 19/20 September 1974), e) the 1961 Council of Europe European Social Charter (ratified by L. 1426/1984). 2) Art.1 L494/1970.

question_text_en: Right of spouse/partner of principal migrant to work.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in: 1) The Constitution of Greece, Articles 5, which states that: “2. All persons who are in the Greek territory enjoy the absolute protection of their life, honor and freedom, without discrimination of nationality, race, language and religious or political beliefs...[…].” 2) Law 494/1970, Article 1. Moreover, Greece has ratified most of the international Conventions regarding the principle of non-discrimination, including: a) the 1965 UN Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (ratified by legislative decree 494/1970), b) the 1966 UN International Covenant on economic, social and cultural rights (ratified by L. 1532/1985), c) the 1966 UN International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ratified by L. 2462/1997), d) the 1950 Council of Europe European Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms (ratified by legislative decree 53 of 19/20 September 1974), e) the 1961 Council of Europe European Social Charter (ratified by L. 1426/1984).

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after loss of employment.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for irregular migrants. However, all other migrants, including refugees are protected in: 1) The Constitution of Greece, Article 22, which states that, “1. [...] All employees, regardless of gender or other discrimination, have the right to equal pay for work of equal value." 2) Article 17 of Presidential Decree 80/4.12.2022: "1. Without prejudice to par. 3 and 4, as well as article 18, the principle of equal treatment regardless of race, color, national or ethnic origin, descent, religious or other beliefs, disability or chronic illness, age, family or social status, sexual orientation, identity or gender characteristics in the working and employment sector, applies to all persons, in the public and private sector, regarding: c) the terms and conditions of work and employment, in particular as regards remuneration, dismissal, health and safety at work [...].”3) Law 4251/2014 (Migration Code), Article 21Α stated: "1. Employees - holders of a uniform residence [permit] enjoy equal treatment with nationals as regards: [...] c) the terms of employment, [...] the working conditions, including the terms of remuneration and dismissal [...]."

question_text_en: Right to equal employment conditions and protection.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece guarantees the right of workers to freely change employers within a specific sector in: 1) Law 4251/2014 (Migration Code), Articles 15, 18, 18A, and 117. Article 18A states, "[...] 2. The residence permit for seasonal work with the purpose of seasonal employment has a validity of one (1) to five (5) years, depending on the employment contract [...] and grants the third-country national the right to seasonal employment and residence in Greece for a period of up to nine (9) months per twelve (12) months…The third-country national, holder of the present residence permit, has the possibility to change employer by virtue of a new employment contract [...]." Article 15 (Grant and renewal of residence permit for dependent work) also states, "4. The third-country national is allowed to sign an employment contract with another employer during the validity of the original residence permit, provided that there is no change in the specialty for which the national entry visa was granted, as well as the insurance service. The holder of a residence permit for work may work in another Regional Unit and change specialty after one year from the grant of the initial residence permit. [This] residence permit that is renewed according to par. 2 of this article, grants the third-country national access to dependent work and to the provision of services or work. The holder of a residence permit for dependent work may, subject to special provisions of this Code, exercise an independent economic activity, only if he/she obtains a long-term residence permit [...]."

question_text_en: Right to form trade unions and other associations.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in: 1) Articles 75 and 76 of the Migration Code (Law 4251/2014), which state that “1. The family members of the dependent have equally with him/her, the right to: […] b. access to dependent work, provision of work or services […]” and “1. Persons who have been accepted for reasons of family reunification are entitled […] to obtain an independent residence permit in Greece in the following cases: a. after five years of the grant of the initial residence permit for family reunification, if a residence permit for one of the other reasons of the Code has not been granted, b. adulthood. […]7. The independent residence permit grants the holder the right to direct access to dependent work ? provision of independent services or work […]”.

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to redress before deportation or withdrawal of residency permit.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for all migrants. Art. 15 of L4251/2014, which provides that:''1. The citizen of a third country, who has received an entry visa for the provision of dependent work in Greece, is granted a residence permit for dependent work, as long as he presents an employment contract from which it does not appear that his remuneration is equal, at least, to his monthly earnings unskilled worker and the required supporting documents. Para 4 of the same article provides that:'' 4. The citizen of a third country is allowed to enter into an employment contract with another employer during the validity of his original residence permit, provided that there is no change in the specialty for which he was granted the national entry visa, as well as the insurance institution.'' Based on the provisions of Law 4251/2014, some categories of migrants can stay and work in Greece without a residence permit with the right to work.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to social security protections.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in: 1) Presidential Decree 80/4.12.2022, Article 17, which states: "1. Without prejudice to par. 3 and 4, as well as article 18, the principle of equal treatment regardless of race, color, national or ethnic origin, descent, religious or other beliefs, disability or chronic illness, age, family or social status, sexual orientation, identity or gender characteristics in the working and employment sector, applies to all persons, in the public and private sector, regarding: c) the terms and conditions of work and employment, in particular as regards remuneration, dismissal, health and safety at work and, in the event of unemployment, reintegration and re-employment [...]." 2) The Migration Code (Law 4251/2014), Article 21, which states: "2. Citizens of third countries legally residing in Greece are insured with the relevant insurance organizations and have the same insurance rights as nationals. 3. The provisions of n.d. 57/1973, as always applicable, for social protection, are also applied to citizens of third countries who reside legally in Greece. The provisions of the n.d. 162/1973 (A' 227, correction of errors A' 298), of article 22 of Law 2646/1998 (A' 236), as well as the regulatory decisions that have been issued under their authority, are also applied to citizens of third countries, who are granted a residence permit for humanitarian reasons."

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to become lawfully settled.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in: 1) Presidential Decree 80/4.12.2022, Article 17. According to this article, "2. Without prejudice to par. 3, 4 and 6 as well as article 18, the principle of equal treatment regardless of race, color, national or ethnic origin, descent applies to all persons, in the public and private sector, regarding: a) Social protection, including social security and health care [...]." 2) Law 4251/2014 (Migration Code), Article 21 which states that: "2. Citizens of third countries legally residing in Greece are insured with the relevant insurance organizations and have the same insurance rights as nationals."

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to settle regardless of initial status.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in: 1) Presidential Decree 80/4.12.2022, Article 17, whcih states that, "1. Without prejudice to par. 3 and 4, as well as article 18, the principle of equal treatment regardless of race, color, national or ethnic origin, descent, religious or other beliefs, disability or chronic illness, age, family or social status, sexual orientation, identity or gender characteristics in the working and employment sector, applies to all persons, in the public and private sector, regarding: c) the terms and conditions of work and employment, in particular as regards remuneration, dismissal, health and safety at work and, in the event of unemployment, reintegration and re-employment […].3. The provisions of this article […] do not apply in the cases where specifically justified different treatment is provided due to nationality and do not affect the provisions and conditions of the legal status of third-country nationals outside the EU or stateless persons living in the territory."

question_text_en: Right to redress following employer breach of employment contract.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right not to have identity documents confiscated.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in article 222 Penal Code L 4619/2019 which provides that "Anyone who, with the intention of harming another, conceals, damages or destroys a document of which he is not the owner or is not the sole owner, or of which another has the right, according to the provisions of civil law, to request its delivery or demonstration, shall be punished by imprisonment for up to two years or by a fine."

question_text_en: Right to birth registration.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in: 1) Law 4483/2017, Article 115 which provides for the creation of a 'Citizens' Registry', where all births of migrant children are registered, regardless of their legal status: “1. An information system named 'Citizens' Registry' is established and maintained at the Ministry of Interior, composed of […]b. all data concerning the registry acts of Greek and alien citizens, for whom registry events are taking place in Greece […]" 2) Article 20(1) of L 344/1976 (L 344/1976 on Civil Registration Acts, Official Gazette 143/A/11.6.1976) provides that ''The birth of a child must be declared within 10 days to the Registry Office of the municipality where the child was born. The required documents for this declaration are: a doctor’s or midwife’s verification of the birth; and the residence permit of at least one of the parents. A deferred statement is accepted by the registrar but the parent must pay a fee of up to ?100 in such a case.''

question_text_en: Right to government document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in different laws for different categories of migrants. Some of the relevant laws are as follows: 1) The Migration Code (L. 4251/2014). According to Article 2A par.3: “3. The uniform residence permit is issued or renewed in accordance with the provisions of articles 8 and 9 hereof, within four (4) months at the latest, from the day of submission of the application, unless otherwise specified in the provisions of this Code." According to Article 7 §3: the residence permits of legally residing migrants in Greece are divided into different categories. “Each residence permit shall indicate if access to the labor market is allowed, subject to the specific provisions of this Code." 2) For international protection applicants, the rules are regulated in International Protection Law (L. 4939/2022). For international protection applicants, the Greek law issues temporary documents according to: a) Article 1 ka: “International protection applicant card" or "card" is the special individual card issued for the applicant during the administrative process of examining his/her application by the competent authorities and allows him/her to stay in Greek territory until its completion […].” b) Article 57 (Employment): “1. International protection applicants, after the lapse of six (6) months from the completion of the process of lodge of the application for international protection […], if no first instance decision has been issued by the competent Authority and the delay cannot be attributed to them, have the right to substantial access to the labor market […]." For beneficiaries of international protection (meaning recognized refugees and beneficiaries of subsidiary protection), the Greek law issues a residence permit according to: a) Article 23: “1. To a third-country national or a stateless person recognized as refugee, a three-year residence permit is granted […]. To a third-country national or a stateless person recognized as beneficiary of subsidiary protection, a one-year residence permit is granted. The residence permit is renewed […] following an application by the interested party, which is submitted to the competent Receiving Authority no later than thirty (30) […] days before its expiration. To a third-country national or a stateless person recognized as beneficiary of subsidiary protection […] a 1-year residence permit is granted. The residence permit is renewed for another two (2) years, after a review, […] following an application by the interested party, which is submitted to the competent Receiving Authority no later than thirty (30) […] days before its expiration. […]. 3. […] residence permits are also granted to family members of beneficiaries of international protection for the period that the residence permit of the beneficiary is valid […]. 5. The above residence permit, which proves the identity of the beneficiaries of international protection, is printed from the National Passport and Secure Document Center of the Hellenic Police Headquarters.” According to Article 74 par. 5 “[…] 5. Applicants have the right to be provided free of charge […] immediately after the full registration of their application […] with the international protection applicant card […]. The international protection applicant card is a temporary title, does not establish a right to issue a residence permit […]." Article 75 states that: “1. The (international protection applicant) card is valid for one (1) year and is renewed until the completion of the examination procedure of the application for international protection. […]."

question_text_en: Right against destruction of document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in Penal Code L 4619/2019, Article 222. This article states that, "Anyone who, with the intention of harming another, conceals, damages or destroys a document of which he is not the owner or is not the sole owner... shall be punished by imprisonment for up to two years."

question_text_en: Right to communicate with consular officials.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in: 1) Law 4251/2014 (Migration Code). Article 21 §4b states that: "Detained third-country nationals are informed, in a language they understand [...], of their rights and obligations. Also, their communication with diplomatic or consular officers of their country is facilitated [...]." 2) Law 3907/2011 (Transposition of Directive 2008/115/EC). Article 31§2 states that, "Third-country nationals in detention are allowed ? on request ? to establish contact with legal representatives, family members, and competent consular authorities."

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. However, the detention of children on the basis of their status as a migrant is strictly regulated and as a last resort. 1) According to Law 4939/2022, Article 52: “2. Juveniles are detained only as a last resort, always after taking under consideration their best interest, and if it is proven that alternative and less restrictive measures cannot be applied. The length of detention is as short as possible, and every effort is made to liberate and refer them to accommodation centers suitable for minors and never to correctional institutions. In any case, the period until the completion of the process of referring minors to accommodation centers cannot exceed twenty-five (25) days. Unaccompanied minors are detained only in exceptional circumstances […].” 2) According to Law 3907/2011, Article 32§1, "1: Unaccompanied minors and families with minors are detained as a measure of last resort only if other sufficient and less burdensome measures cannot be implemented for the same reason and for the shortest appropriate period." Furthermore, "5. The best interests of the child shall be a primary consideration in the context of the detention of minors pending removal." 2) Circular 683/2022 (prot. No. 693319/18.11.2022), Part C of the Ministry of Migration & Asylum, states: "in the context of the detention of minors and families (article 32 of L. 3907/2011) is considered appropriate to apply the measure of detention for the purpose of removal only as a measure of last resort and to choose the use of alternative solutions provided for in article 22 par. 3 of the same law, and of course after individual assessment of each case. The best interest of the child must always be of primary consideration when detaining children and families. […].” 3) Art. 48 (2) l 4636/2019/IPA International Protection Act provides for the detention of minors only in exceptional cases. The article states : "2. Juveniles are detained only as a last resort, always in their best interest, and when it is proven that alternative and less restrictive measures cannot be applied. The detention is as short as possible and every effort is made to remove the detention and refer them to accommodation centers suitable for minors and never to penal institutions."

question_text_en: Right of migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for all migrants. Even if strictly regulated and used as a last resort, detention of migrants is not prohibited. 1) Article 83 §1of Law 3386/2005 states, “A third-country national leaving or attempting to leave the Greek territory or entering or attempting to enter in it without the legal formalities is punished with imprisonment of at least three months and a fine of at least one thousand five hundred euros (1.500e) […].” The above disposition is not to include refugees who, according to articles 31 and 32 of the Geneva Convention of 1951, are not to be punished for illegal entry. 2) Law 3907/2011, Article 30 §1 states: “Third-country nationals who are subjected to return procedures […] are detained to prepare the return [...], only if […] other sufficient and less burdensome measures cannot be implemented effectively […]. Detention is applied when: a) there is a risk of absconding or b) the third-country national avoids or hampers the preparation of return or the removal process or c) reasons of national security occur. Detention is imposed and maintained only for the absolute necessary period, as long as removal arrangements are in progress and executed with due diligence." 3) According to Law 4939/2022, Article 50: ?1. A third-country national or a stateless person is not detained for the sole reason that he/she has applied for international protection, as well as because he/she entered illegally and/or resides in the country without legal residence permit. 2. A third-country national or a stateless person who submits an application for international protection, may be detained exceptionally, if necessary, following an individual assessment and on the condition that no alternative measures can be applied […]. The lack of suitable places of detention, the difficulties of ensuring decent living conditions for those in detention, as well as the vulnerability of the applicants […] are taken into account in imposing or prolonging detention."

question_text_en: Right to appeal legality, conditions, and length of detention
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in: 1) Law 3386/2005 Αrticle 76 (Conditions and procedure of administrative expulsion). According to Article 76, Law 3386/2005, "3. ...the detained alien [...] may object to the detention order or the extension of detention before the President […] of the competent administrative court [...].” 2) Law 4939/2022, Αrticle 40 which states: "b) the third-country national or the stateless person whose freedom is restricted, in addition to the rights he/she has according to the Code of Administrative Procedure (L. 2690/1999, A? 45), can also raise objections against the decision to extend the restriction of freedom before the President or the appointed Judge of First Instance of the Administrative Court, in the district of which operates the Reception and Identification Center or the Closed Controlled Structure. […] for the objections procedure, par. 4 and 5 of article 76 of L. 3386/2005 (Α? 212) apply accordingly. […].” 3) Asylum-seekers have extended rights of appeal. L 4375/2016 introduced a procedure for automatic judicial review of the decisions ordering or prolonging the detention of an asylum seeker. IPA (new L. 4939/2022 - Asylum Code) also provides for an ex-officio judicial control of the detention decision of asylum seekers. The procedure is largely based on the procedure already in place for the automatic judicial review of the extension of detention of third-country nationals in view of return under L 3907/2011. Apart from the automatic judicial review procedure, asylum seekers may challenge detention through “objections against detention” before the Administrative Court, which is the only legal remedy provided by national legislation to this end. Objections against detention are not examined by a court composition but solely by the President of the Administrative Court, whose decision is non-appealable.

question_text_en: Right to an individualized detention decision.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in the Law 4939/2022, Article 50, which states: "2. A third-country national or a stateless person who submits an application for international protection, may be detained exceptionally, if necessary, following an individual assessment and on the condition that no alternative measures can be applied […]." Also, according to article 76 par. 3 of L. 3386/2005: "If the (third country) alien is considered to be suspect of fleeing or dangerous to public order or avoids or obstructs the preparation of his/her departure, […] his/her temporary detention is ordered, until a decision of deportation is issued, within three (3) days. […]”.

question_text_en: Right to be free from torture and inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in: 1) The Greek Constitution, Article 7 §2: "Torture, any bodily harm, health injury or use of psychological violence, as well as any other breach of human dignity is prohibited and punished by law." 2) Article 137A of the Greek Criminal Code protects the right of prohibition of torture in general terms. This right is also protected under article 78A of L. 3386/2005 which states that: “An expulsion is not ordered, if reasons of non-refoulement apply and the return could subjected the alien to torture under article 3 of the Convention against Torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment ratified by Law 1782/1988, or under Article 7 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights ratified by Law 2462/1997, or under Articles 31 and 33 of the Geneva Convention relating to the Status of Refugees of 1951, ratified by Decree 3989/1959, or under Article 3 of the European Convention on Human Rights ratified by Law 53/1974. In this case, the competent authority of article 76 §2 of Law 3386/2005 (Police Director or competent Police Officer) orders the non-removal of the alien on humanitarian grounds [...]”.

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in 1) Law No. 3169/2003 provides regulations and conditions under which firearms can be used. This law allows the use of firearms where there is a threat of an armed attack against a police officer or another person and the use of firearms is proportionate to the severity of the threat. It also says in article 3 para 5(d) : "“5. The use of firearms for reasons of immobilization of a person is permitted, if required: [...] d. To prevent an illegal entry or exit in/from the country of persons who engage in illicit trafficking in human beings or things and carry weapons [...]” The use of force with intent to kill or incapacitate is prohibited under this law if there is a serious threat of harming a third person from a missed shot or ricocheting bullet; the use of force is directed against an armed group and could hurt unarmed people; a child is the target of the use of force, unless using such force is the only means to avert death; or a person flees after being asked to submit to a lawful search. 2) Regulation (EU) 2016/399, Preamble (note no 7) says: “Border checks should be carried out in such a way as to fully respect human dignity. Border control should be carried out in a professional and respectful manner and be proportionate to the objectives pursued.” Article 7 says: “1. Border guards shall, in the performance of their duties, fully respect human dignity, in particular in cases involving vulnerable persons. Any measures taken in the performance of their duties shall be proportionate to the objectives pursued by such measures." 3) While not binding law, the 2004 Code of Police Ethics says that the police "shall respect every person’s right to life and security. Police do not inflict, instigate or tolerate acts of torture and inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment and reports cases of violations of human rights."

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of lethal force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in 1) Law No. 3169/2003 provides regulations and conditions under which firearms can be used. This law allows the use of firearms where there is a threat of an armed attack against a police officer or another person and the use of firearms is proportionate to the severity of the threat. It also says in article 3 para 5(d) : "“5. The use of firearms for reasons of immobilization of a person is permitted, if required: [...] d. To prevent an illegal entry or exit in/from the country of persons who engage in illicit trafficking in human beings or things and carry weapons [...]” The use of force with intent to kill or incapacitate is prohibited under this law if there is a serious threat of harming a third person from a missed shot or ricocheting bullet; the use of force is directed against an armed group and could hurt unarmed people; a child is the target of the use of force, unless using such force is the only means to avert death; or a person flees after being asked to submit to a lawful search. 2) Regulation (EU) 2016/399, Preamble (note no 7) says: “Border checks should be carried out in such a way as to fully respect human dignity. Border control should be carried out in a professional and respectful manner and be proportionate to the objectives pursued.” Article 7 states “1. Border guards shall, in the performance of their duties, fully respect human dignity, in particular in cases involving vulnerable persons. Any measures taken in the performance of their duties shall be proportionate to the objectives pursued by such measures." 3) Whilst not binding law, the 2004 Code of Police Ethics provides that the police "shall respect every person’s right to life and security. Police do not inflict, instigate or tolerate acts of torture and inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment and reports cases of violations of human rights."

question_text_en: Right to be protected from trafficking or smuggling.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in 1) Article 59 para 4 of the Code of Penal Procedure, which states: "in the case of any of the criminal acts of illegal entry/exit into/from the country, possession and use of travel documents or identity cards or residence permits or other forged or genuine documents, issued for another person, illegal work and prostitution or other act of facilitating them, allegedly committed by a victim of a crime under articles 323A, 348 par. 2, 348A, 348B, 348Γ, 349 and 351Α of the Penal Code, of article 29 par. 5 and 6 and of article 30 of L. 4251/2014, due to the conduct of the perpetrator of the above acts, the misdemeanor prosecutor, after the preliminary examination or the ex officio preliminary investigation, postpones by his/her act any further action against the victim until the end of the criminal prosecution for the crime committed against the victim, with the consent of the Appellate Prosecutor. After the irrevocable trial of any of the above crimes committed against the victim, if the decision is a conviction, no criminal prosecution is brought against the latter for the aforementioned acts. The prosecutor, however, may with the consent of the appellate prosecutor definitely refrain from the criminal prosecution, even if the decision is not a conviction or if the complaint is placed in the file of unknown perpetrators, if from the evidence of the case file it is judged that the execution of the criminal act was a consequence of the fact that the alleged perpetrator was victim of human trafficking." 2) Articles 49-56 of L. 4251/2014 (Migration Code), which are applied for both victims of smuggling and of human trafficking.

question_text_en: Right to maintain citizenship status after convictions.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in Law 3284/2004, Article 17. According to this article, only under the following conditions the naturalized migrant can be deprived of Green citizenship: ''1.a. Anyone who has undertaken public service in a foreign state and, following an invitation from the Minister of the Interior, Public Administration and Decentralization to him to refrain within a specified period from this service, as contrary to the interests of the country, adheres to it, and b. Whoever, during his stay abroad, has acted for the benefit of a foreign state, acts incompatible with the status of a Greek and contrary to the interests of Greece.''

question_text_en: Right of economic migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right, in Greek Nationality Code (Law 3284/2004), Article 5. According to Article 5, anyone who fulfill the specified conditions, such as being an adult, having a certain length of legal residence, not having been convicted of certain offenses, not be subject to deportation and hold one of the residence permits specified by law are eligible to apply for naturalization.

question_text_en: Right of humanitarian migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in Greek Nationality Code (Law 3284/2004), Article 5. According to Article 5, anyone who fulfill the specified conditions, such as being an adult, having a certain length of legal residence, not having been convicted of certain offenses, not be subject to deportation and hold one of the residence permits specified by law are eligible to apply for naturalization.

question_text_en: Right of family migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in Greek Nationality Code (Law 3284/2004), Article 5. According to Article 5, anyone who fulfill the specified conditions, such as being an adult, having a certain length of legal residence, not having been convicted of certain offenses, not be subject to deportation and hold one of the residence permits specified by law are eligible to apply for naturalization. Persons who arrive in Greece through family reunification procedures under the asylum legislation or the Migration Code have the right to apply for the Greek nationality if they fulfill the conditions set in the Code of Greek Nationality. For the spouse, according to article 30 of the Code of Greek Nationality, which states that: "Marriage does not result in the acquisition or loss of the Greek nationality”, the same conditions as to the maintainer apply. The same is valid also for the other adult family members. Only for minor children of the naturalized, the acquisition of Greek nationality takes place automatically, according to article 11 of the Code of Greek Nationality, which states that: “The child of an alien who is naturalized becomes Greek, without any other wording, if on the day of his/her parent’s swearing, he/she is minor, unmarried and resides permanently in the country”. Moreover, for minor children, in case their parent(s) are not naturalized, the conditions regarding acquisition of the Greek nationality set in articles 1A (by birth and attendance of school in Greece) and 1B (by school attendance in Greece) of the Code of Greek Nationality also apply.

question_text_en: Right to dual nationality.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in: 1) the Civil Code, Article 31. 2) Law 4251/2014, Article 2. Greek nationality law allows an alien who acquires the Greek nationality to also retain his/her original nationality, without examining whether the law of his/her original nationality does not allow dual nationality. This derives from the fact that the provision of article 5 of the Code of Greek Nationality does not include among the conditions of acquisition of the Greek nationality the dual citizenship precondition.

question_text_en: Right to freedom to hold opinion.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right, in the Constitution of Greece, Articles 5 and 13. Articles 5 and 13 state, "1. Everyone has the right to freely develop his/her personality and to participate in the social, economic and political life of the Country, as long as he/she does not infringe the rights of others and does not violate the Constitution or morals, and “1. Freedom of religious conscience is inviolable. The enjoyment of civil and political rights does not depend on one’s religious beliefs."

question_text_en: Right to freedom of expression.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right, in the Constitution of Greece, Articles 5 and 14. Articles 5 states that: "1. Everyone has the right to freely develop his/her personality and to participate in the social, economic and political life of the Country, as long as he/she does not infringe the rights of others and does not violate the Constitution or morals. 2. All those who are in the Greek Territory enjoy the absolute protection of their life, honor and freedom, without distinction of nationality, race, language and religious or political beliefs. Exceptions are allowed in the cases provided for by international law. It is prohibited to extradite a foreigner who is prosecuted for his action in favor of freedom. 3. Personal freedom is inviolable. No one is persecuted or arrested or imprisoned or in any other way restricted, except when and as prescribed by law.'' Article 14 states: “1. Everyone may express his/her views, orally, in writing and through the press in accordance with the laws of the state. The press is free. Censorship and any other preventive measure are prohibited.[…] 3. Confiscation of newspapers and other brochures, either before or after circulation, is prohibited..."

question_text_en: Right to freedom of association.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right, in the Constitution of Greece, Articles 5 and 14. Articles 5 states that: "1. Everyone has the right to freely develop his/her personality and to participate in the social, economic and political life of the Country, as long as he/she does not infringe the rights of others and does not violate the Constitution or morals. 2. All those who are in the Greek Territory enjoy the absolute protection of their life, honor and freedom, without distinction of nationality, race, language and religious or political beliefs. Exceptions are allowed in the cases provided for by international law. It is prohibited to extradite a foreigner who is prosecuted for his action in favor of freedom. 3. Personal freedom is inviolable. No one is persecuted or arrested or imprisoned or in any other way restricted, except when and as prescribed by law.'' Article 14 states: “1. Everyone may express his/her views, orally, in writing and through the press in accordance with the laws of the state. The press is free. Censorship and any other preventive measure are prohibited.[…] 3. Confiscation of newspapers and other brochures, either before or after circulation, is prohibited..."

question_text_en: Right to freedom of assembly.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for irregular migrants. However, national law in Greece protects this right for regular migrants in: 1) The Migration Code (Law 4251/2014), Article 21A which states that: “Employees holding a uniform residence permit shall enjoy equal treatment with nationals in respect of: [...] (d) the right to strike and to be involved in trade unions in accordance with national law, freedom of association, accession and participation in an employee's or employer's organization or any professional organization, including the advantages provided by such organizations, including the right to negotiate and conclude collective labor agreements, and without prejudice to the provisions regarding public order and public security.” In Greece, the establishment of an association is controlled by the competent Court in accordance to the provisions of articles 78 et seq. of the Greek Civil Code.According to the Greek jurisprudence, the constitutional right of freedom of association extends, in combination of article 12 and 25 of the Constitution, also to aliens. Together with the provisions of articles 11 and 16 of the European Convention of Human Rights as well as those of the No 87 International Convention of the International Labor Organization on the freedom of association (ratified by L. 4204/1961), migrants' rights are protected.

category: Thought, conscience, and religion or belief
question_text_en: Right of freedom of thought, conscience and religion or belief.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Migration Code (L. 4251/2014) Article 70 (Conditions for family reunification) talks about the resource conditions: "2.To exercise the right ..., the person concerned should prove the family relationship with the members of his/her family for whom he/she is requesting reunification in Greece, as well as that he/she fulfills, cumulatively, the following conditions: a. Has an accommodation capable of meeting his/her needs and the ones of his/her family members for whom he/she is requesting the reunification […].b. Has a stable and regular personal income, sufficient for his/her needs and of his/her family's needs, which does not come from recourse to the country's social assistance system. This income cannot be lower than the annual earnings of the person paid the minimum wage, according to national legislation, increased by 20% for the spouse and by 15% for each child. The above increase of 15% for each child is not required in the case where both spouses legally reside in Greece. c. Has full health insurance for all the risks covered for the respective categories of Greek workers, which can also cover his/her family members. […]”

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to access criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in: 1) The Greek Constitution, Article 20, which states that "Everyone has the right to legal protection of the courts and can thereby express his/her views on his/her rights or interests, as provided by law." 2) Law 4443/2016 incorporating the Council Directive 2000/43/EC of 29 June 2000 implementation of the principle of equal treatment between persons irrespective of racial or ethnic origin. 3) Law 4478/2017 which incorporated Directive 2012/29/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 October 2012 establishing minimum standards on the rights, support, and protection of victims of crime. Article 54 states: “1. The purpose of this law is to ensure that victims of crime receive appropriate information, support, and protection to be able to participate in criminal proceedings. Victims are recognized and treated in a respectful, sensitive, tailored, professional, and non-discriminatory manner as regards ethnic group, color, nationality, language, religion, social group, political or other opinion, financial state, age, gender, sexual orientation, identity or other gender characteristics, disability or other state, in every contact with public services […] or a competent authority, operating within the context of criminal proceedings. The rights set out in this law shall apply to all victims in a non-discriminatory manner, irrespective of ethnicity or nationality and their residence status. […].”4) 14 Penal Procedure ''1. Every person has the right to have his case tried by an independent and impartial tribunal that operates legally. This right is guaranteed by the institutions of exclusion, exception and abstention of judicial persons...'' 5) Law 4052/2012 deals with the illegally employed persons' right to complain and states in its Article 83 §1“ that "Illegally employed persons can, like any legally employed worker, submit [...] to the local labor center […] any complaint provided for by national law against their employer.”

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to immigration status or relief from expulsion.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in: 1) Law 4251/2014 (Migration Code), Article 19A, Article 25 §5c, Article 50. Article 19A states that, “1. By decision of the Minister of Interior and Administrative Reconstruction, a residence permit for humanitarian reasons is granted to third-country nationals who are in Greece and fall into one of the following categories: a. Are victims of trafficking in human beings who do not fall under the provisions of articles 49-53 of L. 4251/2014 and if a relevant characterization act is issued by the competent Public Prosecutor... b. Are victims and substantial witnesses of criminal acts as prescribed in articles 81A, 187, 187A, 309 and 310 of the Penal Code...c. Are victims of domestic violence, as defined by L. 3500/2006... d. Are third-country nationals employed either under particularly abusive working conditions or as minors, in accordance with article 89 of L. 4052/2012.” Article 25 §5c states that: "“[...] third-country nationals who: [...] (c) are illegally present in the country and report offenses committed by a criminal organization of article 187 of the Penal Code, provided that […] their deportation is suspended with a relevant order of the Public Prosecutor until the issuance of an irrevocable decision on the reported acts […], a special document of (temporary) legal residence for a duration of one year is then granted, with possible renewal for an equal period of time, if the same conditions are met. This special residence permit gives also access to employed activities […].” National law in Greece provides protection of vulnerable groups, unaccompanied minors and victims of trafficking through regularization in some cases. Art. 50 L4251/2014 states that:''1. The competent Prosecutor of First Instance or the competent Police Authority or the competent social support agencies, provided for in p.d. 233/2003, as it applies, but also any of the bodies referred to in article 49 of this Code, notify the third country citizen - victim of human trafficking or illegal immigration smuggling that he is entitled to submit a request to be granted a residence permit, in accordance with the aforementioned, providing him with the necessary information for this purpose. 2. In the case of a third-country national who is a victim of human trafficking or illegal immigration who is an unaccompanied minor, the competent Prosecutorial Authority shall take all necessary steps to determine his identity and nationality and to establish the fact that he is unaccompanied, making every effort to locate his family as soon as possible and immediately take the necessary steps to secure his legal representation and, if necessary, his representation in the criminal proceedings. The competent Juvenile Prosecutor or, where there is no Juvenile Prosecutor, the competent First Instance Prosecutor, if the minor's family cannot be found or if he judges that under the specific circumstances his repatriation does not serve his interest, he may order any appropriate measure for the protection until the issuance of a decision by the Court, to which it must be addressed within thirty (30) days, for the appointment of a Commissioner, in accordance with the provisions of articles 1532, 1534 and 1592 of the Civil Code.''

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: Nation law in Greece protects this right in: 1) Law 4251/2014 - Code of Migration and Social Inclusion and other provisions, Article 19A which states that residence permits for humanitarian reasons can be granted to: "third-country nationals who were employed either under particularly abusive working conditions or as minors." It also establishes different durations for the initial residence permits based on the circumstances. Article 19A's Articles 49§2 - 50§2 deal with the granting of residence permit for humanitarian reasons as it relates to children victims of human trafficking and smuggling. Article 49§2 states: "Especially for minors - victims of trafficking in human beings or smuggling of migrants, the […] (reflection) period may be extended for two more months following a decision of the competent Public Prosecutor's Office and on the basis of the minor's best interest." Article 50§2 states: "In the case of unaccompanied minor - third-country nationals victims of human trafficking or smuggling, the competent Prosecutor takes the necessary steps to establish his/her identity and nationality and the fact that he/she is unaccompanied and makes every effort to locate his/her family as quickly as possible and […] ensure legal representation, including, if needed, representation in criminal proceedings. The competent Juvenile Prosecutor or, where there is no Juvenile Prosecutor, the competent First Instance Prosecutor, if the minor's family cannot be found or if he/she judges that under the specific circumstances minor’s repatriation does not serve his/her interest, may order any appropriate measure for his/her protection until the issuance of a decision by the Court [...].” 2) Law 4939/2022 - Ratification of Code of Legislation on the reception, international protection of third country nationals and stateless persons and the temporary protection in the event of a mass influx of displaced aliens. This law which ratifies the Code of Legislation on the reception, international protection of third country nationals and stateless persons, and temporary protection in the event of a mass influx of displaced aliens, includes provisions specifically focused on the protection of migrant children which include: ensuring decent accommodation in special reception structures for unaccompanied children; representing and assisting the child in all judicial and administrative procedures; accompanying the child to clinics or hospitals; guaranteeing that the child is safe during their stay in the country; ensuring that legal assistance and interpretation services are provided to the child; providing access to psychological support and health care when needed; taking care of enrolling the child in formal or non-formal education; taking necessary steps to assign custody of the child to an appropriate family (foster family), in accordance with the applicable legal provisions; ensuring that the child’s political, philosophical and religious beliefs are respected and freely expressed and developed; and behaving with sympathy and respect to the unaccompanied child. As an example, Article 37 regarding reception of international protection applicants "applies to minors, unaccompanied or not, and to separated minors, regardless of whether they have submitted an application for international protection, subject to any more favorable provisions." In Article 40- Submission to the reception procedure, which implies being in a state of restriction of freedom, it says: "Special care is taken for persons belonging to vulnerable groups and in particular for unaccompanied minors." In Article 41- registration and medical examination- it says: "special care" is given "to cover the special needs of families with children under fourteen years of age, and especially infants and toddlers." Some of the other articles of this law that mentions protections for migrant children include: a) Article 43: further referral and transfer where special consideration is given to the principle of family unity and of the best interest of the child. b) Article 44: Obligations of the administration during reception and identification procedures to ensure the stay of children in private areas. c) Article 52: Detention of vulnerable people and applicants with special reception needs where is mentionned that unaccompanied minors are detained only in exceptional circumstances. d) Article 63 Minors which states: "1: The best interest of the minor is the primary concern of the competent authorities when implementing the provisions of the code. Minors are guaranteed an adequate standard of living for their physical, mental, intellectual, moral, and social development." e) Article 80 par. 3e: Applications of Unaccompanied Minors, with special reference to minors under 15 years old and minors victims of trafficking and other forms of violence who are always examined under the normal procedure . f) Article 82: Personal interview. g) Article 97: Right of appeal. h) Article 132: Representation of unaccompanied minors who are beneficiaries of temporary protection.

question_text_en: Right of women migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in: 1) Law 4939/2022, Article 52: Detention of vulnerable people and applicants with special reception needs, which states, "4. Women who are detained shall be housed separately from men, unless the latter are members of their family and subject to the consent of all persons concerned. Exceptions may also apply to the use of common areas designed for recreational or social activities, including the provision of meals. The competent authorities ensure that the detention of women during pregnancy and for three (3) months after childbirth is avoided, and that their transfer and accommodation in appropriate accommodation facilities is pursued." This is expanded upon further in Article 82, detailing procedures for the personal interview of women, that states, "5. When the interview concerns a woman, special care is taken so that it is conducted by a female operator, in the presence of a female interpreter, if requested."

question_text_en: Rights of migrants with disabilities to special protection.
citation_text_en: National law in Greece protects this right in: 1) Law 4251/2014 ? Code of Migration and Social Inclusion and other provisions. According to Article 19A par. 2e: "e. To persons suffering from serious health problems. The existence of serious health problems, as well as the duration of the treatment, are confirmed by a recent medical certificate. [...] Precondition for the granting of a residence permit for persons suffering from serious health problems is the possession by the applicant of a valid residence permit. The duration of the initial residence permit is two years and can be renewed for up to two years each time if the same conditions are met, otherwise it can be renewed for one of the reasons of this Code." 2) Law 4939/2022 - the Code of Migration and Social Inclusion. Article 1 provides definitions of vulnerable groups and states that: " 'applicants in need of special procedural guarantees’ are applicants whose ability to enjoy the rights and comply with the obligations provided for in this Code is limited due to special circumstances concerning their personal situation and in particular their state of health.” In Article 52 - detention of vulnerable people and applicants with special reception needs- says: "health, including mental health, of applicants in detention who are vulnerable is of primary concern for the competent authorities." In Article 83, it says: "3: Applicants are required to appear in person before the Receiving Authorities, without delay, to apply for international protection...4: In case of force majeure, such as serious ilness or serious physical disability [...] that made it impossible for the applicant to appear in person, this obligation is suspended for the duration of the force majeure [...]." In Article 129- Accomodation centers, social assistance, medical care- it says: "4: Cases of persons with special needs, such as infants, elder persons, unaccompanied minors, sick persons, injured, as well as persons who have suffered torture, rape, or other serious forms of mental, physical or sexual violence, are treated as a matter of priority." 2) L 4636/2019 on international protection Act (IPA), entered into force in January 2020 and has made significant amendements to the definition of vulnerable persons and persons in need of special procedural amendments. According to Articles 39(5)(d) and 58(1) IPA the following groups are considered as vulnerable groups: “children; unaccompanied children; direct relatives of victims of shipwrecks (parents, siblings, children, husbands/wives); disabled persons; elderly; pregnant women; single parents with minor children; victims of human trafficking; persons with serious illness; persons with cognitive or mental disability and victims of torture, rape or other serious forms of psychological, physical or sexual violence such as victims of female genital mutilation.” Persons with posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) have been deleted as a category of persons belonging to vulnerable groups. According to Article 58(2) IPA “The assessment of vulnerability shall take place during the identification process of the Art. 39 of this law without prejudice to the assessment of international protection needs.” According to article 58(4) L 4636/2019 “Only the persons belonging to vulnerable groups are considered to have special reception needs and thus benefit from the special reception conditions.” Article 58(3) IPA provides that “[…] the special condition of applicants, even if it becomes apparent at a later stage of the examination of the application for international protection, is taken into account throughout this procedure […]” According to article 67 (1) IPA relating to special procedural guarantees “The Receiving Authorities shall assess within a reasonable period of time after an application for international protection is submitted, or at any point of the procedure the relevant needs arise, whether the applicant requires special procedural guarantees, due to their age, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, psychological disorder or because they are a victim of torture, rape or other serious forms of psychological, physical or sexual violence."

question_text_en: What country are you coding?
citation_text_en: Hungary

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to vote in local and/or regional elections.
citation_text_en: National Law in Hungary recognizes and protects this right in 1) the Constitution of Hungary, Article 8, which states that "everyone has the right to freedom of peaceful assembly." 2) Act LV of 2018 on the Right of Assembly, Article 3(3), which stipulates that settled migrants can be the organizers of said assembly, commiserate with citizens.

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to stand for election.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for all migrants. However, national law in Hungary protects this right for European Economic Area migrants in 1) the Constitution of Hungary, Article XXIII, which states that "(1) Every adult Hungarian citizen shall have the right to vote and to be voted for in elections of Members of the National Assembly, of local government representatives and mayors and of Members of the European Parliament. (2) Every adult citizen of another Member State of the European Union (EU) with domicile in Hungary shall have the right to vote and to be voted for in elections of local government representatives and mayors and of Members of the European Parliament. (3) Every adult person recognised as a refugee, immigrant or resident in Hungary shall have the right to vote in elections of local government representatives and mayors." Long-term migrants with an immigration permit, EU citizens and their family members if they are registered under their right of free movement and have a registered address in Hungary, and refugees are also entitled to vote in local municipal elections. However, only Hungarian citizens have the right to participate in national general elections (even if they have multiple citizenship), and only members of a traditional national minority who are Hungarian citizens can elect their local/regional or national governments (bodies of cutural autonomy).

question_text_en: Right to equal protection of the law before courts.
citation_text_en: National Law in Hungary protects this right in 1) the Hungarian Constitution, Article XV, which states that, “(1) Everyone shall be equal before the law. Every human being shall have legal capacity. (2) Hungary shall guarantee fundamental rights to everyone without discrimination and in particular without discrimination on the grounds of race, colour, sex, disability, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or any other status. (3) Women and men shall have equal rights.” 2) The Code on Criminal Proceedings, Articles 1, and 44. Article 44 stipulates procedures for when the accused does not speak Hungarian language. 3) Act LXXX of 2003 on Legal Aid, Article 1, which stipulates provisions to provide legal aid to those who require it4) Act CXXV of 2003 on Equal Treatment and the Promotion of Equal Opportunities, Article 1.

question_text_en: Right to government-provided counsel in proceedings related to migrant status.
citation_text_en: National Law in Hungary protects this right in 1) Act LXXX of 2003 on Legal Aid, Articles 3-5, 17, and 64 set broad guidelines for citizens and migrants for who can request legal aid, and under what circumstances. 2) Act II of 2007, Article 92/A, 92/B. Article 92/A and 92/B of Act II of 2007 sets guidelines for the right to a legal counsel for migrants, and whether an interpreter can be used. However, there are some conditions on the use of legal aid, and who can qualify for free legal aid. 3) The Code on Criminal Proceedings, Article 44(d).

question_text_en: Right to government-provided interpretation in criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: National law in Hungary protects this right in Act XC of 2017 on Procedure for Criminal Proceedings. Article 8. Article 8 states, "(1) The language of criminal proceedings shall be Hungarian. Members of nationalities living in Hungary and recognised by law may use their national mother tongue in criminal proceedings. (2) No one shall be disadvantaged because he or she does not know Hungarian. (3) Everyone shall have the right to use his or her mother tongue in criminal proceedings. 78. § (1) If a person participating in criminal proceedings wishes to use his or her non-Hungarian mother tongue, his or her national minority mother tongue or any other mother tongue specified in an international treaty promulgated by law, an interpreter, preferably one with an adequate knowledge of a legal language, shall be used."

question_text_en: Right to be protected from prosecution for unauthorized entry.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. If the migrant commits the criminal offence of illegal entry as specified in the Criminal Code, e.g. , illegal crossing of the border fence (Article 352/A of the Criminal Code), damage to the border fence (Article 352/B of the Criminal Code), obstruction of construction work related to the border fence (Article 352/C of the Criminal Code), the migrant is not exempt from civil and criminal sanctions and will be prosecuted for damages.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to public adult education institutions.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right of access to public adult education institutions regardless of status.
citation_text_en: Nation law in Hungary protects this right in 1) Act CCIV of 2011 on National Tertiary Education. 2) Act CXC of 2011 on National Public Education. 3) Act LXXVII of 2013 on Adult Education. Persons of compulsory school age who have some right of residence (legal residents) have access to education and training in essentially the same way as Hungarian citizens. Children of irregular migrants are excluded.

question_text_en: Right to be free from discrimination on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: Nation law in Hungary protects this right in 1) Act CCIV of 2011 on National Tertiary Education. Particularly, Article 39 of Act CCIV of 2011 on National Tertiary Education states that, "39 (1) Every Hungarian citizen has the right to study at an institution of higher education under the conditions set out in this Act, with a Hungarian state scholarship, a Hungarian state partial scholarship [hereinafter together referred toas Hungarian state (partial) scholarship] or a self-financed course. This right shall also apply to a)persons with the right of free movement and residence according to a special law, b) stateless persons, refugees, subsidiary protected, temporary protected, tolerated migrants, immigrants, settled third country nationals not covered by point a) living in the territory of Hungary, c) foreign nationals who are treated in the same way as Hungarian nationals on the basis of an international agreement, d) nationals of countries in which Hungarian citizens may receive higher education services on the basis of reciprocity, e) persons who are subject to the Act on Hungarians Living neighboring States (Preferential Treatment Act) but who do not have Hungarian citizenship or the right of free movement and residence, f) third-country nationals as defined in the Act on the Entry and Residence of Third-Country Nationals, provided that they are not subject to the Preferential Treatment Act and do not have Hungarian citizenship g) a third-country national holding a permit for work and residence requiring a high level of qualification (European Union (EU) Blue Card), h)third-country nationals holding a single permit (labour and residence permit in one). (2) A person not referred to in paragraph 1 may pursue his/her studies only on a self-financed basis." 2) Act CXC of 2011 on National Public Education. 3) Act LXXVII of 2013 on Adult Education. Foreign nationals can have equal treatment with Hungarian nationals in tertiary education if they are union citizens or long-term third-country national residents or there are special norms or EU directives that grant them this right.

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after convictions.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. According to Article 59 of the Criminal Code, "a non-Hungarian offender whose stay in Hungary is undesirable shall be expelled from the territory of Hungary." In practice, it falls within the discretionary power of the authorities to decide whether a person is a threat to the public order of Hungary and must be expelled. In practice, in 2020 there were 287 court expulsion orders effectuated against third-country nationals (TCNs), in 2021 there were 482 court expulsion orders effectuated against the same TCNs. The overall number of expulsion (including also orders passed by the immigration authorities and not only the courts) amounted to 882 in 2020 and 1120 in 2021.

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of torture or inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in Hungary Protects this right in 1) the Constitution of Hungar Article XIV, which states that, “Hungary shall grant the right of asylum, upon application, to non-Hungarian nationals who are persecuted in their home country or in the country of their habitual residence." 2) Act LXXX of 2007 on Asylum, Article 45, which states, “if the applicant would be in danger of being persecuted or subjected to any of the behaviors defined in Article XIV(3) of the Fundamental Law in his or her country of origin, non-refoulement shall apply.”3) Act II of 2007 on the entry and residence of third-country nationals.

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of persecution.
citation_text_en: National law in Hungary protects this right in 1) the Constitution of Hungary, Article XIV, which states, "Hungary shall grant the right of asylum, upon application, to non-Hungarian nationals who are persecuted in their home country or in the country of their habitual residence on account of their race, national origin, membership of a particular social group, religion or political opinion, or where there is a well-founded fear of being persecuted directly, if neither their country of origin nor any other country offers protection." 2) Act LXXX of 2007 on Asylum, which states that, "a non-refoulement shall apply if the applicant would be in danger of being persecuted or of being subjected to any of the behaviors defined in Article XIV(3) of the Fundamental Law in his or her country of origin on racial or religious grounds, on grounds of nationality, membership of a particular social group or political opinions, and there is no safe third country which would accept them." 3) Act II of 2007 on the Entry and Residence of Third-Country Nationals.

question_text_en: Right to not return to a deprivations of fundamental human rights.
citation_text_en: National law in Hungary protects this right in 1) the Constitution of Hungary, Article XIV which states, "no one may be expelled to a State or extradited to a State where there is a risk that he or she would be sentenced to death, tortured or subjected to other inhuman treatment or punishment." 2) Act II of 2007 on the Entry and Residence of Third-Country Nationals, Article 45 which states, "(1): "Refoulement or expulsion may not be ordered or carried out to the territory of a country that is not considered a safe country of origin or a safe third country for the applicant, so in particular where the third country citizen's race, religion, nationality or belonging to a specific social group or political opinion would be exposed to the risk of persecution, and also to the territory of a state or the border of a territory where there is a compelling reason to fear that the repatriated or expelled third-country national is subject to the action as defined in Article XIV (3) of the Basic Law (non-refoulement)." 3) Act LXXX on Asylum.

question_text_en: Right to be advised of availability of asylum before expulsion.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The authorities are not obliged to provide information on the right to asylum, but in certain cases they must detect ex officio that an alien is in need of international protection because he or she belongs to a vulnerable group (in particular unaccompanied minors) and apply the nonrefoulement requirement in the removal procedure.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from chain refoulement.
citation_text_en: National law in Hungary protects this right in 1) Act LXXX of 2007 on Asylum, Article 2, which prevents removal except to "a country for which the determining authority is satisfied that the applicant will be treated in accordance with the following principles: (ia) his/her life and freedom will not be threatened on grounds of race, religion, nationality, membership of a particular social group or political opinion, or he/she will not be exposed to serious risk of harm; (ib) respect the principle of non-refoulement in accordance with the Geneva Convention; (ic) recognise and apply the rule of international law that an applicant may not be expelled to the territory of a country where he or she would be subject to conduct defined in Article XIV(3) of the Constitution (Fundamental Law); and (id) the possibility of applying for recognition as a refugee is guaranteed and, if recognised as a refugee, protection in accordance with the Geneva Convention is guaranteed. 2) Article XIV(2) of the Fundamental Law, an alien residing in Hungary territory may only be expelled on the basis of a lawful decision. Group expulsions are prohibited. Paragraph (3) provides that no person shall be expelled or extradited to a State where he or she risks being subjected to the death penalty, torture or other inhuman treatment or punishment. 3) Act II of 2007 on Entry and Residence of Third-country nationals, which states that, "The alien policing authority is obliged to examine the requirement of non-refoulement in its procedure for ordering and enforcing refoulement or expulsion."

question_text_en: Right to protection against expulsion except following a legal judgment.
citation_text_en: National Law protects this right in 1) the Constitution of Hungary, Article XIV states that a foreigner can only be expelled based on a lawful decision. 2) Act II of 2007, Article 87/M states that the decision of the immigration authority contains all data necessary to identify the acting immigration enforcement authority, the client and the case, the decision of the authority, the position of the specialist authority, information about the use of legal remedies and the procedural costs incurred, as well as the established a justification covering the facts, the evidence, the justification of the professional authority’s position, the reasons for the consideration and decision, as well as the indication of the legal provisions that underpin it. 3) Act C of 2012 on Penal Code, which addresses the duration and conditions of expulsion as part of criminal sentencing. It outlines cases where expulsion is mandatory, the duration of expulsion, and the start of the expulsion period.

question_text_en: Right to submit reasons against expulsion and have case reviewed before deportation.
citation_text_en: National Law protects this right in 1) Section 42(1) of Act II of 2007 on the Entry and Residence of Third-Country Nationals, which states that, if the aliens authority finds that a third-country national legally residing in the territory of the Hungary no longer has the right to reside, in its decision rejecting the application for a residence permit or withdrawing his or her residence document, it shall expel the third-country national from the territory of the Member States of the European Union, He or she may appeal against the expulsion decision rejecting the application for a residence permit or withdrawing the residence document. 45/B. § (1) The aliens authority shall not expel an illegally staying third-country national who will be readmitted by another Member State of the European Union on the basis of a bilateral readmission agreement concluded before 13 January 2009 or under another agreement. (2) The decision to return pursuant to the readmission agreement shall be taken by order of the aliens authority, against which the third-country national may lodge an enforcement objection within twenty-four hours of notification of the order.
