question_text_en: What country are you coding?
citation_text_en: Mexico

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to vote in local and/or regional elections.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.The right of freedom of assembly is recognized as a human right for everyone in Mexican territory; however, the Constitution provides that only citizens can exercise this right to participate in political matters of the country.

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to stand for election.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. According to Articles 33 and 35-1 of the Constitution, only naturalized citizens and citizens have the right to vote in Mexican elections.

question_text_en: Right to equal protection of the law before courts.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right for administrative, civil and criminal courts in the Migration Law, Articles 6, 11, 12, and 66.

question_text_en: Right to government-provided counsel in proceedings related to migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The Immigration Law recognizes the right to legal representation in their migratory procedure. However, legal aid is not provided by the Government of Mexico. The Law only provides that the agents of the National Institute of Immigration can collaborate with migrants, and facilitate the legal representation of non-governmental organizations.

question_text_en: Right to government-provided interpretation in criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in the Criminal Proceedings Code, Articles 14 and 45, which provides that interpretation will be made available for asylum and general immigrations proceedings, the cost of which will be covered by the state.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from prosecution for unauthorized entry.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. National law in Mexico does not provide for criminal sanctions for irregular migration in Migration Law, Article 2, which states that irregular migrants will not be criminally charged for unauthorized entry. However, aside from asylum seekers, other migrants can be charged with administrative offenses, including deportation and prohibition of entry (Article 144) or in the event that they seek regularization, fines (Articles 145 and 146).

question_text_en: Right to equal access to public adult education institutions.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) Article 4 of the Constitution, which states that every family has the right to enjoy a decent and respectable house. The constitution also stipulates that the law will create instruments and support necessary to achieve this objective. 2) Article 3 of the Housing law, which establishes that "the provisions of the Law require restrictions under the principles of equity and social inclusion so that every person, regardless of origin, gender, age, disability, social or economic status, conditions of health, religion, opinions, preferences or marital status, can exercise their right to housing." Under this provision, migrants can enter social programs for housing.

question_text_en: Right of access to public adult education institutions regardless of status.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) the Constitution, Article 3. 2) The Migration Law, Article 8, which recognizes the right to education for migrants independent of their migration status. Furthermore, it states the prohibition of establishing greater requirements to access this right than those provided for Mexican citizens. 3) The Education Law, Articles 8, 9(X), and 11. However, children without a regular status that lack a population ID ("CURP") have a difficult time to get certifications and diplomas from schools.

question_text_en: Right to be free from discrimination on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right for regular migrants in 1) Migration Law, Article 8, which recognizes the right of migrants to access to education provided in the public and private sectors, regardless of their migration status. However, the documentation needed to register and study in the National Institute of Adult Education (Instituto Nacional para la Educaci?n de los Adultos) includes an ID such as a passport as well as the "CURP". 2) Education Law, Article 3. Access to education is practically limited to those with a resident status or humanitarian condition status, since a population ID ("CURP") would be required by all institutions in Mexico.

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after convictions.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) the Migration Law, Articles 43, 64, 144. 2) The Regulations of the Migration Law, 244-III. According to articles 64(VI) and 144(IV), the National Institute of Immigration is able to cancel the condition of temporal or permanent resident and order deportation if the person has been sentenced to a serious crime under national criminal laws or international treaties, or if the person could compromise national security or public safety. In addition, the person could be subject to a prohibition of reentry for 5 to 20 years.

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of torture or inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) the Asylum Law, Articles 5, 6, and 28. 2) M?xico, Ley General para Prevenir, Investigar y Sancionar la Tortura y Otros Tratos Crueles, Inhumanos o Degradantes, Diario Oficial de la Federaci?n: 26 June 2017 (Law on Torture), Article 15.. The Law on Torture forbids to deliver, extradite, expel, deport or return to another State to any person when there are well-founded reasons to assume that he would be in danger of being subjected to acts of torture; or that would be tried by exceptional or ad hoc tribunals in the requesting State. Similarly, in the Refugee Law, complementary protection is provided to persons in risk of return to torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment.

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of persecution.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in the Asylum law, Articles 5, 6, and 13.

question_text_en: Right to not return to a deprivations of fundamental human rights.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in the Asylum Law, Articles 6, 13, and 28. Article 6 establishes the non-refoulement principle for those whose life is at risk or they risk torture. Article 13 establishes the protected grounds to be recognized as a refugee. Article 28 allows the possibility of complementary protection to migrants at risk of deprivation of their right to life in their country of origin.

question_text_en: Right to be advised of availability of asylum before expulsion.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) the Migration Law, Articles 13(III), 37(III)(e), 42, 63, 109(II). According to the provisions, migrants have the right to receive information about the right to asylum and authorities the obligation to inform them about this right when they are detained in the immigration detention centers. 2) The Regulation of the Migration Law, Articles 62, 63(1), and 64.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from chain refoulement.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to protection against expulsion except following a legal judgment.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) the Constitution, Article 33. 2) The Migration Law, Articles 70, and 144. 3) The Regulation of the Migration Law, Article 222.

question_text_en: Right to submit reasons against expulsion and have case reviewed before deportation.
citation_text_en: Naitonal law in Mexico protects this right in 1) the Migration Law, Articles 70, and 122. 2) Amparo Trial, Article 2. The right to have their case reviewed by the competent authority before being expelled is guaranteed via amparo trial which has an automatic suspensive effect.

question_text_en: Right of settled migrants to family reunification.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. While Articles 54(I) and 59 of the Migration Law, and Article 20 of the Nationality Law allow for stateless migrants to apply for citizenship after a residency period, the application is not guaranteed to lead to citizenship.

question_text_en: Right to judicial remedy for denials of right to family reunification.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico conditionally protects this right in 1) the Migration Law, Articles 44 and 58. 2) The Regulation of the Migration Law, 107-III, 109-I, and 100-113. 3) The Asylum Law, Article 44 and 58. 4) The Regulation of the Asylum Law, Articles 13, 80, 82. Temporal and permanent residents have the right to family reunification; they can either come with their family or request entry later. Likewise, in cases where a visa is granted for a job offer or for humanitarian reasons, Article 41 of the Migration Law provides the possibility of requesting a visa in the facilities of the National Immigration Institute. Temporary and permanent residents are allowed family reunification for the following members of their families: children of temporary resident and children of their partners (child or adolescents) while they are under their custody; spouse or partner in free union (according to Mexican law); father or mother of the temporary or permanent resident; siblings that are children or adolescents and under the custody of the resident (only for permanent residents). Refugees also have the right to family reunification for their children, spouse or partner in a free union (according to Article 58 of the Asylum Law) and her/his relatives economical dependant of the refugee until second grade; and blood relatives until the fourth grade

question_text_en: Right to recognition of same-sex marital relationships.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) the Federal Law on Administrative Procedure, Articles 53 and 83. 2) The Amparo Law, Article 1. The Federal Law on Administrative Procedure is supplementary to the Migration and the Asylum laws and establishes the possibility to appeal to the courts who issued any decision on family reunification. In addition, it is possible to appeal before the Federal Court of Justice for Tax and Administrative Matters (without the need of exhausting the review established on the Federal Law on Administrative Procedure) or Amparo Law before a Federal Judge.

question_text_en: Right to family reunification without resource conditions
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) the Migration Law, Artilce 167. On December 2015, the Mexican Supreme Court recognized same sex marital relationships. For this reason, as long as the migrant provides a valid marriage certificate, an even though same-sex marriage is not explicitly recognized in the migration framework, the interpretation of definition of the "family" also applies to same sex relationships.

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. National law allows some, but not all temporary migrants to transfer to permanent status in 1) the Migration Law, Articles 53 and 62. 2) The Regulation of the Migration Law, Article 127. Temporary frontier workers, for example, cannot switch from temporary to permanent status.

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services regardless of status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Irregular migrant workers have no way to become lawfully settled (unless they marry a Mexican or a resident; or they have Mexican children). The Government ihas operated temporary programs for regularization in the past, but these special programs are not part of the Migration Law and more like a benefits programs for those who have been living irregularly for years. The last program was open during 2017, with no plans to start another program in the near future.

question_text_en: Right of access to public housing programs.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) the Federal Labor Law, Articles 2, 5, 21, 25, 26, 42, 56, and 837-846. 2) Amparo Law, Articles 103 and 107. 3) The Migration Law, Articles 10 and 11. Migrants may request compensation or sue their employer via the labor authorities and courts just as any other Mexican citizen.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to free primary education for migrant children.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) the Constitution, Article 4, which states that, every individual regardless of their nationality or migration status shall receive health care. 2) The Migration Law, Articles 8 and 27. Article 8 of the Immigration Law establishes the right to receive any medical attention (public or private), regardless of their migration situation. In cases in which urgent medical attention is needed to preserve the migrant's life, medical attention will be provided without restrictions and for free. 3) The Asylum Law, Article 44(II).

question_text_en: Right to equal pay for the same work.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. According to Article 35(II) of the Constitution, only citizens can stand in elections. Article 33 further stipulates that migrants are not allowed to interfere in the internal affairs of the country.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of choice of employment.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) Article 1 of the Constitution, which establishes that every person is entitled to the human rights granted by this Constitution and the international treaties signed and ratified by the Mexican State, as well as to the guarantees for the protection of these rights. It also establishes that "any form of discrimination, based on ethnic or national origin, gender, age, disabilities, social status, medical conditions, religion, opinions, sexual orientation, marital status, or any other form, which violates the human dignity or seeks to annul or diminish the rights and freedoms of the people, is prohibited." 2) The Migration Law, Articles 67 and 109. Article 67 establishes that migrants in irregular situation have the right of non-discrimination and the respect of their human rights. 3) The Federal Law Against Discrimination.

question_text_en: Right of spouse/partner of principal migrant to work.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) Article 1 of the Constitution (which prohibits discrimination based on ethnic or national origin or any other form which violates human dignity). 2) Article 1 of the Federal Law against Discrimination. 3) The Migration Law, Article 67. Also, the Supreme Court ruled that racial profiling is discriminatory in a case challenging migrant control checkpoints inside Mexican territory (amparo en revisi?n 275/2019, Primera Sala de la Suprema Corte)

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after loss of employment.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in Article 56 of the the Labor Law, which protects the principle of equality and the right to equal conditions for equal work, without differences or exclusions for any reason, including nationality and racial origin.

question_text_en: Right to equal employment conditions and protection.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) the Migration Law, Articles 52 and 63. 2) The Regulation of the Migration Law, Articles 131, 138, 165, 166, and 167. Employers that wish to sponsor a temporary residence status for labor purposes need to apply for a permit ("constancia de empleador"). If a migrant worker with such residency wishes to change employers, they need to make sure the new one has such permit in order to renew its resident status. Only a few employers in the country have such permit; there is also a limit: an employer personnel may not be more than 10% foreign (as per Article 7 of the Federal Labor Law). Assuming the new employer has such a permit, the migrant is only required by law to give notice to the National Institute of Immigration of any change in their jobs 90 days after the change of employment; otherwise, they can be fined.

question_text_en: Right to form trade unions and other associations.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. According to the Migration Law, Articles 52 and 63, and the Regulation of the Migration Law, Articles 131, 138, 165, and 166, only the sponsoring migrant can work if they have a work permit; the spouse/partner cannot work without requesting a work permit on their own. The exception to this are family members of recognized refugees, who obtain the same benefits as the sponsoring migrant, including the right to work immediately.

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to redress before deportation or withdrawal of residency permit.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) the Migration Law, Article 52. 2) Articles 115 and 131 of the Regulation of the Migration Law. Visas tied to employment will expire and may not be renewed without a valid job. However, if the migrant loses their job within the term of their current visa, they are able to find new employment and request renewal of their visa using their new employment contract.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to social security protections.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in the Federal Labor Law, Articles 2, 5, 7, and 56. The Federal Labor Law recognizes the principle of non-discrimination and equal conditions for equal work, without differences or exclusions for any reason, including nationality and racial origin. However, is also important to note that the Federal Labor Law establishes that employers are obliged to hire Mexican citizens as 90% of their workforce.

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to become lawfully settled.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) the Social Security Law ("Ley del Seguro Social"), Article 12. 2) The General Population Law ("Ley General de Poblaci?n"), Articles 87 and 90. 3) The Federal Labor Law, Article 56. 4) The Constitution, Article 1. Migrants with a valid work permit receive a population ID ("CURP") which is necessary to receive a tax ID ("RFC") and a social security number ("NSS"), and open a bank account. These are necessary requirement for entry into the Social Security system in Mexico.

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to settle regardless of initial status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Mexico does not have unemployment benefits at the federal level; however, the program for unemployment Insurance in Mexico city (which is the only one in existence today) includes migrants, regardless of their status.

question_text_en: Right to redress following employer breach of employment contract.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right for some temporary migrants in 1) the Migration Law, Articles 53 and 62. 2) The Regulation of the Migration Law, Article 127. However, some temporary migrants with a temporary frontier worker permit are barred from applying for a permanent residency status, unless they have a connection to a Mexican national such as marriage.

question_text_en: Right not to have identity documents confiscated.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) Articles 17, 94, and 147 of the Migration Law. The Migration Law provides that only immigration agents are authorized to withhold identity documents in case of the presumption that they are apocryphal. In other cases, confiscation of documents is subject to sanctions according to Article 147 of the Immigration Law. 2) Article 81 of the Regulation of the Migration Law.

question_text_en: Right to birth registration.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in the Migration Law, Article 9, which recognizes the authorization of the civil acts before authorities as well as the expedition of certificates regarding birth, recognition of children, marriage, divorce and death, regardless of their migratory status.

question_text_en: Right to government document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) the Migration Law, Areticles 40-65. 2) The Regulation of the Migration Law, Articles 58, 101-118. 3) M?xico: Secretar?a de Gobernaci?n, Manual de Criterios y Tr?mites Migratorios del Instituto Nacional de Migraci?n, Diario Oficial de la Federaci?n, 20 January 2010. The National Institute of Immigration issue visas for: i) visitors (with permit to work, without permit to work, regional, border worker, humanitarian reasons, for adoption purposes); ii) temporary residents, for no longer than four years with the possibility to obtain a work permit (as a family member of a Mexican national or a temporary or permanent resident, student); and iii) permanent residents (after five years as a temporary resident).

question_text_en: Right against destruction of document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) the Federal Criminal Code, Article 399, which provides a general prohibition to destroy another person's property. 2) the Migration Law, Articles 17 and 147. 3) The Regulation of the Migration Law, Article 81.

question_text_en: Right to communicate with consular officials.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this obligation in 1) the Migration Law, Articles 69, 107(VIII), 109(III), 112(II), 119(I), 120, 122(II). 2) The Migration Law Regulation, Articles 3, 60, 180, 191, 226(V), 232(II), 233. 3) Article 21 of the Asylum Law. 4) Articles 22, 28 of the Regulation of the Asylum Law. 4) The Mexican Supreme Court of Justice, Protocol of Action for judges in cases involving migrants and people in need of international protection. Consular assistance is established as a right for migrants and as an obligation for authorities in all the procedures in which a migrant is involved.

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico prohibits the detention of children based on their status as a migrant in 1) the Migration Law, Article 74. 2) The General Law for the Protection of Children and Adolescents, Article 94. 3) The General Law for the Protection of Children and Adolescents Regulation, Article 111.

question_text_en: Right of migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The Migration Law, Articles 68 and 111 allows for the arrest of those with an irregular status; their detention is labeled as "lodging" ("alojamiento"), and therefore, constitutional protections against administrative arrests are not applied.

question_text_en: Right to appeal legality, conditions, and length of detention
citation_text_en: National Law in Mexico protects this right in 1) Articles 70, 109, 111(V) of the Migration Law. 2) The Migration Law Regulation, Articles 226 and 233. 3) Article 1 of the Amparo Law. 4) Protocol of Action for judges in cases involving migrants and people in need of international protection. Notably, migrants are mandatorily detained if they seek to appeal. When an administrative or judicial remedy is presented regarding the migrant's immigration status or if an amparo procedure is filled, the limit of 15 working days in detention which may be extended to 60 working days as a maximum, does not apply and the person shall remain in detention for the whole duration of the procedure (Article 111-V); in other words, the right to access to justice is conditioned on the deprivation of liberty. Likewise, legal representation for migrants in detention is not guaranteed even when the National Immigration Institute is entitled to create collaboration agreements with this objective. However, if the migrant uses the amparo action, the district judge has the purview to release them as the proceedings continue. This right is enshrined in the Tribunales Colegiados de Circuito, Tesis Aislada (com?n): I.9o.P.3 K (10a.), which states that migrants can appeal their detention via amparo, and grants the District Judge overseeing the case to grant the migrant provisional freedom under caution, according to the Immigration Law and the Protocol of Action for judges in cases involving migrants and people in need of international protection, D?cima ?poca, Libro 16, March 2015, p. 2431.

question_text_en: Right to an individualized detention decision.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to be free from torture and inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) Articles 20(B)(II), 22, 73(XXI)(a) of the Constitution. 2) The Migration Law Regulation ("Reglamento") Article 227. 3) The Asylum Law ("Ley sobre Refugiados, Protecci?n Complementaria y Asilo Pol?tico"), Articles 6, 20, 28 and 54. 4) Articles 1, 24, 25, 29, 27.VI of the Torture and Cruel, Inhumane and Degrading Treatment Law.

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. In principle, migration agents are not entitled to exercise the use of force against migrants. However, the Migration Law provides that the National Guard can support the Federal Police in immigration control and verification operations (Article 81). Additionally, the Law on the National Guard grants members of the National Guard the ability to review the documents of migrants (both on or within the border) to verify their migration status situation in coordination with the National Institute on Migration (except for the facilities for international transit), and, if applicable, proceed to escort them to migration authorities. In that sense, the National Guard is obliged to follow the standards on the use of force established in the National Law on the Use of Force (with no specific provision for migrants). There is no express prohibition to the use of force, however, and instead there are rather vague provisions stating that security forces can assist in national security activities. There is no prohibition. However, violence has been used to stop caravans; such "security measures" are not coded.

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of lethal force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. There is no textual prohibition regarding the use of force to prevent migrants from entering the country. There is only a general Constitutional prohibition against the use of lethal force for the State.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from trafficking or smuggling.
citation_text_en: National law protects this right in Article 38 of the General Law Against Human Trafficking, which explictly establishes that trafficked migrant victims are to be exempt from sanctions in the Migration Law or other similar laws, for their irregular situation or for fake documents. Additionally, Article 159 of the Migration Law clearly establishes culpability for the crime of smuggling, and does not proscribe any criminal sanctions against migrant victims of smuggling. Normally, smuggled migrants are sent to immigration detention centers and deported to their countries unless they are considered as important witnesses in an investigation, in which case they can access a humanitarian visa.

question_text_en: Right to maintain citizenship status after convictions.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in the Constitution, Article 37.

question_text_en: Right of economic migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) the Nationality Law, Articles 19, and 20. 2) The Regulation of the Nationality Law, 16-21. In general, economic migrants require 5 years of residency status; if they come from a Latin American country or the Iberian peninsula, they only need 2 years of residency status.

question_text_en: Right of humanitarian migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) the Nationality Law Articles 19 and 20. 2) The Regulation of the Nationality Law, 16-21. 3) The Migration Law, Article 53. Humanitarian migrants do not have any special procedures or criteria for citizenship that are separate from other migrants. They only need to satisfy the general residency requirement. Refugees have different requirements, for example, they do not need to present original/apostilled documents, and do not take a Mexican History exam required for citizenship.

question_text_en: Right of family migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) the Nationality Law, Articles 19 and 20. 2) The Regulation of the Nationality Law, 52-55. Family migrants have to fulfill residency requirements, but the requirements for are shorter. For instance, migrants married to a Mexican citizen may request naturalization after two years of residency in Mexico. Children under 18 of a Mexican need only one year of residency.

question_text_en: Right to dual nationality.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) the Constitution, Article 37. 2) Nationality Law, Articles 19 and 20. 3) Regulation of the Nationality Law, Articles 6, 12-VIII.

question_text_en: Right to freedom to hold opinion.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in the Constitution, Articles 3 and 24. Article 24 of the Constitution recognizes the right of freedom of thought, conscience and religion or belief to every person in Mexican territory and the prohibition of discrimination on this ground in Article 3.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of expression.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico Protects this right in Articles 6 and 24 of the Constitution. Article 6 establishes the right to hold opinions without interferences for every person in Mexico; regardless of explicit recognition of the Migration and Asylum laws, this right is recognized for migrants as it is recognized to citizens.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of association.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Articles 6 and 7 of the Constitution protects the right to freedom of expression as a human right for every person in Mexican territory. However, there is a limitation for migrants regarding this right as established in Article 33 of the Constitution, which provides that foreigners are not allowed in any way to interfere in the internal affairs of the country.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of assembly.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. While national law in Mexico protects the right for migrants to join trade unions in Article 9 of the Constituion, Article 372 of the Labor Law prohibits them from taking leadership positions in said unions.

category: Thought, conscience, and religion or belief
question_text_en: Right of freedom of thought, conscience and religion or belief.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The Guidelines for issuing visas of the Minister of Interior require the sponsor to prove the familial relationship, their residency status (temporary, permanent or student visas), and sufficient funds in inversions or bank accounts for every family member equivalent to 100 days of the minimum wage in Mexico City per month during the last 12 months; or an income equivalent to 100 days of the minimum wage in Mexico City per month during the last 6 months.

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to access criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) the Migration Law, Articles 6, 11, 12, 28(IV), 66, 73, 75, and 120. 2) Regulation of the Migration Law, 178-184. According to Article 178, the migration authority ("INM") and the Department of Justice ("FGR") have to support foreign nationals when they file criminal proceedings. Additionally, relevant authorities should also work to detect possible victims of crime.

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to immigration status or relief from expulsion.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) the Migration Law, Article 52(V)(a). 2) Regulaiton of the Migration Law, Artilces 37, 137, 141(III)(a), 144(II). 3) The Procedure for the National Immigration Institute for the detection, identification and attention of foreigners victims of a crime of 2011 of the National Institute of Migration. Foreign nationals are allowed to remain in the country with a visa for humanitarian reasons for the duration of their procedures. This visa has to be renewed every year if the procedure is still active, there is also a possibility of exchange the document to a permit of temporary residence.

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: National law in Mexico protects this right in 1) Articles 2, 6, 11, 29, 68, 71-73, 79, 95, 98, 99, 112, 120 of the Migration Law. Article 73 provides the obligation of authorities to grant a humanitarian visa to children while their procedures are resolved to avoid the risk of immediate deportation before having he opportunity to explore possibilities of seeking protective status. Likewise, it provides the obligation to determine and guarantee the best interest of the child. It also provides that these procedures must be resolved by the Federal Office for the Protection of Boys, Girls and Adolescents, authority that is specialized in children's rights. 2) Articles 144(III), 144(IV)(a), 169-177, 180(IV), 226(XVII) and 230 of the Regulation of the Migration Law. 3) Articles 5(III), 9, 20 of the Asylum Law. 4) Articles 35, 36, 37, 57 of the Regulation of the Asylum Law. 6) Articles 10, and 89-101 of the General Law on the Rights of Children and Adolescents. Article 92 establishes the following guarantees of due process: i) notification of the procedure and its correspondent decision; ii) information about their rights; iii) participation in their procedures; iv) translation and interpretation; v) consular assistance; vi) legal representation; vii) representation in absence; viii) best interest of the child and ix) information about the duration of the process. 7) Rules in cases involving migrant children of the Protocol of Action for judges in cases involving migrants and people in need of international protection, p. 96-100. The Protocol of Action for judges in cases involving migrants and people in need of international protection contains specific rules for judges in their role in determining the best interest of the child. In that sense, The Federal Court of Justice for Tax and Administrative Matters resolved in two occasions that the best interest of the child in asylum procedures must include the UNHCR Guidelines on Determining the Best Interest of the Child. Finally, the Twentieth First Collegiate Circuit Court in Administrative Matters of the First Circuit of Mexico City resolved the suspension incident (Queja 205/2019) in an amparo recognizing that children are in a situation of vulnerability and require special protection. The resolution requested to identify migrant children under detention and to refer them to the National System for the Integral Development of the Family, among other protections, such as to provide legal representation and access to their consulates.

question_text_en: Right of women migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: National Law in Mexico protects this right in 1) Articles 2, 30, 73, 107, 110, 113, and 120 of the Migration Law. 2) Articles 185, 186 of the Regulation of the Migration Law. 3) Articles 20, 54-58 of the Asylum Law. 4) Article 75 of the Trafficking Law. The law requires that the vulnerability of woemn must be addressed, especially during pregnancy. The Women Protection Institute provides training in gender issues and violence for officials. Women in detention will also be kept separate from men during detention, and vulnerability should be assessed when considering removal.

question_text_en: Rights of migrants with disabilities to special protection.
citation_text_en: National Law in Mexico protects this right in 1) Articles 73, 109, 111, 113, and 120 of the Migration Law. 2) Article 85 of the Regulation of the Migration Law, which stipulates that persons with disabilities are considered a group in a situation of vulnerability entitled to special protections in the Immigration Law, together with women, older adult, children, and victims or witnesses of crimes. The authorities are obliged to identify persons in a situation of vulnerability and to pay special attention to their needs. 3) Article 20 of the Asylum Law contemplates assistance for the integration of refugees with disabilities in Mexico. 4) Article 4 of the Law for the Inclusion of persons with Disabilities, forbids discrimination on the grounds of migrant status.

citation_text_en: Coder 1: Said Saddiki Coder 2: Nabil Ferdaoussi

question_text_en: What country are you coding?
citation_text_en: Morocco

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to vote in local and/or regional elections.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco protects this right in 1) Article 29 of the Moroccan Constitution, which states that, "The freedoms of reunion, of assembly, of peaceful demonstration, of association and of syndical and political membership [appartenance], are guaranteed. The law establishes the conditions of the exercise of these freedoms. The right to strike is guaranteed." 2) Law 00-76 on public meetings and demonstrations issued by Royal Decree No. 200-02-1 of July 23, 2002, Official Gazette No. 5046, October 10, 2002, p. 2890.

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to stand for election.
citation_text_en: The right to vote in Moroccan elections is regulated by reciprocity agreements, and, as such, being lawfully present, on its own, does not give migrants a legal right to vote. Article 30 of the Moroccan Constitution states that "All the citizens [feminine] and the citizens [masculine] of majority, enjoying their civil and political rights[,] are electors and eligible. The law provides[prevoit] the provisions of [a] nature encouraging the equal access of women and men to the elective functions. The vote is a personal right and a national duty. Foreigners under [Moroccan] jurisdiction [ressortissants etrangers] enjoy the fundamental freedoms recognized to Moroccan citizens [feminine] and citizens [masculine], in accordance with the law. Those among them who reside in Morocco can participate in local elections by virtue of the law, of the application of international conventions or of practices of reciprocity."

question_text_en: Right to equal protection of the law before courts.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco protects this right in 1) Article 30 of the Moroccan Constitution. The Constitution affirms the principle of equal enjoyment of rights and freedoms between Moroccan and foreign citizens in accordance with the law. All the aforementioned texts also affirm in principle the right of everyone to access the judiciary, and approve equal treatment of the victim without discrimination and regardless of administrative status. In addition, foreigners enjoy all the guarantees granted to Moroccan citizens, such as the right to a fair trial, the presumption ofinnocence, respect for the rights of defense, and the right to translation and judicial assistance. 2) Law No. 1.74.447, relating to civil procedure, Official Gazette No. 3230, September 30, 1974, p. 2741. 3) Law No. 22.01 relating to criminal procedure, Official Gazette No. 5078 dated January 30, 2003, p. 315. 4) Law No. 38.15, relating to judicial organization, Official Gazette No. 71.08, July 14, 2022. 5) Law No. 90.41 regarding the establishment of administrative courts of September 10, 1993, Official Gazette No. 42.27, November 3, 1993.

question_text_en: Right to government-provided counsel in proceedings related to migrant status.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco protects this right in 1) Articles 23, 34, and 36 of Law 02.03. Article 36 states that: "The person concerned may request the assistance of an interpreter, a doctor, or a lawyer, and may, if he or she so wishes, communicate with the consulate of his or her country or with a person of his or her choice; he or she is informed of this when the decision to detain is notified." 2) Code of Criminal Procedure, Dahir n° 1-58-261 of February 10, 1959. These provisions apply to all migrants irrespective of their status.

question_text_en: Right to government-provided interpretation in criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco protects this right in Artilces 23, 34, 36, and 38 of Law no. 02-03. Article 36 states that "foreigners detained may request the assistance of an interpreter, a doctor or a lawyer, and may, if he or she so wishes, communicate with the consulate of his or her country or with a person of his or her choice; he or she is informed of this when the decision to detain is notified."

question_text_en: Right to be protected from prosecution for unauthorized entry.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Articles 41 to 49of Law 02.03 criminalizes irregular residence and irregular entry, and punishes offenders with fines and imprisonment. Specifically, Article 41 states that: "Any foreigner who enters or attempts to enter Moroccan territory in breach of the provisions of Article 3 of the present law, or who remains on Moroccan territory beyond the period authorized by his visa, except in cases of force majeure or recognized valid excuses, is liable to a fine of between 2,000 and 20,000 dirhams and to imprisonment for between one and six months, or to one of these two penalties only. In the event of a repeatoffence, the penalty is doubled."

question_text_en: Right to equal access to public adult education institutions.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. All financial laws that stipulate support for adequate housing every year stipulate a requirement for Moroccan citizenship, with the exception of the Finance Law of 2014, which stipulates an exception for the possibility of benefiting from this support because it coincides with Morocco’s launch of new immigration policy.

question_text_en: Right of access to public adult education institutions regardless of status.
citation_text_en: National law protects this right in 1) The 51-17 framework-law relating to the system of education, training and scientific research issued by Dhir No. 1.19.113 issued on August 9, 2019, Official Gazette No. 6805, August 19, 2019. 2) Acion A of the SNIA. The Moroccan law determining access to public schools does not include any distinction between Moroccan and foreign children. Rather, it stipulates in the framework law referred to in Article 2 that special attention be given to children of foreigners coming from abroad and who are in a difficult situation. Article 19 of the same law stipulates compulsory education from the age of 4 to the age of 16 without discrimination, including discrimination on the basis of nationality. Article 25 of the same law stipulates that the state must mobilize all means to facilitate the integration of persons with a disability or in a difficult situation into the system of education, training and scientific research. In addition, there are many memorandums issued by the Ministry of National Education that were approved since 2013, that is, with the launch of the new national policy for immigration and asylum in Morocco, stipulating the necessity of registering migrant children in public schools, regardless of their legal status or the status of their parents, and integrating them into the Moroccan education and training system.

question_text_en: Right to be free from discrimination on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Law No. 183-72-1 regarding the establishment of the Office of Vocational Training and Labor Promotion, which governs access to vocational training limits access to Moroccan citizens. However, the government has recently established a new policy, adopted in Rabat on June 27, 2014, expanding access to vocational training for regular migrants and refugees with residence permits.

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after convictions.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco protects this right in paragraph 6 of Article 26 of Law no. 02-03 of November 11, 2003, on the entry and residence of foreigners in Morocco, which made migrants residing regularly and who had previously been sentenced to a prison sentence of less than one year among the categories that cannot be subject to expulsion proceedings. The same law exempted convictions related to irregular entry and terrorism from this time limit.

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of torture or inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco protects this right in Article 29 of Law 02-03, on entry and residence, which explicitly prohibits the return of any person to a country where he or she may face danger to his or her life or where he or she may be exposed to inhuman, cruel or degrading treatment. Article 29 of Law 02.03 states: "Pregnant foreign women and foreign minors may not be deported. Similarly, no foreigner may be removed to a country if he or she establishes that his or her life or freedom are threatened or that he or she would be exposed to inhuman, cruel or degrading treatment."

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of persecution.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco protects this right in 1) Article 33 of the Geneva Convention relating to the Status of Refugees of July 28, 1951, which was ratified, and published in Official Gazette No. 2341, September 6, 1957, p. 1978. 2) Protocol relating to the status of refugees annexed to the Geneva Convention and ratified by Morocco, July27, 1970, Official Gazette No. 3145, 1973. 3) Article 29 and Article 38 of Law no. 02-03 of November 11, 2003, on the entry and residence of foreigners in Morocco. 4) Decree No. 2.57.1256,by which the modalities for implementing the Convention relating to the Status of Refugees are determined, Official Gazette No. 2341, 09/06/1957, p. 1978. International treaties have been incorporated into Moroccan law by the provisions of the Moroccan Constitution of 2011, which emphasizes on the supremacy of international agreements that were ratified by Morocco.

question_text_en: Right to not return to a deprivations of fundamental human rights.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco protects this right in Article 29, which states: “No foreigner may be deported to a country if he proves that his life or freedom is threatened or he is exposed to inhuman, cruel or degrading treatment.”

question_text_en: Right to be advised of availability of asylum before expulsion.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from chain refoulement.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco bans expulsion to any country where a migrant is likely to be subjected to refoulement through subsequent expulsion in paragraph C of Article 29. Article 29: A foreign national who is the subject of a deportation order, or who is to be deported, is deported :a) to the country of which he or she is a national, unless refugee status has been granted or a decision has not yet been taken on his or her application for asylum; b) to the country which issued him or her with a valid travel document; c) to another country in which he or she is legally admissible.

question_text_en: Right to protection against expulsion except following a legal judgment.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco protects this right in Articles 21, 22, 34, and 38 of Law no. 02-03 of November 11, 2003, on the entry and residence of foreigners in Morocco. Article 21 states that, expulsion may be ordered by the authorities, by justified decision in the following cases: 1 - if the foreigner cannot prove that he/she has entered Moroccan territory legally unless his/her situation was regularized after entry; 2 - if the foreigner has remained on Moroccan territory beyond the validity of his/her visa or, if he/she is not required to have a visa, after the expiry of a period of three months from entry into Moroccan territory, without holding a duly issued registration card; 3 - if the foreigner, to whom the issue or renewal of a residence permit has been refused or withdrawn, has remained on Moroccan territory beyond a period of 15 days from the date of notification of the refusal or withdrawal; 4 - if the foreigner has not applied for renewal of his residence permit and has remained on Moroccan territory beyond the 15-day period following expiry of the residence permit; 5 - if the foreigner has been convicted by final judgment of forgery, falsification, or establishment under a name other than his or her own, or for lack of a residence permit; 6 - if the receipt for the registration card application issued to the foreign national has been withdrawn; 7 - if the foreign national has had his or her registration or residence card withdrawn, or has been refused the issue or renewal of one of these two cards, in cases where this withdrawal or refusal has been ordered, in the application of the legislative and regulatory provisions in force, on the grounds of a threat to public order."

question_text_en: Right to submit reasons against expulsion and have case reviewed before deportation.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco protects this right in Articles 23, 24, 30, 32, and 33 of law No. 02.03. Article 23 states that, "A foreign national who is the subject of a deportation order may, within 48 hours of notification, apply to the president of the administrative court, in his or her capacity as an interim relief judge, to have the order annulled. The president or his or her delegate shall rule within 4 clear days of the referral. If the foreign national is detained in the application of article 34 of the present law, the president of the administrative tribunal or his delegate may request the assistance of an interpreter and the communication of the file containing the documents on the basis of which the contested decision was taken. The hearing is public; it takes place in the presence of the person concerned, unless the latter, duly summoned, fails to appear at the hearing. The foreigner is assisted by his lawyer if he has one. The foreign national may ask the Chairman or his delegate to appoint a lawyer." article 23 gives to the foreigner (immigrant) the right to appeal against the decision to betaken to the border before the head of the Administrative Court in his capacity as an emergencyjudge, within a period of 48 hours of notifying him. Also, the migrant is entitled to attach the appeal request to suspend the implementation of the decision in accordance with Article 33, as the foreigner has the right to appeal the initial decision within one month. This appeal does not automatically suspend the implementation of the decision to be taken to the border according to Article 24. In contrast, Articles 32 and 33 of the same law state the possibilities available to foreigners to appeal against expulsion decisions from the territory, the procedures of which are subjected to the same procedures as those related to being taken to the borders, but the reasons for taking them are mainly related to the threat to public order or the urgent necessity of preserving the security of the state.

question_text_en: Right of settled migrants to family reunification.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for adult stateless migrants. National law in Morocco only conditionally provides citizenship for stateless children in Article 7 of the Moroccan Nationality Act, which states that "a child born in Morocco of unknown parents is deemed never to have been Moroccan if, during his or her minority, filiation is established with a foreigner and if, in accordance with the nationality of that foreigner, the child has the nationality of that foreigner. A child of unknown parents found in Morocco is presumed, until proven otherwise, to have been born in Morocco."

question_text_en: Right to judicial remedy for denials of right to family reunification.
citation_text_en: Nationally law allows for legal avenues to facilitate reunification with immediate family members in paragraph 4 of Article 17 of Law No. 02.03, which states, "Article 17: Subject to lawful residence and entry into Moroccan territory, and unless otherwise exempted, the residence card is issued: 1 - to the foreign spouse of a Moroccan national; 2 - to the foreign child of a Moroccan mother, and to the stateless child of a Moroccan mother, who does not benefit from the provisions of article 7 (1°) of dahir n° 1-58-250 of safar 21, 1378 (September 6, 1958) on the Moroccan nationality code, if this child has reached the age of civil majority, or ifhe/she is dependent on his/her mother, as well as to the foreign ascendants of a Moroccan national and his/her spouse, who are dependent on him/her; 3 - to a foreigner who is the father or mother of a child resident and born in Morocco, and who has acquired Moroccan nationality by operation of law within the two years preceding his or her majority, in application of the provisionsof article 9 of the aforementioned dahir n° 1-58-250 of 21 safar 1378 (September 6, 1958), on condition that he or she legally represents the child, has custody rights or effectively provides forthe child's needs; 4 - to the spouse and minor children of a foreign national holding a residence permit."

question_text_en: Right to recognition of same-sex marital relationships.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco protects this right in Law No. 02.03: Article 20, which states: "A foreign national whose application for a residence permit or renewal of a residence permit has been refused or whose permit has been withdrawn may lodge an appeal with the President of the Administrative Court in his capacity as interim relief judge within fifteen (15) days of the date of notification of the refusal or withdrawal decision. The appeal referred to in the first paragraph above shall not prevent a decision to deport or expel the foreign national in accordance with Chapters III, IV and V of Title I of the present law."

question_text_en: Right to family reunification without resource conditions
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. National law in Morocco criminalizes same-sex relations in Article 489 of the Penal Code, which states that: "[a]ny person who commits a lewd or unnatural act with a person of the same sex shall be punished by a term of imprisonment of six months to three years and a fine of 200 to 1,000 dirhams."

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services.
citation_text_en: NA

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services regardless of status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for all migrants. Law no. 02-03 of November 11, 2003, on the entry and residence of foreigners in Morocco, does not provide for any possibility for migrants who were irregular upon entry to regularize their status. However, the law does provide a mechanism for the regularization of irregular migrants who originally enter with authorization. Decree No. 2-09-607 of April 1, 2010, regarding the implementation of Law No. 02-03 regarding entry and residence in the national territory and combating irregular migration, Official Gazette No. 5831 dated April 19, 2010, p. 2541. Article 15 of the above decree outlines the conditions for a foreigner wishing to reside in Morocco and obtain a registration card as a visitor. The individual must have obtained an entry visa with the phrase 'visitor,' prove sufficient means to live in Morocco, and commit not to engage in any professional activity. The same article also specifies the requirements for a foreigner seeking a registration card for work. They must have an employment contract signed by the government authority in charge of employment, or an entry visa with the phrase 'for work.' If a foreigner wishes to practice a professional activity, prior authorization from the authorities overseeing that activity is required, or an entry visa indicating the 'license for the activity to be practiced.' For students, an entry visa with the label 'study' is necessary. In addition, under Article 10 of the same decree, the Director General of National Security can grant an exceptional residence permit to irregular migrants for more than three months and less than a year. In addition, Morocco organized two exceptional campaigns to regularize migrants. The first in 2014 and the second in 2016, based on a special joint memorandum between the Ministry of the Interior and the Ministry in charge of Moroccans residing abroad and foreign affairs.

question_text_en: Right of access to public housing programs.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco protects this right in a limited way in Articles 9, 516 and 517 of the Moroccan Labor Code. Article 516 of the Labor Code requires the employment of foreigners to have an employment contract approved by the authorities in charge of employment. Accordingly, immigrants enjoy the same rights as Moroccan citizens in accordance with the principle of equality contained in Article 9. Meanwhile, Articles 516 to 5021 outline the regulations and processes for employing foreigners, which include obtaining authorization from the relevant employment authority. This implies that there is no discrimination in terms of the right to compensation if a foreigner is working legally, which includes the right to compensation when the employer violates the terms of the employment contract.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to free primary education for migrant children.
citation_text_en: National law protects this right for migrants with regular status in 1) Law No. 65.00 on Basic Health Insurance Code, issued by Dhir No. 296-02-1 of October 3, 2002, Official Gazette No. 5058, November 21, 2002, p. 3449. It was also amended and supplementedby Dahir No. 77- 22-1, issued on December 9, 2022, implementing the law. 2) Framework No. 22-06 relating to the National Health System, Official Gazette No. 7151, December 9, 2022. 3) Decree No.797-22-2 issued on November 29, 2022, implementing Law No. 00-65 relating to basic compulsory sickness insurance, regarding the basic compulsory sickness insurance system for persons unable to bear the subscription duties, Official Gazette No. 7147, November 29, 2022. 4) Dahir No. 30-21-1 issued on March 23, 2021, implementing the law. 5) Framework No. 21-09 related to social protection, published in Official Gazette No. 2178, April 5, 2021. 6) Dahir No. 203-61-1 dated June 30, 1962, relating to charging the expenses of indigent foreign patients, Official Gazette No. 2549, July 13, 1962. 7) Decree No. 2.08.177 implementing Book III of Law No. 65.00 relating to the medical assistance system, as amended and supplemented by Decree No.2.11.199. The aforementioned health insurance code does not include any discrimination between Moroccans and foreigners with regard to health coverage. Other legal texts, including the law relating to basic compulsory sickness insurance, the framework law relating to social protection, as well as the implementing decrees issued in this section, do not include any kind of discrimination between foreigners and citizens, provided that the foreigner is in the regular status.

question_text_en: Right to equal pay for the same work.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Article 30 of the Constitution stipulates the possibility of migrants participating in elections, which may only mean participation by voting and not candidacy. The ability for foreigners to stand in elections is an open legal question that has not been challenged.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of choice of employment.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Though Moroccan law provides broad protections against discrimination, it does not specifically prohibit discrimination based on migrant status.

question_text_en: Right of spouse/partner of principal migrant to work.
citation_text_en: National law protects this right in the Moroccan criminal law, Chapter 1-431. Chapter 1-431 criminalizes the crime of discrimination, and defines it as “any discrimination between natural persons because of national origin, social origin, color, sex, family function, health condition, disability, political opinion, trade union affiliation, or because of affiliation or “real or presumed non-belonging to a particular race, nation, breed, or religion.” The crime of discrimination is punishable under Moroccan law by imprisonment from one month to two years and a fine of one 1200 dirhams to 50,000 dirhams.

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after loss of employment.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for irregular migrants. However, national law in Morocco protects this right or all regular migrants in Artcle 9 of the Moroccan Labour Code only for migrants with a regular status. Article 9 stipulates the principle of equality, as the second paragraphprohibits all discrimination between employees in terms of race, color, sex, disability, marital status, creed, political opinion, trade union affiliation, or national origin, or social origin, that wouldviolate or distort the principle of equal opportunities, or lack of reciprocity in the employment or the exercise of a profession, especially with regard to employment, management and distribution ofwork, vocational training, wages, promotion, and benefit from social privileges, disciplinary measures, and dismissal from work.

question_text_en: Right to equal employment conditions and protection.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco protects this right in Article 516 of the Moroccan labour Code. Article 516 states that, "Any employer wishing to recruit a foreign employee must obtain authorization from the government labor authority. This authorization is granted in the form of a visa affixed to the employment contract. The date of the visa is the date on which the employment contract takes effect. Any modification of the contract is also subject to the visa referred to in the first paragraphof this article. The authorization may be withdrawn at any time by the government authority in charge of labor."

question_text_en: Right to form trade unions and other associations.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Article 516 of the Labor Code requires every employer who wants to employ a foreign (immigrant) to first obtain permission from the authority in charge of employment in the form of a visa placed on the employment contract. There is no exception on this matter. Moreover, Article 521 punishes anyone who employs foreigners without obtaining this permission.

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to redress before deportation or withdrawal of residency permit.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for temporary labor migrants. Article 516 of the Labor Code requires every employer who wants to employ a foreign (immigrant) to first obtain permission from the authority in charge of employment in the form of a visa placed on the employment contract. Article 518 of the Moroccan Labour Code, states that "The contract must stipulate that in the event of refusal to grant the authorization referred to in paragraph 1 of article 516, the employer undertakes to bear the cost of returning the foreign employee to his country or to the country where he was residing." For those entering Morocco for the first time to engage in professional activity or paid work, the loss of employment due to termination or refusal to sign or renew employment contracts necessitates their departure from the national territory.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to social security protections.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco protects this right for most employment conditions and protections 1) Article 9 of the Labor Code guarantees equality between all employees who have authorized employment contracts, and there is no discrimination between citizens and foreigners in the Labor Code with regard to the enjoyment of rights ancillary to the right to work. 2) Article 517 of the Moroccan labour Code, which states that "the employment contract reserved for foreigners must conform to the model laid down by the governmental labor authority."

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to become lawfully settled.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco protects this right in Article 2 of the law on social security, which stipulates that all employers are obligated to declare their work to the National Social Security Fund (CNOPS) without any distinction between citizens and non-citizens. Therefore, there is no distinction or exception between foreigners with employment contracts and Moroccan citizens with regard to enjoying social security. The Labor Code also confirms in Article 520 that international agreements must be taken into account when employing foreign workers, in addition to referring in other provisions to the principle reciprocity with regard to the enjoyment of certain benefits and rights.

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to settle regardless of initial status.
citation_text_en: National law conditionally protects this right in 1) Law on Compensation for Loss of Work and Article 9 of the Labor Code, which ensures the principles of equality and fair working conditions. 2) Dahir (Royal Decree) No. 1.14.143 issued on August 22, 2014, implementing Law No. 03.14 amending and supplementing the Royal Decree as Law No. 1.72.184 issued on July 27, 1972, relating to the social security system. This law provides citizens and migrants access to compensation relating to loss of employment.

question_text_en: Right to redress following employer breach of employment contract.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right as Morcco does not offer a permanent residence visa. Article 6 and Article 8 of the Entry and Residence Law require foreigners wishing to reside in Morocco to apply to the competent authorities to obtain a registration card. The latter isconsidered as a residence permit whose duration ranges between one and ten years. It can alsobe replaced by a residence card after four years of normal and regular residence in accordancewith Article 16. According to Article 13, the registration card issued to a foreigner who proves thathe can live on his own resources, and who is committed not to practice any professional activity inMorocco that is subject to licensing, refers to him as a “visitor.” For a foreigner who proves that heis pursuing education or study in Morocco, and that he has sufficient means of livelihood, hisregistration card refers to him as a “student.” The registration card issued to a foreigner wishing topractice a professional activity in Morocco subject to a license, which proves that he has obtainedit, indicates the specific

question_text_en: Right not to have identity documents confiscated.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco protects this right in 1) Article 24 of the Moroccan Constitution of 2011 protects the private life of all persons. 2) Article 3 of Law 02-03, which obliges border control authorities to monitor personal documents. 2) Article 1 of Law 27-14 on combating human trafficking, which states that withholding travel documents can be one of the indicators of the possible existence of ahuman trafficking crime and is an element of exploitation and abuse of power leading to the occurrence of the crime. Personal documents are considered part of the identity of the immigrant person, and the same legal requirements that apply to Moroccan citizens apply to migrants in Morocco. Only competent authorities have the right to monitor and examine the personal documents of immigrants in accordance with the conditions and procedures stipulated in the law, especially Law No. 08 -09, regarding the protection of individuals regarding the processing of personal data, February 18, 2009.

question_text_en: Right to birth registration.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco protects this right in Article 3 of Civil Status Law No. 37.99, which states that: 'All Moroccans are obligatorily subject to the civil status system, and the same system applies to foreigners regarding births and deaths that occur on national territory.' In accordance with this provision, Article 17 of the Implementing Decree of Civil Status Law 37.99 specifies that 'Foreigners residing on the national territory have the right to declare births occurring within the Kingdom. The foreigner must support the birth declaration with a certificate issued by the obstetrician, legal midwife, or competent local authority, confirming the place of birth in Morocco.' Additionally, they are required to provide documents substantiating the identity of the parents. It's crucial to note that documents verifying the identity of the parents pertain to origin and birth, such as a passport, and not residence papers. Despite the protection of this right, the civil status registration system imposes the same conditions for Moroccans and foreigners, requiring a declaration supported by a medical certificate within one month of birth or through the court if more than a month has passed since birth, as stated in Article 1 of Law No. 36.21.

question_text_en: Right to government document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for all migrants at the time of their legal entry into Morocco. National Law in Morocco in Article 16 of Law 02.03 mandates the issuing of documents that recognize migrants' residency status if they can prove at least 4 years' uninterrupted residence on Moroccan territory. The decision to grant orrefuse the residence card is taken taking into account the foreigner's means of subsistence, including the conditions of his professional activity and, where applicable, the facts he can invoke in support of his intention to settle permanently on Moroccan territory.

question_text_en: Right against destruction of document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco protects this right in 1) the Moroccan Criminal Code( Article 10),, Royal Decree No. 1-59-413 issued on November 26, 1962, approving the Code of Criminal Law, Official Gazette No. 2640 bis, June 5, 1963, p. 1253. 2) Article 24 of the Moroccan Constitution contains a specific provision related to privacy. Article 24 states: "Any person has the right to the protection of their private life. The domicile is inviolable. Searches may only intervene in the conditions and the forms provided by the law. Private communications, under whatever form that may be, are secret. Only justice can authorize, under the conditions and following the forms provided by the law, the access to their content, their total or partial divulgation or their summons [invocation] at the demand [charge] of whosoever."

question_text_en: Right to communicate with consular officials.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco protects this right in 1) Articles 4, 24, and 36 of Law 02.03. Article 36 states that "The person concerned may request the assistance of an interpreter, a doctor or a lawyer, and may, if he or she so wishes, communicate with the consulate of his or her country or with a person of his or her choice; he or she is informed of this when the decision to detain is notified. A note of this is made in the register provided for above, signed by the person concerned." 2)

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Though Morocco ratified the Convention on the Rights of the Child in 1993, Law no. 02-03 still allows for the detention of child migrants, as the legal provisions only deal directly with "migrants" and does not make a distinction between children or adults in this context.

question_text_en: Right of migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. National Law in Morocco does not prohibit the detention of migrants on the basis of their status as a migrant. Article 42 of 02.03 Law states that, "Any foreigner who enters or attempts to enter Moroccan territory in breach of the provisions of Article 3 of the present law, or who remains on Moroccan territory beyond the period authorized by his visa, except in cases of force majeure or valid excuses, is liable to a fine of between 2,000 and 20,000 dirhams and to imprisonment for between one and six months, or to one of these two penalties only. In the event of a repeat offence, the penalty is doubled."

question_text_en: Right to appeal legality, conditions, and length of detention
citation_text_en: Naitional law in Morocoo protects this right in 1) Article 23 of the Morccoan Constitution, which specifically protects the right to appeal the legality of the detention. 2) Articles 34 and 36 of Law 02.03 protects the right to appeal the conditions of their detention. Article 35 also protects the right of appeal for the length of detention. All decisions related to the detention of a foreigner are reasoned administrative decisions and are subject to judicial oversight within 24 hours. Extending their period is done by issuing judicial orders and not by administrative decisions.

question_text_en: Right to an individualized detention decision.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco protects this right in 1) Articles 4, 24, 34, 35, 36, and 38 of Law 02.03. According to Article 36, the detainee must be able to request the assistance of an interpreter, doctor, lawyer, and/or their consulate or a person of their choice. All decisions related to the detention of a foreigner are reasoned administrative decisions and are subject to judicial oversight within 24 hours. Extending their period is done by issuing judicial orders and not by administrative decisions.

question_text_en: Right to be free from torture and inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco protects this right in 1) Article 29 of Law 02.03, which states that "No foreigner may be removed to a country if he or she establishes that his or her life or freedom are threatened or that he or she would be exposed to inhuman, cruel or degrading treatment." 2) Article 22 of the Moroccan Constitution of 2011 stipulates that “The physical or moral integrity of anyone may not be infringed, in whatever circumstance that may be,and by any party that may be, public or private. No one may inflict on others, under whateverpretext there may be, cruel, inhuman, [or] degrading treatments or infringements of human dignity. The practice of torture, under any of its forms and by anyone, is a crime punishable by the law.” 3) Chapters 1-231 to 8-231 of Law No. 04/43 amended the Code of Criminal Law (Dahir No. 1-59-413 issued on November 26, 1962, approving the Code of Criminal Law, Official Gazette No. 2640bis dated 5 June 1963, p. 1253), relating to the definition of torture, criminalization and punishment of its perpetrators with varying penalties according to each case, as it may reach life imprisonment. This provisions includes prohibition and prevention of the practice of torture for all persons regardless of legal status or nationality. 4) Article 29 of Law no. 02-03 of November 11, 2003, on the entry and residence offoreigners in Morocco, prohibits the return of foreigners who, if returned, are likely to be subjected to inhuman or degrading treatment.

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco protects this right in 1) Article 13 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, which Morocco ratified on May 3, 1979, Official Gazette No. 3525, May 21, 1980. 2) Articles 9, 11, 16, 24, and 27, of the International Convention for the Protection of the Rights of All Migrant Workers and Members of their Families, which Morocco signed on August 15, 1991 and ratified on June 21, 1993, and waspublished in Official Gazette No. 6015 issued on January 23, 2012. 3) Article 3 related to the protection of bodily integrity of the United Nations Convention against Torture, which Morocco signed on January 8, 1986, and issued its ratification and accession papers on June 21,1993, Official Gazette No. 4440, December 19, 1996, p. 1477. 4) Article 22 and 23 of the MoroccanConstitution of 2011. 5) Articles 1, 2, 3, 4, 21, 23, 28, 30, 33, of Law 02-03 regarding entry and residence. International treaties have been incorporated into Moroccan law by the provisions of the Moroccan Constitution of 2011, which emphasizes on the supremacy of international agreements that were ratified by Morocco.

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of lethal force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: National law in Morocco protects this right in 1) Article 13 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, which Morocco ratified on May 3, 1979, Official Gazette No. 3525, May 21, 1980. 2) Articles 9, 11, 16, 24, and 27, of the International Convention for the Protection of the Rights of All Migrant Workers and Members of their Families, which Morocco signed on August 15, 1991 and ratified on June 21, 1993, and waspublished in Official Gazette No. 6015 issued on January 23, 2012. 3) Article 3 related to the protection of bodily integrity of the United Nations Convention against Torture, which Morocco signed on January 8, 1986, and issued its ratification and accession papers on June 21,1993, Official Gazette No. 4440, December 19, 1996, p. 1477. 4) Article 22 and 23 of the MoroccanConstitution of 2011. 5) Articles 1, 2, 3, 4, 21, 23, 28, 30, 33, of Law 02-03 regarding entry and residence.International treaties have been incorporated into Moroccan law by the provisions of the Moroccan Constitution of 2011, which emphasizes on the supremacy of international agreements that were ratified by Morocco.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from trafficking or smuggling.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for smuggled migrants. Law no. 02-03 of November 11, 2003, on the entry and residence of foreigners in Morocco, criminalizes irregular entry and residence on the national territory, which would include those smuggled. While the law does not criminalize being a victim of smuggling or human trafficking, the criminalization of crossing the border when undocumented means that migrants are subject to criminal prosecution. However, victims of human trafficking are specifically exempted from this prosecution due to Chapter 448-14 of Law 27-14, which expressly exempts from any judicial prosecution those considered as victims of this crime.

question_text_en: Right to maintain citizenship status after convictions.
citation_text_en: National Law in Morocco provides that convictions for criminal or other offenses leads to a loss of citizenship status for naturalized migrants in Articles 22, 23, and 24 of Moroccan Nationality Code.
