citation_text_en: [1]: Cecile Blouin (for backcoded questions Chiara Marinelli). [2]: Isabel Berganza Setien.

question_text_en: What country are you coding?
citation_text_en: Peru

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to vote in local and/or regional elections.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Constitution of Peru, Article 2 - Fundamental rights of the person, which states that: "Every person has the right: 12. To meet peacefully without weapons. Meetings in premises private or open to the public do not require prior notice. The ones in squares and public roads require advance notice to the authority, which can prohibit them only for proven reasons of public safety or health." Article 9 of Legislative Decree No. 1350 recognizes that migrants enjoy and exercise the fundamental rights established in the Constitution. Additionally, Article 6 of the aforementioned law states that the migrant, when admitted to the territory, is subject to the same rights and duties as a Peruvian citizen.

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to stand for election.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for all parts of Peru. However, migrants do have the right to vote in most municipalities under the Peruvian Municipal Elections Law (Law N° 26864), Article 7, which states that: "Foreigners over 18 years of age, residents for more than two continuous years prior to the election, are empowered to elect and be elected, except in border municipalities, provided and when they are duly registered in the corresponding registry. To exercise this right, the Foreigner is identified with their respective immigration card."

question_text_en: Right to equal protection of the law before courts.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in 1) the Peruvian Constitution, Article 2, which states that, "Every person has the right: 2. To equality before the law. No one should be discriminated on the basis of origin, race, sex, language, religion, opinion, condition economic, or of any other nature." Furthermore, regarding due process of law in administrative, civil, and criminal courts and tribunals, the Peruvian Constitution also states in Aricle 139 that, "The principles and rights of the jurisdictional function are: 3. Observance of due process and judicial protection. No person may be diverted from the jurisdiction predetermined by law, nor subjected to a procedure other than those previously established, nor judged by courts of exception or special commissions created for that purpose, whatever its denomination." 2) Peruvian Immigration Law (Legislative Decree N° 1350), Article 9, which guarantees access to justice for foreign people: "9.1. The Judiciary and the Public Ministry guarantee the foreign person access to the justice services, without discrimination on grounds of the immigration status."

question_text_en: Right to government-provided counsel in proceedings related to migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. National law in Peru protects this right only in criminal proceedings. The Public Defense Service Law (Law N° 29360), Article 8 - Public defense services states "The General Directorate of Public Defense provides the following services: a) Public criminal defense, which provides legal advice and sponsorship to those investigated, denounced, detained, accused, accused or convicted in criminal proceedings, including adolescent offenders of criminal law. b) Popular legal clinics, which provide legal advice and sponsorship to victims of family violence, sexual violence, moral and material abandonment, and in favor of children, adolescents, old men, and women who are wronged by crimes against life, the body and health, freedom and the family; and to people with limited economic resources in matters of Civil and Family Law, according to the conditions established in the regulations of this Law." Additionally, the Constitutional Court, Ruling N° STC 2744-2015-PA / TC, states that: "In this context, this Court understands that, within the framework of an immigration procedure Immigration, it is necessary to recognize foreigners in irregular situations the following minimum formal guarantees: i) the right to be informed expressly and formally of the reasons that resulted in the imposition of the administrative penalty (fine, exit mandatory, cancellation of permanence or residence, or expulsion) and of charges against her/him if any. The knowledge can be given by written communication addressed to the last address registered by the foreigner before the immigration authority, and will contain a full copy of the respective resolution, or failing that, at the time the foreigner in irregular situation belongs to the competent authority to regularize its stay in the country. Here, what is noted above regarding the character is particularly important in case of exceptional administrative detention of a migrant in an irregular situation, which will only be justified when there is an imminent risk of escape that can affect future legal proceedings or administrative proceedings and when there are not alternative less harmful measures that guarantee their appearance before the immigration authority, or when the person represents a danger to their own safety or to public safety; it should last the shortest possible amount of time and from an individual evaluation of each case, with respect for the corresponding procedural safeguards; ii) the possibility of exposing and proving the reasons that assist against it of the administrative penalty imposed; iii) the possibility of requesting and receiving legal advice, including through free public service if applicable and, if applicable, translation or interpretation, as well as consular assistance, if applicable; iv) in case of an unfavorable decision, the right to submit your case to review before a competent and impartial authority, which is obliged to resolve the corresponding resources within a reasonable time. The migrant may appeal in their own right or through a representative; y) the eventual expulsion may only be made after a decision based on the law and duly notified."

question_text_en: Right to government-provided interpretation in criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Criminal Procedure Code (Legislative Decree N° 957), Article 114, which states: "1. Procedural actions are carried out in Spanish. 2. When a person does not understand the language or does not express himself easily, the necessary help will be provided so that the act can develop regularly. 3. A translator or interpreter must be provided, as appropriate, to people who do not know Spanish, who are allowed to use their own language, as well as deaf-mutes and those who have some impediment to making themselves understood."

question_text_en: Right to be protected from prosecution for unauthorized entry.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Peruvian Immigration Law (Legislative Decree N° 1350), Article 57, which states that the only penalty for unauthorized entry is compulsory deportation only in cases where the migrant has not requested or gone through the steps necessary to regularize.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to public adult education institutions.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. However, Peru also offers the Mi Vivienda Fund, which is a mortgage loan that allows you to buy any home, build on your own land or in independent airs, or improve your home. The Mi Vivienda Fund also contemplates the possibility that the beneficiaries may be migrants. For this purpose, they must have a Residence Card, so temporary permit holders cannot apply.

question_text_en: Right of access to public adult education institutions regardless of status.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right for all migrants in the Regulation of the General Education Law (Supreme Decree N° 011-2012-ED), article 2: "b) The right of access to a quality, equitable, relevant, intercultural, and inclusive education, and to free public education. Accessibility implies the elimination of barriers (physical, administrative, technological, among others) that prevent or hinder the exercise of the right to education in equal opportunities, for people with disabilities and health problems, among other conditions, as well as excluded and vulnerable social groups, regardless of ethnicity, language, religion, age, gender or any other cause of discrimination." 2) The "Technical Standard that guides the process of evaluation of student learning and basic education programs" (Vice Ministerial Resolution N° 025-2019-MINEDU), Article 7.5 provides for a placement test, which is "recognition [of] official learning independently achieved or achieved (as in the case of those who did not join the school system in a timely manner or who interrupted their studies for more than a year) and who do not have the necessary requirements for validation or revalidation; provided they have seven or more years of age as of March 31. It also includes students from abroad who do not have the documents required for the validation or revalidation of studies." However, there is a barrier for students who finish school and do not have residency documents, since they cannot receive an official certificate of completion since the education system does not distribute other forms of identification other than a Residence Card for migrant students. This creates a barrier for adult learners, and means they are unable to continue studying at a technical school or university.

question_text_en: Right to be free from discrimination on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: National law protects this right for all regular migrants. Though the University Law (Law N° 30220), Article 97 states that: "Foreign students do not require a visa to enroll," registration to all universities requires a valid identity card: a national identity card or an immigration card. Furthermore, regular migrants can access Alternative Basic Education (General Education Law, Law N° 28044, Article 37) which is a series of studies aimed at young people and adults who do not have access to regular or non-culinary education. However, this also requires a valid identity document for the registration procedure. The Ministry of Work and Employment Promotion holds vocational training programs, as well, but these too require a valid identity document to access.

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after convictions.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The Peruvian Immigration Law, Article 57 sets out the situations where a migrant can lose their residence status. This criteria includes: "a. For being in an irregular immigration status for entering the country without carrying out the migratory control and not having applied for regularization. b. For being in irregular immigration status due to exceeding the residence time granted and not having requested its regularization in the period set by the regulation. c. For breaking or contravening the rules of public health imperatives. d. For having been penalized for serious conduct or very serious infringement in environmental matters by the competent authority." Additionally, Peruvian Immigration Law (Legislative Decree N° 1350), Article 58, sets out criteria for expulsion. Article 58 states that, "58.1. Foreigners will be expelled if they are involved in the following cases: ...e. For violating the cultural heritage of the Nation. F. Carry out activities that violate the public order, internal order, or security national. g. By order of the Judiciary. h. Upon obtaining freedom after serving a sentence ordered by a Peruvian court."

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of torture or inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Peruvian Refugee (Law N° 27891), Articles 5 and 11. Article 5 - the Right to non-refoulement, states that, "5.1 Any person who invokes refugee status can enter national territory, unable to be rejected, returned, expelled, extradited or subject to any measure that may mean your return to the country where their life, integrity, or freedom are threatened for the reasons stated in the Article 3 of this Law". Article 111, which states that, "In the exercise of migration control, MIGRATION may carry out the following actions: a) Admit or prevent the entry or exit of the territory national, according to the provisions contained in the regulations in force, and must respect the Principle of Non-Return and non-rejection at the border for the case of applications for refuge and asylum." 2) The Peruvian State has also signed and ratified the Convention against Torture, and has incorporated the Convention into its domestic law through Legislative Resolution No. 24815 of May 24, 1988. This provision is also referenced in Article 5 of the Refugee Law.

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of persecution.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru Protects this right in the Peruvian Refugee Law (Law N° 27891), Articles 3, and 5. Article 5 - Right to non-refoulement, states that: "5.1 Any person who invokes refugee status can enter national territory, unable to be rejected, returned, expelled, extradited or subject to any measure that may mean your return to the country where their life, integrity, or freedom are threatened for the reasons stated in the Article 3 of this Law." Article 3 - Definition of Refugee, clarifies: "One is considered as a refugee: a) To the person who, due to well-founded fear of being persecuted for reasons of race, religion, nationality, belonging to a certain social group or political opinions, is outside the country of his nationality and is unable or, due to such fears, is unwilling to take refuge to the protection of that country; or who lacking nationality and being, as a result of such events, outside the country where he previously had his habitual residence, cannot or, at because of such fears, do not want to return to it."

question_text_en: Right to not return to a deprivations of fundamental human rights.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Peruvian Refugee Law (Law N° 27891), Articles 3, and 5. Article 5 - Right to non-refoulement, states that: "5.1 Any person who invokes refugee status can enter national territory, unable to be rejected, returned, expelled, extradited or subject to any measure that may mean your return to the country where their life, integrity, or freedom are threatened for the reasons stated in the Article 3 of this Law." Article 3 - Definition of Refugee, clarifies: "One is considered as a refugee: a) To the person who, due to well-founded fear of being persecuted for reasons of race, religion, nationality, belonging to a certain social group or political opinions, is outside the country of his nationality and is unable or, due to such fears, is unwilling to take refuge to the protection of that country; or who lacking nationality and being, as a result of such events, outside the country where he previously had his habitual residence, cannot or, at because of such fears, do not want to return to it."

question_text_en: Right to be advised of availability of asylum before expulsion.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from chain refoulement.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to protection against expulsion except following a legal judgment.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Peruvian Immigration Law (Legislative Decree N° 1350), Article 64 - Formalization and execution of immigration sanctions, which states that: "a. Mandatory departure and expulsion sanctions are formalized by administrative resolution of MIGRATION and are of immediate execution, of according to what is established in the Regulation of the present Legislative Decree.” Additionally, the Constitutional Court, Ruling N° STC 2744-2015-PA / TC states that, "In this context, this Court understands that, within the framework of an immigration procedure Immigration, it is necessary to recognize foreigners in irregular situations the following minimum formal guarantees: i) the right to be informed expressly and formally of the reasons that resulted in the imposition of the administrative penalty (fine, exit mandatory, cancellation of permanence or residence, or expulsion) and of charges against her/him if any. The knowledge can be given by written communication addressed to the last address registered by the foreigner before the immigration authority, and will contain a full copy of the respective resolution, or failing that, at the time the foreigner in irregular situation belongs to the competent authority to regularize its stay in the country. Here, what is noted above regarding the character is particularly important in case of exceptional administrative detention of a migrant in an irregular situation, which will only be justified when there is an imminent risk of escape that can affect future legal proceedings or administrative proceedings and when there are not alternative less harmful measures that guarantee their appearance before the immigration authority, or when the person represents a danger to their own safety or to public safety; it should last the shortest possible amount of time and from an individual evaluation of each case, with respect for the corresponding procedural safeguards; ii) the possibility of exposing and proving the reasons that assist against it of the administrative penalty imposed; iii) the possibility of requesting and receiving legal advice, including through free public service if applicable and, if applicable, translation or interpretation, as well as consular assistance, if applicable; iv) in case of an unfavorable decision, the right to submit your case to review before a competent and impartial authority, which is obliged to resolve the corresponding resources within a reasonable time. The migrant may appeal in their own right or through a representative; y) the eventual expulsion may only be made after a decision based on the law and duly notified.

question_text_en: Right to submit reasons against expulsion and have case reviewed before deportation.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in 1) the Peruvian Immigration Law (Supreme Decree N° 007-2017-IN), Article 211 - Administrative appeal: "211.1. Against the resolution that imposes a sanction, an appeal may be filed within fifteen (15) business days, counted from the day following the occurrence of the notification. 211.2. After the period stipulated in the preceding numeral, without having presented the resource, the right to articulate it will be lost and the sanction imposed remains firm. 211.3. For the other resources, it will be applied the provisions of Law No. 27444, Law of the General Administrative Procedure." 2) Rules of Procedure (Supreme Decree N? 007-2017-IN), Articles 208 and 209.

question_text_en: Right of settled migrants to family reunification.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. However, the law does provide a pathway for children who are born in Peru, and those who live in Peru before 5 years old according to the Peruvian Nationality Law, article 4: "They can exercise the right of option to acquire nationality: a) persons born outside the territory of the Republic, children of foreign parents, who have resided in Peru since the age of five and who, upon reaching the age of majority, according to Peruvian laws, express their will to be so before the competent authority".

question_text_en: Right to judicial remedy for denials of right to family reunification.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Peruvian Immigration Law (Legislative Decree N° 1350), Article 37- Family Reunification, which states, "37.1 The national who has a family relationship with a foreigner or foreigner, can request to MIGRATION and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs as appropriate, the immigration status of a resident of any of the members of his/her family nucleus. The arrangement also assists the foreigner to request family reunification in the foreseen situations in the Regulation. 37.2. To relatives abroad with temporary migratory quality with permanence greater than 90 days, due to family reunification, they are assigned the same migratory status as the foreign holder. The migratory status of the foreign holder extends to their relatives. 37.3. Relatives from abroad with a resident migrant category may or may not opt ??for the migratory status of a resident or another at his/her choice if they meet the requirements of the regulations. The migratory status of the foreign holder is not extended to their relatives, and may be different."

question_text_en: Right to recognition of same-sex marital relationships.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Peruvian General Administrative Procedure Law (Law N° 27444), Articles 199 and 226, which states, "199.3 Negative administrative silence has the effect of enabling the person to file administrative appeals and pertinent judicial actions." The refusal of family reunification is due to negative administrative silence (no answer from the administration) and consequently, the General Administrative Procedure Law is applicable. Furthermore, if the acts is not a negative administrative silence act (if the refusal is done by a written decision), an appeal is also possible: "If the administrative route is exhausted, the administrative acts may be challenged before the Judiciary through the administrative contentious process referred to in article 148 of the Political Constitution of the State." 2) Legislative Decree N? 1350. 3) Rules of Procedure (Supreme Decree N? 007-2017-IN), Article 26. 4) The Refugee Law, Article 12.

question_text_en: Right to family reunification without resource conditions
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. National law in Peru does not recognize same-sex relationships under the family reunification framework in the Peruvian Civil Code, Articles 234 and 326. This is because it defines marriage as, "the union voluntarily arranged by a man and woman legally fit for it and formalized subject to the provisions of this Code, in order to make common life.” Furthermore, Article 326: “The de facto union, voluntarily carried out and maintained by a man and a woman, free from marital impediment, to achieve purposes and fulfill duties similar to those of marriage, originates a company of goods that is subject to the company regime Earnings, as applicable, provided that the said union has lasted at least two continuous years.”

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Peruvian Immigration Law (Legislative Decree N° 1350), article 30 - Change of Immigration Status, which states that: "30.1 The foreigner can change their migration status. The change must be processed before MIGRATION according to the conditions and requirements established in the Regulation. 30.2 The foreigner can only have one migration status at the same time".

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services regardless of status.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right for irregular migrants whose status becomes irregular after the enter the country in the Peruvian Immigration Law (Legislative Decree N° 1350), Article 36 - Immigration regularization, which states that: "Foreigners who are in an irregular migratory situation, can request the lifting of their impediment to entry and/or regularize their situation in accordance with the provisions set forth in the Regulations." The Regulations of the Peruvian Immigration Law (Supreme Decreee N° 007-2017-IN), Article 220.- Migratory regularization due to overstay of stay. 220.1. The foreigner with a temporary migratory status that irregular situation due to expiration of the term of stay, have a period of thirty (30) calendar days to regularize their migratory situation". Supreme Decree No. 010-2020-IN enabled a temporary regime that allowed any foreigner in an irregular migratory situation to regularize his/her status. However, there was a time limit to apply, since it was aimed at people whose entry was prior to 10/22/2020. There are no regularization options for people who entered after that date.

question_text_en: Right of access to public housing programs.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Unique Ordered Text of the Productivity and Labor Competitiveness (Supreme Decree No. 003-97-TR), Article 34, which states that the dismissal is arbitrary if it does not express a cause or if this cause is not able to be proved in court. In this situation, the worker is entitled to the payment of the compensation established in Article 38, as the only reparation for the damage suffered. Workers can simultaneously demand payment of any other pending social rights or benefits. In cases of null dismissal, if the claim is declared well founded, the worker will be replaced in his employment, unless in the execution of sentence, opt for the compensation established in Article 38. 2) The Peruvian Immigration Law (Legislative Decree N° 1350), Article 9 - Rights of foreigners, which states: "9.1. The State recognizes the foreigner the enjoyment and exercise of fundamental rights established in the Political Constitution of Peru, such as access to health, education, and work on equal terms with nationals, except for the prohibitions and limitations established in current regulations." 3) The Regulations of the Foreign Workers Recruitment Law (Supreme Decree N° 014-92-TR), article 23 states: "In no case do the remunerations, rights, and benefits of the foreign workers will be less than those recognized for the Labor Regime of the Private Activity."

question_text_en: Right to equal access to free primary education for migrant children.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right for regular migrants. While the Constitution of Peru, Article 7 states that, "Everyone has the right to protection of his health, his family environment, and his community, just as it is his duty to contribute to their development and defense. Any individual unable to care for himself due to physical or mental disability has the right to respect for his dignity and to a regime of protection, care, rehabilitation, and security," the Administrative Directive N° 001- 2020-SIS/GA?V.01 Article 5.4, which regulates access to the health care system further stipulates that a migrant needs: "5.4.1 National Identity Document (DNI) or Immigration Card (CE)," to apply.

question_text_en: Right to equal pay for the same work.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for all parts of Peru. However, migrants do have the right to stand for elections in most municipalities under the Peruvian Municipal Elections Law (Law N° 26864), Article 7, which states that: "Foreigners over 18 years of age, residents for more than two continuous years prior to the election, are empowered to elect and be elected, except in border municipalities, provided and when they are duly registered in the corresponding registry. To exercise this right, the Foreigner is identified with their respective immigration card." This right exists only for local elections, and does not apply to border municipalities.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of choice of employment.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Peruvian Constitution, Article 2 - Fundamental rights of the person, which states that: "Every person has the right: 2. To equality before the law. No one should be discriminated against the reason of origin, race, sex, language, religion, opinion, condition economic or any other nature." Additionally, the Constitutional Court has stated that "(...) is noted in our Constitution, which hosts equal legal treatment in matters of fundamental rights between nationals and foreigners, with exceptional limitations in the exercise of certain rights (freedom of transit - Article 2.11, property - Article 71-, among others). This follows from the provisions of the introductory part of its Article 2, which prescribes that "everyone has the right to [...]", without making any distinction between the two legal conditions; and it also falls within the provisions of subsection 2 of the same provision, which recognizes that "everyone has the right to equality before the law. No one should be discriminated against on grounds of origin, race, sex, language, religion, opinion, economic condition or of any other nature" (Foundation 7, File No. 042744-2015-PA / TC, November 8, 2016).

question_text_en: Right of spouse/partner of principal migrant to work.
citation_text_en: National law protects this right in the Peruvian Constitution, article 2 - Fundamental rights of the person: "Every person has the right: 2. To equality before the law. No one should be discriminated against the reason of origin, race, sex, language, religion, opinion, condition economic or any other nature." Article 9 of Legislative Decree No. 1350 recognizes that migrants enjoy and exercise the fundamental rights established in the Constitution. Additionally, Article 6 of the aforementioned law states that the migrant, when admitted to the territory, is subject to the same rights and duties as a Peruvian citizen.

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after loss of employment.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Peruvian Immigration Law (Supreme Decree N° 007-2017-IN), Articles 9, 11, and 26. Article 9 recognizes "the enjoyment and exercise of the fundamental rights established in the Political Constitution of Peru, such as access to health, education and work on equal terms as nationals, except for the prohibitions and limitations established in current regulations." Article 11 states: "11.1. The Ministry of Labor and Employment Promotion dictates the rules and establishes the necessary measures to protect the labor rights of foreign persons subject to the private regime, even in irregular immigration status. In the case of persons subject to the public regime, SERVIR provides for the protection of said rights. 11.2. The immigration irregularity situation of a foreign person does not affect the exercise or claim of labor rights in front of their employer." Article 26 provides that "The following principles are respected in the employment relationship: Equal opportunities without discrimination..."

question_text_en: Right to equal employment conditions and protection.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Peruvian Immigration Law (Legislative Decree N° 1350), Article 29.2, which states: "h. Employee Residence Quality: Allows the foreigner to carry out profit-making activities, subordinately or independently, for the public or private sectors, under an employment contract, administrative relationship, or contract for the provision of services. The benefits stipulated in international conventions on the matter are granted to border workers. This residence quality is granted under a contract of work previously approved by the Ministry of Work and Employment Promotion. Includes employees of a transnational company or international corporation and that travels to Peru to work in a company of the same economic group or holding, to perform as senior management or trusted personnel, or as a specialist. This residence quality is granted by MIGRATION. The term of stay for this residence quality is three hundred sixty-five (365) days." Employee Residence Quality is a type of residence that any migrant who has a job can ask for. During the 365 days, they can change jobs but they need to ask for a new permit. If they lose the job during the 365 days, they will mantain the permit. However, they will need to have a contract at the moment they have to renew the permit.

question_text_en: Right to form trade unions and other associations.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Peruvian Immigration Law (Legislative Decree N° 1350), Aticle 29.2, which states that: "Y. Relative of resident: Permits residence to the foreign member of the family migratory unit of a Peruvian or resident alien. Allows lucrative activities in a subordinate or independent way. This immigration quality is granted by MIGRATION. The term of permanence is up to two years." So long as the migrant's spouse has entered Peru on a family reunification basis, their visa class will confer "relative of resident" status, meaning automatic right to work.

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to redress before deportation or withdrawal of residency permit.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right for most migrants in the Peruvian Immigration Law (Legislative Decree N° 1350), Article 29.2, and 32. For regular migrants whose status is not linked specifically to a work requirements, loss of employment does not affect immigration status. However, if the visa is one of "Employee residence status", loss of employment implies loss of immigration status unless a new job is found before the initial residence permit expires.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to social security protections.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in 1) the Peruvian Immigration Law (Legislative Decree N° 1350), Article 9 - Rights of foreigners: "9.1. The State recognizes the foreigner the enjoyment and exercise of fundamental rights established in the Political Constitution of Peru, such as access to health, education, and work on equal terms with nationals, except for the prohibitions and limitations established in current regulations." 2) The Regulations of the Foreign Workers Recruitment Law (Supreme Decree N° 014-92-TR), article 23 states: "In no case do the remunerations, rights, and benefits of the foreign workers will be less than those recognized for the Labor Regime of the Private Activity." 3) Articles 24 and 25 of the Constitution of Peru.

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to become lawfully settled.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in 1) the Peruvian Immigration Law (Legislative Decree N° 1350), Article 9 - Rights of foreigners, which states: "9.1. The State recognizes the foreigner the enjoyment and exercise of fundamental rights established in the Political Constitution of Peru, such as access to health, education, and work on equal terms with nationals, except for the prohibitions and limitations established in current regulations." 2) The Regulations of the Foreign Workers Recruitment Law (Supreme Decree N° 014-92-TR), Article 23, which states: "In no case do the remunerations, rights, and benefits of the foreign workers will be less than those recognized for the Labor Regime of the Private Activity." 3) Article 10 of the Peruvian Constitution, which states, "the State recognizes the universal and progressive right of each person to social security for his protection from contingencies specified by law, and for the elevation of his quality of life." In Peru, there are two types of pensions: the public system and the private system. In either case, disbursement depend on the time and magnitude of contributions.

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to settle regardless of initial status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right as Peruvian law does not establish provisions for unemployment for anyone.

question_text_en: Right to redress following employer breach of employment contract.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Peruvian Immigration Law (Legislative Decree N° 1350), article 30 - Change of Immigration Status: "30.1 The foreigner can change the migratory quality. The change must be processed before MIGRATION according to the conditions and requirements established in the Regulation. 30.2 The foreigner can only have one migration quality at the same time".

question_text_en: Right not to have identity documents confiscated.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in 1) the Constitutional Procedure Code, Law N° 31307, Article 33, which states that "habeas corpus proceeds before the action or omission that threatens or violates the following rights that, by way of example, make up individual freedom: 11) The right not to be deprived of the national identity document, as well as to obtain the passport or its renewal inside or outside the Republic."

question_text_en: Right to birth registration.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in Law Nº 26497 "Organic Law of the National Registry of Identification and Civil Status", article 46, which states that, "Registrations of births produced in the Ministry's hospitals of Health and the Peruvian Institute of Social Security will be carried out compulsorily within the third day of birth, in the civil registry offices installed in said hospitals. Registrations of births not contemplated in the previous paragraph will be carried out within a period of thirty (30) days and will be carried out, preferably in the dependence of the registry under whose jurisdiction the birth occurred or the place where the child resides".

question_text_en: Right to government document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Peruvian Immigration Law (Legislative Decree N° 1350), Articles 17 and 127. Article 17 states that "The Immigration Card is a foreigners' official identity document in the national territory, issued by MIGRATION to prove their identity and residence, including temporary residence, in Peru. Regulatory provisions issued by MIGRATION regulates the conditions for its granting." The Peruvian Migrant agency assigns a specific type of residence to people when they enter the country, including information about the period of stay in the territory. The document shows what type of residence they have, for example, for work, studies, and family.

question_text_en: Right against destruction of document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Peruvian Criminal Code (Legislative Decree N° 635), Article 430, which states that, "Whoever suppresses, destroys or hides a document, in whole or in part, in a way that could be detrimental to another, will be punished with the penalty indicated in articles 427 and 428, as the case may be."

question_text_en: Right to communicate with consular officials.
citation_text_en: National law protects this right in the Peruvian Immigration Law (Decreto Legislativo 1350), Articles 150, 200, and 212. Article 150 states that "150.2. MIGRATION must inform the foreign person who may request to communicate with her/his consular authority if she/he considers it necessary." Article 200, which states, "200.4. The Peruvian National Police (PNP), within the framework of its powers, may detain the offending person in order to make her/his identification and determine her/his migratory situation. The foreign person will be informed of her/his right to communicate with the consular representatives within the framework of international treaties and conventions of which Peru is part." Article 212, which states that, "212.2. For the execution of the imposed sanction, and within the framework of its powers, the PNP may detain the offending person in order to guarantee her/his departure from the country. The foreign person will be informed of their right to communicate with their consular representative in the framework of treaties and international agreements to which Peru is a signatory."

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Peruvian Immigration Law (Legislative Decree N° 1350), Article 53, which states that "in no case MIGRATION will apply sanctions on girls, boys, and adolescents." Additionally, Article 66 states that "minors and people with absolute incapacity are not subject to a disciplinary procedure or administrative sanction for immigration infractions."

question_text_en: Right of migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. National law in Peru allows the detention of migrants on the basis of their status as a migrant in the Peruvian Immigration Law (Legislative Decree N° 1350), article 200.4. The National Police, within the framework of its powers, may retain the person offender in order to make his identification and determine his immigration status. It is also possible to retain them for the enforcement of an expulsion sanction (Article 212.2 of the Regulations).

question_text_en: Right to appeal legality, conditions, and length of detention
citation_text_en: The law does not provide migrants deprived of their liberty on account of their migratory status an opportunity to appeal legality, conditions or length of detention because there is no detention sanction related to migration status. Detention of migrants is possible only if they commit a crime and, in that case, they have the same rights as any Peruvian citizens. Migrants who are accused of crime receive the same protections as citizens and are able to appeal conditions, legality, length of criminal detention under: the Peruvian Constitution, Article 200 - Constitutional Guarantee Actions, which guarantees: 1. The Action of Habeas Corpus, which proceeds before the fact or omission, by any authority, official, or person, that violates or threatens individual liberty or related constitutional rights.

question_text_en: Right to an individualized detention decision.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in 1) the Criminal Procedural Code, Articles 67 and 262. Article 262 states that, "The arrest warrant must contain the identity data of the accused, a concise statement of the facts subject to imputation, factual and legal grounds, and expressly mention the applicable legal regulations". In cases where migrants are to be detained, detention is usually a consequence of police preventive operations to identify irregular migrants or migrants with criminal records. It is important to notice that in Peru police can confiscate the identity documents of every person (national or foreign), consequently, these preventive operations are authorized by the individual officers suspicions. However, once the police identify an irregular migrant (or one with criminal records), it informs the migration authority that analyzes the case and determines the sanction (usually, expulsion from the national territory). This sanction requires an individualized determination.

question_text_en: Right to be free from torture and inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law protects this right in the Constitution of Peru, Article 2, sub-section 24, which states that "h. No one should be a victim of moral, psychological or physical violence, or subjected to torture or inhuman or humiliating treatment."

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The Legislative Decree N? 1186, Law of Use of Force (Article 8) does not establish that officers can or cannot apply force for preventing migrants from entering the state’s territory. However, the National Police are responsible for implementing compulsory departure under Article 64 of Peruvian Immigration Law (Legislative Decree N? 1350) and its Regulations(Supreme Decree N? 007-2017-IN).

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of lethal force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: National law protects this right in the Peruvian Use of Force Law (Decreto Legislativo 1186), article 8.3, which states that "agents of the National Police of Peru, exceptionally, may use the firearm when strictly necessary, and only when less extreme measures prove insufficient or inappropriate, in the following situations: a. In self-defense or that of others in case of real and imminent danger of death or serious injuries. b. When a situation occurs that involves a serious threat to life during the commission of a particularly serious crime. c. When a real and imminent danger of death or serious injury is generated as a result of the resistance offered by the person who is going to be arrested. d. When a person's life is put at real, imminent, and current risk by whoever is running away. e. When a real or imminent danger of death of police personnel or another person is generated by the action of someone who participates in a violent riot."

question_text_en: Right to be protected from trafficking or smuggling.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. There is no provision on the Law Against Trafficking in Persons and Illicit Traffic in Migrants (Law N° 28950) or other national law that protects of migrant victims of smuggling and trafficking from criminal prosecution. However, defense lawyers can use the non-imputability exception if applicable to the case under Article 20 of the Peruvian Criminal Code ("anyone who, in the face of a current and otherwise unavoidable danger, which means a threat to life, bodily integrity, or freedom, performs an unlawful act to avert the danger from himself or from a person with whom he is close linkage").

question_text_en: Right to maintain citizenship status after convictions.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru provides that convictions for criminal or other offenses lead to a loss of the citizenship status of naturalized migrants in the Regulation of the Peruvian Citizenship Law (Supreme Decree N° 004-97-IN), article 12: "Naturalization will be canceled for the following reasons: a. For crimes against the State and National Defense. b. For crimes against Public Security, in the form of illicit drug trafficking. c. For delusions of terrorism and treason against the Homeland, provided for in Decree Laws N° 25475, 25659 and its amendments. d. For committing acts that could affect National Security and the interest of the State, prior report from the competent bodies. and for having improperly obtained Naturalization, transgressing established norms as requirements to grant it. F. For affecting the international relations of Peru with other States or International. h. For reasons that affect the public interest and the national interest".

question_text_en: Right of economic migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Peruvian Nationality Law (Law N° 26574), Article 3, which states that, economic migrants can gain citizenship through naturalization if they meet the following criteria: a) Reside legally in the territory of the Republic for at least two consecutive years; b) Regularly exercise profession, art, trade or business activity; and, c) Have no criminal record, have good conduct and moral solvency.

question_text_en: Right of humanitarian migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Peruvian Nationality Law (Law N° 26574), Article 3, which states that humanitarian migrants have a pathway to citizenship if they meet the following criteria: a) Reside legally in the territory of the Republic for at least two consecutive years; b) Regularly exercise profession, art, trade or business activity; and, c) Have no criminal record, have good conduct and moral solvency.

question_text_en: Right of family migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Peruvian Nationality Law (Law N° 26574) in Article 4, which states that family migrants have a pathway to citizenship if: "1. Persons born outside the territory of the Republic, children of foreign parents, who have resided in Peru since they were five years old and who at the time of reaching the age of majority, according to Peruvian law, express their willingness to be so before the competent authority. 2. The foreign person united in marriage with a Peruvian or Peruvian and resident, in this condition, in the territory of the Republic for at least two years, who expresses his desire to do so before the competent authority. The husband naturalized by marriage does not lose Peruvian nationality in the event of divorce or death of the spouse."

question_text_en: Right to dual nationality.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Peruvian Nationality Law (Law N° 26574), Articles 9, 10, and 11. Article 10 states that, "People who enjoy dual nationality, exercise the rights and obligations of the nationality of the country where they reside." Article 11 states that "dual citizenship does not confer upon foreigners who naturalize, the exclusive rights of Peruvians by birth."

question_text_en: Right to freedom to hold opinion.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Constitution of the Republic of Peru, Article 2 - Fundamental rights of the person, which states that, "Every person has the right: 3. To freedom of conscience and religion, individually or associate. There is no persecution for reasons of ideas or beliefs. There are no crimes of opinion The public exercise of all confessions is free, as long as it does not offend morality or disturb public order." Article 9 of Legislative Decree No. 1350 further recognizes that migrants enjoy and exercise the fundamental rights established in the Constitution, and further stipulates in Article 6 that migrants, when admitted to the territory, are subject to the same rights and duties as Peruvian citizens.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of expression.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Constitution, Article 2 - Fundamental rights of the person, which states that, "Every person has the right: 3. To freedom of conscience and religion, individually or associate. There is no persecution for reasons of ideas or beliefs. There are no crimes of opinion The public exercise of all confessions is free, as long as it does not offend morality or disturb public order." Article 9 of Legislative Decree No. 1350 recognizes that migrants enjoy and exercise the fundamental rights established in the Constitution. Additionally, Article 6 of the aforementioned law states that the migrant, when admitted to the territory, is subject to the same rights and duties as a Peruvian citizen.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of association.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Constitution of Peru, Article 2 - Fundamental rights of the person, which states that: "Every person has the right: 4. To freedom of information, opinion, expression, and dissemination of thought through the oral or written word or image, for any means of social communication, without prior authorization or censorship or any impediment, under the responsibilities of law." Article 9 of Legislative Decree No. 1350 recognizes that migrants enjoy and exercise the fundamental rights established in the Constitution. Additionally, Article 6 of the aforementioned law states that the migrant, when admitted to the territory, is subject to the same rights and duties as a Peruvian citizen.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of assembly.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Constitution of Peru, Article 2 - Fundamental rights of the person, which states that: "Every person has the right: 13. To associate and establish foundations and various forms of non-profit legal organization, without prior authorization and with according to law. They can not be dissolved by administrative decisions." Additionally, Article 28 - Collective rights of the worker, states that: "Right of unionization, collective bargaining, and the right to strike." Article 9 of Legislative Decree No. 1350 recognizes that migrants enjoy and exercise the fundamental rights established in the Constitution. Additionally, Article 6 of the aforementioned law states that the migrant, when admitted to the territory, is subject to the same rights and duties as a Peruvian citizen.

category: Thought, conscience, and religion or belief
question_text_en: Right of freedom of thought, conscience and religion or belief.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in 1) the Regulation of the Peruvian Immigration Law (Supreme Decree N° 007-2017-IN), Article 89-A. 2) The Legislative Decree N? 1350 and its Rules of Procedure (Supreme Decree N? 007-2017-IN). There are no resource requirements for family reunification. Any migrant can apply; but the sponsor has to prove that they do not have a criminal record, and they must prove they have an actual family link with the sponsored migrant.

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to access criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Peruvian Immigration Law (Legislative Decree N° 1350), Article 9, which states that : "9.1. The Judiciary and the Public Ministry guarantee the foreign person access to justice services, without discrimination on grounds of immigration status. 9.2. The National Police of Peru is in the obligation to receive the complaint made by any foreign person, establishing special protection measures for cases of foreigners in a vulnerable situation." 2) Article 94 of the Criminal Procedure Code stipulates that an aggrieved person is any person who is directly affected by the crime or harmed by its consequences. The law does not distinguish by nationality or legal status.

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to immigration status or relief from expulsion.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in 1) the Peruvian Immigration Law (Legislative Decree N° 1350), Article 11, which provides migrants in vulnerable situations (children, girls and adolescents, older adults, people with disabilities, or who belong to an indigenous community indigenous, migrants victims of human trafficking and human smuggling, victims of family and sexual violence, and who require protection in response to a serious threat or affectation of their fundamental rights) documents and/or temporary stay permits or relevant residence statuses. 2) Regulation of the Legislative Decree N° 1350, Article 91, reasserts this avenue for victims of human trafficking or illicit trafficking.

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: National law protects this right in 1) Peruvian Immigration Law (Decreto Legislativo 1350), Articles VI and 11. Article IV stipulates that "every measure concerning the child and adolescent that the State adopts through all its institutions, as well as in the action of society, will consider the principle of the best interests of the child and adolescent and respect for their rights." Article 11 states that, "Foreign people in a vulnerable situation 11.1 MIGRATION and the Ministry of Relations Foreign Affairs notify the competent authorities of migrants' situations of vulnerability in order to adopt the administrative or judicial actions that correspond to the protection of their rights, in particular, those related to boys, girls, and adolescents 2) Regulations of the Peruvian Immigration Law No. 1350 (Decreto Supremo 007-2017-IN), Article 146, which states that "protection measures for unaccompanied foreign girls, boys, and adolescents 146.1. MIGRATION will evaluate and arrange the granting of special migratory status to allow the entry of the unaccompanied girl, boy, or adolescent to Peruvian territory and transfer the child or adolescent to the Ministry of Women and Vulnerable Populations until the end of the procedure that determines their permanence or exit of the Peruvian territory [...]". 146.2. The Ministry of Women and Populations Vulnerable can request a change of the migratory status if necessary, and will carry out the steps to maintain regularity migratory status of the girl, boy, or adolescent."

question_text_en: Right of women migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: National law in Peru protects this right in the Peruvian Immigration Law (Decreto Supremo 007-2017-IN), Article 227, which states that women victims of violence or pregnant women are explicitly considered as a vulnerable category deserving of protections.

question_text_en: Rights of migrants with disabilities to special protection.
citation_text_en: National law protects this right in 1) the Peruvian Immigration Law (Decreto Legislativo 1350), Article 11, which states: "Foreign people in a vulnerable situation 11.1 MIGRATION and the Ministry of Relations Foreign Affairs notify the competent authorities of migrants' situations of vulnerability in order to adopt the administrative or judicial actions that correspond to the protection of their rights, in particular, those related to people with disabilities. 11.2 MIGRATION and Relations Ministry of Foreign Affairs within the scope of its powers adopt criteria to assist people in a situation of vulnerability; being able to issue the documents and/or temporary stay permits or relevant residence." 2) Regulations of the Peruvian Immigration Law (Decreto Supremo 007-2017-IN), Article 227, which states, "Assumptions of situations of vulnerability [...] f) People with disabilities [...]. Regulations of the Peruvian Immigration Law (Decreto Supremo 007-2017-IN), article 230: Immigration protection measures 230.1. The Immigration Authorities will issue the documents and/or temporary permit of permanence to foreigners in situations of vulnerability, it requires the technical report of the specialized unit in the matters; measures could include granting terms extensions and exoneration of stipulated fines and processing fees in current immigration regulations or others, according to each specific case. 230.2. MIGRATION, in cases of situations of vulnerability may exempt the foreign person from the presentation of requirements established for the procedures stipulated in the current immigration regulations or others, following a report from the specialized unit in the matters. 230.3. MIGRACIONES may grant the Special Migration Quality to foreigners in an extreme situation of vulnerability, allowing their permanence in situations not contemplated in the others migratory qualities, the quality that will be granted prior report from the specialized unit in the matter."
