citation_text_en: [1]: Kirill Boychenko (for backcoded questions Dmitrii Poletaev) [2]: Roman Rybakov

question_text_en: What country are you coding?
citation_text_en: Russia

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to vote in local and/or regional elections.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this Constitutional right for citizens and migrants alike and does not impose any further restriction under Federal law: 1) Article 31 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation: Citizens of the Russian Federation shall have the right to assemble peacefully, without weapons, hold rallies, meetings and demonstrations, marches and pickets. In conjunction, Part 3, Article 62 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation states that: “ 3. Foreign citizens and stateless persons in the Russian Federation enjoy the rights and bear obligations on an equal basis with citizens of the Russian Federation, except in cases established by federal law or an international treaty of the Russian Federation.” 2) Federal Law No. 54-FZ of June 19, 2004 "On Meetings, Rallies, Demonstrations, Processions and Picketing" does not prohibit migrants from exercising this right.

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to stand for election.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Article 32 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation gives "the right to elect and be elected to state bodies of power and local self-government bodities" and to "participate in referenda" only to Russian citizens. Suffrage for permanently residing foreign citizens is theoretically possible but has never been implemented in the Russian Federation: Article 12 of the Federal Law “On the legal status of foreign citizens in the Russian Federation” “Attitude of foreign citizens to the right to vote” 1. Foreign citizens in the Russian Federation shall not have the right to elect and be elected to federal bodies of state power, bodies of state power of constituent entities of the Russian Federation, as well as to participate in a referendum of the Russian Federation and referendums of constituent entities of the Russian Federation. 2. Foreign citizens permanently residing in the Russian Federation, in the cases and in the manner prescribed by federal laws, have the right to elect and be elected to local self government bodies, as well as to participate in a local referendum.

question_text_en: Right to equal protection of the law before courts.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in the Constitution of the Russian Federation: Article 19 which states: "1. All people shall be equal before the law and court. 2. The State shall guarantee the equality of rights and freedoms of man and citizen, regardless of sex, race, nationality, language, origin, property and official status, place of residence, religion, convictions, membership of public associations, and also of other circumstances. All forms of limitations of human rights on social, racial, national, linguistic or religious grounds shall be banned." According to Article 25.1 of the Code of the Russian Federation on Administrative Offenses of December 30, 2001 N 195-FZ (the rights of a person in respect of whom proceedings are being conducted in an administrative offense are granted to everyone equally, regardless of the presence of citizenship of the Russian Federation. The national law of the Russian Federation protects this right in relation to the criminal court in accordance with: Article 19 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation; Article 42, 46, 47. Code of Criminal Procedure of the Russian Federation (gives the same rights to all victims, accused, suspects, regardless of their citizenship of the Russian Federation); Section 13, 15 of the Code of Criminal Procedure of the Russian Federation (gives the same rights to appeal against court verdicts, regardless of the presence of citizenship of the Russian Federation). The national law of the Russian Federation protects this right in relation to the civil court in: Article 19 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation; Article 36 of the Civil Procedure Code of Russia “Civil Procedural Legal Capacity”: Civil procedural legal capacity is equally recognized for all citizens and organizations that, in accordance with the legislation of the Russian Federation, have the right to judicial protection of rights, freedoms and legitimate interests.

question_text_en: Right to government-provided counsel in proceedings related to migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to government-provided interpretation in criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: National law in Russia have a right to interpretation at government expense in criminal proceedings, in: 1) Part 2 of the article 18 of the Criminal Procedure Code of the Russian Federation, No. 174-FZ of December 18, 2001: "To participants in criminal court proceedings who have no command or just a poor command of the language in which the proceedings in the criminal case are conducted, shall be explained and guaranteed the right to make statements, to give explanations and testimony, to lodge petitions and complaints, to get acquainted with the materials of the criminal case and to take the floor in the court using their native tongue or another language of which they have a good command, and to make use free of charge of interpreter's services in accordance with the procedure established by the present Code." 2) Criminal Procedure Code of the Russian Federation of December 18, 2001, No. 174-FZ: Article 59 "Interpreter." 3) Federal Constitutional Law "On Judicial System of the Russian Federation" of December 31, 1996, No. 1-FKZ: Article 10 "The language of court proceedings."

question_text_en: Right to be protected from prosecution for unauthorized entry.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Migrants can be held criminally and administratively liable for unauthorized entry into the Russian Federation in accordance with Article 322 of the Russian Federation Criminal Code (June 13, 1996), N63-FZ: "Illegal Crossing of the Russian Federation state border." An exception to the general rule is the unauthorized entry of victims of human trafficking.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to public adult education institutions.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for migrants because housing is guaranteed only for citizens as outlined in part 2, article 49 of the Housing Code of the Russian Federation (December 29, 2004).

question_text_en: Right of access to public adult education institutions regardless of status.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in Part 1 and 2 of the article 78 of the Federal Law of the Russian Federation (December 29, 2012, No. 273-FZ): "About education in the Russian Federation": 1. Foreign nationals and stateless persons (hereinafter -foreign citizens) have the right to receive education in the Russian Federation in accordance with international treaties of the Russian Federation and the present Federal Law. 2. Foreign citizens shall have equal rights with citizens of the Russian Federation to receive pre-school, primary general, basic general and secondary education as well as vocational training programs for training in the professions of workers, positions of employees within the development of the educational program of secondary education on principles of equality and free of charge."

question_text_en: Right to be free from discrimination on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. National law in the Russian Federation does provide access to such education, however, it is not on an equal basis with citizens because it is subject to quotas: Part 1 and 2 of the article 78 of The Federal Law of the Russian Federation (December29, 2012), of No. 273-FZ: "About education in the Russian Federation" 1. Foreign nationals and stateless persons (hereinafter - foreign citizens) have the right to receive education in the Russian Federation in accordance with international treaties of the Russian Federation and the present Federal Law. 2. Foreign citizens shall have equal rights with citizens of the Russian Federation to receive pre-school, primary general, basic general and secondary education as well as vocational training programs for training in the professions of workers, positions of employees within the development of the educational program of secondary education on principles of equality and free of charge. 3. Foreign citizens have the right to receive secondary vocational education, higher education and additional vocational education from the budget allocations of the federal budget, budgets of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation or local budgets in accordance with international treaties of the Russian Federation, federal laws or the quota established by the Government of the Russian Federation for the education of foreign citizens in the Russian Federation (Hereinafter - quota), as well as at the expense of individuals and legal entities in accordance with agreements on provision of paid educational services.

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after convictions.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Russian law provides broad discretion for loss of residence status under a range of circumstances. 1) Article 26 Federal Law No. 114-FZof August 15, 1996 "On the Procedure for Departure from the Russian Federation and Entry into the Russian Federation:"With regard to migrants who have repeatedly (two or more times) within one year been brought to administrative responsibility for committing an administrative offense related to an encroachment on public order and public safety or in violation of the regime of stay (residence) of foreign citizens or stateless persons in the Russian Federation or the procedure for their labor activity on the territory of the Russian Federation, a decision may be made to ban entry into the Russian Federation. If a migrant is in the Russian Federation at the time such a decision is made, a decision is made to reduce the period of his stay and, as a result, the migrant is obliged to leave the Russian Federation. 2) Article 7 Federal Law No. 115-FZ of July 25, 2002 "On the Legal Status of Foreign Citizens in the Russian Federation.": Grounds for refusal to issue or annul a temporary residence permit. 3) Article 9 Federal Law of July 25, 2002 N 115-FZ "On the Legal Status of Foreign Citizens in the Russian Federation.": Grounds for refusal to issue or annul a residence permit The Federal Law "On the Russian Federation (RF) Citizenship" from May 31, 2002 N 62-FZ, Article 16: "Grounds for rejection of applications for receiving the Russian Federation (RF) citizenship, admission to the RF citizenship or for the restoration of the RF citizenship." A temporary residence permit is not issued or canceled if the Migrant: a) has been convicted by a court verdict that has entered into legal force for committing a grave or especially grave crime or for committing a crime related to illicit trafficking in narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances and their analogues or precursors, plants containing narcotic drugs or psychotropic substances or their precursors, as well as their parts containing narcotic drugs or psychotropic substances or their precursors; b) has an outstanding or unexpunged conviction for committing a grave or especially grave crime on the territory of the Russian Federation or outside it, recognized as such in accordance with federal law. For some administrative offenses, a migrant may be deprived of the status of TRP / residence permit, or a migrant may be denied these statuses. A migrant may be denied admission to Russian citizenship if they: a) have an unexpunged or outstanding conviction for committing intentional crimes on the territory of the Russian Federation or outside it, recognized as such in accordance with federal law; b) are prosecuted by the competent authorities of the Russian Federation or by the competent authorities of foreign states for crimes recognized as such in accordance with federal law (until a court verdict is passed or a decision is made on the case); c) have been convicted and are serving a sentence of imprisonment for actions prosecuted in accordance with federal law (until the expiration of the sentence).

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of torture or inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in: 1) Article 12 of the Ruling of The Plenary Session of The Supreme Court of The Russian Federation (14.06.2012) No. 11 "On the practice of review by courts of cases related to extradition of persons for criminal pursuit or execution of criminal punishment or imprisonment.": “Courts shall consider that in accordance with article 7 of the The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights in interpretation of the UN Committee on Human Rights and the article 3 of the Convention against Torture and Other Cruel, Inhuman or Degrading Treatment or Punishment Adopted and opened for signature, ratification and accession by General Assembly resolution 39/46 of 10 December 1984, "No State Party shall expel, return ("refouler") or extradite a person to another State where there are substantial grounds for believing that he would be in danger of being subjected to torture, or to inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment." 2) Article 4 of the Instructions approved by the Order of the Federal Security Service of the Russian Federation (23.12.2008) No. 631 "On approval of the Instruction on organization of actions of the border control bodies on administrative refoulement of foreign citizens and stateless persons from the territory of Russian Federation" states that: "A Foreign citizen shall not be expelled to another State where there are substantial grounds for believing that he would be in danger of being subjected to torture. For the purpose of determining whether there are such grounds, the competent authorities shall take into account all relevant considerations including, where applicable, the existence in the State concerned of a consistent pattern of gross, flagrant or mass violations of human rights." 3) Q 50(2) The Ruling Of The Plenary Session Of The Supreme Court cited in the above answer to this question refers to the extradition. It is common practice for the case law to refer to this ruling during the refoulement cases.

question_text_en: Right to not return to a risk of persecution.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in Article 4 of the Instructions approved by the Order of the Federal Security Service of the Russian Federation from 23.12.2008 No. 631 "On approval of the Instruction on organization of actions of the border control bodies on administrative refoulement of foreign citizens and stateless persons from the territory of Russian Federation" Expel or return (" refouler ") a refugee in any manner whatsoever to the frontiers of territories where his life or freedom would be threatened on account of his race, religion, nationality, membership of a particular social group or political opinion.

question_text_en: Right to not return to a deprivations of fundamental human rights.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in article 4 of the Instructions approved by the Order of the Federal Security Service of the Russian Federation from 23.12.2008 No. 631 "On approval of the Instruction on organization of actions of the border control bodies on administrative refoulement of foreign citizens and stateless persons from the territory of Russian Federation": "A Foreign citizen shall not be expelled to another State where there are substantial grounds for believing that he would be in danger of being subjected to torture. For the purpose of determining whether there are such grounds, the competent authorities shall take into account all relevant considerations including, where applicable, the existence in the State concerned of a consistent pattern of gross, flagrant or mass violations of human rights."

question_text_en: Right to be advised of availability of asylum before expulsion.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from chain refoulement.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Article 12 of the Order of the Federal Security Service of the Russian Federation of December 23,2008 No. 631 "On Approval of the Instruction on Organization of Activities of Border Authorities on Administrative Expulsion of Foreign Citizens or Stateless Persons from the Russian Federation": "12. In accordance with the article 32.10 of the Administrative Code of the Russian Federation, a decision on the administrative expulsion of a foreign citizen taken by a designated person of a Border Authority is implemented by means of: ...Controlled independent departure of a foreign citizen, who is a subject to administrative expulsion, from border checkpoint of the Russian Federation to the territory of the State from which he/she came to the Russian Federation or to the country of origin."

question_text_en: Right to protection against expulsion except following a legal judgment.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in part 2 of the article 3.10 of the Code of Administrative offences of The Russian Federation No. 195-Fz of December 30, 2001: "Administrative deportation from the Russian Federation as an administrative punitive measure shall be established in respect of foreign citizens and stateless persons and shall be imposed by a judge, but in the event, a foreign citizen or a stateless person commits an administrative offense when entering the Russian Federation, it shall be done by appropriate officials."

question_text_en: Right to submit reasons against expulsion and have case reviewed before deportation.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in: 1) Article 4 of the Administrative Court Proceedings Code of the Russian Federation (08.03.2015) 21-FZ: "Each concerned person has a right to apply to a court for protection of violated or disputed rights, freedoms, and legitimate interests." 2) Constitution of the Russian Federation (RF), Part 3, Article 62: “Foreign citizens and stateless persons in the Russian Federation enjoy the rights and bear obligations on an equal basis with citizens of the Russian Federation, except in cases established by federal law or an international treaty of the Russian Federation.” 3) Code of the Russian Federation (RF) on Administrative Offenses: a) Article 30.2: "Procedure for appealing against a decision in a case on an administrative offense" b) Article 30.1: "The right to appeal against the decision in the case of an administrative offense" c) Article 26.3: “Explanations of the person in respect of whom proceedings are being carried out in the case of an administrative offense."

question_text_en: Right of settled migrants to family reunification.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for all migrants. However, migrant children who are at risk of becoming stateless do have a right to acquire citizenship by birth under Article 12 of the Federal Law “On Citizenship of the Russian Federation” Acquisition of citizenship of the Russian Federation by birth : 1. A child acquires citizenship of the Russian Federation by birth if on the child's birthday: в) one of his parents has the citizenship of the Russian Federation, and the other parent is a foreign citizen, provided that the child was born on the territory of the Russian Federation or if otherwise he becomes a stateless person; г) both of his parents or his only parent residing on the territory of the Russian Federation are foreign citizens or stateless persons, provided that the child was born on the territory of the Russian Federation, and the state of which his parents or his only parent are citizens does not provide child his nationality. Adult migrants who are stateless and have legal capacity are entitled to apply for admission to the citizenship of the Russian Federation in a simplified manner without complying with the conditions for a five-year period of residence on the basis of a Residence Permit in the Russian Federation under Part 1, Article 14 of the Federal Law “On Citizenship of the Russian Federation.” After obtaining a Residence Permit, Stateless Persons have the right to immediately apply for citizenship but this is not guaranteed.

question_text_en: Right to judicial remedy for denials of right to family reunification.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation conditionally protects this right in Federal Law No. 115-FZ of July 25, 2002, "On the Legal Position of Foreign Citizens in the Russian Federation." Conditionality is based on visa type of the sponsoring migrant, and the family members they can sponsor.

question_text_en: Right to recognition of same-sex marital relationships.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in Article 46 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation which states: "1. Everyone shall be guaranteed the judicial protection of his rights and freedoms. 2. Decisions and actions (or inaction) of bodies of state authority and local self government, public associations and officials may be appealed against in court. 3. Everyone shall have the right to appeal, according to international treaties of the Russian Federation, to international bodies for the protection of human rights and freedoms, if all the existing internal state means of legal protection have been exhausted. The article 4 of the Administrative Court Proceedings Code of the Russian Federation from 08.03.2015 21-FZ: Each concerned person has a right to apply to a court for protection of violated or disputed rights, freedoms, and legitimate interests."

question_text_en: Right to family reunification without resource conditions
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. According to national law in Russia, same sex marital relationships are not recognized under the family reunification framework. Article 12 of the Family Code of The Russian Federation no. 223-fz (December 29, 1995) explains that "to enter into a marriage, the voluntary consent of the man and of the woman entering into it, and their reaching the marriageable age, shall be necessary."

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation provides temporary migrant workers with the opportunity to legally obtain permanent residence status, regardless of the type of visa. Temporary residence permit and residence permit give migrants the right to stay in Russia without obtaining additional visas and documents. The period of residence with a Temporary Residence Permit is 3 years. The period of residence with a residence permit is not established; it is unlimited.

question_text_en: Right of access to health care services regardless of status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right.

question_text_en: Right of access to public housing programs.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in Article 391 of the Labor Code of the Russian Federation (31 December 2001). Furthermore, Article 72 of the Labor Code, Federal Law No. 197-fz of 2001 Amending the Labor Contract Terms Defined by Parties Amending the terms of a labor contract defined by the parties, including transfer to another job, is admissible only by agreement of the parties thereto, except for the cases specified by the present Code. An agreement on amending the labor contract terms defined by the parties shall be made in writing. Migrants have the right to compensation for damage both in court and out of court on an equal basis with citizens of the Russian Federation.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to free primary education for migrant children.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in Article 19 of the Federal Law of November 21, 2012, No. 323-FZ "On Public Health Protection in the Russian Federation" : 3. The right to health care of foreign citizens living and staying in the territory of the Russian Federation, established by the Russian Federation legislation and relevant international treaties of the Russian Federation. Stateless persons permanently residing in the Russian Federation have the right to medical care on a par with Russian citizens, unless otherwise provided by international treaties of the Russian Federation. Article 5 Decree of the Government of the Russian Federation of March 6, 2013 N 186 "On approval of the Rules for the provision of medical care to foreign citizens on the territory of the Russian Federation" 5. Emergency, including emergency specialized, medical care is provided to foreign citizens in case of diseases, accidents, injuries, poisoning and other conditions requiring urgent medical intervention. Medical organizations of the state and municipal health care systems provide this medical care to foreign citizens free of charge. As a general rule, only emergency medical care is provided free of charge to temporarily staying foreign citizens. Planned medical care will not be provided free of charge. Refugees, persons who have received a temporary residence permit, a residence permit, have the opportunity to receive a wider range of medical services in Russia free of charge on the basis of Article 10 of the Federal Law of November 29, 2010 N 326-ФЗ “On Compulsory Medical Insurance in the Russian Federation.” Labor migrants from the countries of the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) have the right to receive medical care on an equal basis with Russian citizens in the case of official employment. Starting from 1 January 2023, foreign citizens temporary staying in the Russian Federation (except for highly qualified specialists) receive an access to health care services on an equal basis with Russian citizens, under the condition that the insurant has been paying insurance premium for them during the last three years (changes came into force on 1 January 2023 in accordance with Federal Law no.237-fz of14 July 2022).

question_text_en: Right to equal pay for the same work.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Article 32 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation gives "the right to elect and be elected to state bodies of power and local self-government bodities" and to "participate in referenda" only to Russian citizens. Article 12 of the Federal Law “On the legal status of foreign citizens in the Russian Federation", “Attitude of foreign citizens to the right to vote”: "1. Foreign citizens in the Russian Federation shall not have the right to elect and be elected to federal bodies of state power, bodies of state power of constituent entities of the Russian Federation, as well as to participate in a referendum of the Russian Federation and referendums of constituent entities of the Russian Federation..."

question_text_en: Right to freedom of choice of employment.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in part 2, Article 19 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation: “The state guarantees equality of rights and freedoms of man and citizen, regardless of gender, race, nationality, language, origin, property and official status, place of residence, attitude to religion, beliefs, membership in public associations, as well as other circumstances. Any form of restriction of the rights of citizens on the grounds of social, racial, national, linguistic or religious affiliation is prohibited.”

question_text_en: Right of spouse/partner of principal migrant to work.
citation_text_en: National law in Russia prohibits discrimination against migrants on the ground of race or ethnicity, in: 1) Constitution of the Russian Federation: Article 19; Article 62. 2) Code of the Russian Federation on Administrative Offenses "Discrimination": Article 5.62. 3) Labor Code of the Russian Federation: Article 3.

question_text_en: Right to maintain immigration status after loss of employment.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in Article 3 of the Labor Code of The Russian Federation of 31 December 2001 Federal Law No. 197-fz Of 2001: "Everyone shall have equal opportunities to realize his/her labor rights. No one can be constrained in his/her labor rights and freedoms or get any advantages irrespective of sex, race, color of skin, nationality, language, origins, property, social or position status, age, domicile, religious beliefs, political convictions, affiliation or non-affiliation with public associations as well as other factors not relevant to professional qualities of the employee. Establishment of distinctions, exceptions, preferences as well as limitation of employees' rights which are determined by the requirements inherent in a specific kind of work as set by federal laws or caused by the especial attention of the state to the persons requiring increased social and legal protection shall not be deemed discrimination. The persons considering themselves to be discriminated against in the sphere of labor shall be entitled to petition the federal labor inspectorate bodies and/or courts applying for restoration of their violated rights, compensation of the material loss and redress of the moral damage."

question_text_en: Right to equal employment conditions and protection.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right at different levels for different categories of migrants in Article 13.3 of the Federal Law of Russia # 115-FZ from 25.07.2002 On the Legal Position of Foreign Citizens in the Russian Federation. While foreign citizens of non-visa countries have a right to a free choice of employment within a specific region, other foreign citizens from countries with established visa regime are tied to a specific employer. According to Article 13.3: "Labor of foreign citizens from non-visa countries employed based on a patent 1. Employers or service providers registered as organizations or individual entrepreneurs, or notaries, attorneys acting in form of attorney's office, or other organizations which should be registered or licensed in accordance with federal laws have the right to attract to labor regulated foreign citizens arrived at the territory of the Russian Federation from non- visa countries, reached 18 years if such foreign citizen has a patent issued in accordance with respective Federal Law. 2.Employers or service providers who are citizens of the Russian Federation have the right to attract for provision of personal, domestic and other similar needs, not related to business activities, foreign citizens arrived at the territory of the Russian Federation from non- visa countries, reached 18 years if such foreign citizen has a patent issued in accordance with respective Federal Law. 15. If it is necessary for a foreign citizen to perform work in a profession (specialty, position, type of work) not specified in the patent, the foreign citizen has the right to apply to the territorial body of the federal executive body in the field of internal affairs, which issued the patent, for appropriate changes to the information contained in the patent. 16. A foreign citizen is not entitled to carry out work outside the limits of the subject of the Russian Federation on the territory of which he has been granted a patent. The employer or service provider is not entitled to involve a foreign citizen in employment under a patent outside the limits of the subject of the Russian Federation on the territory of which the foreign citizen has been issued a patent. In order to perform work on the territory of another subject of the Russian Federation, the foreign citizen is obliged to apply for a patent to the territorial body of the federal executive body in the field of internal affairs in the constituent entity of the Russian Federation, on the territory of which the foreign citizen intends to carry out work activities."

question_text_en: Right to form trade unions and other associations.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. As a general rule, in order to work in the Russian Federation, a migrant must obtain an individual work permit.

question_text_en: Right of regular migrants to redress before deportation or withdrawal of residency permit.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right, in a limited way, in part 5, article 5 of the Federal Law of Russia # 115-FZ from 25.07.2002 "On the Legal Position of Foreign Citizens in the Russian Federation." The period of temporary stay in the Russian Federation of a foreign citizen is extended upon issuance of a patent to a foreign citizen, upon extension of the validity of a patent Article 13.3. The term of a patent (work permit) can be repeatedly extended for a period of one month. At the same time, the total term of a patent, taking into account extensions, cannot be more than twelve months from the date of issue of the patent. The term of a patent is considered to be extended for the period for which personal income tax has been paid in the form of a fixed advance payment. It is important to note that an employer is not actually needed for a monthly patent renewal. The extension occurs by paying an advance taxpayment. After losing a job, if the migrant continues to pay the patent fee, the migration status will not be cancelled. However, migrants working under a patent have an obligation: within two months from the date of issuance of a patent, they are obliged to submit personally or send by registered mail with a return receipt to the territorial body of the federal executive body in the field of internal affairs that issued the patent, a copy of the employment contract or civil law contract for the performance of work (provision of services) (Clause 7 of Article 13.3 of Law N 115-FZ "On the Legal Status of Foreign Citizens in the Russian Federation"). In connection with non-fulfillment of this norm, the patent may be canceled and the migrant loses his migration status. If a visa migrant lost his job for the following reasons: - cancellation of the permission to attract and use foreign workers issued to the previous employer (customer of works, services); -termination of the activities of the employer (customer of works, services). Then, as a general rule, he has the right to conclude a new contract with another employer without losing his migration status. If the loss of a job is due to other circumstances, the migrant must obtain a new work permit. Otherwise, the status will be lost. For citizens of the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), there are greater protections in place as outlined in Article 97 of the Treaty on the Eurasian Economic Union" (Signed in Astana on May 29, 2014) / Labor activity of workers of the Member States 5. The period of temporary stay (residence) of a member state worker and family members in the territory of the state of employment is determined by the term of the labor or civil law contract concluded by the worker of the member state with the employer or customer of works (services). 9. In case of early termination of an employment or civil law contract after the expiration of 90 days from the date of entry into the territory of the state of employment, the worker of the Member State has the right to conclude a new labor or civil law contract within 15 days without leaving the territory of the state of employment.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to social security protections.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in article 11 of the Labor Code of The Russian Federation (31 December 2001) Federal Law No. 197-fz Of 2001. In the Russian Federation territory the rules set by this Code, the laws, other normative legal acts containing the labor law norms shall cover labor relations of foreign nationals, stateless persons, organizations established by them or with their participation, of employees at international organizations and foreign legal entities, unless otherwise provided for by a federal law or an international treaty of the Russian Federation. Part 4.1 article 2 Federal Law of December 29, 2006 N 255-FZ "On compulsory social insurance in case of temporary disability and in connection with motherhood" states that "Foreign citizens and stateless persons temporarily staying in the Russian Federation (with the exception of highly qualified specialists in accordance with the Federal Law of July 25, 2002 N115-FZ On the Legal Status of Foreign Citizens in the Russian Federation") are entitled to receive insurance coverage in the form of temporary disability benefits, subject to the payment of insurance premiums for them by insurers, for a period of at least six months preceding the month in which the insured event occurred. Payment of sick leave to citizens of the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) working under labor contracts, including highly qualified specialists temporarily staying in the Russian Federation, is no different from paying sick leave to Russian citizens (part 2, article 1.1 of Law N 255-FZ, paragraph 3, article 98 section XXVI of the Treaty on the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), Letter of the Ministry of Labor of Russia dated November18, 2015 N 17-3/B-560).

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to become lawfully settled.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right, as it relates to some types of social security protections, in: 1) Part 1, Article 3 of the Federal Law from 15.12.2001, No. 166-FZ "On State pensions in the Russian Federation." According to this article, "1. The right to a pension in accordance with this Federal Law have following persons: foreign citizens and stateless persons permanently residing in the territory of the Russian Federation - on the same basis as the citizens of the Russian Federation, unless otherwise provided by this Federal Law or the international treaties of the Russian Federation. 2) Part 4.1, Article 2, of the Federal Law No. 255-FZ of 29 December 2006 on Compulsory Social Insurance for Temporary Working Disability and Cases Related to Maternity: "Foreign nationals and stateless persons, temporary staying in the Russian Federation (except for highly qualified specialists) have the right to obtain social benefits on temporary working disability (payment of benefits for disability, pregnancy and childbirth, a one-time allowance for women registered with medical organizations in the early stages of pregnancy, a one-time allowance for the birth of a child, a monthly allowance for child care, social allowance for burial in case the insurant paid insurance premiums during the last 6 months before insurance case (changes came into force on 1 January 2023 in accordance with Federal Law no.237-fz of 14 July 2022).

question_text_en: Right of temporary migrants to settle regardless of initial status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Article 3 of the Russian Federal Law No. 1032-1 "On Employment in the Russian Federation” (19 April 1991): "The unemployment status shall be assigned to citizens who do not have job and earnings, registered with employment agencies in order to find a suitable job, looking for work and ready to start." Article 6 of the Russian Federal Law No. 1032-1 "On Employment in the Russian Federation" (19 April 1991).

question_text_en: Right to redress following employer breach of employment contract.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in Article 2.1, Article 6, Article 6.1, and Article 8 of the Federal Law dated July 25, 2002 No. 115-FZ “On the Legal Status of Foreign Citizens in the Russian Federation." The status of permanent residence is assigned only from the moment of obtaining a residence permit. A temporary residence permit does not grant the migrant the status of permanent residence, but nevertheless gives the right to stay in the Russian Federation for a long time (three years), without obtaining additional documents. To obtain the status of a Temporary Residence Permit, it is necessary to apply for a quota, within which the possibility of submitting documents for obtaining the status is distributed. After the allocation of the quota, it is necessary to provide a package of documents specified in the Order of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Russia dated 08.06.2020 N 407. Federation”). After obtaining a Temporary Residence Permit, migrants have the right to apply for a Residence Permit. To be eligible to receive a Residence Permit, a migrant must live in the Russian Federation with the status of a Temporary Residence Permit for one year. To obtain a residence permit, a migrant provides a package of documents specified in the Order of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Russia dated June 11, 2020 N 417 There are a number of categories that have the right to obtain a residence permit without obtaining a temporary residence permit (Part 2, Article 8 of the Federal Law “On the Legal Status of Foreign Citizens in the Russian Federation”).

question_text_en: Right not to have identity documents confiscated.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in: 1) Part 2 of the article 325 of the Criminal Code of The Russian Federation: Theft of a passport or any other important personal document from a person shall be punishable with a fine in an amount of up to 80 thousand roubles or in the amount of the wage or salary, or any other income of the convicted person for a period of up to six months, or by compulsory works for a term of up to 360 hours, or by corrective labour for a term of up to one year, or by arrest for a term of up to three months. 2) The Russian Federation (RF) Administrative Offenses Code: Article 19.16. Deliberate damage of the document certifying the identity of the citizen (passport) or the loss of the citizen's identification document (passport) (edition of the Federal Law of December 21, 2013 N 376-FZ). Article 19.17. Illegal confiscation of a document certifying the citizen's identity (passport), or receipt of the document certifying the citizen’s identity (passport) as a deposit. 3) The article 19.17 of the Code Of Administrative Offences Of The Russian Federation No. 195-Fz Of December 30, 2001: Unlawful Seizure by an Official of the Identification Card of a Citizen (Passport) or Accepting an Identification Card of a Citizen (Passport) as a Pledge: 1. Unlawful seizure by an official of an identification card(passport) - shall entail the imposition of an administrative fine in the amount of one hundred to three hundred roubles.

question_text_en: Right to birth registration.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in the Order of the Ministry of Health of Russia dated October 13, 2021 N 987n "On approval of the form of a birth document and the procedure for issuing it." Based on this order, a medical birth certificate is issued. Upon receipt of a medical birth certificate, it is possible to register the child with the relevant state bodies on the basis of the article 14 of the Federal Law No. 143-FZ of 1997, on Acts of Civil Status: The basis for the state registration of birth is a document issued by the medical organization, regardless of its legal form of organization in which the birth took place.

question_text_en: Right to government document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en:
No protection of this right. Various migration laws require migrants maintain and require their passports from their country of origin as a proof of their identity. National legislation in the Russian Federation prescribes the issuance of documents confirming the identity of only certain categories of migrants:
 1) Stateless persons. Article 5.2. Federal Law No. 115-FZ of July 25, 2002 "On the Legal Status of Foreign Citizens in the Russian Federation" provides for the possibility of issuing a temporary identity card for a stateless person in the Russian Federation 2) Article 7 Federal Law of February 19, 1993 N 4528-1 "On Refugees" establishes that a person recognized as a refugee who has reached the age of eighteen years is issued a certificate of the established form. A refugee certificate is an identity document of a person recognized as a refugee and confirms his right to stay on the territory of the Russian Federation. 3) Article 12 Federal Law No. 4528-1 of February 19, 1993 "On Refugees" establishes that the Certificate of Temporary Asylum is an identity document of a person who has received temporary asylum on the territory of the Russian Federation and confirms his right to stay on the territory of the Russian Federation. a) A person who has been granted temporary asylum on the territory of the Russian Federation and who has received a certificate of temporary asylum is subject to registration at the place of stay in the manner prescribed by the legislation of the Russian Federation. b) Documents certifying the working status of a migrant in the Russian Federation in accordance with Article 13 of the Federal Law of July 25, 2002 N 115-FZ "On the Legal Status of Foreign Citizens in the Russian Federation" are: a work patent (visa-free foreigners) and a work permit (visa foreigners ). c) The national legislation of the Russian Federation requires migrants to have valid documents confirming their legal status in the Russian Federation. Legal basis, article 5, 6, 8 Federal Law of July 25, 2002 N 115-FZ "On the Legal Status of Foreign Citizens in the Russian Federation"

question_text_en: Right against destruction of document recognizing residency, work status, and identity.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in Article 325 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation: "Abduction or damage of documents, stamps, seals or abduction of excise labels, special labels or marks of conformity." According to part 2 of this article: "Theft of a passport or any other important personal document from a person shall be punishable with a fine in an amount of up to 80 thousand roubles, or in the amount of the wage or salary, or any other income of the convicted person for a period of up to six months, or by compulsory works for a term of up to 360 hours, or by corrective labor for a term of up to one year, or by arrest for a term of up to three months."

question_text_en: Right to communicate with consular officials.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this obligation in Part 9 of the article 12 of the Criminal and Executive Code of The Russian Federation from January 8, 1997, Of No. 1-FZ.: "Foreign citizens sentenced to compulsory labor, arrest or deprivation of freedom have the right to maintain contacts with diplomatic missions and consular sections of their States in the Russian Federation. Citizens of States that do not have diplomatic representations and consular sections in the Russian Federation have the right to maintain contacts with the diplomatic missions of States that have undertaken to protect their interests or with intergovernmental bodies concerned with the protection of these convicts." According to Part 3 of the article 96 of the Criminal-procedural Code of The Russian Federation no. 174-fz Of December 18, 2001: "If the suspect is a citizen or a subject of another state, the Embassy or the Consulate of this state shall be notified within the term, pointed out in the first part of the present Article."

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The law permits the detention of migrant children. According to Part 2-3, Article 22 of the Federal Law from June 24, 1999: "On systems of prevention of neglect towards minors and crimes committed my minors", underage offenders can be placed in centers of temporary detention. The law does, however, provide for seperation of minor children within immigration centers. Article 14 of the order of the Government of the Russian Federation from December 30, 2013 of No. 1306: "About approval of Rules of content (stay) in special organizations of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Russian Federation of foreign citizens and the stateless persons which are subject to administrative expulsion out of limits of the Russian Federation in the form of exclusion...deportation or readmission." Under the law, spouses, parents, children can be "placed together in the separate premises of a detention center."

question_text_en: Right of migrants to be free from detention on the basis of migrant status.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in: 1) Article 25.10 of the Federal Law No. 114-FZ of August 15, 1996, "Concerning the Procedure for Exit from the Russian Federation and Entry into the Russian Federation." 2) Article 34. 3 of the Federal Law No. 115-FZ of July 25, 2002, "On the Legal Position of Foreign Citizens in the Russian Federation." 3) Article 1.5 and Article 3.10 of the "Code of Administrative Offenses of the Russian Federation" No. 195-FZ dated December 30, 2001. Detention of migrants is a complex procedure that could be applied only by the court. It is not sufficient to just solely identify the immigration status (for example unauthorized immigrants). In addition, the court should identify that detention is a well-proportioned measure to be applied in each particular case, and a guilt in violation of the migration legislation should be proven. Migration status and guilt are different terms of the law.

question_text_en: Right to appeal legality, conditions, and length of detention
citation_text_en: National law in Russia allows migrants to appeal legality, conditions, and length of detention, in: 1) The Code of Criminal Procedure of the Russian Federation: Article 19 and Article 50 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation. According to this article, “Actions (inaction) and decisions of the court, the prosecutor, the head of the investigative body, the investigator, the body of inquiry, the head of the body of inquiry, the head of the unit of inquiry and the interrogating officer can be appealed. Each convicted person has the right to review the sentence by a higher court and Part 3 of Article 50 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation.” 2) Article 30.1 of the "Code of the Russian Federation on Administrative Offenses" dated December 30, 2001 No. 195-FZ. Article 30.1 establishes the right to appeal against a decision in a case on an administrative offense. 3) Resolution of the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation of May 23, 2017 N 14-P "On the case of checking the constitutionality of the provisions of Articles 31.7 and 31.9 of the Code of Administrative Offenses of the Russian Federation in connection with the complaint of a stateless person N.G. Mskhiladze." 4) Article 4 of the Administrative Court Proceedings Code of the Russian Federation from 08.03.2015 21-FZ: Each concerned person has a right to apply to a court for protection of violated or disputed rights, freedoms, and legitimate interests ...Chapter 28 of the Administrative Court Proceedings Code of the Russian Federation from 08.03.2015 21-FZ "Procedures on administrative cases on placement of a foreign citizen who is undergoing deportation or readmission into a specialized institution or on cases on prolongation of term of stay in a specialized institution of a foreign citizen undergoing deportation or readmission."

question_text_en: Right to an individualized detention decision.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in: 1) Article 91-92 of the Code of Criminal Procedure of the Russian Federation. 2) Article 27.4. "Code of the Russian Federation on Administrative Offenses" dated December 30, 2001, N 195-FZ Report on Administrative Detention: "1. A protocol is drawn up on administrative detention, which indicates the date and place of its compilation, position, surname and initials of the person who drew up the protocol, information about detained person, time, place and motives for detention." 3) Part 5 of the article 34 of the Federal Law No. 115-FZ of July 25, 2002, On the Legal Position of Foreign Citizens in the Russian Federation: "The foreign citizens subject to the administrative banishment out of the boundaries of the Russian Federation shall be kept by court decision in the specially allocated premises of the bodies of internal affairs or of the security, or in the special institutions set up in accordance with the procedure laid down by the law of the subject of the Russian Federation, until the execution of the decision on the administrative banishment from the boundaries of the Russian Federation."

question_text_en: Right to be free from torture and inhumane treatment.
citation_text_en: National law in Russia provides that migrants have a right to be free from torture and cruel, inhumane, and degrading treatment or punishment in the Constitution of the Russian Federation: Article 21. According to this article, "1. The dignity of the individual is protected by the state. Nothing can be grounds for belittling him. 2. No one shall be subjected to torture, violence, other cruel or degrading treatment or punishment. No one can be subjected to medical, scientific or other experiments without voluntary consent.” Furthermore, Article 117 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation establishes a general ban on the infliction of physical or mental suffering by systematic beatings or other violent acts criminalized in the Russian Federation.

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for all migrants. However, the law does limit the use of force against migrant women and migrant children. Article 35 of the Law Of The Russian Federation No. 4730-i Of April 1, 1993, On The State Border Of the Russian Federation. The Use of Weapons and Combat Material: "As they carry out the protection of the State Border within the boundaries of the border territory, the border guard agencies, the Air Defense Troops and the forces of the Navy shall use weapons and combat material ….against persons, air, sea and river craft and vessels and other means of transportation which have crossed (which are crossing) the State Border in violation of the rules established under the present law, in response to their using force or in the events when the stopping of a violation or the detaining of the violators may not be effected by other means; for the protection of citizens from an assault threatening their life and health ….for countering assaults against servicemen…. The use of weapons and combat material shall be preceded by an explicit warning of the intent to use them and warning shots. …. It shall be prohibited to use weapons and combat material in respect to women and minors excluding the cases of armed assault on their part or of armed resistance on their part or a group assault threatening life."

question_text_en: Right to be free from use of lethal force to prevent entry to territory.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for all migrants. However, the law does limit the use of force against migrant women and migrant children. Article 35 of the Law Of The Russian Federation No. 4730-i Of April 1, 1993, On The State Border Of the Russian Federation. The Use of Weapons and Combat Material: "As they carry out the protection of the State Border within the boundaries of the border territory, the border guard agencies, the Air Defense Troops and the forces of the Navy shall use weapons and combat material ….against persons, air, sea and river craft and vessels and other means of transportation which have crossed (which are crossing) the State Border in violation of the rules established under the present law, in response to their using force or in the events when the stopping of a violation or the detaining of the violators may not be effected by other means; for the protection of citizens from an assault threatening their life and health ….for countering assaults against servicemen…. The use of weapons and combat material shall be preceded by an explicit warning of the intent to use them and warning shots. …. It shall be prohibited to use weapons and combat material in respect to women and minors excluding the cases of armed assault on their part or of armed resistance on their part or a group assault threatening life."

question_text_en: Right to be protected from trafficking or smuggling.
citation_text_en: National law in Russia exempts trafficked and smuggled migrants from criminal prosecutions in The Criminal Code of the Russian Federation exempts trafficked/smuggled migrants from criminal prosecution: Article 24; Article 127.1; Article 322.1. Article 24.1 specifically exempts trafficked and smuggled migrants from criminal prosecution.

question_text_en: Right to maintain citizenship status after convictions.
citation_text_en: National law in Russia protects this right in Article 22 of the Federal Law no. 62-fz Of May 31, 2002, on Russian Federation Citizenship. According to Article 22, acquired citizenship may only be revoked in the following cases: the applicant submitted fraudulent documents or false information; the applicant refused to take an Oath; the individual commited and was convicted of a crime indicated in the Article 22 (convictions for criminal offenses of a terrorist nature).

question_text_en: Right of economic migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation provides pathway to citizenship for economic migrants via obtaining the primary status of a Temporary Residence Permit, then obtaining a Residence Permit and only then Russian Citizenship. The procedure for obtaining these statuses and citizenship is regulated in Article 6, 8 of the Federal Law of July 25, 2002 N 115-FZ "On the Legal Status of Foreign Citizens in the Russian Federation" and Art. 13-14 Federal Law No. 62-FZ of May 31,2002 "On Citizenship of the Russian Federation." Part 2 of the article 14 of the Federal Law no. 62-fz (May 31, 2002) on Russian Federation Citizenship: " 2. Foreign citizens and stateless persons residing on the territory of the Russian Federation shall be entitled to apply for admittance to Russian citizenship in a simplified manner without observing the condition concerning the time of residence established by Item "a" of Part One of Article 13 of this Federal Law if the said citizens and persons: ...g) entrepreneurs who carry out business activities in Russia no less than three years before the date of application for admission to citizenship of the Russian Federation. In this case, the total sum of taxes and insurance contribution paid by the entrepreneurs each year should not be less than 1 million rubles (changes came into force in accordance with Federal Law no.569-fz of 28 December2022). z) investors, whose share of the contribution in the authorized (share) capital of a Russian legal entity at least 10%-- continuously during three years before the day of application for the citizenship . The amount of the authorized (share) capital of such entity must not be less than 100 million rubles and the amount paid by the entity in tax and insurance contributions to the Pension Fund during this period shall not be less than 6 million rubles (changes came into force in accordance with Federal Law no.569-fz of 28 December 2022) i)migrant workers working in the Russian Federation no less than a year in accordance with an approved list of professions (changes came into force in accordance with Federal Law no.569-fz of 28 December 2022)."

question_text_en: Right of humanitarian migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation provides a pathway to citizenship for humanitarian migrants via obtaining the primary status of a Temporary Residence Permit, then obtaining a Residence Permit and only then Russian Citizenship. The procedure for obtaining these statuses and citizenship is regulated in Article 6, 8 of the Federal Law of July 25, 2002 N 115-FZ "On the Legal Status of Foreign Citizens in the Russian Federation" and Art. 13-14 Federal Law No. 62-FZ of May 31, 2002 "On Citizenship of the Russian Federation."

question_text_en: Right of family migrants to citizenship.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation provides pathway to citizenship for family migrants via the same grounds as for other categories of migrants is regulated in Article 13 and 14 of Federal Law No. 62-FZ dated May 31, 2002. If one of the family members already has Russian citizenship, then the procedure for obtaining citizenship is simplified. The spouse of a citizen of the Russian Federation can receive a temporary residence permit without taking into account the quota (part 3 of article 6 of the Federal Law “On the legal status of foreign citizens”) A migrant having parents or children of citizens of the Russian Federation can obtain a residence permit without obtaining a Temporary Residence Permit (Part 2, Article 8 of the Federal Law “On the Legal Status of Foreign Citizens”). If there are children or a registered marriage more than 3 years ago, a migrant can obtain citizenship without taking into account the requirement for a five-year period of residence in the Russian Federation.

question_text_en: Right to dual nationality.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation allows migrants to obtain dual nationality by retaining their nationality of origin in Article 6 and Article 13 of the Federal Law “On Citizenship of the Russian Federation" and Article 62 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation. According to these legislations: "1. A citizen of the Russian Federation who also has another citizenship is considered by the Russian Federation only as a citizen of the Russian Federation, except for the cases provided for by an international treaty of the Russian Federation or federal law."

question_text_en: Right to freedom to hold opinion.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right for migrants, commensurate with citizens, in Article 28 and Article 29 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation (RF). Article 28 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation (adopted at National Voting on December 12, 1993) states that "everyone shall be guaranteed the freedom of conscience, the freedom of religion, including the right to profess individually or together with other any religion or to profess no religion at all, to freely choose, possess and disseminate religious and other views and act according to them." Article 29 guarantees freedom of conscience, freedom of religion, including the right to profess individually or jointly with others any religion or not to profess any, freely choose, have and disseminate religious and other beliefs and act in accordance with them.

question_text_en: Right to freedom of expression.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in Articles 28 and 29 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation. Article 28 states that, "Everyone shall be guaranteed the freedom of conscience, the freedom of religion, including the right to profess individually or together with other any religion or to profess no religion at all, to freely choose, possess and disseminate religious and other views and act according to them." Article 29 states: "1. Everyone is guaranteed freedom of thought and speech. 2. Propaganda or agitation that incite social, racial, national or religious hatred and enmity are not allowed. Propaganda of social, racial, national, religious or linguistic superiority is prohibited. 3. No one can be forced to express their views and beliefs or to renounce them."

question_text_en: Right to freedom of association.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in Article 29 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation. Article 29 states that "1. Everyone shall be guaranteed the freedom of ideas and speech. 2. The propaganda or agitation instigating social, racial, national or religious hatred and strife shall not be allowed. The propaganda of social, racial, national, religious or linguistic supremacy shall be banned. 3. No one may be forced to express his views and convictions or to reject them."

question_text_en: Right to freedom of assembly.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. However, national law in the Russian Federation protects this right for all regular migrants in Article 30 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation which states: "1. Everyone shall have the right to association, including the right to create trade unions for the protection of his or her interests. The freedom of activity of public association shall be guaranteed. 2. No one may be compelled to join any association and remain in it." Additionally, Article 6 of the Federal Law No. 82-FZ of May 19,1995 "On Public Associations" : “Founders, members and participants of a public association” does not establish restrictions on citizenship to members of public associations. Article 19 of the same law grants migrants the right to participate in public associations.

category: Thought, conscience, and religion or belief
question_text_en: Right of freedom of thought, conscience and religion or belief.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in the Federal Law No. 115-FZ of July 25, 2002, "On the Legal Position of Foreign Citizens in the Russian Federation." As a general rule, there are no economic requirements for temporary staying migrants in the Russian Federation, but upon obtaining various long-term statuses (temporary residence permit; residence permit etc.), there are requirements to provide evidence confirming the presence of a source of legal income in the Russian Federation, allowing them to suppose themselves.

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to access criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: The national law in the Russian Federation protects this right in the Constitution of the Russian Federation (RF), part 3. Art. 62. “Foreign citizens and stateless persons in the Russian Federation enjoy the rights and bear obligations on an equal footing with citizens of the Russian Federation, except in cases established by federal law or an international treaty of the Russian Federation.” Part 1, Article 19 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation states: "1. Everyone is equal before the law and the courts." Furthermore, Article 43 of the Code of Criminal Procedure of the Russian Federation establishes the rights of the victim, including the right to file a civil suit in criminal proceedings.

question_text_en: Right of victims of crime to immigration status or relief from expulsion.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right, in certain circumstances, in Part 3, Article 5 of Federal Law No. 115-FZ of July 25, 2002 “On the Legal Status of Foreign Citizens in the Russian Federation” which contains provisions on extending the period of temporary stay in exceptional circumstances. Such an exceptional circumstance for extending the period of temporary stay of a migrant may be the recognition of a migrant as a victim in a criminal case. The decision to extend the period of temporary stay in this case is made subjectively by the bodies of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. There are no guarantees that such a decision will be made in relation to the victim. However, this rule applies only to migrants temporarily staying in Russia; migrants with other migration status such as permanent residence and temporary residence are not protected by this article.

question_text_en: Right of child migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in relation to derivative immigration status and use of force at the borders. In relation to derivative immigration status, the rights are protected in: the Federal Law no. 115-fz of July 25, 2002, on the legal status of foreign citizens in the Russian Federation: Article 5; Article 6; Article 8. These provisions expand the duration of immigration status of migrant children who accompany their family members in a manner that is more generous than that provided to other migrants. In relation to the use of force at the borders, the right is protected in: Article 35 of the Law of The Russian Federation No. 4730-i of April 1, 1993, On The State Border of the Russian Federation. The Use of Weapons and Combat Material: "As they carry out the protection of the State Border within the boundaries of the border territory, the border guard agencies, the Air Defense Troops and the forces of the Navy shall use weapons and combat material ….against persons, air, sea and river craft and vessels and other means of transportation which have crossed (which are crossing) the State Border in violation of the rules established under the present law, in response to their using force or in the events when the stopping of a violation or the detaining of the violators may not be effected by other means; for the protection of citizens from an assault threatening their life and health ….for countering assaults against servicemen…. The use of weapons and combat material shall be preceded by an explicit warning of the intent to use them and warning shots. …. It shall be prohibited to use weapons and combat material in respect to women and minors excluding the cases of armed assault on their part or of armed resistance on their part or a group assault threatening life."

question_text_en: Right of women migrants to special protections.
citation_text_en: National law in Russia protects this right in part 4.1 of article 2 of the Federal Law no. 255-fz of 29 December 2006 on Compulsory Social Insurance for Temporary Working Disability and Cases Related to Maternity.

question_text_en: Rights of migrants with disabilities to special protection.
citation_text_en: National law in the Russian Federation protects this right in Part 1 of the article 7 of the Federal Law No. 115-FZ of July 25, 2002. On the Legal Position of Foreign Citizens in the Russian Federation: "A temporary residence permit shall not be issued to a foreign citizen, and a previously issued permit shall be canceled if this foreign citizen...within a regular year as of the date of issuance of a temporary residence permit did not exercise labor activity in the procedure established by the legislation of the Russian Federation within one hundred and eighty days, or has not derived income, or does not have enough means of subsistence to support himself and his family members dependent on him without assistance of the State on a level which is not lower than the cost of living established by the laws of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation on whose territory he is allowed to temporarily reside. The operation of this provision shall not extend to a foreign citizen who is a pensioner or disabled person."

question_text_en: Right to government-provided counsel in proceedings related to migrant status.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. Article 139 of the Criminal Procedure Law provides that those accused of major criminal infractions may request the court to appoint a lawyer at the expense of the State, should they have no financial ability to afford an attorney. However, this resource is specifically not available to migrants.

question_text_en: Right to government-provided interpretation in criminal proceedings.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right for all migrants. While Article 171 of the Criminal Procedure Law states that if the litigants or witnesses or both of them do not understand Arabic, the court may appoint a translator, the law does not clearly state whether this will be at government expense. Additionally, the law is not explicit that this applies to all categories of migrants.

question_text_en: Right to be protected from prosecution for unauthorized entry.
citation_text_en: National law in Saudi Arabia protects this right in Article 50 of the Residence law of 1952. This article states that while migrants who enter the territory illegally, will be put into administrative detention until they are deported, they face no criminal or civil sanctions from illegal entry.

question_text_en: Right to equal access to public adult education institutions.
citation_text_en: No protection of this right. The only migrants with access to publicly supported housing are refugees, who are provided basic accommodation for the duration of their stay. All other forms of public housing programs are only made available to citizens.
